properties.title: Stary Sad

Shalmaneser Gate
properties.description: The “Shalmaneser Gate” gave access from the lower town of Kalhu to the citadel. This entrance, which was flanked by a pair of inscribed stone lions, was located on the east citadel wall, just north of the Nabû temple Ezida. This gate, which its excavators named after the ninth-century-BC Assyrian ruler Shalmaneser III (r. 858–824 BC), is assumed to have been the main east citadel gate, especially since a road ran between it and the armory (Fort Shalmaneser) located in the southwest corner of the city.

properties.title: Mašqû Gate
properties.description: Nineveh's western wall had seven (or eight) gates: the Mašqû Gate was the northernmost one. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Ea-mušēšir-kuppīya, which means "The God Ea Is the One Who Properly Directs (Water Flow into) My Cisterns."

properties.title: Step Gate of the Palace
properties.description: Nineveh's western wall had seven (or eight) gates: the Step Gate of the Palace was the second gate from the northern city wall. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it sometime between 694 and 691 B.C. and he gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Libūr-ēpissa, which means "May Its Builder Endure." The gate is still unlocated, but, based on its everyday name Akkadian name mušlālum ša ēkalli ("Step Gate of the Palace"), it must have led up to Sennacherib's Palace on the citadel, perhaps up to the harem or its northern section.

properties.title: Samshvilde
properties.description: Fortified settlement in southern Georgia. The Samshvilde site is one of the oldest cities in Georgia, with remains from the Bronze Age Kura-Araxes Culture. Samshvilde was an important city in the late antique and medieval periods until it was sacked in 1440 by Jahan Shah; it went in decline but was inhabited as late as the 18th-19th centuries. The site includes a number of structures, including an 11th-13th century citadel, several early medieval churches, homes, and burial grounds.

properties.title: Icknield Street
properties.description: Icknield Street was a road of Roman Britain running from Fosse Way to Templeborough.

properties.description: A land situated on the middle Euphrates, to north and west of the kingdom of Suhu and to the south of the land Bit-Halupê. Eleven of its cities are mentioned in Assyrian inscriptions of the first millennium B.C.

properties.description: A district of ancient Athens located northwest of the Acropolis, the Kerameikos takes its name from the potters' workshops in the area; the portion of the district lying outside the Dipylon Gate served as a necropolis.

properties.description: Predynastic and Early Dynastic burial site containing over 1,000 burials. It is the type-site of the Amratian culture.

properties.title: Villa El Soldán (The Sultan)
properties.description: A Roman villa 300 meters east northeast of the eastern tip of Laguna Cernea, north of the modern village Santa Colomba de Somoza. Constructed under Tiberius, it was likely the residence of the official in charge of gold extraction.

properties.title: Great Bulmore
properties.description: Site of a suburban Roman settlement on the bank of the river Usk, 2 km. north-east of the legionary fortress at Caerleon.

properties.title: Tomb of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus
properties.description: A tomb at Pompeii's Herculaneum gate that may be that of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus.

properties.title: Thermopolium of Vetutius Placidus
properties.description: The house and thermopolium of Vetutius Placidus (I,8,8) opens directly onto the south side of the Via dell'Abbondanza.

properties.title: Roman Forum at Thugga
properties.description: The Roman Forum at Thugga is large, covering more than 900 square meters.

properties.title: Alverdiscott
properties.description: A Roman marching camp identified via cropmarks.

properties.title: Old Burrow
properties.description: A first century Roman fortlet measuring 44 by 85 meters.

properties.title: Clovelly Dykes
properties.description: Clovelly Dykes is an unexcavated Iron Age hillfort.

properties.title: Eukratidia
properties.description: An ancient settlement, mentioned by both Strabo and Ptolemy. While its modern location is uncertain, it may correspond to a fortified settlement in northern Afghanistan known today as Dilbarjin (thus Bernard in EncIran). Hiebert and Kohl (BAtlas) offered only the suggestion that it might have been located somewhere in the territory of modern Uzbekistan.

properties.title: Casiana
properties.description: A fortress (phrourion) and settlement near Apamea on the Orontes river. The precise location is unknown today.

properties.title: Potto Codinu
properties.description: A necropolis in use from the Neolithic period through to the Iron Age with numerous hypogeum-type tombs.

properties.title: Cathedral of St. James, Jerusalem
properties.description: A 12th-century Armenian church in Jerusalem, the principal church of the Armenian Patriarchate of Jerusalem.

properties.title: Areopagus
properties.description: Named after a mythical trial of the god Ares, the Areopagus is a rocky outcropping in Athens located to the northwest of the acropolis. The hill was used as a meeting place for the Council of the Areopagus which functioned as a council of elders for the city of Athens. The Areopagus is also traditionally identified as the setting for Paul's sermon to Athens.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Segobriga
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Segobriga dates to the Flavian period. It measures approximately 75 by 65 meters and could seat 5,500 spectators.

properties.title: Roman theater at Vendeuil-Caply
properties.description: The larger of the two Roman theaters at Vendeuil-Caply was located at the northwest angle of the cardo and the decumanus.

properties.title: Madrasa Gumushtakin
properties.description: Center of the Madrasa Gumushtakin in the Ancient City of Bostra.

properties.title: Peyriac-de-Mer
properties.description: A small pre-Roman trading post on the edge of the Bages-Sigean lagoon.

properties.title: Mullissu Gate
properties.description: Most 7th-century B.C. Assyrian inscriptions record that Nineveh had eight south- and east-facing gates: the Mullissu Gate was the fifth of these. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial names Ištar-zāninki-kurbī ("O Ištar Bless the One Who Provides for You!") and Ša-Sîn-ahhē-erība-manzalti-ereqqi-kinnī-palêšu ("Make Sennacherib's Dynasty as Firm as the Position of the Wagon Constellation!").

properties.title: Aššur Gate
properties.description: Most 7th-century B.C. Assyrian inscriptions record that Nineveh had eight south- and east-facing gates: the Aššur Gate was the second of these. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial names Lilbur-iššak-Aššur ("May the Vice-Regent of the God Aššur Endure") and Libūr-iššak-Aššur ("May the Vice-Regent of the God Aššur Stay in Good Health").

properties.title: Sennacherib Gate
properties.description: Most 7th-century B.C. Assyrian inscriptions record that Nineveh had eight south- and east-facing gates: the Sennacherib Gate was the third of these. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Sāpin-gimir-nakirī, which means "The One Who Flattens All Enemies." During the reign of Sennacherib's grandson, the gate was renamed the Ashurbanipal Gate.

properties.title: Šamaš Gate
properties.description: Most 7th-century B.C. Assyrian inscriptions record that Nineveh had eight south- and east-facing gates: the Šamaš Gate was the fourth of these. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Enlil-mukīn-palêya, which means "The God Enlil Is the One Who Makes My Reign Firm."

properties.title: Circus Maximus Mithraeum
properties.description: A mithraeum adjacent to the Circus Maximus and facing the carceres of the same was located at the margin of the Forum Boarium and now situated beneath a building in the via dell'Ara Massima. The site was excavated in 1931.

properties.title: Circus at Lepcis Magna
properties.description: The Circus at Lepcis Magna is located to the southeast of their city and measures ca. 100 x 450 m.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Carsulae
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Carsulae dates to the first century A.D.

properties.title: Sîn Gate
properties.description: The northern city wall of Nineveh had three gates: the Sîn Gate was the westernmost of the three. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and called it the Gate of the Garden, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Igisigsig-mušammeh-ṣippāti ("The God Igisigsig Is the One Who Makes Orchards Flourish"). Late in 695 B.C. or early in 694 B.C., the gate was dedicated to the moon-god Sîn and renamed Nannāru-nāṣir-agê-bēlūtīya ("The Divine Nannāru Is the One Who Protects My Lordly Crown").

properties.description: A hill located near the acropolis of Athens. Pausanias discusses fortifications in the Hellenistic period; later the Philopappos Monument was built at the summit.

properties.title: Sapinuwa
properties.description: Bronze Age Hittite city at the location of modern Ortaköy, Turkey

properties.title: Van Fortress
properties.description: Van Fortress is an ancient citadel of Urartu built during the ninth through seventh centuries BC.

properties.title: Great Mosque of Aleppo
properties.description: The Great Mosque of Aleppo, also known as the Umayyad Mosque of Aleppo, is the largest and one of the oldest mosques in the city of Aleppo, Syria.

properties.title: tribus Poblilia
properties.description: Tribus Poblilia was a later rural tribe of Rome, which was established in 358 B.C.

properties.title: Walbrook (stream)
properties.description: Historical water course that ran through the heart of Roman London and flowed into the modern River Thames. Completely built over since the 19th century, it exists only as a subterranean stream and part of the London sewer system.

properties.title: Trawscoed fort
properties.description: A Roman auxiliary fort located on the river Ystwyth in Ceredigion, Wales. The fort overlooks a Roman bridge and was built during the AD 70s.

properties.title: Pen Dinas hill fort
properties.description: Pen Dinas hill fort is a large Iron Age enclosure on the coast of Ceredigion, Wales.

properties.title: Pencoedfoel
properties.description: Pencoedfoel is the location of an ancient hill fort in Wales.

properties.title: Ramesseum
properties.description: The funerary temple of Ramesses II, built within the area known as the Ipet-isut, "The Most Selected of Places", along the Nile River.

properties.title: Via Veientana
properties.description: The ancient Via Veientana led from Etruscan Veii to the Tiber river.

properties.title: Doric temple of Segesta
properties.description: The Doric temple of Segesta is an incomplete (6 x 14) temple of the Doric order begun in the 420s B.C.

properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 98 C1 unnamed wall (around Merv, “Gilyakin-Chilburj wall” TKM)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 98 B1 unnamed wall (around Munon tepe and Kushmeikhan, “Antiochus wall” TKM)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 98 G1 unnamed wall (N Maidan kurgan UZB)

properties.title: Kam Pirak wall
properties.description: The Kam Pirak wall is a rammed earth defensive wall located near Kumsar, Afghanistan. It has been traced for ca. 60 km.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 98 G1 unnamed wall (S Maidan kurgan UZB)

properties.title: So-called House of the Mosaic Columns
properties.description: Suburban villa outside the Herculaneum gate in Pompeii

properties.title: Telul eth-Thalathat
properties.description: A site in northern Iraq (approximately 40 km west of Mosul) comprising a cluster of four large tells and several smaller low tells. The site was occupied in the Ubaid, Uruk, and Middle Assyrian periods.

properties.title: Bodhgaya
properties.description: A town in India traditionally identified as the place in which Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment. One of the four main Buddhist pilgrimage sites, it is home to the Mahabodhi Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 98 G1 unnamed pass (N Maidan kurgan (“Iron Gate”) UZB)

properties.title: Dionysopolis
properties.description: This city was founded by Attalos II and Eumenes II. Although its precise location is unknown today, it was located somewhere on the north bank of the Maeander River, near Çal Dag and the Çal Ova.

properties.title: Nuraghe la Prisciona
properties.description: A nuragic site of northeast Sardinia, occupied from the fourteenth until the ninth century BC. At its height the complex covers ca. five hectares.

properties.title: Ponte di Pioraco
properties.description: A single-arch Roman bridge built during the principate of Augustus.

properties.title: Tell Abu en-Ni'aj
properties.description: Archaeological site in the Jordan Valley containing the remains of a village dated to the Early Bronze Age IV (ca. 2500-1900 BCE).

properties.title: Alcala de Guadayra
properties.description: A Spanish village located to the east of Sevilla that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. It is now known as Alcalá de Guadaíra.

properties.title: Varaha Cave
properties.description: The modern name of a seventh-century Pallava cave temple in Mahābalipuram.

properties.title: Arapsu Bridge
properties.description: A Roman bridge near Antalya, Turkey.

properties.title: Timpone della Motta
properties.description: The Timpone della Motta is an archaeological site located near Francavilla Marittima. The site was inhabited from the Middle Bronze Age onward. During the Iron Age, an Oenotrian settlement flourished here, one that developed into an important sanctuary. The site passed into Greek control in the later seventh century B.C. and was eventually abandoned following the Bruttian conquest of the region during the fourth century B.C.

properties.title: Combley Roman villa
properties.description: Site of Romano-British villa of winged corridor type, probably late 3rd century CE in date.

properties.title: Castel Sant'Angelo
properties.description: The Mausoleum of Hadrian, also known as the Castel Sant'Angelo, is an Imperial tomb on the banks of the Tiber river.

properties.title: tribus Sabatina
properties.description: The tribus Sabatina (or Sabatia) was a later rural tribe of ancient Rome, which was established in 387 B.C.

properties.title: Oakwood Roman fort
properties.description: A Roman fort dating ca. A.D. 80 located southwest of Selkirk.

properties.title: Via Popilia (in Aemilia)
properties.description: A road from Ariminum up the Adriatic Coast toward what is now Venice.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Volaterrae
properties.description: The ruins of a sizable Roman amphitheater at Volaterrae came to light in 2016.

properties.title: Regio II (Caelimontium)
properties.description: According to the Regionary Catalogues, Regio II contained 7 streets (vici), 7 shrines, 3,600 blocks of flats, 127 houses, 27 grain warehouses (horrea), 85 bath-houses; 65 cisterns; 15 bakeries/mills, and had a circumference of 12,200 paces. The region had 48 vicomagistri and 2 curators.

properties.title: Capitolium of Verona
properties.description: Excavations have determined the location of the capitolium of Roman Verona, part of an extensive, terraced complex that underpins medieval and later structures of the city. The capitolium itself stretches from the northern end of the modern Piazza Erbe to the via Emilei, lying beneath the Palazzo Maffei, church of San Benedetto, Palazzo Malaspina and surrounding structures.

properties.title: Necropolis at Sutrium
properties.description: Numerous rock-cut tombs are evident at Sutri, most dating from the Hellenistic period and later. In archaeological terms the tombs are poorly understood.

properties.title: Mausoleum of Romulus
properties.description: Tomb of Valerius Romulus (ca. AD 292/295 – 309), son of Maxentius, along the Via Appia.

properties.title: Temple of Augustales at Centuripae
properties.description: An early Imperial (first to third centuries) temple at Centuripae that has been associated with the priestly college of the Augustales.

properties.title: Yalburt Hittite sanctuary
properties.description: A sanctuary dating to the Late Hittite Empire, with a hieroglyphic Luwian inscription commemorating the achievements of Tudhaliya IV (thirteenth century BC).

properties.title: Astakos
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Ani city wall
properties.description: Defensive walls attributed to King Smbat in the tenth centuries.

properties.title: Gaĭ-Kodzor
properties.description: Village in Krasnodar Krai, Russia, located 9 km. southeast of Anapa. Between 1972 and 1986, several separate coin hoards dated to the late Bosporan Kingdom (4th century CE) were found on a farm at the edge of the village.

properties.title: Kurban Höyük
properties.description: Site in eastern Anatolia inhabited from the Neolithic-Middle Bronze Age. The site was excavated in the early 1980s prior to being inundated by the construction of the Atatürk Dam in 1990.

properties.title: Ponte del Gran Caso
properties.description: A Roman bridge across the Torrente Gran Caso located south of Ascoli Piceno.

properties.title: Wittenham Clumps
properties.description: Wittenham Clumps describes a group of small hills in the Thames Valley where archaeological remains of Iron Age hill forts have been identified.

properties.title: Ea-Damkina temple (Kalhu)
properties.description: When Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud) became the principal administrative center of the Assyrian Empire in the ninth century BC, king Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) built (or rebuilt) numerous temples. One of those was dedicated to the god Ea and the goddess Damkina. Although its location is not known, the Ea-Damkina temple at Kalhu is thought to have been situated within the Ninurta temple complex, in the northwest corner of the citadel.

properties.title: Timur (mountain)
properties.description: Timur is a mountain that is situated between Meliddu and Tabal.

properties.title: Tall Deir ‘Allā
properties.description: Site in Balqa Governorate, Jordan, settled from the Late Bronze Age until the 4th century BCE.

properties.title: Illubru
properties.description: Illubru is a city in the western part of Que (kingdom) or in Hilakku that is mentioned in inscriptions of the Assyrian king Sennacherib (r. 704-681 BC). This site is generally connected with classical Lampron, which is likely to be identified with modern Namrun, ca. 20 km northwest of Tarsus.

properties.title: Porta Romanelli
properties.description: A section of ashlar masonry fortification walls, including a gate, at Tarquinii.

properties.title: Stele of Horemheb at Karnak
properties.description: Horemheb was the last pharaoh of the 18th Dynasty of Egypt. The deeds of his career were recorded on a stele that was mountaed at the foot of the Tenth Pylon of the Karnak temple.

properties.title: Khorsabad Gate 1
properties.description: This decorated gate is the northernmost city gate of the northeast wall of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon"), the capital of the Assyrian Empire constructed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC).

properties.title: Khorsabad Gate 2
properties.description: This undecorated gate is the southernmost city gate of the northeast wall of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon"), the capital of the Assyrian Empire constructed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC).

properties.title: Khorsabad Gate 3
properties.description: This decorated gate is the northernmost city gate of the southeast wall of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon"), the capital of the Assyrian Empire constructed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC).

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Scylletium/Scolacium
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Scylletium/Scolacium.

properties.title: Castra Peregrina
properties.description: Located on the Caelian Hill, the Castra Peregrina housed Roman soldiers.

properties.title: The Athenaeum of Hadrian (Rome)
properties.description: The Athenaeum of Hadrian was located in regio VII near the Capitoline Hill in Rome. Founded by the Emperor Hadrian, it was designated for the promotion of literary and scientific studies and named after the city of Athens. Excavations connected to the Metro C line revealed a complex in the vicinity of the modern Piazza Venezia that has been identified as the site of the Athenaeum.

properties.title: Bara
properties.description: A modern village located on the border of Iraq and Syria. An Assyrian stele (possibly of Adad-nerari III) was found there.

properties.title: Tigris Tunnel Inscriptions
properties.description: The so-called Tigris Tunnel is a cave ca. fifty miles north of Diyarbakır, Turkey and it forms a source of the Tigris River. In its vicinity there are several Assyrian monuments, including five inscriptions.

properties.title: Theater at Telmessos
properties.description: The ancient Theater at Telmessos with 1,500 seats dates to the latter days of the Pergamene empire.

properties.title: Hadrian's Wall
properties.description: Hadrian's Wall or Vallum Aelium was the first of two Roman fortifications built across northern Britannia. The project was begun in A.D. 122 and the works eventually stretched from the River Tyne near the North Sea to the Solway Firth on the Irish Sea. The wall represented the northern limit of the Roman Empire.

properties.title: Antonine Wall
properties.description: A series of fortifications approximately 63 km in length, spanning the breadth of modern day Scotland between the Firth of Forth and the Firth of Clyde. The Antonine Wall was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2008.

properties.title: Banbhore
properties.description: Banbhore is located 65 km east of Karachi. Its sequence of occupation stretches from the first century BC to the thirteenth century AD.

properties.title: Kunulua/Tell Tayinat
properties.description: Tell Tayinat (ancient Kunulua) is a large site (comprising both a sizeable citadel and a sprawling lower town) located at the northern bend of the Orontes River, ca. 30 km southeast of Antakya (ancient Antioch). Strategically located, this fortified city served as a royal capital for various historically-attested Bronze and Iron Age kingdoms (ca. 3200-600 B.C.). In 738 B.C., the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III conquered Kunulua (alternately called Kinalua), then the royal city of Syro-Hittite kingdom of Patina, annexed it, and transformed it into an important provincial administrative center. Textual evidence found at the site (e.g., a large tablet inscribed with a copy of Esarhaddon’s Succession Treaty) leaves little doubt that Kunulua should be identified as Tell Tayinat.

properties.title: Simitthu Roman theater
properties.description: The Roman theater at, an ancient Roman-Berber town in northwestern Tunisia.

properties.title: Tarr Steps
properties.description: Tarr Steps is a prehistoric bridge over the River Barle in England. The current phase dates to the Medieval period, although the original phase of the bridge is dated ca. 1000 BC.

properties.title: Sweet Track
properties.description: Sweet Track is an ancient timber causeway of Britain built at the end of the fourth millennium BC.

properties.title: Oppius Mons
properties.description: The Oppian Hill is the southern spur of Rome's Esquiline Hill.

properties.description: Rectangular defensive tower located on the southern end of the defensive circuit walls around the city of Dura-Europos. Built ca. 150 BCE, the city's fortifications were breached in 256 CE and went out of use thereafter.

properties.title: Tower 5
properties.description: Rectangular defensive tower located on the northern end of the defensive circuit walls around the city of Dura-Europos. Built ca. 150 BCE, the city's fortifications were breached in 256 CE and went out of use thereafter.

properties.title: Theater at Segobriga
properties.description: Construction of the Roman Theater at Segobriga began under Tiberius and was completed during the Flavian period.

properties.title: Costa Murata archaeological area
properties.description: A site with votive activity from the Archaic period and a later Roman house in addition to the basalt-paved Roman road.

properties.title: Ponte Sodo
properties.description: A rock-cut tunnel (cuniculus) at the northwest margin of ancient Veii.

properties.title: Torre Maggiore
properties.description: A place located at the 21st km of the via Ardeatina, Torre Maggiore is likely built on the site of a domusculta and is connected to key Roman families, including the Savelli, Altieri, Capodiferro, Serlupi, and Maddaleni families. The tower has a square plan and rises to 34 meters.

properties.title: Tomb of Marcus Servilius Quartus
properties.description: A Roman tomb on the Via Appia dating ca. A.D. 100.

properties.title: Mausoleum of Helena
properties.description: An ancient tomb located on the ancient Via Labicana (now along the Via Casilina) that was built by Constantine I and used as the tomb for his mother, Helena.

properties.title: Nuraghe Cubalciada
properties.description: A Bronze Age nuraghe re-used and re-fortified during the Second World War.

properties.title: Nuraghe Sa Jua
properties.description: A monopteral nuraghe.

properties.title: Porta Collina
properties.description: A gate in Rome's Servian Wall located on the Quirinal Hill.

properties.title: tribus Galeria
properties.description: The tribus Galeria was one of the older rural tribes of ancient Rome

properties.title: Roman villa at Artena
properties.description: A Roman villa built atop the terraced platform of the so-called "Civita di Artena".

properties.title: Santa Liberata
properties.description: A coastal platform villa conneted with the Domitii Ahenobarbi.

properties.title: Horologium Augusti
properties.description: The Horologium Augusti or Solarium Augusti was an ancient monument of the Campus Martius built during the reign of Augustus. In theory, it functioned as a giant solar marker. An obelisk relocated to Rome from Heliopolis served as the gnomon. The obelisk today stands in the Piazza di Monte Citorio.

properties.title: House of Venus in the shell
properties.description: Located on the Via dell'Abbondanza, the so-called "House of Venus in the shell" is also known as the House of D. Lucretius Satrius Valens.

properties.title: Dalmatia (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire at the death of Trajan (117 CE).

properties.title: Mesopotamia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 P4 Mesopotamia

properties.title: Dacia (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire at the death of Trajan (117 CE).

properties.title: Noricum (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire at the death of Trajan (117 CE).

properties.title: Cilicia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 N4 Cilicia

properties.title: Phrygia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 N4 Phrygia

properties.title: Achaia (province)
properties.description: A Roman province of the early empire, comprising the Peloponnese, central Greece, Euboea, most of the Ionian islands and adjacent areas.

properties.title: Ancient Egypt (region)
properties.description: The ancient kingdom(s) and region of Egypt as understood by the Egyptians themselves, their neighbors, and their successors. Individual administrative districts, provinces, nomes, and the like have separate place resources in Pleiades.

properties.title: Paphlagonia
properties.description: The Roman province as defined in the Barrington Atlas (BAtlas 100 N3 Paphlagonia)

properties.title: Numidia (Roman province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman empire at the death of Trajan (117CE).

properties.title: Dacia Inferior (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire, created under the emperor Hadrian.

properties.title: Moesia Inferior (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire created under the Emperor Domitian from part of the older province of Moesia (q.v.).

properties.title: Galatia et Cappadocia
properties.description: Galatia et Cappadocia, a Roman province that results from the union of Galatia and Cappadocia.

properties.title: Lugdunensis (province)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 F2 Lugdunensis

properties.title: Bithynia et Pontus
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire on the Black Sea coast that was formed when the former kingdoms of Bithynia (annexed by Rome in 74 B.C.) and Pontus (annexed in 63 B.C.) were joined together.

properties.title: Pontus Galaticus
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 P3 Pontus Galaticus

properties.title: Africa Proconsularis (Roman province)
properties.description: The late Republican and early Roman imperial province, initially subdivided into two provinces known as "Africa vetus" and "Africa nova", but merged into one province ca. 35 B.C.

properties.title: Germania Inferior
properties.description: Germania Inferior was a province of the Roman empire located on the west bank of the Rhine river. It was established as a province ca. AD 80.

properties.title: Mauretania Caesariensis (Roman province)
properties.description: A Roman imperial province.

properties.title: Sicilia (Roman province)
properties.description: The Roman province of Sicilia (Sicily) was initially organized in 241 BC as a territory with a proconsular governor. The territory fell to the Vandals in AD 440 but was reclaimed by the Byzantines.

properties.title: Armenia Minor (Roman eparcheia)
properties.description: Territory west of the Euphrates and Armenia (Roman province) included in the province of Cappadocia by Vespasian.

properties.title: Asia
properties.description: The Roman province of Asia, located on the eastern coast of the Aegean Sea. The region was bequeathed to the Roman Republic by Attalus III of Pergamum in 133 BCE. It was divided into seven smaller provinces by Diocletian in the 4th century CE.

properties.title: Mauretania Tingitana (Roman province)
properties.description: The Roman imperial province of Mauretania Tingitana. Located in northwest Africa, the province stretched from the Mulucha river (modern Oued Moulouia in Morocco) westward to the Atlantic.

properties.title: Germania Superior
properties.description: Germania Superior was a province of the Roman empire. Its administrative capital was Mogontiacum (Mainz).

properties.title: Aquitania (Roman province)
properties.description: A Roman province formed in 27 B.C. by Augustus. According to Strabo, it incorporated the territories of the Aquitani and 14 other peoples whose territories were located between the Garumna and Liger rivers.

properties.title: Thracia (province)
properties.description: The Roman province as defined in the Barrington Atlas (BAtlas 100 L3 Thracia)

properties.title: Pisidia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 N4 Pisidia

properties.title: Britannia (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire at the Death of Trajan (117 CE).

properties.title: Lusitania
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 E4 Lusitania

properties.title: Arabia (province)
properties.description: A Roman province founded under Trajan shortly after 22 March 106 CE. It included the territory to the east of the Jordan river and the Sinai peninsula to the Red Sea.

properties.title: Tarraconensis
properties.description: The Roman imperial province of Hispania Tarraconensis.

properties.title: Raetia (province)
properties.description: The Roman province of Raetia, located in the central Alps and coincident with the region known by the same name to the Romans (q.v.).

properties.title: Baetica
properties.description: Baetica was one of three Roman Imperial provinces in the Iberian peninsula.

properties.title: Lycia et Pamphylia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 M4 Lycia et Pamphylia

properties.title: Hellespontus
properties.description: A Late Roman province included on Hierokles' list.

properties.title: Iudaea (province)
properties.description: The Roman province of Iudaea, incorporating the historical regions of Judea, Samaria, and Idumaea, was established in 6 CE, when the former tetrarchy of Herod Archelaus came under direct Roman administration. Following the Bar Kokhba War (132-135), Hadrian changed the province's name to Palaestina, and in the mid- to late 4th century CE the area was divided into three provinces (Palaestina Prima, Secunda, and Tertia or Salutaris).

properties.title: Macedonia (Roman province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman empire at the death of Trajan (117 CE).

properties.title: Belgica (province)
properties.description: The Roman province also called Gallia Belgica.

properties.title: Pontus Polemoniacus
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 P3 Pontus Polemoniacus

properties.title: Syria (Roman imperial province)
properties.description: The Roman imperial province of Syria.

properties.title: Armenia (Roman province)
properties.description: A Roman province formed under Trajan in 114 CE, but given up by Hadrian in 118 CE.

properties.title: Moesia Superior (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire created under the Emperor Domitian from part of the older province of Moesia (q.v.).

properties.title: Dacia Porolissensis (province)
properties.description: Sometime after AD 124, Dacia Superior was sub-divided into two provinces: Dacia Apulensis and Dacia Porolissensis.

properties.title: Pannonia Superior (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire at the death of Trajan (117 CE).

properties.title: Creta et Cyrene (Roman province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire at the death of Trajan (117 CE).

properties.title: Pannonia Inferior (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire at the death of Trajan (117 CE).

properties.title: Dacia Superior (province)
properties.description: A province of the Roman Empire created under the emperor Hadrian.

properties.title: Narbonensis
properties.description: The Roman imperial province of Gallia Narbonensis.

properties.title: Ellibir
properties.description: A fortress in the vicinity of Til-garimmu fortified by the Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721-705 BC) against Kasku.

properties.title: Šindarara
properties.description: A fortress in the vicinity of Til-garimmu fortified by the Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721-705 BC) against Kasku.

properties.title: Dasht-e Nawar
properties.description: Dasht-e Nawar is a settlement site beginning in prehistoric times on the shores of the lake of the same name. Based on epigraphic evidence, the Archaeological Gazetteer of Afghanistan (1982) classifies it as Kushan, second-third century AD.

properties.title: Crystal Palace Pub, Bath
properties.description: Remains of sequence of Romano-British deposits found in the cellar of a pub in modern-day Bath.

properties.title: Via Laurentina
properties.description: An ancient road, leading southwards from Rome toward Laurentum. Its course, endpoint, and coincidence with the Via Ostiensis and the Via Ardeatina are matters of scholarly contention.

properties.title: Creiro
properties.description: A Roman garum manufactory.

properties.title: Tumulus of Noville
properties.description: A Gallo-Roman tumulus near Noville, Belgium.

properties.title: Regio IV, Pompeii
properties.description: The so-called Regio IV is a largely unexcavated archaeological subdivision located in the northeastern section of Pompeii.

properties.title: Roman theater at Carsulae
properties.description: The Roman theater at Carsulae dates to the Augustan period, pre-dating the amphitheater.

properties.title: Theater at Alinda/Alexandria ad Latmum
properties.description: The Roman Theater at Alinda could accommodate about 5,000 spectators.

properties.title: Sasso di Furbara
properties.description: A locality in southern Etruria near the Via Aurelia some 50 km north of Rome that has yielded evidence for human activity across multiple periods. Notable is evidence of Protovillanovan and Villanovan necropoleis as well as ritual activity of the Etruscans.

properties.title: Naveta des Tudons
properties.description: A chamber tomb of the late second to early first millennium B.C. located on the island of Minorca.

properties.title: Tholos de El Romeral
properties.description: A megalithic tomb dating ca. 1800 BC located in Antequera (Andalusia), Spain.

properties.title: Dólmenes de Antequera
properties.description: A Chalcolithic necropolis located in Antequera, province of Málaga, Andalusia, Spain.

properties.title: Sant Esteuan
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the northeast of the province of Jaén that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X (thirteenth century). The site's modern name is Santisteban del Puerto.

properties.title: S. Passera hypogeum
properties.description: A hypogeum connected with the S. Passera complex.

properties.title: Padakku/Fadak
properties.description: Ancient Padakku/Fadak is an oasis town in the Arabian Peninsula that is idenified with the modern city al-Ḥā’iṭ.

properties.title: Arco Romano de Dona Isabel
properties.description: The so-called "Arco Romano de Dona Isabel" is a second or third century A.D. city gate of Évora, the ancient site of Ebora Liberalitas Iulia.

properties.title: Alpes Graiae et Poeninae (Roman province)
properties.description: Alpes Graiae et Poeninae, a small Alpine province of the Roman Empire. There were three such provinces in the western Alps. Alpes Graiae et Poeninae comprised the Val d'Aosta region and the Canton Valais in Switzerland.

properties.title: Isauria
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 N4 no. 5 (Isauria)

properties.title: Phrygia Paroreius
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 N4 no. 4 (Phrygia Paroreius)

properties.title: Alpes Maritimae (province)
properties.description: A Roman province established in the early days of the empire and persisting, with changes, into Late Antiquity.

properties.title: Alpes Cottiae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 100 H3 no. 2 (Alpes Cottiae)

properties.title: Sanctuary of Dionysos
properties.description: The Sanctuary of Dionysos, which includes a theater, choregic monument, statue bases, and at least one temple, formed part of the civic center of the Attic deme of Ikarion.

properties.title: Metroon at Olympia
properties.description: Temple at Olympia constructed in the late 4th or early 3rd century BCE

properties.title: Tabo
properties.description: A Kushite site located on Argo Island in Nubia, the location of a large Amun temple.

properties.title: Saint-Plancard
properties.description: The Chapel of Saint Jean is built atop a temple once dedicated to Iuppiter Optimus Maximus.

properties.title: Broxtowe Roman fort
properties.description: Site of Roman fortification dating from 50-75 CE.

properties.title: St Peters Church, Flawford
properties.description: A ruined Medieval church located on the site of a Roman villa.

properties.title: Temple of Jupiter
properties.description: A temple dedicated to the Capitoline triad is located on the forum of Saepinum.

properties.title: Masath / Massa (river)
properties.description: The Massa River of southern Morocco.

properties.title: Roman baths at Oescus
properties.description: The Roman baths at Oescus are dated to the middle of the third century.

properties.title: Qasr al-Abd at Tyrus
properties.description: A Hellenistic palace constructed in the second century CE at the southern end of the Tyrus/'Iraq al-Amir site.

properties.title: Kharab Sayyar
properties.description: Early Islamic town in northern Syria, inhabited during the 8th-9th centuries CE.

properties.title: So-called Oratory of Phalaris
properties.description: A small, rectangular Greek temple-type building dated to the first century B.C. and located in the upper agora of Agrigento, on the Poggetto di San Nicola. The name "Oratory" comes from its later use as a Christian chapel.

properties.title: Qamişvan/Değirmendüzü
properties.description: Değirmendüzü (formerly Qamişvan/Kamişvan) is a modern village situated ca. 8 km in the east of Pathos (Aznavurtepe / Anzavurtepe) in the Ağrı Province in eastern Turkey. Here a column base with an inscription of the Urartian king Minua, son of Išpuini (9th/8th century BCE) has been found (CTU I A 5-70)

properties.title: Pompey's pillar
properties.description: A Roman triumphal column in Alexandria, Egypt.

properties.title: Chatby Necropolis
properties.description: Understood to be the oldest necropolis in Alexandria that dates back to the Ptolemaic period and is located in the modern Chatby area of Alexandria.

properties.title: Camp du Château
properties.description: A large oppidum active in the Late Bronze and early Iron Ages.

properties.title: Grotto of the Sibyl
properties.description: A cave discovered by Amedeo Maiuri in 1932 and connected in the historical tradition with the Cumaean Sibyl. The site features in the sixth book of Virgil's Aeneid.

properties.title: Filitosa
properties.description: Filitosa is a megalithic site in southern Corsica that was in use from the Neolithic period until Roman times. A number of menhirs have been discovered at the site.

properties.title: Araghju
properties.description: A prehistoric site of the Torrean civilization in Corsica.

properties.title: Al-Khawd
properties.description: Find-spot of a hoard of metal objects dated to the early Iron Age, located on the campus of Sultan Qaboos University in Oman.

properties.title: Nubt
properties.description: Type-site of the predynastic Naqada Culture, containing a settlement, a necropolis, and a step pyramid constructed ca. 3500 BCE.

properties.title: Su Nuraxi di Barumini
properties.description: A nuragic site in Barumini, Sardinia that was named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997

properties.title: Tell Abu al-Kharaz
properties.description: A Bronze and Iron Age archaeological site in Gilead in the eastern valley of the Jordan river

properties.title: Tepe Gawra
properties.description: An ancient Mesopotamian settlement located in the Mosul region of northwest Iraq.

properties.title: Valdonega Roman villa
properties.description: The Roman villa of Valdonega near Verona dates to the first century A.D.

properties.title: Maa
properties.description: A fortified settlement on Cyprus dating to the thirteenth and twelfth centuries B.C.

properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Marāġe
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Hilakku (region)
properties.description: Hilakku is a mountainous region near Tabālu and Que in the Cilician plain. Its exact location is still debated among scholars. Nevertheless, Hilakku has been tentatively identified as being in the area of Bolkar Dağları or in that of Göksu-Tal, in the western part of Cilicia, that is, in the classical Cilicia Tracheia/Cilicia Aspera.

properties.title: Que (kingdom)
properties.description: Country in the Cilician Plain (Cilicia Pedias) that is known from first-millennium-BC Neo-Assyrian, Neo-Babylonian, Hebrew, Aramaic and Hieroglyphic Luwian sources.

properties.title: Gran Carro (Bolsena)
properties.description: A Proto-Villanovan settlement at Lake Bolsena. Discovered in 1959, this protohistoric settlement was situated on an island that is now submerged in the waters of the lake.

properties.title: tribus Clustumina
properties.description: The tribus Clustumina (or Crustumina) was a rural tribe of Rome which was established in 495 B.C.

properties.title: Formello villa and mausoleum
properties.description: A Roman villa in the territory of Blera of which a cistern and a mausoleum remain.

properties.title: Silbury Hill
properties.description: Silbury Hill is a prehistoric artificial chalk mound near Avebury and is part of the Stonehenge, Avebury and Associated Sites UNESCO World Heritage Site. The mound stands to 40 meters (131 ft) in height.

properties.title: Temple of Concordia, Agrigento
properties.description: The Temple of Concord, located in the so-called "Valle dei Templi" of Agrigento, dates ca. 440-430 B.C.

properties.title: Untitled

properties.title: Great Wall of Gorgan
properties.description: A linear fortification system, probably built in the Parthian period and used during the Sasanian period, the so-called "Great Wall of Gorgan" stretches almost 200 km from the east coast of the Caspian Sea to near the town of Pishkamar in modern Iran. If the fortification system had a name in antiquity, it has not survived.

properties.title: Fort at Great Wall of Gorgan
properties.description: One of the integral forts spaced along the wall

properties.title: Nuraghe Su Nuraxi 'e Pauli
properties.description: A nuraghe with a single, truncated tower.

properties.title: Central Building at Kalhu
properties.description: Near the middle of the citadel of Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud), the ninth-century-BC Assyrian king Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) constructed a building with a grand, south-facing entrance. This building, constructed east of the southeast corner of the Northwest Palace, might have been one of the temples built by Ashurnasirpal II when he made Kalhu the administrative capital of the Assyrian Empire. Alternatively, the Central Building might have served as a palace.

properties.title: The Theater of Larissa
properties.description: The theater at Larissa was a large stone theater built around the end of the third century BC and used for dramatic performances and as a political meeting place.

properties.title: François Tomb

properties.title: Judeideh
properties.description: Judeideh (also Jedīdē, Judaide) is a site in the middle Euphrates region in what was part of the ancient kingdom of Suhu. The city was situated on the east bank of the Euphrates, about ten kilometers downstream of Anat (Anatho). Like many towns and cities of the ancient kingdom of Suhu, Judeideh is now underwater; the area was flooded after the construction of the Haditha dam. Its ancient name is not known.

properties.title: Dawali
properties.description: Dawali is a site in the middle Euphrates region and was part of the kingdom of Suhu. The city was situated on the east bank of the Euphrates, a few kilometres downstream of Anat (Anatho). The modern city of the same name (Ad Dawālī) is on the west bank of the river. The city's ancient name is not known.

properties.title: Badnigalbilukurašušu
properties.description: Nineveh’s main (or great) inner wall was called Badnigalbilukurašušu ("Wall Whose Brilliance Overwhelms Enemies"). It was constructed by the Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib after he moved the Assyrian capital to Nineveh. Badnigalbilukurašušu’s superstructure was reportedly raised to a height of 200 courses of brick. The visible remains of the twelve-kilometer-long wall and some of its gates are still visible today.

properties.title: Pyramid of Khendjer
properties.description: The pyramid of the Pharaoh Khendjer (Thirteenth Dynasty) who ruled Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period (ca. 1760 B.C.)

properties.title: Basilica
properties.description: An important civic building in Pompeii and an early example of the building type, built between ca. 120 and 78 B.C. (VIII, 1, 1).

properties.title: Mastabet el-Fara'un
properties.description: The site of the burial of Shepseskaf, the last known pharaoh of the Fourth Dynasty of Ancient Egypt.

properties.title: Forum of Suasa
properties.description: The Forum of Suasa measures 50 x 100 meters and was surrounded by a portico.

properties.title: Ponte Lupo
properties.description: Remains of a portion of the Aqua Marcia aqueduct located near Gallicano nel Lazio.

properties.title: Sanctuaries of Apollo Deiradiotes and Athena Oxyderkes
properties.description: At Argos, Pausanias mentions both the sanctuary of Apollo Deiradiotes (Apollo of the ridge) and the sanctuary of Athena Oxyderkes (Athena the clear-sighted).

properties.title: Staigue stone fort
properties.description: An Iron Age ring fort, dating perhaps to the fourth century AD.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Mactaris
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Mactaris dates to the second century.

properties.title: Hellenistic and Roman quarter archaeological area
properties.description: The Hellenistic and Roman area is orthogonally planned and covers more than 15,000 square meters. It is located near Poggio San Nicola.

properties.title: Villa del Río Roman bridge
properties.description: A Roman bridge along the Via Augusta.

properties.title: Villamargo
properties.description: A Roman villa.

properties.title: Samnite Palaestra
properties.description: The so-called "Samnite Palaestra" (VIII, 7, 29) lies behind the temple of Isis. A dedication in the Oscan language dates to the second half of the second century BC.

properties.title: Cloghanmore
properties.description: A megalithic chamber tomb located in County Donegal, Ireland.

properties.title: Via Latina
properties.description: A Roman road running southeast from Rome toward Campania.

properties.title: Teatro Clunia
properties.description: A Roman theater initially constructed during the reign of Tiberius.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Rudiae
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Rudiae is part of the complement of Roman buildings dating to the imperial period.

properties.title: 'Awām
properties.description: The ruins of the Sabaean temple dedicated to Almaqah and its associated burial ground are located near the town of Mārib, Yemen.

properties.title: Persian and Hellenistic Administrative Building (PHAB), Tel Kedesh
properties.description: The Persian and Hellenistic Administrative Building was constructed at Tel Kedesh by the Persians in the mid-4th century BCE and was in use through the middle Hellenistic Period (around 143 BCE).

properties.title: Incheville
properties.description: A Celtic hilltop settlement (oppidum).

properties.title: Sesklo
properties.description: Sesklo is the site of an early Neolithic settlement in Thessaly.

properties.title: Greek theater of Taormina
properties.description: The Greek theater of Taormina was built originally in the third century B.C.

properties.title: Greek theater of Tyndaris
properties.description: The Greek theater of Tyndaris dates originally to the fourth century B.C.

properties.title: Roman baths of Taormina
properties.description: The Roman baths of Taormina are built atop a public building of the Hellenistic period. The Roman baths originally fronted on the forum and were expanded in the second century.

properties.title: Roman castrum at Pyrgi
properties.description: The Roman castrum at Pyrgi seems to re-use, in a direct fashion, elements of the preceding Etruscan city plan, although covering a smaller area.

properties.title: Adro Vello
properties.description: The remains of a Roman villa and necropolis.

properties.title: Rocca Calascio
properties.description: A tenth-century fortress located in the Province of L'Aquila in Abruzzo, Italy.

properties.title: Badajoz
properties.description: The Castillian city of Badajoz was an Islamic foundation under the Muladi nobleman Ibn Marwan who established the city ca. 875. Badajoz was eventually invaded by (and captured by) Christians under Alfonso VI of Castile. Alfonso X established a bishopric and began work on the Cathedral of San Juan Bautista.

properties.title: Roman theater of Fourvière
properties.description: A Roman theater in Lyon, France, that originally dates ca. 15 B.C.

properties.title: Horncastle
properties.description: Site of lesser Roman walled town in present-day Lincolnshire, with occupation possibly as early as 1st century CE. The city walls, however likely do not predate the 4th century CE. Candidate location for Bannovallum (the other being Caistor).

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Santa Maria Capua Vetere
properties.description: Sometimes referred to as the "Anfiteatro Campano", the Roman amphitheater at Santa Maria Capua Vetere is the second largest in the Roman world. Begun under Augustus, it was further renovated under Hadrian and Antoninus Pius.

properties.title: Franks Roman villa
properties.description: The site of a Roman villa with two parallel ranges of rooms dating from the second half of the first century to the fifth century.

properties.title: Ponte Brabaciera
properties.description: A second century Roman bridge on the Riu Brabaciera.

properties.title: Matzanni
properties.description: A sanctuary that includes a Punic temple built in white limestone, a nuraghe, and a sacred well.

properties.title: Gallo-Roman Theater of Lillebonne
properties.description: The Gallo-Roman Theater of Lillebonne was in use from the first to the third century.

properties.title: E(...)gakuga
properties.description: The shrine/seat of the god Ennugi in the Egipar temple at Ur. The name is damaged and the complete Sumerian ceremonial name of the structure is not known.

properties.title: Necropolis of Pantalica
properties.description: A large, rock-cut necropolis of over 5,000 tombs dating from the thirteenth to the seventh centuries BC.

properties.title: Ulucak
properties.description: An ancient settlement mound located 25 km west of İzmir with occupation ranging from the Early Neolithic to Late Roman and Early Byzantine periods.

properties.title: Harappa
properties.description: A Bronze Age fortified city located on the Ravi River, inhabited from the fourth through the second millennia BCE, Harappa was one of the most important settlements of the Indus Valley Civilization.

properties.title: San Giorgio in Velabro
properties.description: A church dedicated to St. George located in Rome's Velabrum. Legend connects the church's location with the spot where the Roman she wolf found the abandoned twins, Romulus and Remus.

properties.title: Santa Maria in Cosmedin
properties.description: A minor basilica church in Rome, Italy. Tradition holds that the church was founded in the sixth century to serve the Greek community at Rome. The beginnings of the present edifice lie in the eighth century.

properties.title: Orton Longueville
properties.description: The site of Orton Longueville has evidence for multi-period human activity. A large timber building is built in the second century A.D., followed by a Romano-British villa dating from the third to fifth centuries.

properties.title: Huntingdonshire Monument 97
properties.description: An Iron Age and early Roman farmstead located near Orton Longueville, Cambridgeshire. Salvage excavations were conducted in 1974 prior to highway construction that destroyed the site.

properties.title: Aquis Querquennis
properties.description: A first century A.D. Roman encampment along the Via Nova.

properties.title: Bussock Camp
properties.description: At Bussock Camp in Berkshire, England, are the remains of a bivallate Iron Age hillfort covering ca. 4.4 ha.

properties.title: S. Pietro ad centum muros
properties.description: On the hill of Grignano, located on the outskirts of Montebuono, the remains of a Roman villa were first excavated in the nineteenth century in the area of the church of "S. Pietro ad centum muros". Excavation in the 1990s revealed further villa remains beneath the church and in the vicinity of its cemetery. Epigraphic evidence attesting to the consulship of M. Vipsanius Agrippa was discovered immured in the church (CIL 9.4677 and 9.4779).

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 95 B4 unnamed mine (N Jabal Kenzan SAU)

properties.title: Wari-Bateshwar
properties.description: An ancient settlement site located in what is now Bangladesh.

properties.title: Stoke Hill
properties.description: The site of a possible Roman signal station.

properties.title: Cividade de Bagunte
properties.description: The Cividade de Bagunte is a fortified Iron Age site that became Romanized. It is located in the municipality of Vila do Conde in the Porto district of Portugal.

properties.title: Whitemoss Roman auxiliary fort
properties.description: A Roman auxiliary fort built ca. A.D. 140 that protected the western flank of the Antonine Wall.

properties.title: Via Annia
properties.description: The Via Annia was a Roman consular road in Cisalpine Gaul that connected (H)Atria to Aquileia. The praetor Titus Annius Rufus constructed the road in 131 BC.

properties.title: Ancient theater of Kourion
properties.description: The Ancient theater of Kourion was first built in the second century B.C. It remained in use until the fourth century.

properties.title: House of the Rhodian Peristyle at Italica
properties.description: Roman house at Italica, also known as the House of the Rhodian Patio. Constructed on a slope, the house has a multileveled patio, with sections of different heights connected by stairs.

properties.description: An ancient city of Arabia, located west of the Persian Gulf.

properties.description: A portion of the Persian Gulf mentioned by Pliny who places it between the Sinus Capeus on the north and the Regio Attene to the south.

properties.title: Qalat al-Bahrain
properties.description: An ancient settlement with evidence from occupation stretching from 2300 BC to the sixteenth century AD that was at one time the capital of the Dilmun civilization. Qal’at al-Bahrain was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.

properties.title: Capeus? Sinus
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 95 C3 Capeus? Sinus

properties.title: Haltwhistle Burn Roman Fortlet and Camp
properties.description: Site of Roman fortlet and temporary camp. The fortlet guarded the crossing of the Burn by the Stanegate. It pre-dates the construction of Hadrian's Wall, which passes 0.5 km to the north.

properties.title: Hiera Oikia at Eleusis
properties.description: The so-called "Hiera Oikia" is a multi-room structure dating to the 7th century BC in the sanctuary of Demeter of Kore at Eleusis.

properties.title: Sanctuary of Kodros, Neleus and Basile at Athens
properties.description: A sanctuary located between the Phaleron gate and the Itonian gate of Athens.

properties.title: Franchthi Cave
properties.description: The Franchthi Cave is located on the Argolic Gulf in southeastern Argolis. The cave was occupied from the Paleolithic (ca. 20,000 BC) through to the Mesolithic and Neolithic periods, ultimately being abandoned ca. 3000 BC. The cave shows continuous human occupation for more than 20,000 years.

properties.title: Erk Kala
properties.description: Erk Kala, founded in the sixth century B.C., was at the center of Merv.

properties.title: Beit She’arim
properties.description: Beit She'arim National Park is the site of a large number of ancient rock-cut Jewish tombs, dating to the second century AD. The necropolis was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2015.

properties.title: Kavuncu
properties.description: Kavuncu is a modern settlement situated near Van in the southeast of Turkey. Here a cylindrical stone (probably a column base) with an inscription of the Urartian king Minua, son of Išpuini (9/8th century BCE) was found (CTU I A 5-53 B).

properties.title: Zvartnots Cathedral
properties.description: A seventh century AD church built by Catholicos Nerses the Builder (AD 641-653) and located in the Armavir Province of Armenia. The ruins of the church were listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 94 C5 unnamed wall (Ardashir-Khurra)

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Porolissum
properties.description: An amphitheater that originated under Hadrian and that was then rebuilt in stone ca. A.D. 157.

properties.title: Kapilikaya Rock Tomb
properties.description: A rock-cut tomb dated to the second century BCE.

properties.title: Monastery of San Juan de Caaveiro
properties.description: A Christian monastery established in AD 934.

properties.title: Serpent Column
properties.description: An ancient bronze column that was displayed in the Hippodrome of Constantinople, the Serpent Column was part of a monument originally installed at Delphi and relocated to Constantinople by Constantine I in A.D. 324. The monument was originally built to celebrate the Greek defeat of the Persian Empire at the Battle of Plataea in 479 B.C.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 94 C3 unnamed quarry (near Bard-i Burideh)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 94 C3 unnamed reservoir (N Masumabad West)

properties.title: Trajanic harbor
properties.description: The hexagonal Trajanic harbor basin at Portus was built between 100 and 112. Its maximum diameter is approximately 716 meters.

properties.title: Amaghu Noravank
properties.description: Armenian monastery constructed in the 13th-14th centuries CE, located 3km east of the modern village of Amaghu.

properties.title: Via Claudia Nova
properties.description: A Roman road built in AD 47 in order to connect the Via Caecilia with the Via Claudia Valeria.

properties.title: archaeological area of Monte Bibele
properties.description: An important later Etruscan and Celtic settlement in the Po Plain with signs of occupation in the Late Bronze Age and then again between the fifth and second centuries BC.

properties.title: Roman theater at Cales
properties.description: The Roman theater at Cales dates to the first century B.C.

properties.title: Kecharis
properties.description: Armenian monastery dated to the 11th-13th centuries CE.

properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 94 D3 unnamed dam (Pulvar Dam, northernmost of three dams N Pasargadae)

properties.title: Via Gemina
properties.description: The Via Gemina was a Roman road linking Aquileia and Emona.

properties.title: Pinnata Castra
properties.description: The Roman legionary fortress at modern day Inchtuthil.

properties.title: Graupius (mountain)
properties.description: Site of Roman military victory over the native Caledonians in AD 83 or 84, chronicled in Tacitus' Agricola. Its location has never been conclusively identified, notwithstanding centuries of scholarly debate. Dozens of candidate sites have been proposed (and dismissed) over the years, however, the general consensus seems to agree upon a location somewhere in northeast Scotland extending north from Perthshire well into Aberdeenshire.

properties.title: Zabala
properties.description: This Sumerian/Babylonian city (also known as Zabalam, now as modern Tell Ibzeikh) was a cult centre of the goddess Inanna/Ishtar. It was located near the Iturungal and Ninagina canals.

properties.title: Thermae Agrippae
properties.description: The Thermae Agrippae, built by M. Vipsanius Agrippa in the Campus Martius, were the earliest of Rome's great public baths.

properties.title: Jebel Akhdar (Oman)
properties.description: Coordinates after GeoHack.

properties.title: Jebel Shams
properties.description: Jebel Shams (Arabic: جبل شمس‎, (mountain of sun) rises to 2,818 m (9,245 ft) asl and is the highest summit of the Al Hajar Mountains in Oman.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: Persepolis → WNW

properties.title: Wickham Bushes Romano-British settlement
properties.description: The Romano-British settlement at Wickham Bushes is located due south from Caesar's Camp. A range of archaeological material was recovered, including numismatic evidence that ranges in date from Agrippa to Valentinian II.

properties.title: Bronze Age Barrow at Old Winchester Hill
properties.description: A number of Bronze Age barrow tombs are found within the general area of the Iron Age hill fort.

properties.title: Oldbury Camp
properties.description: An Iron Age hillfort located in Kent that dates to the first century A.D. and shows signs for at least partial reorganization following the Roman invasion of Britain.

properties.title: Castello di Sant'Alessio
properties.description: A tenth-century castle located near the di Sant'Alessio in Sicily.

properties.title: Villa delle Terme degli Stucchi Dipinti
properties.description: An imperial villa, perhaps abandoned in the late first century A.D., located near Tor Vergata.

properties.title: Le Caldane
properties.description: Ancient thermal baths in use from the Etrusco-Roman period onward.

properties.title: Castro Chao Sanmartín
properties.description: A fortified settlement occupied from the Bronze Age (second millennium BC) to the second century AD.

properties.title: Untitled

properties.title: Chiesa di Sant'Ilario a Port' Aurea
properties.description: A sixth-, seventh-, and eighth-century Christian church located near the Port' Aurea of Benevento built during the Longobard period. The church was built atop Imperial remains and was an apsidal hall.

properties.title: Balāwāt
properties.description: Balāwāt is the site of the ancient Assyrian city of Imgur-Enlil. A place from the TAVO Index.

properties.title: Poggio all'Aglione
properties.description: A cistern likely connected with a Roman villa.

properties.title: Arco Etrusco
properties.description: The so-called "Arco Etrusco" is one of the gates of ancient Perusia. The gate dates originally from the third century B.C. when it was one of seven gates in the Etruscan wall. In 40 B.C. it was refashioned under Augustus.

properties.title: Arco di Sant'Ercolano
properties.description: The Arco di Sant'Ercolano of Perugia is the ancient Porta Cornea of the Hellenistic walls of the city.

properties.title: Porta Marzia
properties.description: The so-called Porta Marzia at Perugia began as a third century B.C. gate of the Etruscan city and was engulfed in the fortifications of the Rocca Paolina in 1540.

properties.title: Mithraeum at Casa del Mitreo in Emerita Augusta
properties.description: The well-preserved remains of a second century Mithraeum at Emerita Augusta (mod. Merida, Spain).

properties.title: Ponte delle Chianche, Buonalbergo
properties.description: A Roman bridge of the second century A.D. along the Via Traiana that crosses the torrente Buonalbergo.

properties.title: Tell Habuba Kabira
properties.description: The northernmost of two associated settlements located on the western bank of the Euphrates, showing signs of habitation from the Late Uruk period through the Middle Bronze Age. Rescue excavations were conducted at the site before it was inundated by the Tabqa Dam Reservoir in the early 1970s.

properties.title: Red Basilica
properties.description: A Roman temple built above the Selinus river which was originally constructed for the worship of Egyptian gods, most likely Isis and/or Serapis. In the Byzantine era it was converted into a church of St. John. It was subsequently ruined, although the rotunda on the north side is still an active mosque.

properties.title: Pentrich
properties.description: A Roman fortlet with a small rectangular earthwork lying within a larger enclosure.

properties.title: Ekarzagina
properties.description: The temple of the god Ea within the Esagil(a) complex at Babylon. The Sumerian ceremonial name Ekarzagina means "Pure Quay"or "Quay of Lapis Lazuli."

properties.title: Basilica di Santo Stefano in via Latina
properties.description: The now-ruined basilica of Santo Stefano in Via Latina was a fifth-century CE early Christian basilica. It is now located within the confines of the archaeological park of the Via Latina tombs.

properties.description: Necropolis in Pontecagnano containing fifty burials from the Orientalizing Period (725-550 BCE) and an additional six burials from the Lucanian period (4th-3rd centuries BCE).

properties.title: Eigikalamma
properties.description: The temple of the god Lugal-Marda at Marad. The Sumerian ceremonial name Eigikalamma means "House, Eye of the Land."

properties.title: Circus Varianus
properties.description: A circus that was part of the Sessorium palace next to the Amphitheatrum Castrense. The obelisk currently situated on the Pincian Hill was discovered on the site in the sixteenth century. It had been moved to the spina of the circus during the reign of Elagabalus.

properties.title: Tomb of the Winged Demons
properties.description: The so-called Tomb of the Winged Demons (Sovana, Italy), a third-century BC Etruscan tomb located in the Poggio Felceto necropolis.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Luna
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Luna was built in the second century, perhaps during the Antonine period.

properties.title: Matiātu
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources that is identified with modern Midyat. Midyat originated as a Hurrian settlement in the third millennium B.C.

properties.title: Manṣuāte
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources; the name of the place in Egyptian sources is Mnḏt. Manṣuāte is probably to be identified with modern Maṣyāf (Maṣyāt).

properties.title: Pauli Stincus
properties.description: A Punic farm site occupied from the fourth to the second century B.C.

properties.title: Babil
properties.description: The small village of Babil (now Kebili) is located about 25 km southwest of Cizre, near the Tigris river, directly on the Turkish-Syrian border. The name of the ancient site whose ruins lay beneath the modern village is not known.

properties.title: Yoncalı
properties.description: Yoncalı is located near the modern cities of Malazgirt and Bulanık, at the western end of the Bulanık-Malazgirt plain. The Assyrian king Tiglat-pileser I had a placed an inscribed, rock-cut relief here to commemorate his victories in the region.

properties.title: Nuraghe Sa Mandra 'e Sa Giua
properties.description: A nuraghe and associated village.

properties.title: Hadda
properties.description: Haḍḍa, a Greco-Buddhist archeological site, is located in the ancient region of Gandhara, near the Khyber Pass, some ten kilometers south of the city of Jalalabad. This major archaeological site from which archaeologists recovered over 23,000 Greco-Buddhist sculptures in the twentieth century is thought to have been destroyed by ongoing military conflict in Afghanistan.

properties.title: Enlil Gate
properties.description: The Enlil Gate is one of Babylon's eight city gates and it is situated on the northwestern side of the inner city, directly north of the Bāb-Lugalerra quarter. King Nebuchadnezzar II built the gate ca. 575 B.C.

properties.title: The Great Pyramid
properties.description: The Great Pyramid of Khufu was built ca. 2580–2560 B.C. during the 4th dynasty of ancient Egypt. It initially stood to a height of 146.5 meters (481 feet).

properties.title: Murgaual (castle)
properties.description: A Spanish castle and village located in the north of the province of Córdoba that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. Today it's known as Castillo de Murgabal or Castillo de Almogábar. It is part of the village of Torrecampo and the region of Fuencaliente.

properties.title: Sîn temple (Khorsabad)
properties.description: As part of the palatial complex of Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad), the eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) constructed six temples, including one to the god Sîn.

properties.title: Tomb of the Dolphin
properties.description: An early Hellenistic painted tomb at Vulci.

properties.title: Tomb of Cuccumella
properties.description: An archaic tumulus-type tomb at Vulci.

properties.title: Monte Amiata
properties.description: Monte Amiata is a lava dome located about 20 km northwest of Lake Bolsena in Italy.

properties.title: Gran Sasso d'Italia
properties.description: The Gran Sasso d'Italia is a mountain located in the Abruzzo region of central Italy.

properties.title: Ekalte
properties.description: Ekalte, modern Tall Munbāqa, is a medium-sized Bronze Age settlement on the left bank of the Euphrates in northern Syria, ca. 85 kilometres east of Aleppo. Inhabited as early as 2,000 BCE, Ekalte grew to become a significant urban centre in the Late Bronze Age (ca. 1600-1200 BCE). Excavations by the German Oriental Institute since 1969 have unearthed extensive tracts of the urban landscape. Today, the site is partially submerged beneath the waters of the Lake Assad.

properties.title: Bridgeness Distance Slab
properties.description: Findspot of the Bridgeness distance slab, near the eastern terminus of the Antonine Wall

properties.title: Untitled

properties.title: Roman theater at Gosbecks
properties.description: A Roman-British theater was excavated some 125 yards due south of the Gosbecks sanctuary.

properties.title: tribus Oufentina
properties.description: The tribus Oufentina was a later rural tribe of Rome, established in 318 B.C.

properties.title: Mithraeum at Segontium
properties.description: A mithraeum was excavated at Segontium (modern Caernarfon) in 1959, ca. 137m from the east corner of the Roman auxiliary fort. The site was abandoned in the late fourth century A.D.

properties.title: Lago di Monterosi
properties.description: A volcanic crater lake located near Viterbo, Italy. The study of lacustrine sediments has revealed palynological evidence that has helped to reconstruct the ancient environment and vegetation of peninsular Italy.

properties.title: Villa San Giovanni in Tuscia
properties.description: A Roman villa of the third and fourth centuries A.D.

properties.title: Roman theater at Ferentinum
properties.description: The Roman theater at Ferentinum is today poorly preserved.

properties.title: Tappino (river)
properties.description: The Tappino river is located in the modern Molise region of Italy.

properties.title: Başkale
properties.description: Başkale (Turkish "Main Castle") is a town and district located in Van Province in south-eastern Turkey. According to an inscription in the Urartean language of the Urartean king Minua (9th/8th century BCE) on a stone block (A 5-52) the fortress located here was built by Minua and was given the name "City of the God Haldi".

properties.title: Septizonium
properties.description: The Septizonium (or Septizodium) is a monument located at the extreme at the extreme southeastern corner of the Palatine hill built by the Severan emperors. It is attested textually in the Historia Augusta, its footprint appears on the Severan marble plan (Forma Urbis Romae), and its foundations have been explored via excvavation.

properties.title: Tel Hazor
properties.description: Tel Hazor (Hebrew: תל חצור‎‎) is an archaeological site located in the southern Hula Valley overlooking Lake Merom. From the Middle Bronze Age to the Israelite period in the ninth century B.C., Hazor was the largest fortified city in the region. It served as a commercial center with links to Babylon and Syria. In the Book of Joshua, Hazor is described as “the head of all those kingdoms” (Josh. 11:10).

properties.title: Cypro-Phoenician port hangars of Kition
properties.description: Covered sheds (neoria) in the ancient harbor of Kition used in the construction and repair of warships by the Phoenician rulers of the city during the fifth century BCE.

properties.title: Domus of the Lararium
properties.description: The so-called "Domus of the Lararium" in Assisi was discovered at a depth of 7 meters beneath the Palazzo Giampè. The surviving remains are those of a well-appointed domus with floor mosaics and wall paintings. The domus, dating to the second half of the first century. B.C. and the first decades of the first century. A.D., was comprised of at least 13 rooms and a peristyle.

properties.title: Sheikh Abd el-Qurna
properties.description: A necropolis located on the West Bank at Thebes in Upper Egypt that is now part of the archaeological area of Deir el-Bahari.

properties.title: Via Valeria
properties.description: An ancient road from Rome to Corfinium.

properties.title: Canaria? (island)
properties.description: Canaria? (Gran Canaria) is an island of the Canary Islands archipelago.

properties.title: Arkadiko Bridge
properties.description: An arched Bronze Age bridge near the Mycenaean center of Tiryns. The bridge is located along an ancient highway connecting Tiryns to Epidauros.

properties.title: Sanctae Mariae in Palmis
properties.description: A Medieval Christian sanctuary along the Via Appia, perhaps best known as the Church of Domine Quo Vadis.

properties.title: Casale di Giovio
properties.description: The Casale di Giovio was originally a Roman funereal monument that was re-worked in seventeenth century to assume its current form.

properties.title: Dharmaraja Cave
properties.description: Modern name of a seventh-century Pallava cave temple in Mahābalipuram.

properties.title: Eurmeiminanki
properties.description: The ziggurat of the god the god Nabû at Borsippa. The Sumerian ceremonial name Eurmeiminanki means "House which Gathers the Seven (Me's) of Heaven and Underworld."

properties.title: tribus Voltinia
properties.description: The tribus Voltinia (or Votinia) was an older rural tribe of ancient Rome.

properties.title: Demircihöyük
properties.description: An ancient Settlement located in Eskişehir Province, Turkey.

properties.title: Casacce necropolis
properties.description: A rock-cut necropolis at Blera with tombs of the Hellenistic period.

properties.title: Temple of the Winged Lions
properties.description: The Temple of the Winged Lions is a colonnaded temple built in Petra in order to honor the Arabian goddess al-Uzza.

properties.title: Great Temple of Petra
properties.description: The Great Temple of Petra is one of the major archaeological and architectural components of central Petra. It is located to the south of the Colonnaded Street and southeast of the Temenos Gate and covers 7560 square meters.

properties.title: Pen-y-Gaer Roman fort
properties.description: A Roman auxiliary fort in Powys, situated midway along the Roman road linking the forts at Brecon Gaer (Cicutio) and Abergavenny (Gobannio).

properties.title: Pizzone necropolis
properties.description: A Roman necropolis located at Nocera Superiore which was buried by the volcanic ejecta of the Vesuvian eruption of A.D. 79.

properties.title: Mokarta
properties.description: A Bronze Age settlement located near Salemi, Sicily. The site has multiple settlement phases, including the Medival ruins referred to as the Castello di Mokarta. A combination of excavation and geophysical prospection has revealed the remains of Bronze Age settlement atop the plateau as well as evidence for outlying necropoleis.

properties.title: Ab Asturica Burdigalam
properties.description: A Roman road connecting Asturica Augusta (modern Astorga) and Burdigala (modern Bordeaux).

properties.description: The site is located in modern Lausanne-Vidy

properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Verona dates to ca. A.D. 30.

properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources; it is generally identified with Aušur ar-Rafi'a (Tell Aušerīya).
