properties.title: South Etruria Survey area
properties.description: The original and pioneering South Etruria Survey was led by J.B. Ward-Perkins of the British School at Rome from the 1950s to the 1970s. The initial focus was the territory of the city of Veii (Ager Veientanus). A revisiting of this survey area and the project's outcomes was part of the Tiber Valley Project led by Helen Patterson and initiated in 1997.

properties.title: Nuraghe S'Urachi
properties.description: A nuragic site near San Vero Milis in west central Sardinia, occupied from the Late Bronze Age into the Roman period.

properties.title: Kirkbride
properties.description: A Roman fort at Bowness on Solway on the Stanegate.

properties.title: Apadana Palace
properties.description: A monumental hypostyle building at Persepolis dating to the sixth century B.C.

properties.title: Roman Agora of Athens
properties.description: The Roman agora at Athens is located to the north of the Acropolis and to the east of the ancient Agora.

properties.title: Hippodrome of Constantinople
properties.description: The Hippodrome was the great racetrack of the city of Constantinople and was connected to the no longer extant imperial palace. At about 450 m in length, the Hippodrome once accommodated about 100,000 spectators.

properties.title: Castell Henllys
properties.description: Castell Henllys is an Iron Age hill fort located in north Pembrokeshire, Wales.

properties.title: Cala Minnola, Levanzo, Province de Trapani
properties.description: A productive site connected with fish processing the production of fish sauce.

properties.title: Bab adh-Dhra'
properties.description: An early Bronze Age settlement near the Dead Sea inhabited from approximately 3150-2150 BCE.

properties.title: St. Catherine's Hill
properties.description: St. Catherine's Hill, Hampshire, England, is the site of an Iron Age hill-fort.

properties.title: Nuraghe Santa Giusta
properties.description: A nuragic site located near Tortoli, Sardinia.

properties.title: Thorikos Residential and Production District
properties.description: The residential and production district of Thorikos features the remains of a number of classical period houses and a silver refinement center.

properties.title: Villa del Pastore
properties.description: A large villa at Stabiae covering more than 17,000 square meters.

properties.title: Necropolis of Campovalano
properties.description: A Picene necropolis located near Campovalano (Campli) in the province of Teramo. While more than 600 tombs were identified, there may have been as many as 20,000 originally.

properties.title: Casa del pomarius Felix
properties.description: This house (I.8.2) opens onto the Via dell'Abbondanza and is connected to the taberna at I.8.1 and the shop at I.8.3. It was named the "Casa del pomarius Felix" from electoral programmata painted on its facade. It has a typical atrium-peristyle plan.

properties.title: Horti Largiani
properties.description: Gardens that were located in regio VII, but whose precise location is uncertain. They could have been in the Campus Martius or on the slopes of the Pincian Hill.

properties.title: Vicus sandalarius
properties.description: A street in regio IV, the Vicus Sandalarius ("street of the sandal-makers"), likely was located north-east of the Templum Pacis. The magistri of the Vicus sandalarius dedicated an altar to Augustus in 2 B.C. Augustus also dedicated a statue to Apollo in the same street. In later times many of the city's bookshops were located there.

properties.title: San Teodoro al Palatino
properties.description: A church on the Palatine Hill in Rome sacred to Saint Theodore of Amasea dating originally to the sixth century AD.

properties.title: Synagogue phase 1
properties.description: Synagogue adapted from a private house building in Dura-Europos.

properties.title: Synagogue phase 2
properties.description: Renovation of the synagogue at Dura-Europos c. 244 CE. The date for the renovation and expansion of the Synagogue (phase 2) is based on Aramaic inscriptions painted on decorative ceiling tiles from the building's assembly hall.

properties.title: Block L7
properties.description: City block of Dura-Europos labeled according to modern excavators' scheme. The city's grid plan was established c. 150BCE and the site went out of use in 256 CE.

properties.title: Building (house?) preceding Synagogue phase 1
properties.description: Traces of preceding building of uncertain type (house?) detected below the synagogue levels in Block L7.

properties.title: House L7-H
properties.description: Private house at Dura-Europos later adapted for use as synagogue phase 1.

properties.title: Medina of Essaouira
properties.description: The Medina of Essaouira, formerly Mogador, is a late eighteenth century fortified town with ancient Phoenician origins. It is located on the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

properties.title: Citadel Wall of Nineveh
properties.description: The citadel of Nineveh was surrounded by a thick mud-brick wall. When the 7th-century B.C. king Sennacherib made Nineveh the capital of the Assyrian empire, that wall was rebuilt and strengthened; its base was reinforced with limestone blocks along its southern stretch.

properties.title: Parys Mountain
properties.description: Parys Mountain is the site of ancient copper mining, with activity in the Bronze Age as well as in the Roman period.

properties.title: Zawiyah
properties.description: Zāwiyah (also Zawiyeh) is a site in the middle Euphrates region in what was part of the ancient kingdom of Suhu. The city was situated on the north bank of the Euphrates, a few kilometers west of Sur Jureh and Gleieh. Like many towns and cities of the ancient kingdom of Suhu, Zāwiyah is now underwater; the area was flooded after the construction of the Haditha dam. The city's ancient name is not known.

properties.title: Klaudianon
properties.description: A Roman and Late-antique fort and quarry at Mons Claudianus (modern Jabal Faţīrah) and in the associated Deir Wadi Umm Hussein in Egypt's eastern desert. It is often referred to in scholarly literature and the press simply as "Mons Claudianus" because of its location. Excavations at the site are notable in part for the recovery of a large textual archive that details the operations and daily life of soldiers and workers at the site.

properties.title: Tomb of Cossinia
properties.description: A Roman tomb on the right bank of the Anio discovered in 1929. The tomb dates to the first century A.D. and is associated with Cossinia, a priestess of the cult of Vesta.

properties.title: Villa of Manlius Vopiscus
properties.description: A villa site near Tivoli that has long been associated Manlius Vopiscus, who is mentioned by Statius. Excavations began in 1825. In 1835 Pope Gregory XVI began construction of his eponymous Villa Gregoriana on the grounds of the Roman villa.

properties.title: Brislington Roman villa
properties.description: Site of a late third or fourth century winged corridor-type villa first excavated in 1899.

properties.title: Green Ore
properties.description: Site of a Roman lead-working settlement at Rookery Farm, and findspot of a group of four lead ingots excavated in the 1950s.

properties.title: Roman arch (Medinaceli)
properties.description: A triple-bay Roman Imperial arch near Medinaceli, Spain, that was originally dedicated to the emperor Domitian and later re-dedicated to Trajan.

properties.title: Castle Hill
properties.description: Castle Hill is located about 350 m south-east of Round Hill and was the site of an Iron Age hill fort.

properties.title: Cave of Saint Peter
properties.description: A cave in the outskirts of Antioch that was converted into a church.

properties.title: Segouiola
properties.description: Segouiola was an old Spanish village located in the west of the province of Sevilla during the kingdom of Alfonso X. Previously, the Arab population called it Boriauenzohar. Afterwards, this place assumed other names, including Torre del Guadiamar. Since the nineteenth century, Torre del Guadiamar county has been part of Benacazón.

properties.title: Ekagula
properties.description: The dais of the Anunnakū gods, Ekagula (“House, Big Gate”), was located in the TE.E (read as either Tê or Kisīri) district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of two daises in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Col di Marzo, Perugia
properties.description: Survey and excavation at Montelabate overlooking the upper Tiber valley in the territory of Perugia have revealed evidence for an Etruscan settlement on the hill of Col di Marzo (Perugia). This place is located some 10 km from Arna and rises to 645 meters above sea level.

properties.title: Citania de Santa Luzia
properties.description: A fortified protourban site located near the modern city of Viana do Castelo in northern Portugal.

properties.title: Leonforte
properties.description: A modern Sicilian town in the province of Enna, thought to be located in the area of the ancient settlement of Assorus.

properties.title: Minor Acropolis, Norba
properties.description: The so-called Minor Acropolis is located on the hill to the south of the Porta Maggiore. This area is surrounded by the urban enclosure wall and is terraced in polygonal masonry. Two platform temples of unknown assignation are to be found here.

properties.title: Roman baths of Coriovallum
properties.description: The site of Coriovallum is known for its well-preserved bath complex. These baths were first built ca. A.D. 40 and then re-built during the reign of Hadrian. They remained in use until the fourth century.

properties.title: "Western Theater" at Laodicea ad Lycum
properties.description: Digitized by eye in Google Earth on 13 July 2012 at an eye altitude of 683m. Dates are general settlement dates, following Foss and Mitchell in BAtlas.

properties.title: Emašmaš
properties.description: The most important temple in the citadel of Nineveh was dedicated to the city's tutelary deity, the goddess Ištar. The temple was located in the center of the citadel and went by the Sumerian ceremonial name Emašmaš (meaning uncertain).

properties.title: Tell Wilaya
properties.description: Tell Wilaya is a small site that was occupied from the Jemdet Nasr Period to the Old Babylonian Period. Its ancient name is not known, but it may have been Keš.

properties.title: The Gordian Palace
properties.description: A large Roman Peristyle House with interior gardens, pools, and baths.

properties.title: Anmurru
properties.description: A fortress in the vicinity of Til-garimmu fortified by the Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721-705 BC) against Urarṭu.

properties.title: Torraccio a Poggio Moiano
properties.description: A Roman mausoleum of the second century A.D.

properties.title: Castra Bonnensia
properties.description: The Roman legionary base at Bonna.

properties.title: Bukhara
properties.description: Bukhara began as part of the Persian empire in the sixth century B.C. The site is especially important as an example of an Islamic city of central Asia. The city center was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

properties.title: Theater at Philippi
properties.description: The initial phase of the Theater at Philippi dates to just after 356 B.C. when Philip II conquered the city.

properties.title: Bolʹshoĭ Salbykskiĭ kurgan
properties.description: The Great Salbyk Mound is the largest burial mound in the Khakassia region of Russia. The mastaba-like tomb, associated with the Bronze Age Tagar culture, was constructed in the 7th century BCE, and may have had an astronomical function.

properties.title: Martu
properties.description: An unlocated well in the middle Euphrates region, near the city Ḫindānu.

properties.title: Unnamed Roman bridgehead
properties.description: Ancient bridgehead west of Milecastle 27 (Hadrian's Wall), providing link to Cilurnum.

properties.title: Vejano
properties.description: Vejano, located in the Province of Viterbo, is located on the Mignone river approximately 60 km northwest of Rome. While the most visible monument on the site today is the fifteenth century castle known as "La Rocca", the site has a long settlement history reaching back to the Bronze Age.

properties.title: Bolʹshoĭ Petropavlovskiĭ burial ground
properties.description: Burial complex along a stretch of over 3 km of the northern bank of the Siniukha River, a stream in the Laba River valley (Krasnodar region). The necropolis contains over 200 individual burials dated to the Middle Bronze-Early Iron Ages (3rd millennium BCE-3rd century CE).

properties.title: Adad Gate
properties.description: The northern city wall of Nineveh had three gates: the Adad Gate was the easternmost of the three. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Adad-šārik-hegalli-ana-māti, which means "The God Adad Is the Provider of Prosperity to the Land."

properties.title: Šibaniba Gate
properties.description: Most 7th-century B.C. Assyrian inscriptions record that Nineveh had eight south- and east-facing gates: the Šibaniba Gate was the seventh of these. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Dumuq-ašnan-u-lahar-qerebša-kayyān, which means "The Choicest of Grain and Flocks Are Constantly Inside It."

properties.title: Halahhu Gate
properties.description: Most 7th-century B.C. Assyrian inscriptions record that Nineveh had eight south- and east-facing gates: the Halahhu Gate was the eighth and last of these. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Bābilat-ḫiṣib-huršānī, which means "The Bearer of the Produce of the Mountains."

properties.title: Arene Candide
properties.description: A cave in Liguria with Palaeolithic, Neolithic and temporary Late Roman occupation

properties.title: Cisterns of La Maalga
properties.description: A group of 15 large cisterns constructed during the late Punic era as a water supply for the city of Carthage.

properties.title: Roman theater of Scythopolis
properties.description: The Roman theater of Scythopolis.

properties.title: Ward Law
properties.description: Ward Law, site of a temporary marching camp and hillfort on the river Nith, was identified via cropmarks.

properties.title: Roman theater at Tusculum
properties.description: The Roman theater at Tusculum was first excavated in 1839.

properties.title: Khabiṣ
properties.description: Neolithic site located about 5 km east of the town of Shadad on the edge of the Dasht-i Lut (Lut desert) in southeastern Iran.

properties.title: Via cava del Cavone, Sovana
properties.description: A hollowed roadway created by cutting the natural tufaceous bedrock. These roads link necropoleis and settlements in the area between Sovana, Sorano, and Pitigliano.

properties.title: Shio-Mgvime monastery
properties.description: Monastery near the town of Mtskheta in Georgia. According to tradition, the monastery was founded in the 6th century CE by St. Shio the Anchorite. It was one of Georgia's largest monastic communities in the early Middle Ages, and it remained in active use throughout the Medieval and Early Modern periods.

properties.title: Ponte Nepesino
properties.description: A bridge along the Via Amerina, just south of ancient Nepet (modern Nepi in Italy)

properties.title: Anavlochos
properties.description: An archaeological site in Crete, Anavlochos (Vrachasi, Lasithi), provides evidence of a settlement straddling the end of the Bronze Age and the Early Iron Age, carrying on to the Archaic period (ca 1200-650 BCE).

properties.title: Baths of Pozzo Pantaleo
properties.description: A public bath (thermae) of the Roman Imperial period.

properties.title: Pozzo Pantaleo
properties.description: The 'Pozzo Pantaleo' is a Roman mausoleum that made use of a cistern of the early Imperial period. In a third phase the site was repurposed as a shrine dedicated to the Christian Saint Pantaleon.

properties.title: Temple F at Selinus
properties.description: Temple F at Selinus is a Doric temple located on the site's so-called "East Hill". Dedicated either to Athena or Dionysus, the temple dates to the middle of the sixth century B.C. The non-canonical ground plan of 6 x 14 columns gives the temple an elongated aspect.

properties.title: Tatev Monastery
properties.description: Armenian monastery located in Syunik Province, Armenia. Constructed beginning in 848, the monastery complex was expanded several times from the 10th-13th century.

properties.title: Shortugai
properties.description: An ancient trading colony on the Oxus river in the vicinity of the lapis lazuli mines of northern Afghanistan dating to ca. 2000 BC.

properties.title: House of the Centenary
properties.description: A Pompeian domus re-discovered in 1879, the so-called House of the Centenary is among the largest domus in Pompeii.

properties.title: Banditaccia necropolis, Caere
properties.description: The Etruscan necropolis of Caere, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

properties.title: Temple of Amphiaraus
properties.description: The Temple of Amphiaraus is an oracular temple dedicated to the hero/god Amphiaraus, located within the sanctuary of the Amphiareion. The site was believed to have healing powers and was particularly important in the Late Classical and Hellenistic periods (fifth to third centuries BCE).

properties.title: Via Statilia tombs
properties.description: Late Republican chamber tombs (ca. 100 B.C.) located at the intersection of the modern Via Statilia and Via di Santa Croce in Rome.

properties.title: Costești-Cetățuie
properties.description: Costești-Cetățuie Dacian fortress.

properties.title: Tomb of the Ottavii
properties.description: A mid-third century AD hypogeum tomb.

properties.title: Basilica Hilariana
properties.description: A basilica erected on the Caelian Hill in Rome under the patronage of Manius Publicus Hilarus and connected to the cult of Cybele and Attis.

properties.title: Heznalcaçar
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the southwest of the province of Sevilla that once belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. Today known as Aznalcázar.

properties.title: Prestatyn
properties.description: The modern-day site of a Romano-British settlement dating from first and second centuries A.D.

properties.title: Tel Jatt
properties.description: A site between the Sharon Plain and the Samarian Hills on which the modern town of Jatt is built. The site contains numerous Bronze Age burials and signs of habitation as late as the Bronze Age. The site has been proposed as a possible location for the town of Ginti-kirmil mentioned in the Amarna letters.

properties.title: Maadi
properties.description: A Predynastic settlement located on the eastern bank of the Nile on the outskirts of modern Cairo.

properties.title: Fidenates
properties.description: The Fidenates number among the lost peoples of Latium enumerated by Pliny the Elder.

properties.title: 'Ir David/Wadi Hilweh
properties.description: The City of David is the name given in the 20th century to an archaeological site located in the Arab neighborhood of Wadi Hilweh, located south of the Temple Mount and the Ophel in East Jerusalem. The site contains pottery from as early as the Chalcolithic Age, and has been proposed as a possible original core of the city of Jerusalem. The Silwa necropolis, a burial site dated to the 9th-7th centuries BCE, is located within this area.

properties.title: Monte Semprevisa
properties.description: The highest peak of the Monti Lepini.

properties.title: Castro de Zoñán
properties.description: A settlement dating to the second through fourth centuries.

properties.title: Colle S. Lucia-Maceralonga (Castelnuovo Parano)
properties.description: A Pre-Roman fortified center in the territory of Frosinone.

properties.title: Villa romana di via Carciano
properties.description: A Roman villa dating to the second century A.D.

properties.title: Mahabodhi Temple
properties.description: One of the four main Buddhist pilgrimage sites, identified as the place where Gautama Buddha attained Enlightenment. The first temple on the site was built by Emperor Asoka in the third century B.C., and the present temple dates from the fifth or sixth centuries. It is one of the earliest Buddhist temples built entirely in brick, still standing in India, from the late Gupta period. The site was largely abandoned from the twelfth-eighteenth centuries. It was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002.

properties.title: Roman Theater of Baelo
properties.description: A Roman theater in Baelo that dates to the reign of Claudius.

properties.title: Dūru
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources that is identified with modern Anaz Höyük.

properties.title: Winningen
properties.description: A Roman villa rustica.

properties.title: Nuraghe di Sant'Itroxia
properties.description: A Middle Bronze age nuragic site with evidence of a giant's tomb and a nuragic tower.

properties.title: Fountain of Anna Perenna
properties.description: Sacred to the goddess Anna Perenna and the nymphs, this rectangular fountain surrounded by rupestral inscriptions was excavated on the modern Via Guidubaldo del Monte in Rome's Pinciano neighborhood during the late 20th century. Rich votive deposits complement the picture of the goddess' worship painted by Ovid in the Fasti entry for the Ides of March.

properties.title: Thrypti
properties.description: Thrypti, a mountain range of eastern Crete.

properties.title: Mount Kedros
properties.description: Mount Kedros is a mountain of Crete located southwest of the Ida massif (1,777 m (5,830 ft) asl).

properties.title: Mashkan-Shapir
properties.description: Mashkan-Shapir, covering 56 ha, was occupied during the Uruk period and becomes more prominent during the Akkadian period and then during the Ur III period.

properties.title: Domus Confuleius
properties.description: The domus of the freedman P. Confuleius Sabbio at Capua.

properties.title: Santa Sabina
properties.description: A Christian basilica on the Aventine hill in Rome founded in the fourth century AD. The church takes its name from a Christian martyr who was said to have lived on the Aventine. The church is the oldest extant Roman basilica structure that preserves its original plan in the city of Rome.

properties.title: Sanctuary of Monte Sant'Angelo
properties.description: A Catholic sanctuary on Mount Gargano, in northern Apulia, Italy. Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011.

properties.title: Lamiospito Tholos Tomb, Dimini
properties.description: Late Helladic III B tholos tomb on the west foot of the Neolithic hill settlement.

properties.title: Topazios (island)
properties.description: An island in the Red Sea. The island is noted by Pliny as a source of topaz.

properties.title: Liverdun
properties.description: Excavations in and around Liverdun carried out in the 1960s revealed evidence for "fairly dense" habitation from prehistoric to Merovingian times. Notable archaeological features included a Gallo-Roman villa (destroyed in the third century A.D.) at the locality known as Rupt-Chaudron and a Merovingian necropolis of more than 1,000 tombs dating to the ninth century A.D.

properties.title: Valladolid
properties.description: The site of Celtiberian and Roman settlement eventually gave way to Moorish and, later, Christian foundations. Valladolid grew rapidly during the twelfth and thirteenth centuries under the kings Alfonso VIII and Alfonso X.

properties.title: Vilarenc
properties.description: The villa dates from the first century B.C. to the third century A.D. when it was transformed into a bath complex. It was partially reclaimed as a villa in late Roman and Medieval times.

properties.title: Irno (river)
properties.description: The Irno river is a river of Campania that flows into the Tyrrhenian Sea. While its ancient name is unknown, the river valley is the site of first millennium B.C. settlement and also the site of numerous clay beds exploited for pottery production.

properties.title: Church in Sidi Khiribech
properties.description: Ruins of a church likely built around the fifth century AD, on the summit of the low hill of Sidi Khiribech in Berenike. The character of the building and its position has suggested to some archaeologists a defensive as well as a religious purpose.

properties.title: Villa Romana ai Cavallacci
properties.description: A Roman villa first occupied in the Late Republican period and abandoned ca. the fifth century AD.

properties.title: Catacombs of San Senatore
properties.description: A Christian catacomb located at the fifteenth mile of the Via Appia in use from the late third century A.D. until the Middle Ages.

properties.title: Orto della Regina
properties.description: An archaeological site located on Monte La Frascara at Roccamonfina that is enclosed by a megalithic fortification executed in polygonal masonry.

properties.title: Adad Gate
properties.description: The Adad Gate, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Adad-mukīn-ḫegallīya ("The God Adad Is the One Who Establishes My Prosperity"), is the second of the eight city gates of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") listed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in inscriptions recording the construction of his new capital. This gate is the second of the eastward-facing entrances to the city.

properties.title: Silla de Papa
properties.description: The archaeological site of an oppidum of either Punic or bastulo-Punic origin located in the Spanish municipality of Tarifa (Cádiz). It was likely a precursor of Baelo Claudia.

properties.title: Temple of Apollo
properties.description: The Temple of Apollo (VII,7,32) in Pompeii is one of the city's oldest cults, dating to the sixth century BC. The sanctuary assumed its present appearance in the second century BC.

properties.title: Grave Circle A at Mycenae
properties.description: Grave Circle A encloses a royal cemetery within the walls of the citadel of Mycenae; inside it are six shaft graves constructed around 1600 BC.

properties.title: Csopak
properties.description: Roman ruins were discovered on the shores of Lake Balaton.

properties.title: Tempa Cortaglia
properties.description: An Archaic settlement in Lucania located near moderm Oliveto Lucano.

properties.title: Aula Palatina
properties.description: The Aula Palatina is a Roman Imperial Basilica of the emperor Constantine (German: Konstantinbasilika) located at Trier, Germany. It was built ca. A.D. 310 as part of a Roman palace complex.

properties.title: Adab
properties.description: Bismaya, ancient Adab, is a major archaeological mound in southern Iraq. The site is located in the present-day Wāsiṭ Province about 65 kilometres south of al-Kūt. Excavations by E.J. Banks from 1903-05 uncovered extensive remains of the ancient city of Adab, predominantly dating to the 3rd and early 2nd millennium BCE. In its day, Adab was renowned especially for its temple, the Emaẖ, dedicated to the goddess Ninẖursag.

properties.title: Tino di Moscona
properties.description: The remains of a fortification located in the territory of Grosseto. While the visible architectural remains date to the Medieval period, the hilltop likely was occupied earlier by Etruscans and Romans.

properties.title: Chil Zena
properties.description: A mountainous outcropping located to the west of Kandahar. A flight of forty stone steps leads to the top of the outcropping. The bilingual inscription of the third century BCE known as the Kandahar Bilingual Rock Inscription is found here.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Teate

properties.title: Elephantine

properties.title: Archaeological Sites of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn

properties.title: Forum of Segobriga
properties.description: The Forum of Segobriga is traditionally dated to the early Iulio-Claudian period when Segobriga became a municipium.

properties.title: Byzantine fortress at Thignica
properties.description: A Byzantine fortress located at the site of Thignica.

properties.title: Bernashivka
properties.description: Site of a settlement from the Neolithic Cucuteni-Trypillia culture, located on the left bank of the Dniester River.

properties.title: Selva del Lamone
properties.description: The Selva del Lamone is a modern forest reserve that preserves undeveloped natural and cultural landscapes of Lazio.

properties.title: Alyscamps
properties.description: Alyscamps is a necropolis located outside the walls of Arles, France.

properties.title: Khorsabad Palace F
properties.description: The armory (ekal māšarti) of Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad) was located in the lower city, adjacent to the southern stretch of the southwest wall. No inscriptions of the eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) record the construction of "Palace F," although several objects of that ruler were discovered there.

properties.title: Khorsabad Residence L
properties.description: The residence of Sîn-aḫu-uṣur, brother of the Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) and grand vizier of the Assyrian Empire, was constructed in the citadel of Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad), near the royal palace Egalgabarinutukua ("Palace That Has No Equal"). "Residence L" was largest of the four royal residences (J, K, L, and M) built in Dūr-Šarrukīn's citadel.

properties.title: Khorsabad Residence K
properties.description: The eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) had several royal residences constructed in the citadel of his new capital, Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad). Residence K, which has constructed on the western side of the citadel, is presumed to have been for one of the highest officials of the Assyrian Empire, possibly even Sargon’s heir designate Sennacherib.

properties.title: Coastal Tower 16b (Old Mawbray)
properties.description: Coastal Tower 16b, part of the Hadrian's Wall Coastal defences

properties.title: Basilica of Hildeguns
properties.description: A basilica dating to the time of the Vandals.

properties.title: Suburbium Toletanum
properties.description: The location of the Late Roman and Visigothic suburbium beyond the Roman circus. Transition from suburban villas to a large-scale Visigothic expansion, which included various churches and the Praetorium, or Royal Palace. Destroyed during the ninth century. Excavations carried out in the early 2000s.

properties.title: Polygonal wall of Roman castrum
properties.description: The polygonal masonry wall of the Roman castrum at Pyrgi encloses an area of ca. 5.7 ha.

properties.title: Basilica of St. Crispinus
properties.description: The fourth century Basilica of St. Crispinus is one of the largest known in Africa.

properties.title: Strata Diocletiana
properties.description: A Roman road built in the third century A.D. under the emperor Diocletian that ran along the limes Arabicus of the eastern Roman empire.

properties.title: Santalla de Bóveda
properties.description: The Roman sanctuary of Santalla de Bóveda dates to the second through fourth centuries A.D. It is located in the parish of Santalla de Bóveda de Meralocated near Lugo. Discovered in 1926, the site is a protected national monument.

properties.title: Tall-e Bakun B
properties.description: The second of the two mounds comprising the Tall-e Bakun site.

properties.title: Solenyĭ Dol
properties.description: Burial complex in the southern Ural Mountains region containing a number of Late Antique burials.

properties.title: Madhukeshwara temple
properties.description: A Shiva temple at Banavasi in India whose foundation may date as early as the 7th century CE.

properties.title: Western necropolis at Egnatia/Gnathia
properties.description: The western necropolis at Egnatia/Gnathia includes some tombs of the Messapian culture dating from the middle of the fourth to the second centuries B.C.

properties.title: Oldberry Castle
properties.description: Oldberry Castle is an Iron Age hill fort in Somerset, England.

properties.title: Great Dolmen of Comenda da Igreja

properties.title: Palaiosouda (island)

properties.title: Marlik

properties.title: Porta Romana

properties.title: Ea temple (Khorsabad)
properties.description: As part of the palatial complex of Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad), the eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) constructed six temples, including one to the god Ea.

properties.title: Ekklesiasterion at Poseidonia/Paestum

The structure retained its function after the Lucanian conquest but was abandoned, buried, and built over after the Roman conquest.

properties.title: Jemdet Nasr
properties.description: An ancient site in Iraq's Babil Governorate (Iraq) that lends its name to the Jemdet Nasr period (ca. 3100–2900 B.C.).

properties.title: Anu Gate
properties.description: The Anu Gate, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Anu-mušallim-epšēt-qātīya ("The God Anu Is the One Who Makes My Undertakings Successful"), is the fifth of the eight city gates of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") listed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in inscriptions recording the construction of his new capital. This gate is the first of the west-facing entrances to the city.

properties.title: Mullissu Gate
properties.description: The Mullissu Gate, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Mullissu-muddišat-ḫiṣbi ("The Goddess Mullissu Is the One Who Restores Abundance"), is the fourth of the eight city gates of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") listed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in inscriptions recording the construction of his new capital. This gate is the second of the north-facing entrances to the city.

properties.title: Santa Susanna
properties.description: The current Church of Saint Susanna at the Baths of Diocletian located on the Quirinal Hill in Rome dates from 1585. A titular church has existed on the site since ca. A.D. 280. The remains of an elite house (domus) are preserved beneath the church.

properties.title: Porta Aurelia

properties.title: Piazza d'Armi
properties.description: The site of the arx of ancient Veii located on the southern spur of the volcanic plateau on which the city is located. There is archaeological evidence for an initial occupation phase of the ninth century B.C. By the seventh century B.C., the area shows evidence for adoption of rectilinear huts and assumes an orthogonal street grid.

properties.title: Bryn Celli Ddu

properties.title: Anaktoron at Pantalika

properties.title: Lusanda
properties.description: Lusanda is a fortified city in Que, probably in the eastern part of the Cilician plain. The city is mentioned with Abarnani and Kisuatni in royal inscriptions of the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III (r. 858-824 BC).

properties.title: Kisuatni
properties.description: Kisuatni is a fortified city in Que, probably in the eastern part of the Cilician plain. The city is mentioned with Abarnani and Lusanda in royal inscriptions of the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III (r. 858-824 BC).

properties.title: Basentello (river)
properties.description: A river of southern Italy, Basentello flows near the border between Apulia and Basilicata. It flows from its source near Palazzo San Gervasio to Bradano.

properties.title: Mura Greche
properties.description: The so-called "Mura Greche" are remains of the later third century B.C. fortifications of Neapolis.

properties.title: The "Auditorium site" at the Auditorium Parco della Musica (Rome)
properties.description: An Early Republican to Middle Imperial elite complex along the Via Flaminia in the outskirts of Rome.

properties.title: Ninurta temple (Khorsabad)
properties.description: As part of the palatial complex of Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad), the eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) constructed six temples, including one to the god Ninurta.

properties.title: Abu Simbel
properties.description: The site of two temples constructed by Ramesses II, one dedicated to the triad of Amun, Ra-Horakhty, and Ptah, as well as the deified Ramesses, and another dedicated to Hathor and the pharaoh's wife Nefertari. The temple was relocated between 1964 and 1968 to prevent its submersion under Lake Nasser after the construction of the Aswan High Dam.

properties.title: Porticus Vipsania
properties.description: The Porticus Vipsania was a public complex located along the eastern side of the via Lata in the Campus Martius. This complex contained a map commissioned by Agrippa. The project was begun under Polla (Agrippa's sister) and completed under Augustus.

properties.title: Arcus Novus
properties.description: A now-lost arch on the ancient Via Lata. It was dedicated to Diocletian either in 293 CE (marking the occasion of his decennalia) or in 303-304 (joint triumph with Maximian). The present church of Santa Maria in Via Lata occupies the site of the arch.

properties.title: Black Ball Camp
properties.description: Black Ball Camp or Gallox hill fort is an Iron Age hill fort in Dunster, Somerset, England.

properties.title: Grabbist Hillfort
properties.description: Grabbist Hillfort is an Iron Age hill-fort located west of Dunster in Somerset, England.

properties.title: So-called twin sanctuary
properties.description: A double sanctuary on the forum of Carsulae. It is no longer clear to which gods these temples belonged.

properties.title: Kinneil
properties.description: The site of a Roman fortlet on the Antonine Wall. The fortlet measures ca. 21.5 x 18.5 m, covering an area of ca. 0.04 ha.

properties.title: Woden Law hill fort
properties.description: Woden Law hill fort is a multi-vallate Iron Age site in Scotland.

properties.title: Torre dei Conti
properties.description: A fortified Medieval tower located in Rome, dating to AD 1238, and built by Richard Conti, brother of Pope Innocent III.

properties.title: Roman Road in Sutton Park
properties.description: An urban park in Birmingham, England, containing a stretch of preserved Roman road.

properties.title: Forum Holitorium
properties.description: The Forum Holitorium was the vegetable market of ancient Rome, situated outside the Porta Carmentalis in the southern Campus Martius. This area was bounded by the Forum Boarium and the Circus Flaminius.

properties.title: Greolieres Roman Milestone
properties.description: A Roman milestone located in France, in the town of Gréolières in the Alpes-Maritimes department in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region. The inscription on the milestone honors the Roman emperor Caracalla and is dated to 213.

properties.title: Temple of Apollo at Thermos
properties.description: A temple to the Apollo built in the late seventh century B.C. atop the ruins of the previous megaron in Thermos.

properties.title: Library of Hadrian at Athens
properties.description: The Library of Hadrian is located on the north side of the Acropolis, immediately north of the Roman Agora. The complex was built by the Roman emperor Hadrian in A.D. 131/2 and subsequently destroyed during the Herulian sack of Athens in A.D. 267.

properties.title: Gymnasium at Olympia
properties.description: The Gymnasium of Olympia was a practice and training field constructed in 250 BC for male Hellenic athletes competing in the Olympic Games.

properties.title: Nekou Diorux
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 74 G3 Nekou Diorux

properties.title: Santa Maria della Libera
properties.description: An eleventh century church near Aquinum built largely from spolia.

properties.title: Manoppello Roman Villa
properties.description: A Late Republican villa in Abruzzo that later became a productive estate. The archaeological remains of the villa are located in the locality of Piano S. Maria Arabona in Manoppello, Italy.

properties.title: Temple of Juno Caelestis
properties.description: Juno Caelestis, a successor divinity of the Punic Tanit, is celebrated by a sanctuary built at Dougga ca. 222-235 CE, and sponsored by Q. Gabinius Rufus Felix.

properties.title: Roman Circus at Mérida
properties.description: The Roman Circus at Mérida dates ca. 20 B.C.

properties.title: Waddon Hill
properties.description: A Roman fort in Dorset, England, that began as a temporary camp under Vespasian.

properties.title: Fosso Marangone
properties.description: A small stream that flows into the Tyrrhenian Sea. It now lies in the territory of the municipalities of Allumiere, Civitavecchia, and Santa Marinella and forms the geographical boundary between the latter two. The watercourse originates at Poggio Ombricolo.

properties.title: Torre di Mercurio
properties.description: A tower associated with Pompeii's fortification wall that is also sometimes designated as "Tower XI".

properties.title: Bardsey Island
properties.description: Bardsey Island, occupied since the Neolithic period, lies off the Llŷn Peninsula of Wales.

properties.title: Roman cistern
properties.description: A large Roman cistern at Albano Laziale.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Burnum
properties.description: A Roman amphitheater associated with the legionary establishment of Burnum.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Salona
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Salona.

properties.title: Acquoria
properties.description: A basis villae near Tivoli in opus incertum on the river Aniene measuring 70 x 20 m. Two phases have been identified: second-first century B.C. and first century A.D.

properties.title: Dragoncello
properties.description: Dragoncello is a modern district of Rome's metropolitan area where archaeological evidence for a series of late republican villas was uncovered. At least four in number, these villa rustica sites have evidence for domestic production.

properties.title: Aristanis
properties.description: A Byzantine site in western Sardinia, made important by the location of a bishopric there by Torcotorio in AD 1070; now the modern city of Oristano.

properties.title: Tomb of the Shields and Chairs, Caere
properties.description: The so-called Tomb of the Shields and Chairs at Caere dates ca. 520 - 500 B.C. The organization of this tomb is similar to that of the Tomb of the Capitals and the Tomb of the Cornice. It has a short dromos and a large vestibule. In the vestibule are two seats carved from the tuff bedrock as well as a series of hanging shields carved in relief.

properties.title: Santa Lucia in Selci
properties.description: The church of Santa Lucia in Selci was founded by the eighth century and perhaps as early as the sixth century.

properties.title: Eastern Outer Wall of Babylon
properties.description: The Neo-Babylonian ruler Nabopolassar (r. 625–605 BC) started planning and constructing an outer wall around the eastern side of Babylon. This massive mudbrick brick wall, together with its protective quay wall and a wide moat, remained unfinished at the time of Nabopolassar’s death. His son and successor Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–562 BC) finished the work started by his father. Traces of Babylon’s once-impressive eastern outer wall are still visible today.

properties.title: Ponte Cardona
properties.description: An aqueduct bridge near Nequinum dating ca. A.D. 24 - 33.

properties.title: Tell Arpachiyah
properties.description: A Neolithic site occupied in the Halaf and Ubaid periods.

properties.title: Ayanis
properties.description: Ayanis (or Ayanıs, now Ağartı Kalesi) is an Urartean fortress and settlement located 35 km north of Van on a rocky outcrop 250 m above Lake Van (1867 m above sea level). It was founded in the 7th century BCE under Rusa, son of Argišti, and was named Rusahinili Eidurukai ("The City of Rusa in front of Mount Eiduru"). Here two inscriptions of Rusa, son of Argišti (7th century BCE), have been found which report that Rusa cultivated the barren land, built the fortress and the city as well as a “tower temple” (“susi temple”) and a “Gate for the God Haldi” (A 12-01 and A 12-09).

properties.title: Burgus Szentendre-Dera
properties.description: Burgus Szentendre-Dera is a late antique Roman military encampment located along the Hungarian Danube at Szentendre (St. Andrae). The fort secured the Pannonian Limes.

properties.title: Tell Afis
properties.description: Iron Age settlement in Syria. The site has been tentatively identified as Hadarikka/Hazrek, the capital of the region of Luhuti/Luash, which became part of the kingdom of Hamath around 796 BCE.

properties.title: Via Tiberina
properties.description: An ancient Roman road.

properties.title: Stoa of Attalos
properties.description: The Stoa of Attalos, located on the eastern side of the ancient Athenian agora, is a long, rectangular, two-story building of limestone and marble, with an external and internal colonnade. It was originally constructed around 150 BCE and then reconstructed in the 1950s.

properties.title: Tomb of Thutmose III (KV34)
properties.description: KV34 served as the tomb of 18th dynasty Pharaoh Thutmose III.

properties.title: Tineida
properties.description: The ancient village of Tineida, in Egypt's Dakhleh Oasis.

properties.title: Erechtheion
properties.description: The Erechtheion is a temple on the north side of the Athenian Acropolis dedicated to Athena Polias and other deities and heroes; the temple is of the Ionic order with several distinctive features, including its famous caryatid porch.

properties.title: San Demetrio ne' Vestini

properties.title: Roman theater at Sparta

properties.title: Villa of Masseria Ciccotti

properties.title: Burnt Palace at Kalhu
properties.description: The Burnt Palace, which was destroyed by fire when Kalhu fell to anti-Assyrian Babylonian and Median forces in 612 BC, has the longest building sequence yet identified at Nimrud (biblical Calah). This royal residence, which was constructed in the southeast quarter of the citadel, had at least nine phases of occupation between the Middle Assyrian and Hellenistic Periods. The so-called Burnt Palace was rebuilt/renovated three times during the ninth to seventh centuries BC and it might have temporarily served as a royal residence during the reign of Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC), while that Assyrian king was building his new capital Dūr-Šarrukīn. An immense collection of burnt ivories (the ‘Loftus ivories’) was discovered in and near the throne room in 1954–55; these are now in the British Museum (London).

properties.title: Asharne
properties.description: Tell ‘Acharneh is located 35 km northwest of Hama, on the north bank of the Orontes River, at the crossroads of two main trade routes. This center for the production of oil, wax, and wheat was occupied during the Bronze and Iron Ages, as well as during the First Crusades. Its ancient name, Tunip, is known from second-millennium-BC sources. A stele fragment bearing an inscription of the Neo-Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BCE) found there attests to the city’s occupation during the Iron Age.

properties.title: Reccopolis
properties.description: Reccopolis is an urban, Visigothic, ex-novo foundation made under king Liuvigild in A.D. 578. The archaeological remains at the site include a palace complex, public area, basilica, walls, and aqueduct. The site is known today by the Spanish version of its Latin name (Recópolis); it is located near the modern village of Zorita de los Canes in the Spanish province of Guadelajara.

properties.description: A rock-cut Christian sanctuary located on Monte Altino in the Monti Aurunci that was begun ca. A.D. 830.

properties.title: Church of Saint Panteleimon
properties.description: The Church of Saint Panteleimon (Thessaloniki) is a late Byzantine church.

properties.title: Temple of Artemis at Sardis
properties.description: A large temple dedicated to Artemis at the city of Sardis in western Asia Minor. A sanctuary to Artemis was constructed on the site during the Persian Era (ca. 547-334 BCE), and construction on a new temple on the site began during the third century BCE. The temple was never fully completed. A small church was built on part of the site in the 5th century CE, but the structure declined from the 7th century onwards, and many of its stones were reused or burned.

properties.title: Temple of Venus
properties.description: The Temple of Venus (VIII,1) is located adjacent to Pompeii's Porta Marina. The site was cleared in the early years of the colony to make way for the temple. Seriously damaged by the AD 62 earthquake, the sanctuary was still being rebuilt at the time of its ultimate destruction.

properties.title: Arco de los Blanco
properties.description: A Roman gateway.

properties.title: Ekišnugal
properties.description: The temple of the moon god Nanna/Suen/Sîn at Ur from the third to first millennium B.C. Over the course of its long history, it was rebuilt (and expanded) numerous times. A few of its more famous builders were Narām-Sîn of Agade, Ur-Nammu of Ur, and Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon.

properties.title: Coccium?
properties.description: A minor Romano-British settlement located at Wigan, Lancashire.

properties.title: Bronze Age Cemetery at Mursia
properties.description: A cemetery (referred to collectively in Italian as "sesi") consisting of multi-burial stone cairns associated with the Bronze Age settlement at Mursia on Mediterranean island of Pantelleria.

properties.title: Mursia
properties.description: A modern village on the northwest coast of the Mediterranean island of Pantelleria. Mursia lies atop a settlement of late Bronze Age date that is associated with the cemetery (Sesi) that lies immediately to its south.

properties.title: Shadwell Roman Bathhouse
properties.description: A second to fourth century A.D. Romano-British bathhouse that was excavated in 2002. Findspot of RIB 3012.

properties.title: Erana
properties.description: An ancient city in Cilicia, defeated by Roman troops under Cicero's command as governor of the Roman province of Cilicia. The city's precise location is not known, but it seems to have been located on the north side of the Amanus mountain range (the modern Nur Dağları in Turkey).

properties.title: Hellenistic-Roman theater at Sarno

properties.title: Haua Fteah
properties.description: A karstic cave located in northeastern Libya that is a significant site for modern human prehistory. The cave was occupied during the Middle and Upper Paleolithic, the Mesolithic and the Neolithic periods. Evidence for modern human presence in the cave dates back to 200,000 BP.

properties.title: Aqua Augusta (Naples)
properties.description: The Aqua Augusta (Naples), also known as the Acquedotto romano del Serino, is a complex aqueduct system supplying Roman-period sites in the Bay of Naples. The aqueduct system was built between ca. 33 and 12 B.C. It supplied a number of Campanian centers, including Pompeii, Herculaneum, and Puteoli.

properties.title: Handuru Gate
properties.description: Most 7th-century B.C. Assyrian inscriptions record that Nineveh had eight south- and east-facing gates: the Handūru Gate was the first of these. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Šarur-mušamqit-ayyāb-šarri ("The God Šarur Is the One Who Cuts Down the King's Enemy"). This unlocated gate is now generally thought to have been located near southwest corner of the city.

properties.title: Rocca San Silvestro, Campiglia Marittima
properties.description: The Rocca San Silvestro is a tenth century fortified village on Monte Rombolo near Campiglia Marittima in the Alta Maremma. The village was built in order to exploit rich mineral resources in the area.

properties.title: Villa Arianna
properties.description: The so-called "Villa Arianna" at Stabiae is typically considered one of the earliest villas at the site and is often dated to the second century B.C.

properties.title: Villa San Marco
properties.description: The Villa San Marco originates in the Augustan period and was subsequently expanded during the reign of Claudius. Its owner may have been a freedman of Claudius.

properties.title: Lucena
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the south of the province of Córdoba that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X.

properties.title: Almoguera
properties.description: The Spanish village of Almoguera is located in the southeast of the province of Córdoba, near Baena. It belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X in the thirteenth century.

properties.title: Matrera castle
properties.description: Castillo de Matrera is a Spanish castle that originally dates to the ninth century and is located in the northeast of the province of Cádiz. It belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X (in the thirteenth century). Today it is located in the municipality of Villamartín.

properties.title: Via Claudia Augusta
properties.description: The Via Claudia Augusta was a Roman road that traversed the Alps, connecting the Po river valley to Rhaetia. It was begun by Claudius in AD 46/7.

properties.title: Tomb of Publius Aelius Callistion
properties.description: The tomb of Publius Aelius Callistion, a freedman (libertus) of the emperor Hadrian, is colloquially known as the "Sedia del Diavolo". It is located in a piazza that derives its name from the tomb's occupant (piazza Elio Callistio) in Rome's Trieste neighborhood.

properties.title: Baths at Conimbriga
properties.description: The Roman baths at Conimbriga.

properties.title: Pons Fabricius
properties.description: The Pons Fabricius (sometimes referred to as the Ponte dei Quattro Capi) is a first century BC bridge in Rome that spans part of the Tiber from the area of the Circus Flaminius to the Tiber island.

properties.title: Roman theater at Tergeste
properties.description: The Roman theater at Tergeste dates to the late first century A.D.

properties.title: Roman Theater at Mérida
properties.description: The Roman Theatre of Mérida was sponsored by Marcus Agrippa and dates ca. 16-15 B.C.

properties.title: Mülheim-Kärlich
properties.description: A Roman villa dating to the second and third centuries A.D.

properties.title: Remstecken
properties.description: Site of a Roman villa rustica, dating from the first to third centuries AD.

properties.title: Fatimid Cemetery in Aswan
properties.description: The Fatimid Cemetery in Aswan includes tombs dating from the seventh to the twelfth centuries CE. The site is included in the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae".

properties.title: Temple of Amada
properties.description: The Temple of Amada is the oldest Egyptian temple known in Nubia. Founded by Pharaoh Thutmose III (18th dynasty), the temple was dedicated to Amun and Re-Horakhty. The decorative program is attributed to Amenhotep II, his son and successor. The temple was relocated to its current position in 1964 along with the Temple of Derr.

properties.title: Farah Bala Hisar
properties.description: According to Ball (1982), Farah Bala Hisar is the site of a large fortified enclosure of mud with multi-period remains, the latest of which are those of a castle dating from the Timurid period.

properties.title: Stari Ras
properties.description: Stari Ras, the first capital of Serbia, is the site of an impressive group of medieval monuments consisting of fortresses, churches and monasteries listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

properties.title: Nuraghe Rumanedda
properties.description: A nuraghe located near Tottubella in the territory of Sassari.

properties.title: Nuraghe Unia
properties.description: A well-preserved monopteral nuraghe located in northwestern Sardinia.

properties.title: Aenos
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 69 unlocated Aenos

properties.title: Ishtar Temple at Mari
properties.description: Temple dedicated to the goddess Ishtar located in the western section of the city of Mari.

properties.title: Vitozza
properties.description: Vitozza is an ancient settlement located near the village of San Quirico. Its rock-cut habitations were in use by the Etruscans and Romans and again during the medieval period, continuing up to the eighteenth century. Over 200 caves (columbaria) have been cut in the local tufo bedrock.

properties.title: Nuraghe Appiu
properties.description: A nuragic complex in northwest Sardinia.

properties.title: Theater of Dionysus Eleuthereus
properties.description: Theatre on the south slope of the Acropolis in Athens.

properties.title: Stoa of Zeus (Eleutherios)
properties.description: The Stoa of Zeus Eleutherios was built on the west side of the Agora of Athens between 430-425 BC, in honor of Zeus "of Freedom"; the stoa, Doric in its external order, housed the shields of Athenians who had died fighting for the city.

properties.title: Coemeterium Maius
properties.description: A major Roman necropolis and catacomb along the Via Nomentana.

properties.title: Tırmıl Tepe Höyüğü
properties.description: An unexcavated mound on the outskirts of modern Mersin in Turkey. Archaeological surface survey yielded pottery dating from the Calcolithic to the Medieval periods. Atop the mound lie the much-depleted ruins of a possibly medieval fortification. Tırmıl Tepe Höyüğü numbers among the proposed locations of ancient Kundu/Kyinda.

properties.title: Mila Mergi
properties.description: The mountain now called Mila Mergi was called Ilimeru in Assyrian texts of the 8th century B.C. The identification is provided by an Assyrian rock relief dating to the reign of Tiglath-pileser III. The mountain is located ca. 25 kilometers northwest of Dohuk in northern Iraq.

properties.title: Roman Forum at Syracuse
properties.description: The area, roughly situated between the island of Ortygia and the district of Acradina, was used as an agora and, in later years, as the forum of the city of Syracuse. It is now a public park where ancient ruins are still visible.

properties.title: So-called Roman Gymnasium at Syracuse
properties.description: A monumental complex in the ancient city of Syracuse, probably built around the first century AD. It was initially identified as a gymnasium or a thermal bath; it includes the ruins of a theatre, a quadriporticus, and a temple.

properties.description: A sixth century B.C. aqueduct on Samos, the Tunnel of Eupalinos is an amphistomon, meaning it was excavated simultaneously from each terminus. The tunnel measures 1,036 m in length.

properties.description: A ramped, megalithic structure in Sardinia dated to around 2700-2000 BC.

properties.title: Early fortified site at Ghuzza
properties.description: An unexcavated, eroded fortified site at the gold-processing complex at al-Ghuzza in Egypt's eastern desert. It may date to the New Kingdom period.

properties.title: Tabard Square Temple Complex
properties.description: A Romano-Celtic temple complex located near the junction of Stane Street and Watling Street in modern Southwark.

properties.title: Horti Liciniani
properties.description: A complex of elite gardens on the Esquiline Hill connected to the gens Licinia. The gardens were located between the via Labicana and via Praenestina.

properties.title: Campus Agrippae
properties.description: "Campus Agrippae" describes an area within regio VII of ancient Rome that is connected to the building activities of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa in the first century BCE.

properties.title: Crofton Roman villa
properties.description: A villa occupied between ca. AD 140 and 400 now located in Orpington, in the London Borough of Bromley.

properties.title: Ekitušgarza
properties.description: The temple of the goddess Bēlet-Eanna, Ekitušgarza (“House, Abode of the Regulations”), was located in the Tuba district of Babylon, in the western half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of three temples in that part of Babylon. Ekitušgarza was rebuilt by the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–652 BC).

properties.title: Esabad
properties.description: The temple of the goddess Gula, Esabad (“House of the Open Ear”), was located in the Tuba district of Babylon, in the western half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of three temples in that part of Babylon. Esabad was rebuilt by the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal (r. 668–ca. 631 BC) and Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–652 BC). The temple survived into Arsacid times (247 BC–AD 224).

In the twentieth century it was the subject of major investigations under M. Cristofani and, later, M. Bonamici.

properties.title: Khorsabad ziggurat

properties.title: Ninurta temple (Kalhu)
properties.description: When Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud) became the principal administrative center of the Assyrian Empire in the ninth century BC, king Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) built (or rebuilt) numerous temples. The most important of those was dedicated to the god Ninurta, the patron deity of city, which Ashurnasirpal had constructed between his palace and the ziggurat, a building also consecrated to Ninurta.

properties.title: Kalhu ziggurat
properties.description: The temple-tower of the god Ninurta, which was started by the ninth-century-BC Assyrian ruler Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) and completed by his son and successor Shalmaneser III (r. 858–824 BC), is still the most prominent feature of Kalhu (modern Nimrud). This multi-staged ziggurat, whose remains are now a pyramid of eroding mud-brick, was constructed in the northwest corner of the citadel, next to Kalhu's principal sanctuary, the Ninurta temple.

properties.title: Kundu/Kyinda
properties.description: Kundu is mentioned in Akkadian royal inscriptions of the seventh-century-BC Assyrian king Esarhaddon. In Classical times, Strabo describes Kyinda as a fortress where Macedonian kings deposited treasure. Eumenes reportedly captured the treasure when he revolted against Antigonus. The site is now unlocated.

properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Antinoeion at Hadrian's Villa
properties.description: A sacred precinct at the western end of Villa Hadriani, comprising two temples at opposite (north and south) ends of a plaza or garden, and (on the western edge of this complex) a small colonnaded hemicycle. Here, Hadrian may have planned to build a large, semi-circular temple-tomb for Antinous, in place of which his successors built the colonnaded hemicycle.

properties.title: Roman baths at Hydata Hypsitana/Forum Traiani
properties.description: The Roman baths Fordongianus dates to the first through third centuries.

properties.title: Broch of Mousa
properties.description: The Broch of Mousa is a drystone broch in Scotland, dating ca. 400-200 BC.

properties.title: Aiano-Torraccia di Chiusi Roman villa
properties.description: The Villa Romana di Aiano-Torraccia di Chiusi, located near San Gimignano, is notable for a tri-apsidal courtyard.

properties.title: Barburgh Mill Roman fortlet
properties.description: A Roman fortlet lying on a small hill near the line of a Roman road (R77). Excavated in the 1970s, the site has now been largely destroyed by a gravel quarry.

properties.title: Abd al Kuri (island)
properties.description: Abd al Kuri is an island located about 65 miles southwest of Socotra in the Indian Ocean and is part of the Socotra Archipelago.

properties.title: S'Illot

properties.title: Duino Mithraeum

properties.title: Zahhak Castle
properties.description: A fortified citadel located in Hashtrud, East Azerbaijan Province, Iran. It takes its name from the mythological figure Zahhak. The site is in use from the second millennium BC until the Timurid era.

properties.title: Roman theater of Privernum
properties.description: The Roman theater of Privernum is attested mainly by means of epigraphic evidence.

properties.title: House of Pansa
properties.description: The House of Pansa (VI,6,1) is an atrium house in Pompeii that occupies an entire insula. Architectural elements date the structure ca. 140-120 BC in its original phase. The merchant and duumvir Cn. Alleius Nigidius Maius owned the property.

properties.description: Ancient Parentium, now Poreč, Croatia, was a city on the western coast of the Istrian peninsula. properties.description: Pašime is an ancient settlement located at Tall Abū Šījah, an archaeological site in the Maysan province of southeastern Iraq, close to the Iranian border. The site was inhabited perhaps already from the fourth millennium BCE, and particularly in the third and early second millennium BCE. The name Pašime appears in an Old Akkadian inscription discovered at the site in the course of excavations by the Iraq State Board of Antiquities and Heritage in 2007. The inscription was dedicated to the god Šuda, indicating that a temple devoted to this deity may have been located at Pašime.

properties.title: Nahal Hemar Cave
properties.description: Cave site located on the banks of Nahal Hemar in the southern Judean Desert. The site contains traces of habitation dated to the pre-pottery Neolithic (ca. 6900-6300 BCE).

properties.title: House of the Ship Europa
properties.description: The so-called "House of the Ship Europa" is a large house in the Roman city of Pompeii (I,15,3) that takes its conventional, archaeological name from a large graffito of ship bearing the legend 'Europa'.

properties.title: Achaean League (Second)
properties.description: Established in 280 BCE, the second Achaean League was centered in the northern and central Peloponnese. Allied to Rome in the Second Macedonian War (200-196 BCE), the league extended its control over all of the Peloponnese. In the Third Macedonian War (171–168 BCE) the League's relationship with Rome deteriorated; in ca. 146 BCE this led to open warfare, which resulted in the defeat and dissolution of the league.

properties.title: Cappuck
properties.description: Site of a Roman fort occupied during the Flavian and Antonine periods. It lies 4 miles east of Jedburgh in the Scottish Borders, along the line of Dere Street.

properties.title: Cantiano
properties.description: An ancient place at modern Cantiano may have stood along the line of a branch of the Via Flaminia. The so-called "Sassoferrato milestone" was located about one mile from Cantiano (CIL 6629).

properties.title: Bibbiena
properties.description: Bibbiena likely originated as an Etruscan hilltop settlement. A Medieval castle is eventually built atop the hill, which stands 425 metres (1,394 ft) above sea level.

properties.title: Vaticanus Ager
properties.description: A district on the right bank of the river Tiber, between the lower course of the river and the territory of Veii.

properties.title: Ṣanʿāʾ
properties.description: Ṣanʿāʾ is the largest city in Yemen. Its "Old City" was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

properties.title: Campo Valdés Roman Baths, Gijón
properties.description: Roman baths dating from the first to fourth centuries.

properties.title: Castro de Santaia
properties.description: A settlement of the Castro Culture covering > 4 hectares near Santai in Spain.

properties.title: Forre di Corchiano
properties.description: The Forre di Corchiano is a preserved landscape significant not only for its landforms but also for cultural heritage remains pertaining to many periods.

properties.title: Rollright Stones
properties.description: A complex of three Neolithic and Bronze Age megalithic monuments dating from the fourth to second millennia B.C. located on the borders of Oxfordshire and Warwickshire in the English Midlands.

properties.title: Arx of Cosa
properties.description: The citadel of the ancient city and location of its Capitolium.

properties.title: Comitium of Poseidonia/Paestum
properties.description: The comitium is a component of a monumental forum complex constructed at Paestum after the city became a Latin colony in 273 B.C.

properties.title: Sacred Area of S. Omobono
properties.description: An archaeological area in the Forum Boarium comprising an ancient ritual precinct with twin temples ranging in date from the Archaic period through the time of the Roman Empire. The Medieval church dedicated to S. Omobono stands atop the remains of one of the two ancient temples.

properties.title: Murus Servii Tullii
properties.description: The Republican city wall of Rome.

properties.title: Ancient Stadium of Rhodes
properties.description: The Hellenistic Stadium on the Acropolis of Rhodes.

properties.title: Scratchbury Camp
properties.description: Scratchbury Camp, Wiltshire, England, is the site of a 15 hectare hill fort.

properties.title: Temple of Zeus at Cyrene
properties.description: The Doric Temple of Zeus at Cyrene

properties.title: Susegana bridge
properties.description: A Roman bridge along the Via Claudia Augusta.

properties.title: Theater at Bodrum
properties.description: The Theater at Bodrum is dedicated to Ares.

properties.title: Jerwan Aqueduct
properties.description: The Assyrian king Sennacherib had an aqueduct constructed between 703 and 690 B.C. near the ancient city of Girmua. The structure is part of the "Khinnis [Canal] System." The identification of the structure's builder is confirmed by means of several inscriptions.

properties.title: Monte Novo do Castelinho
properties.description: A Roman earthen embankment dam of ca. 56 m length.

properties.title: Puente Melchor Roman villa
properties.description: A Roman villa with mosaic decoration located in an archaeological area of Puente Melchor, in Puerto Real, Cádiz, Spain.

properties.title: Fonte Coberta
properties.description: A Roman dam

properties.title: El Gallinero
properties.description: The remains of a Roman ceramic workshop and manufactory.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater of Venusia
properties.description: A Roman amphitheater dating to the first and second centuries.

properties.title: Piazza Ronchi Roman cistern
properties.description: A Roman cistern dating to the second-third centuries CE.

properties.title: Cursus Barrows (Burial Mounds)
properties.description: A grouping of burial mounds (named Cursus Barrows) located very close to Stonehenge.

properties.title: Greppe S . Angelo necropolis
properties.description: A rock-cut necropolis of Caere noted as the findspot of the Sarpedon krater of the artists Euphronios.

properties.title: 'Izbet Sartah
properties.description: An Iron Age site near the modern town of Rosh Ha'ayin.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Aosta
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Aosta likely dates to the first century A.D. Its remains are englobed within Medieval structures.

properties.title: Roman theater at Aosta
properties.description: The Roman theater at Aosta dates ca. 25 B.C.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 18 D3 unnamed centuriation (Genava)

properties.title: Baths of Caracalla (Albano Laziale)
properties.description: Public baths generally dated to the reign of Caracalla.

properties.title: Palace of Sennacherib
properties.description: The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib built a magnificent royal residence in the citadel of Nineveh. This extensive architectural complex was given the Sumerian ceremonial name Egalzagdinutukua, which means "Palace Without a Rival." A small portion of the once-grand Assyrian palace is still visible today.

properties.title: Theater of Pyrrhus
properties.description: The Hellenistic theater at Dodona is linked to the reign of Pyrrhus in the third century B.C.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 17 I3 unnamed pass (N Segusio)

properties.title: Fayyum (oasis)
properties.description: Large depression (not a true oasis) west of the Nile River containing arable land watered by the flooding of the Nile. Inhabited from the Mesolithic period, the Fayyum contains the earliest evidence of farming in Egypt. The water levels of the Fayyum's lake varied significantly until a land reclamation project during the 12th dynasty implemented artificial water controls. During the Ptolemaic and Roman periods, the Fayyum was administered as the Arsinoite Nome.

properties.title: Grotte di Seiano a Pietramelara
properties.description: A ruined, terraced megalithic complex covering an area of some 900 square meters. The complex likely dates to the second century B.C. and was destroyed in the time of Sulla. The complex is interpreted as a Samnite sanctuary.

properties.title: Ramla bay villa
properties.description: A villa maritima discovered in 1910-11.

properties.title: House of Many Colors
properties.description: A large and well-appointed house located in the Villa Section of Olynthus, proposed as an Olynthian type-house

properties.title: Church of Saint Catherine, Thessaloniki
properties.description: A late Byzantine church in Thessalonica

properties.title: Koumasa prepalatial cemetery
properties.description: A prepalatial cemetery on the island of Crete that includes three tholos tombs and one rectangular tomb.

properties.title: Kom el-Ahmer
properties.description: Archaeological site in the province of Beheira in the Western Delta, inhabited from the Roman through the Early Islamic periods. Along with the nearby site Kom Wasit, it has been identified as a possible location of Metelis, the capital of the Metelite Nome.

properties.title: Great Palace of Constantinople
properties.description: Palace complex constructed by Constantine I in 330 CE that served as the primary residence of the Eastern Roman/Byzantine Emperors until 1081 CE. Use of the palace declined beginning in the 11th century, and it had been abandoned by the time of the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453. Most of the structure was demolished in the early Ottoman period. The Sultan Ahmed Mosque was built on the primary site of the palace in the early 17th century.

properties.title: Finca del Secretario
properties.description: An archaeological site that comprises remains of an urban area of the Roman period ranging in date from the first to the fifth centuries. Among the complexes in evidence are a salting factory, a pottery works, and thermal baths.

properties.description: A Roman settlement at Petinesca replaced a Celtic oppidum located on the plateau of the Jensberg. The site was located along the military highway from Aventicum to Salodurum.

properties.title: Tenedo
properties.description: Tenedo lies at the confluence of the Aare and the Rhine. In pre-Roman times a key trade route crossed the Rhine here.

properties.title: Tumulus de Péré
properties.description: The Péré tumulus, or Pairé tumulus, is a Neolithic tumulus that dates from the fifth millennium B.C. The site is located in Prissé-la-Charrière, in Deux-Sèvres, in New Aquitaine, France. It is composed of three main megalithic structures, built at different times.

properties.description: An ancient phrourion in the Attalid Kingdom, which modern scholarship places at Yüntdağ.

properties.title: Attalid kingdom
properties.description: Founded by Philetaerus, who took command of Pergamum in 282 BCE, and declared independent by Attalus I in the 230's BCE, the Attalid kingdom was allied closely to Rome; the kingdom expanded after the Peace of Apamea in 188 BCE. The last king, Attalus III, willed the kingdom to Rome, and after his death in 133, the former kingdom formed the core of the Roman province of Asia.

properties.title: tribus Maecia
properties.description: Tribus Maecia (originally Maicia) was a later rural tribe of ancient Rome, established in 332 B.C.

properties.description: The site of a palatial Roman villa dating to the first and second centuries A.D. Discovered in 1841, the site is noted for its extensive in situ mosaic pavements.

properties.title: Liestal
properties.description: A Roman villa located some 1.2 km NW of Liestal, in the territory of Augusta Raurica. The villa dates to the middle of the first century A.D. and was sacked ca. A.D. 259.

properties.title: Gallaberry Camp
properties.description: A Roman temporary marching camp that was identified via cropmarks in June 1939. The camp covered 1.33 acres and measured 64 x 110 meters.

properties.title: Agios Elias Doric temple
properties.description: The Doric temple at Agios Elias, above Asea in Arcadia, dates to ca. 500 B.C.

properties.title: Marcellinus and Peter
properties.description: An ancient Christian catacomb located at the third milestone of the Via Labicana. The name refers to two Christian martyrs.

properties.title: London Mithraeum
properties.description: A temple sacred to Mithras in Londinium that was discovered in 1954. The visible remains of the temple do not sit on the original site, but have been reassembled at Temple Court, Queen Victoria Street, London.

properties.title: Ponte di Pratolungo
properties.description: Remains of a Roman Republican bridge crossing the Fosso di Pratolungo along the line of the via Tiburtina.

properties.title: Grutenhäuschen
properties.description: The Grutenhäuschen is a Roman funereal temple of the third or fourth century A.D. It has been reconstructed on site.

properties.title: Tall Bazi
properties.description: Archaeological site on the eastern bank of the Euphrates in northern Syria. The site contains a town dated to the Early Bronze Age III-IVA (mid-3rd millennium BCE), as well as a Roman sanctuary used only briefly from about the late 1st-late 2nd century CE. The western part of the site was flooded by the construction of the Tischrin Dam in 1999. Tall Bazi and the nearby site of Banat have been tentatively identified as the city of Armi/Armium mentioned in texts from Ebla.

properties.title: Artulu
properties.description: A city in Tabal mentioned in royal inscriptions of the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III (r. 858-824 BC).

properties.title: Necropolis of Madonna d'olivo
properties.description: An Etruscan necropolis located about 2 km south-west of Tuscania that overlooks valley of the Marta river. The necropolis takes its name from the adjacent Church of the Madonna dell’Olivo.

properties.title: Tell Agrab
properties.description: Tell Agrab, or Ajrab, is a medium-sized archaeological mound in the Diyala Province of central Iraq, some forty kilometers east of Baghdad. The site was excavated by archaeologists from the Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago in 1936 and 1937. Tell Agrab seems to have been inhabited from the early 3rd millennium BCE until the beginning of the Old Babylonian Period (ca. 1800 BCE). In its early history, the site held a temple possibly dedicated to the god Šara.

properties.title: Arch of Alexander Severus
properties.description: The Arch of Alexander Severus at Thugga was built in 228.

properties.title: Monte Gentili
properties.description: A villa associated with Aulus Vitellius Germanicus.

properties.title: Theater at Sybaris/Thurii/Copia
properties.description: The Roman Theater at Sybaris/Thurii/Copia dates originally to the Augustan period.
