properties.title: Ring of Brodgar
properties.description: The Ring of Brodgar (also known as Brogar, or the Ring o' Brodgar) is a Neolithic henge and stone circle monument in Orkney, Scotland.

properties.title: Via Aurelia
properties.description: An ancient Roman road begun ca. 241 B.C. by the censor C. Aurelius Cotta.

properties.title: Welzheim: Ostkastell
properties.description: One of two Roman forts located at modern Welzheim in Germany, the excavated remains of the "Ostkastell" are largely preserved. The west gate and a portion of the associated defensive wall was reconstructed in the 1970s.

properties.title: Basilica Julia
properties.description: The Basilica Julia was built on the south side of the Forum Romanum in 46 B.C. on the site of the former Basilica Sempronia.

properties.title: Puig de Sa Morisca
properties.description: A first millennium B.C., pre-Roman settlement of Majorca.

properties.title: Sapperton and Cirencester amphitheatre
properties.description: The Cirencester amphitheater is the second largest known in Britannia. Its earthworks supported tiered seats that could accommodate about 8,000 spectators. The amphitheater was converted to a fortified site in the fifth century during the Saxon invasions.

properties.title: Vapheio Tholos Tomb
properties.description: The Vapheio Tholos Tomb is a Mycenaean tholos built around 1500 BC that is assumed to have held an elite burial or burials. It is best known for the two golden Minoan-style cups it housed.

properties.title: Pazarlı Höyük
properties.description: Settlement located about 30 km. from Alaca Höyük in modern Turkey's Çorum province. The site contains structures dated to the Neolithic, Hittite, and Phrygian periods.

properties.title: Ninurta-mukīn-temmēn-ālišu-ana-labār-ūmē-rūqūti
properties.description: The Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) surrounded his new capital Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") with a rectangular-shaped, 16,280-cubit-long inner and outer city wall. The name of the outer/lower city wall (šalḫû) was Ninurta-mukīn-temmēn-ālišu-ana-labār-ūmē-rūqūti ("The God Ninurta Is the One Who Establishes the Foundation of His City for (All) Days to Come") according to some Akkadian royal inscriptions, but Ninurta-mukīn-temmēn-adušši-ana-labār-ūmē-rūqūti ("The God Ninurta Is the One Who Establishes the Foundation of the Wall for (All) Days to Come") according to other texts written in the name of Sargon II.

properties.title: Via Olevano Romano columbarium
properties.description: A late republican to early imperial columbarium along the Via Praenestina. The columbarium is of rectangular plan and was last used during the early Flavian period.

properties.title: Prato Rosello necropolis
properties.description: An Etruscan necropolis with a number of tumulus-type tombs dating between the eighth and sixth centuries BC.

properties.title: Eduranna
properties.description: The ziggurat of the god Šamaš at Larsa. The Sumerian ceremonial name Eduranna means "House, Bond of Heaven."

properties.title: Castro de São Lourenço

properties.title: Masseria De Carolis
properties.description: A Roman villa with an associated bath complex destroyed by the AD 79 eruption of Vesuvius, the Masseria De Carolis site is located in the comune of Pollena Trocchia near Naples, Italy.

properties.title: Street of Facades, Petra
properties.description: The so-called "Street of Facades" is a necropolis that is lined with tall, rock-cut tombs that have elaborate facades.

properties.title: Enamtila
properties.description: The temple of the god Bēl-mātāti (Enlil), Enamtila (“House of Life”), was located in the Kumar district of Babylon, in the western half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of seven temples in that part of Babylon. Enamtila is mentioned in Old Babylonian and Kassite Period texts.

properties.title: Osteria del Gladiatore
properties.description: A Roman tavern in Pompeii.

properties.title: Library of Pergamum

properties.title: Anazarbos city wall
properties.description: The Anazarbos city wall visible today was built in the 10th century of the current era.

properties.title: Sarissa

properties.title: Church of St. Etchmiadzin at Soradir

properties.title: via Taranto columbaria
properties.description: Two Roman columbaria are located under the present via Pescara, 2. This accounts for the tomb being referred to interchangeably with two modern, street-derived toponyms, namely "via Taranto" and "via Pescara". These tombs are situated near the ancient crossroads of the via Latina and the via Labicana.

properties.title: Munychia

properties.title: Frascole, S. Martino a Poggio

properties.title: Yeşilova Höyük
properties.description: A prehistoric settlement in Bornova, Turkey, that represents the earliest known settlement in the area of İzmir. The site was occupied ca. 6500 to 4000 B.C.

properties.title: Palace of Mausolos at Bodrum
properties.description: The fortified Palace of Mausolos at Bodrum.

properties.title: Eʾesirkalama

According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of seven temples in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Carmine Roman tomb

properties.title: Regio IV, Ostia Antica

properties.title: Regio III, Ostia Antica

properties.title: Casa dei Crescenzi

properties.title: Madonna del Parto

properties.title: Dur-Bel-Harran-belu-uṣur

properties.title: Solucar Albayda
properties.description: A Spanish village located to the west of Sevilla, Spain. In the thirteenth century, it belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. The modern toponym is a derivation of the Arabic toponym "Solucar Al-bayda", meaning "the white one". The site was known as Sanlúcar de Albaida until it took the definitive name of Albaida de Aljarafe.

properties.title: Monte Aguzzo tumulus
properties.description: Monte Aguzzo di Formello (Rome), the site of a tumulus along the road leading for Veii to the Ager Faliscus.

properties.title: Ponte Funicchio
properties.description: A Roman bridge dating to the late second century B.C.

properties.title: Sha'ar Hagolan
properties.description: A Neolithic settlement of the Yarmukian culture, located on the northwestern bank of the Yarmuk River approximately 1.5 km south of the Sea of Galilee. At 20 hectares, it is one of the largest known Neolithic settlements in the Near East.

properties.title: Thracian Tomb of Sveshtari
properties.description: A third century B.C. Thracian tomb discovered in 1982 and inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.

properties.title: Tall-e Bakun
properties.description: Prehistoric archaeological site located 3 km south of Persepolis. The site consists of two mounds (Tall-e Bakun A and B).

properties.title: Beni Hasan
properties.description: A Middle Kingdom cemetery known for its rock-cut tombs of local officials.

properties.title: Baptistery of Butrint
properties.description: The Baptistery of Butrint is a round structure, with a diameter of 14.5 meters. It was built in the sixth century A.D. and was excavated in May 1928 by Luigi Maria Ugolini.

properties.title: Church of Saint Demetrius
properties.description: A seventh century AD church dedicated to the patron saint of Thessalonica; the present basilica stands on the site of a precursor with phases beginning in the fourth century AD.

properties.title: Catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa
properties.description: The Catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa contain Roman period tombs, second to fourth centuries A.D.

properties.title: Stadium at Laodicea ad Lycum
properties.description: The ancient Stadium at Laodicea ad Lycum dates initially to the later first century A.D.

properties.title: Roman theater at Aizanoi
properties.description: The Roman theater at Aizanoi is part of a theater-stadium complex. The complex is built after A.D. 160 with the patronage of one M. Apuleius Eurycles.

properties.title: Temple to Nefertari at Abu Simbel
properties.description: The smaller of the two temples at Abu Simbel, dedicated to the goddess Hathor and the deified queen Nefertari. The temple was relocated between 1964 and 1968 to prevent its submersion under Lake Nasser after the construction of the Aswan High Dam.

properties.title: Uchkakar
properties.description: Fortified settlement on the banks of the Cheptsa River, inhabited from the 9th-13th centuries CE and associated with the Cheptsa culture

properties.title: Tell el-Farkha
properties.description: Settlement near the village of Ghazalah in the eastern Nile Delta inhabited from the Naqada II through the Old Kingdom period.

properties.title: Emeurur
properties.description: The temple of the goddess Nanāya, Emeurur (“House which Gathers the Me’s”), was located in the TE.E (read as either Tê or Kisīri) district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was the only temple in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Eurunanam
properties.description: The temple of the god Nabû, Eurunanam (“House, the Very City”), was located in the New City district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was the only dais in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Akripos
properties.description: An ancient settlement whose precise location can not be determined today

properties.title: Ianus Augustus
properties.description: The remains of a Roman arch may mark the boundary between the Roman provinces of Hispania Baetica and Hispania Tarraconensis.

properties.title: Etemenanki
properties.description: The ziggurat of the god Marduk at Babylon. The Sumerian ceremonial name Etemenanki means "House, Foundation Platform of Heaven and Underworld."

properties.title: Baths of Faverges
properties.description: The Roman Baths of Faverges date to the first century.

properties.title: Villa of Diomedes
properties.description: A suburban villa of Pompeii located outside the Herculaneum gate, the Villa of Diomedes was excavated between 1771 and 1774 and named after the tomb of Marcus Arrius Diomedes which faces the entrance on the opposite side of the road.

properties.title: Strophades/Plotai (island group)
properties.description: The modern Strophades/Strofades islands (Stamfani and Arpi): an Ionian island group mentioned in Vergil and other ancient sources.

properties.title: Tomen y mur
properties.description: The Roman fort at modern day Tomen y Mur, presumably Flavian in date, was likely abandoned by the middle of the second century A.D.

properties.title: Mausoleum of Lucius Sempronius Atratinus
properties.description: A first-century B.C. circular funerary monument at Gaeta.

properties.title: Afyonkarahisar Castle
properties.description: Afyonkarahisar Castle is a Late Bronze Age fort (ca. 1350 B.C.) and may be the site of the Hittite settlement known as Hapanuwa.

properties.title: Ruborough Camp
properties.description: Ruborough Camp is a triangular-shaped promontory fort, comprised of double bank with a medial ditch.

properties.title: Tyrrhenum/Inferum Mare
properties.description: The Tyrrhenian Sea is part of the Mediterranean Sea off the western coast of Italy. It takes its name from the Tyrrhenian people, another name for the Etruscans.

properties.title: Ustica (island)
properties.description: An island in the Tyrrhenian Sea occupied since the middle of the second millennium B.C. when Phoenician traders were present there.

properties.title: Syria

properties.title: Thessalia
properties.description: Thessalia (Thessaly) was a region of ancient Greece.

properties.title: Es Trepucó
properties.description: Es Trepucó, Minorca, is the site of a Talaiotic village that dates from 1500 to 1300 BC.

properties.title: Roman theater at Falerii
properties.description: The Roman theater at Falerii was excavated in 1829.

properties.title: Vosgepag
properties.description: Vosgepag was the Armenian name for a small village near Van in eastern Turkey (now officially called Beşçatak in Turkish). In its church, a reused building inscription of the Urartian king Minua (9th / 8th century BCE) was found.

properties.title: Temple of Artemis Orthia
properties.description: An Archaic temple dedicated to Artemis Orthia within the sanctuary of this goddess at Sparta. The site contained rich deposits of votives and masks.

properties.title: Tell Hassuna
properties.description: Tell Hassuna is a settlement of northern Iraq, located in the Nineveh Province approximately 35km south-west of Nineveh. This is the type site for the Hassuna culture of the early sixth millennium B.C.

properties.title: Gallo-Roman amphitheater at Grannum
properties.description: The Gallo-Roman amphitheater at Grannum dates to the late first century B.C.

properties.title: Enamhe
properties.description: The temple of the god Adad, Enamhe (“House of Plenty”), was located in the Kumar district of Babylon, in the western half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of seven temples in that part of Babylon. Enamhe was (re)built by the the Old Babylonian kings Sūmû-lā-El (r. ca. 1881–1845 BC) and Hammu-rāpi (r. ca. 1792–1750 BC) and the Neo-Babylonian ruler Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–562 BC).

properties.title: Eʾešmah
properties.description: The temple of the god Ea, Eʾešmah (“Exalted House”), was located in the Kumar district of Babylon, in the western half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of seven temples in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Step Gate of the Armory
properties.description: Nineveh's western wall had seven (or eight) gates: the Armory Gate (later Step Gate of the Armory) was the fifth gate from the northern city wall. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial names Pāqidat-kalāma ("The One Who Regulates Everything") and Lū-dāri-bānûša ("May Its Builder Live Forever").

properties.title: Quay Gate
properties.description: Nineveh's western wall had seven (or eight) gates: the Quay Gate was the fourth gate from the northern city wall. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Mušēribat-miširti-dadmē, which means "The One Who Brings in Income from the Settlements."

properties.title: Tomb of Menidi
properties.description: A Mycenaean tholos tomb first discovered in 1872. It is one of four such tholoi known in Attica.

properties.title: Bouleuterion at Aspendos
properties.description: The Bouleuterion at Aspendos dates to the early second century.

properties.title: Faroe Islands
properties.description: An archipelago made up of 18 islands situated between the Norwegian Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean.

properties.title: Roman forum at Cupra Maritima
properties.description: The Roman forum at Cupra Maritima.

properties.title: Via Francigena
properties.description: The Via Francigena is a Medieval pilgrimage route connecting Canterbury, England, and Rome.

properties.title: Seyitömer Höyük
properties.description: Settlement in west-central Anatolia inhabited in the Early-Middle Bronze Age (3000-1700 BCE) and again during the Achaemind and Roman periods (500 BCE-395 CE).

properties.title: Quartucciu
properties.description: The archaeological site of Pill'è Matta preserves remains of a Punic-Roman necropolis in use from the fourth century B.C. until the fifth century A.D.

properties.title: Amphitheatre of El Jem
properties.description: Third century A.D. Roman amphitheater; declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979.

properties.title: Cappadocia Gate at Kerkenes
properties.description: Gate on the southeastern side of the large fortified Iron Age site at Kerkenes (ancient Pteria).

properties.title: Pedroches Roman Bridge
properties.description: A Roman bridge over the arroyo Pedroches near Corduba, Spain. The bridge lies along the ancient road to Augusta Emerita.

properties.title: Los Toscanos
properties.description: A Punic settlement in Iberia.

properties.title: Corinth Canal
properties.description: The Corinth Canal cuts across the Isthmus of Corinth, connecting the Gulf of Corinth to the Saronic Gulf and the Aegean Sea. Several abortive attempts in antiquity were made at creating the canal, although its final (and functional) realization occurred in modernity.

properties.title: Credenhill Camp
properties.description: Site of a bi-vallate Iron Age hill fort in present-day Herefordshire.

properties.title: Mausoleum of Lucius Pomponius Grecinus
properties.description: A Roman funerary monument of the first century B.C. that is traditionally associated with the prefect Lucius Pomponius Grecinus.

properties.description: Diqdiqah is a small satellite of the ancient city of Ur in the present-day Dhi Qar province of southern Iraq ca. 20 kilometres southwest of Nasiriyah. properties.title: Castel Malnome (Ponte Galeria)
properties.description: An imperial necropolis with at least 326 tombs was identified at modern Castel Malnome (Ponte Galeria) in Italy. Archaeological evidence marks these as burials belonging to working-class people of the Roman imperial period, with most graves having either no grave goods or very few. The osteoarchaeological analysis led excavators to speculate that the individuals buried here many have worked in the salt flats.

properties.title: Ešiddukišara
properties.description: The temple of the god Nabû, Ešiddukišara (“House of the Director of the Universe”), was located in the Tuba district of Babylon, in the western half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of three temples in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Lepcis Magna
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Lepcis Magna dates to the first century A.D. and was dedicated to Nero.

properties.title: Camp celtique de la Bure
properties.description: A Gallo-Roman settlement of a commercial nature located on the Meurthe river. Archaeological evidence for earthworks, as well as ritual activity, has been discovered. The Gallo-Roman ramparts, in a later phase, make use of marble sculpture as spolia.

properties.title: Zitānu
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources; the modern site is Zaytān.

properties.title: Lago di Castiglione

properties.title: Roman theater at Italica

properties.title: Basilica Manastirine
properties.description: An important extra-mural Christian site at Solina. The site includes the basilica and the cemetery of Manastirine, associated with a Christian martyr.

AD 450 ) is the presumed, likely patron of the building, though she is very unlikely to have been entombed within one of three sarcophagi found inside.

properties.title: Fox-Amphoux
properties.description: At Fox-Amphoux the remains of a Roman villa were discovered, adjacent to those of a sanctuary ad fines that may have been dedicated to the Capitoline triad. The site was in use from the time of Augustus until the third century AD.

properties.title: Alb(i)um Intimilium/Albintimilium
properties.description: Alb(i)um Intimilium/Albintimilium (modern Ventimiglia) was the main settlement of the Ligurian tribe of the Intemelii. In the 2nd century BC it came under control of the Roman Republic. Albintimilium became a municipium in 89 BC in the tribus Falerna. In the same period the city walls were built, with several towers. The city flourished in the early Imperial period, with baths, an acqueduct and a theater. In the 6th and early 7th century it was a Byzantine kastron, coming under control of the Longobards in 641. During the 7th and 8th century the Roman city was slowly abandoned in favour of a smaller hilltop settlement focused around the Cathedral.

properties.title: Antipolis
properties.description: Antipolis (modern Antibes) was founded as a colony from Massilia in the fifth century BC and it emerged as a key trading center. In the late first century BC the city was incorporated into the Roman province of Gallia Narbonensis.

properties.title: Alconis
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 B3 Alconis

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Tusculum
properties.description: Today the Roman amphitheater at Tusculum is poorly preserved. These ruins have never been systematically investigated.

properties.title: Agora of Halaesa
properties.description: The agora of the ancient city of Halaesa (second century B.C.), now within the archaeological area of Alesa Arconidea, Sicily.

properties.title: Aşağı Pınar
properties.description: A Neolithic site in Eastern Thrace near the town of Kırklareli.

properties.title: Bethania
properties.description: A village located near Jerusalem, at the Mount of Olives.

properties.title: Sakarya-Ebene
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Äußerer Westtaurus
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Zominthos
properties.description: A Minoan settlement dating from ca. 1800 BC onwards, Zominthos is well known for a large Minoan building discovered in 1982.

properties.title: Nestor's Palace
properties.description: A Mycenaean palace complex excavated by the American School of Classical Studies, linked with the Homeric Pylos of Nestor.

properties.title: Castrum Caetani
properties.description: A Medieval fortification that incorporates and repurposes the Roman mausoleum of Caecilia Metella.

properties.title: City Wall of Dura-Europos
properties.description: The fortified wall encircling the city of Dura-Europos built primarily of locally-quarried ashlar limestone blocks. Built ca. 150 BCE, the walls were breached in 256 CE and went out of use thereafter.

properties.title: Desert Gate
properties.description: Nineveh's western wall had seven (or eight) gates: the Desert Gate was the southernmost gate along that stretch of wall. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it sometime between 695 and 691 B.C. and he gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Kadrê-Tēme-u-Sumuʾel-qerebša-irrub ("The Presents of the People of Tēma and Sumuʾel Enter Through It").

properties.title: Barhalzi Gate
properties.description: Nineveh's western wall had seven (or eight) gates: the Barhalzi Gate was the sixth gate from the northern city wall. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it sometime between 694 and 691 B.C. and gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Anum-nāṣir-napištīya, which means "The God Anu Is the Protector of My Life."

properties.title: Roman aqueduct, Spello
properties.description: An aqueduct carrying water to Spello from the hills below Collepino.

properties.title: Temple of Maharraqa
properties.description: A temple sacred to Isis and Osiris of Roman date, relocated before the completion of the Aswan dam in the 1960s.

properties.title: Porta Nigra
properties.description: The so-called "Porta Nigra" is a surviving Roman city gate that dates to ca. A.D. 186-200. It was enlisted as part of the "Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St. Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier" UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

properties.title: Necropolis of Ponte Messato
properties.description: A pre-Roman and Roman period necropolis on the outskirts of Teramo.

properties.title: Villa of the Frescoes
properties.description: Referred to both as the House and the Villa of the frescoes, this seaside Roman domestic complex with a peristyle garden covered more than 1,000 square feet and dates to the second century A.D.

properties.title: Caztalliella
properties.description: Now modern Cazalilla, Caztalliella was a Spanish village located in the north of the province of Jaén that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X.

properties.title: Roman theater at Iuvanum
properties.description: The Roman theater at Iuvanum is located at the foot of the acropolis.

properties.title: Villa urbana
properties.description: A Roman villa that has now been reconstructed.

properties.title: Ponte Sereno
properties.description: A bridge near Ferentinum (modern Ferentino in Italy) that is traditionally dated to A.D. 260 or after. A substructure in polygonal masonry supports the bridge.

properties.title: Tomb of the Kings near Enkomi
properties.description: Royal tombs of the Middle Bronze Age located near Enkomi.

properties.title: Circus Flaminius
properties.description: Located in the southern Campus Martius, the Circus Flaminius is a large area built by C. Flaminius Nepos in 221 B.C. Various games, including the ludi plebeii, ludi Taurii, ludi saeculares, were celebrated here. The circus was also a place of popular assembly.

properties.title: Acropolis of Aletrium
properties.description: The Acropolis of Aletrium, often referred to as the "Civita", is the fortified citadel of the ancient city. Surrounded by polygonal walls, it is accessed via two gates.

properties.title: Roman theater at Carthage
properties.description: The Roman theater at Carthage was built around the middle of the second century A.D. It was re-discovered in 1904.

properties.title: Aqueduct supplying Alb(i)um Intimilium
properties.description: Ancient name, if any, unknown (BAtlas 16 E2 unnamed aqueduct at Alb(i)um Intimilium)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 unnamed aqueduct (Cemenelum)

properties.title: Unnamed aqueducts
properties.description: unnamed aqueduct group (Antipolis)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C3 unnamed aqueduct (Col. Forum Iulii)

properties.title: Cangas de Onís
properties.description: A Medieval bridge built by Alfonso XI of Castile and León that possibly rests on earlier Roman foundations.

properties.title: Pyramid of Sekhemkhet
properties.description: The Pyramid of Sekhemkhet, also known as "The Buried Pyramid", is an unfinished step pyramid at Saqqara that was begun ca. 2645 B.C. for Sekhemkhet Djoserty.

properties.title: Ugal-amaru
properties.description: According to an inscription of the Neo-Babylonian king Nabonidus, the name of the wall of Cutha was Ugal-amaru, whose ceremonial name means "Great Storm, (which is) a Deluge."

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at *Moridunum
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Moridunum is located in Carmarthenshire. It is one of only seven surviving Roman amphitheaters in Britain.

properties.title: Clivus Capitolinus
properties.description: The principal road leading to the Capitolium and the Arx in the city of Rome.

properties.title: Ištar Gate
properties.description: The Ištar Gate, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Ištar-mušammeḫat-nišīšu ("The Goddess Ištar Is the One Who Makes Its People Flourish"), is the sixth of the eight city gates of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") listed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in inscriptions recording the construction of his new capital. This gate is the second of the west-facing entrances to the city, but its precise location is uncertain.

properties.title: Bergantino nymphaeum
properties.description: A nymphaeum on the shores of the Alban Lake that is located in a natural grotto that is assigned to the Flavian period and associated with the complex of the Villa of Domitian.

properties.title: Mura dell Arce
properties.description: The so-called "Mura dell Arce" of Vetulonia served as the sixth- and fifth-century B.C. fortifications of Etruscan Vetulonia. These are massive walls built in megalithic technique using limestone.

properties.title: Belvedere tomb
properties.description: An Etruscan tomb of the seventh century B.C.

properties.title: Templum Pacis
properties.description: The Temple of Peace in Rome was vowed by Vespasian following the Jewish War.

properties.title: Pollina
properties.description: Modern town in Sicily, near Cefalù, that has been associated with the ancient settlement of Apollonia.

properties.title: Tamuli
properties.description: A Middle Bronze Age nuragic complex near Macomer, Sardinia.

properties.title: Marsicovetere Roman villa
properties.description: A Roman villa rustica belonging to the senatorial family of the Bruttii Praesentes that has been connected with Bruttia Crispina, the wife of Commodus. The villa was inhabited from the second century B.C. to the seventh century A.D. The villa's archaeological remains are found in the locality of Barricelle in the territory of the community of Marsicovetere in the province of Potenza.

properties.title: Tang-i Var Rock Relief
properties.description: The Tang-i Var rock relief of the eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) is carved on a rack face of the Kūh-e Zīnāneh in the Tang-i Var pass in Iranian Kurdistan, about 50 km southwest of Sanandaj and 85 km northwest of Kermanshah. This difficult-to-reach relief was carved in a niche cut into the cliff face about 40 m above ground level. The Akkadian inscription, now badly weathered, records several of Sargon II’s campaigns, especially the military expeditions against the land Karalla, against which the Assyrian army campaigned in 716, 713, and 706 BC.

properties.title: Roman villa at West Mersea
properties.description: Remains of a tessellated floor pavement likely indicate the presence of a villa.

properties.title: House of the Thunderbolt
properties.description: A Vespasianic domus in Ostia Antica, built c. 70-75 CE, situated outside Porta Marina, and north of the continuation of the Decumanus Maximus. It had a slightly concave façade, comprising six shops and an entrance corridor leading to an interior peristyle garden.

properties.title: Palaiokastro
properties.description: Settlement/fortress descibed by Stählin (1924, 224-225); Béquignon (1937, 322-324; Fig. 16).

properties.title: Asia Minor
properties.description: An ancient region, coincident with a peninsula of the continent of Asia. It is bounded on the south by the Mediterranean Sea, on the west by the Aegean Sea, and on the north by the Black Sea. Today it is part of the territory of the modern country of Turkey.

properties.title: Atlas Mon(te)s
properties.description: A major mountain range, located in northwest Africa (primarily modern Morocco).

properties.title: Atlanticus Oceanus
properties.description: Atlanticus Oceanus (The Atlantic Ocean) likely derives its name from Atlas, one of the Titans of Greek mythology. The Atlantic Ocean covers ca. 20% of the surface of the Earth.

properties.title: Baetica
properties.description: Hispania Baetica was a Roman senatorial province that beings with the Augustan restructuring of the provinces in 27 B.C. The provine was bounded by the Anas river in the west and the Sierra Morena mountains to the north.

properties.title: Ap(p)enninus M.
properties.description: The Apennine Mountains extend ca. 1,200 km (750 miles) along the length of peninsular Italy.

properties.title: Basilica di Santa Sinforosa
properties.description: A minor Paleochristian basilica located in Guidonia Montecelio that was dedicated to the patron saint of Tivoli.

properties.title: Odeon at Hadrian's Villa
properties.description: The Odeon at Hadrian's Villa is also referred to as the South Theater. It is located at the southern end of the Villa Adriana.

properties.title: Tuba
properties.description: According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon, Tuba was one of the four city districts of the western half of the inner city of Babylon and it contained three temples.

properties.title: Zamahu
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources that is identified with modern Tell ar-Rimāḥ.

properties.title: Catacombs of Praetextatus
properties.description: A vast Roman catacomb along the Via Appia that began to be used at the close of the second century A.D.

properties.title: Aballava
properties.description: Roman fort, cited: BAtlas 9 D6 Aballava

properties.title: ‘Abraouannos’? (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 9 C6 ‘Abraouannos’? fl.

properties.title: (A)Esica
properties.description: (A)Esica, also known as Great Chesters, was a fort on the line of Hadrian's Wall.

properties.title: Alauna
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 9 F5 Alauna

properties.title: Alauna
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 9 D4 Alauna

properties.title: Alauna/Alione
properties.description: A Roman fort at present-day Maryport. Part of Cumbrian coastal defenses.

properties.title: Dolciano
properties.description: Dolciano is located in the environs of Chiusi and abundant evidence of Etruscan necropoleis has been documented there.

properties.title: Ermita de la Virgen del Pilar Dam
properties.description: An early Imperial Roman dam located in Teruel province, Aragon, Spain.

properties.title: Horomos
properties.description: Armenian monastery constructed in the 10th century CE.

properties.title: Thermes de Cluny
properties.description: A Gallo-Roman bath complex of the third century CE at Lutetia (modern Paris).

properties.title: Karbalāʾ
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Khosr River
properties.description: The Khosr River was a tributary of the Tigris River that ran directly through the center of the Assyrian city Nineveh. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib reinforced its banks with large stone blocks to prevent it from flooding or damaging the citadel wall.

properties.title: Royal Road of Nineveh
properties.description: As part of transformation of Nineveh’s lower town at the beginning of the 7th century B.C., the Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib created a broad royal road that ran all the way through the city. That fifty-two-cubit-wide road, whose ancient ceremonial name is not known, is still unlocated, but it is generally thought to have run north from the Aššur Gate, east past the armory and the citadel, to the Sîn Gate (formerly the Gate of the Gardens).

properties.title: Cogulló
properties.description: A Pre-Roman Iberian oppidum located in the region of Bages.

properties.title: Castro da Cola
properties.description: A Bronze and Iron Age oppidum.

properties.title: Public administration buildings
properties.description: The administration buildings on Pompeii's forum were built before 80 B.C. and renovated following the earthquake of A.D. 62. The central building is generally regarded as the tabularium.

properties.title: Arderikka
properties.description: A now unlocated site in Assyria located on the Euphrates river upstream from Babylon.

properties.title: Gyndes (river)
properties.description: The Gyndes was a river of Assyria and Susiana that is discussed by Herodotus. Its precise location can not be determined with certainty, but some scholars have identified it with the modern Diyala river in Iraq.

properties.title: Listercombe Bottom
properties.description: The site of a Roman villa discovered ca. 1760 and excavated in 1930. It lies ca. 2.5 km SE of Chedworth Roman villa.

properties.title: Achaiachala
properties.description: A fortified island in (or fort alongside) the Euphrates mentioned by Ammianus. Possibly to be identified with the modern island of Bidjan or the city of Haditha in Iraq.

properties.title: Temple of Zeus Trossou
properties.description: An epigraphically attested temple at or near ancient Atyochorion (modern Akkent in Turkey).

properties.title: Tiona/Titana
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 91 unlocated Tiona/Titana fl.

properties.title: King's Gate
properties.description: The King's Gate is one of Babylon's eight city gates and it is situated on the western side of the inner city, directly west of the nu-x-ù quarter. King Nebuchadnezzar II built the gate ca. 575 B.C.

properties.title: Gula temple (Kalhu)
properties.description: When Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud) became the principal administrative center of the Assyrian Empire in the ninth century BC, king Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) built (or rebuilt) numerous temples. One of those was dedicated to the goddess Gula. Although its location is not known, the Gula temple at Kalhu is thought to have been part of the Ninurta temple complex (in the northwest corner of the citadel), east of the Šarrat-niphi temple and north of the Kidmuri temple.

properties.title: Nēmed-Enlil
properties.description: The outer wall of Babylon was called by the ceremonial Akkadian name Nēmed-Enlil/ Nēmetti-Enlil, which means "Bulwark of the God Enlil." According to the text Tintir = Babylon, Nēmed-Enlil (and the inner wall Imgur-Enlil) had eight city gates, four on the eastern side of the Euphrates and four on the western side of the river. The Assyrian kings Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal and the Babylonian kings Nabopolassar, Nebuchadnezzar II, and Nebonidus all undertook construction on Babylon’s outer wall.

properties.title: Imgur-Marduk
properties.description: The city wall of Nippur according to the so-called "Kuyunjik Ziqqurrat List" (7th century B.C.). Its Akkadian ceremonial name means "The God Marduk Showed Favor."

properties.title: Uvecik Tepe
properties.description: Uvecik Tepe or Üvecik Tepe is a tumulus in the Troad built for one Festus, a freedman of the emperor Caracalla.

properties.title: Tuvixeddu Punic necropolis
properties.description: A Punic necropolis near Caralis in Sardinia.

properties.title: Lucretilis Mons
properties.description: A mountain in the ager Sabinus.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 91 F5 unnamed wall (around Babylon)

properties.title: Wall of Media
properties.description: The Wall of Media, also known as Mēdías teîchos or the Wall of Semiramis, at Habl as-Sahr is mentioned by Xenophon in the Anabasis as a defensive ditch at the Euphrates built on the orders of Artaxerxes in the fifth century BC.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 91 E4 unnamed wall (Umm Rus)

properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 91 D3 unnamed wall (Sur Umm al-Khawashij)

properties.title: Luxmanda archaeological site
properties.description: A large settlement in Tanzania dating to the Pastoral Neolithic period in eastern Africa.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 91 A2 unnamed dam (at Zenobia)

properties.title: Croy Hill
properties.description: The site of a Roman fort and fortlet on the Antonine Wall.

properties.title: Watercrook Roman Fort and Settlement
properties.description: The Roman Fort near Watercrook Farm (at Kendal in northwest England) was originally built ca. AD 90 and rebuilt ca. AD 130. It may have been called Alone?/Alauna? in antiquity. Its poorly preserved remains are coincident with those of a contemporaneous civilian settlement.

properties.title: Bearsden
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 9 C5 Bearsden

properties.title: Cataractonium
properties.description: The remains of a Roman fort and settlement located at Catterick, North Yorkshire.

properties.title: Castlecary
properties.description: Site of Roman fort on Antonine Wall.

properties.title: Habitancum
properties.description: A Roman fort at present-day Risingham.

properties.title: Eburacum
properties.description: The site of a Roman legionary fortress, municipium, and colonia at modern-day York, England.

properties.title: Botis Ins.
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 9 B5 Botis Ins.

properties.title: Brav(o)niacum

properties.title: Cargill
properties.description: The remains of a Roman fort and its annex located on the left bank of the River Isla. The site was first identified by Eric Bradley in 1941 and again re-confirmed in 1977.

properties.title: Bodotria (river)

properties.title: Corda?

properties.title: Castra Exploratorum

properties.title: Crawford
properties.description: Site of a small Roman fort between Castledykes and Tassiesholm. The fort was discovered in 1938 and excavated in 1961-66.

properties.title: Balmuildy Roman Fort
properties.description: Balmuildy was the site of a Roman fort on the Antonine Wall in Scotland. This is one of only two Antonine Wall forts found to have stone ramparts.

properties.title: Caledonia (region)
properties.description: Caledonia was the northern part of Britannia.

properties.title: Derventio
properties.description: A Roman fort at present-day Papcastle, cited: BAtlas 9 D6 Derventio

properties.title: Easter Happrew Roman Fort
properties.description: A Roman fort, likely constructed and later abandoned during the first century CE, possibly with an associated mansio. Easter Happrew is located in the modern parish of Stobo in Scotland. It may correspond to Karbantorigon, which is listed by Ptolemy.

properties.title: Bremenium
properties.description: A Roman fort at present-day High Rochester.

properties.title: Cramond
properties.description: Site of Roman fort occupied during the Antonine period, located 4.5 miles NNW of Castle Rock, Edinburgh.

properties.title: Arbeia
properties.description: A Roman fort at present-day South Shields.

properties.title: Bannatia?
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 9 D4 Bannatia?

properties.title: Clota (river)
properties.description: The River Clyde, the eighth-longest river in the United Kingdom, flows into the Firth of Clyde.

properties.title: Dounon Kolpos
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 9 F6 Dounon Kolpos

properties.title: *Brocolitia

properties.title: Nimrud
properties.description: In the ninth century BC, Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883-859 BC) built himself a new administrative center. Kalhu (biblical Calah) — modern Nimrud, a site identified as Larissa, a city mentioned in Xenophon’s Anabasis — became the capital of the Assyrian Empire, replacing Ashur, which had served as Assyria’s capital since the third millennium BC. The city — which is located twenty miles south of the modern Mosul and which occupied a strategic position six miles north of the point where the Tigris River meets the Greater/Upper Zab — served as Assyria’s capital until the reign of Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC). Although Kalhu never again became the primary residence of Assyria’s kings, that city remained a vital administrative, military, and religious center until the fall of the Assyrian Empire.

properties.title: Nineveh/Ninos
properties.description: This important Mesopotamian city flanks the eastern edge of the Tigris flood plain, opposite modern Mosul, of which it is now a suburb. From the third millennium B.C. onwards, Nineveh was the most important religious center of the goddess Ištar in the area that would become the Assyrian heartland. Starting in the Middle Assyrian period, the city came under the authority of the kings of Assyria, who often sponsored large-scale building activities there. However, it was not until 704 B.C. that Nineveh became the administrative capital of Assyria, when the Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib moved the royal family and court there and transformed the city into a thriving imperial metropolis. Nineveh remained Assyria’s capital until 612 B.C., when it was captured and destroyed by a Babylonian-Median collation led by Nabopolassar and Cyaxares. The visible remains of the (7th-century) Assyrian city include the citadel mound Kuyunjik, the smaller mound of Nebi Yunus, and the twelve-kilometer-long city wall.

properties.title: Mesopotamia (region)
properties.description: An important region surrounding the Tigris–Euphrates river system, in the northern part of the Fertile Crescent, roughly corresponding to most of modern Iraq and Kuwait, eastern Syria, and Southeastern Turkey. Mesopotamia was a critical part of many empires and kingdoms, including the Sumerians, Akkadians, Assyrians, Babylonians, the Achaemenids, Alexander the Great, and the Seleucids. It was also a site of intense conflict between the Roman, Parthian, and Sassanid Empires until the 7th century Muslim conquest.

properties.title: Dur-Sharrukin
properties.description: Dūr-Šarrukīn (“Fort Sargon”), modern Khorsabad, became the capital of the Assyrian Empire during the reign of the eighth-century-BC ruler Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC). According to the Assyrian Eponym Chronicle, the foundations of the city were laid in 717 BC and the city itself was completed in early 706 BC, one year before Sargon was killed on the battlefield. Sargon’s newly-constructed, rectangular-shaped capital, which he modelled on the general plan on Babylon, was abandoned upon his death in 705 BC; his son and successor Sennacherib (r. 704–681 BC) made Nineveh Assyria’s principal administrative center.

properties.title: Bavian/Khinnis
properties.description: Just a few kilometers upstream of the city, the 7th-century B.C. Assyrian king Sennacherib had an architectural complex built and several stele-like panels (with accompanying inscriptions) carved into a nearby cliff face. The site may have served as a summer residence for the Assyrian king and may have been used as a headquarters to supervise the construction of a vast network of canals and aqueducts that was created specifically for providing water to Nineveh and the Assyrian heartland. The "Khinnis Reliefs" were included on the 2014 World Monuments Watch to increase awareness of cultural heritage in the Khinnis/Bavian area.

properties.title: Esag
properties.description: The temple of the god Lugalbanda, Esag (“Foremost House”), was located in the Kullab district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of four temples in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Abbaye Saint-Pierre de Moissac
properties.description: An important monastery founded probably in the seventh century of the common era.

properties.title: Roman Temple of Évora
properties.description: The Roman Temple of Évora, also referred to as the Temple of Diana, is a Roman temple of the first century A.D.

properties.title: Guadaíra (river)
properties.description: A tributary of the Guadalquivir river that rises in Pozo Amargo in the province of Cadiz.

properties.title: Tell el-ʻAbd
properties.description: Mound site along the eastern bank of the Euphrates in northern Syria. The site shows signs of habitation from the Early Bronze Age through the Byzantine period. Tell el-ʻAbd was flooded by the construction of the Taqba Dam in 1975, though a portion of it has reemerged due to declining water levels in Lake Assad.

properties.title: Italia, Regio IV
properties.description: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Samnium. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

properties.title: Aventinus mons
properties.description: One of the seven hills of Rome. Until the reign of the emperor Claudius, the hill lay outside the pomerium of the city.

properties.title: Sanctuary at Agios Konstantinos (Methana)
properties.description: A Late Helladic sanctuary was excavated by Helene Konstolakis-Jiannopoulou in 1990 near the chapel of Agios Konstantinos and Elenis. Activity at this site dates between 1500 and 1300 B.C.

properties.title: Dongola
properties.description: The late antique capital of the Nubian state of Makuria, Dongola remained an important center of trade through the medieval period.

properties.title: Basilica of San Clemente al Laterano
properties.description: The eleventh-century Basilica of San Clemente al Laterano is a Roman Catholic basilica dedicated to Clement I. It sits atop a three-tiered series of architectural remains stretching back to the Republican period. The earliest phase is represented by the foundations of a building destroyed by the fire of A.D. 64.

properties.title: Purpurariae (islands)
properties.description: An island group off the western coast of Morocco.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 88 H3 unnamed wall group (SE Dzhanakhyr)

properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 88 G3 unnamed wall (SE Bilidzhi)

properties.title: Forum of Paestum
properties.description: The forum of Roman Paestum stands north of the Hera sanctuary and measures ca. 57 x 150 meters. It occupies the site of the Greek agora and was surrounded with a peristyle of re-used Doric columns. Tabernae stood at its south side and baths funded by M. Tullius Venneianus stood to the southwest. A triple-podium structure - lararium? - stands on the western side.

properties.title: Roman theater at Teate
properties.description: The Roman theater at Teate measures 80 meters in diameter.

properties.title: Glanum dam
properties.description: A Roman dam that created the Lac du Peirou and supplied Glanum with water. While the ancient dam was destroyed in the late nineteenth century, the reservoir remains.

properties.title: Shunet ez Zebib
properties.description: A large mudbrick structure located at Abydos in Upper Egypt that dates to the Second Dynasty (ca. 2700 B.C.) of ancient Egypt.

properties.title: Villa Marittima della Tagliata
properties.description: A maritime villa of the first century A.D. adjacent to the port of Cosa.

properties.title: Collegium at Italica
properties.description: A building that has been identified as the seat of a Collegium because of its internal structure and size, was previously known as the"House of the Exedra".

properties.title: Public Square at Italica
properties.description: A small triangular plot near the northern wall of Italica that contained a garden in antiquity.

properties.title: Mura Messapiche
properties.description: Well-preserved remains of the ashlar fortification walls at Manduria.

properties.title: Gallicia
properties.description: A region of northwest Spain that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. It is now known as Galicia.

properties.title: Murcia
properties.description: A city located in southeastern Spain that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. The city on the present location was an Islamic foundation under the name Madinat Mursiyah and was established in A.D. 825 by Abd ar-Rahman II, the emir of Córdoba.

properties.title: Cardo Maximus (Apamea)
properties.description: The Cardo Maximus of Apamea in Syria is the site of the so-called "Great Colonnade", a portico that flanks the road for some 2 kilometers.

properties.title: Far Wadi al Qattafi
properties.description: The Wadi al Qattafi in Jordan's Black Desert is the site of numerous sites of occupation dating to the Neolithic period.

properties.title: San Menna
properties.description: The church of San Menna in Rome was recorded by the anonymous pilgrim author of the Einsiedeln in the eighth century. It was located along the Via Ostiensis. Likely founded in 589, the church is not attested after the tenth century.

properties.title: Lucera Castle
properties.description: A castle originally built by Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor in AD 1233.

properties.title: Castrum Rauracense
properties.description: A Late Roman fortress located on the southern bank of the Rhine adjacent to Augusta Raurica.

properties.title: Casa dei Grifi
properties.description: A late Republican domus of the Palatine Hill that was later consumed by the substructures of the Domitianic wing of the Flavian palace. The Casa dei Grifi preserves important wall paintings that are transitional from the First to the Second Pompeian style. Giacomo Boni discovered the domus in 1912.

properties.title: Ayio Gala
properties.description: Site in the northwestern corner of the island of Chios consisting of a two caves, both containing pottery and other remains dated to the Neolithic period. The entrance to the upper cave is located inside the Panayia Galactonosera chapel.

properties.title: Poggio La Croce
properties.description: A fortified Etruscan settlement.

properties.title: Ara Pacis Augustae
properties.description: The "Altar of Augustan Peace" was located in the Campus Martius of Rome. It was originally situated to the west of the Via Lata, near the eastern end of Augustus' Horologium. The reconstructed fragments of the altar are now housed in a museum located on the Tiber's banks in the Piazza Augusto Imperatore, a square created during the Fascist era in order to spotlight the ruins of the Mausoleum of Augustus.

properties.title: Eridu Ur Survey
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Castronuovo di Sicilia
properties.description: A modern location in Sicily that has been associated with the location of the ancient settlement of Krastos.

properties.title: Aqua Crabra
properties.description: An aqueduct supplying villas in the area of the city of Tusculum, mentioned by both Cicero and Frontinus.

properties.title: Aridi
properties.description: A town in the province of Guzana that is mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources. Aridi is identified as modern Tell ʿArāda.

properties.title: Dargues
properties.description: The remains of the earthworks of a Roman temporary camp.

properties.title: Doric temple
properties.description: A temple of the Doric order (VIII,7,30-34) located in the so-called Triangular Forum of Pompeii.

properties.title: Najafabad
properties.description: Najafabad (Persian: نجف‌آباد‎) is a city in Iran and the capital of Najafabad, Isfahan Province. The discovery of a stele of the Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721-705 BC) indicates that the settlement’s ancient name, at least in the eighth century BC, might have been Kišesim.

properties.title: Andelos reservoir
properties.description: A reservoir that functioned as part of the water supply of Andelos.

properties.title: Church of Saint Alexander Nevsky, Jerusalem
properties.description: The nineteenth century Russian Orthodox church preserves within it remains of Constantine's original fourth century church of the Holy Sepulchre.

properties.title: Eurguba
properties.description: The temple of the god Pisangunuk, Eurguba (“House, Established Foundation”), was located in the Kullab district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of four temples in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Ain Dara temple
properties.description: The Ain Dara temple, an archaeological site located near the village of Ain Dara, in Afrin, Syria, was the location of an Iron Age Syro-Hittite temple. The structure was noted for the similarities it bore to Solomon's Temple in Jerusalem. The site was in use from ca. 1300 until 740 BCE. It finds comparison with the temples at Emar, Mumbaqa, and Ebla's Temple D. In January 2018 the ruins of the temple were substantially damaged by air strikes carried out by the Turkish Air Force during the Afrin offensive. The site also subsequently suffered further damage, wanton destruction, and looting.

properties.title: Venice
properties.description: The city of Venice in northern Italy.

properties.title: Terrace of the Lions at Delos
properties.description: Nine white marble lions arranged in a single row along a terrace facing the sacred lake. The pathway marks an entry point into the city from the Bay of Skardana towards the shrine of Leto.

properties.title: Torreblanca del Sol (Fuengirola)
properties.description: An imperial Roman bath site.

properties.title: Arch of Augustus (Fano)
properties.description: A city gate in the form of a triumphal arch with three vaults. The gate marks the entry of the via Flaminia into the city.

properties.title: Theater of Ephesus
properties.description: The Theater of Ephesus sits at the foot of the Panayir mountains. It could host up to 25,000 spectators.

properties.title: Iathrippa
properties.description: Iathrippa was an oasis settlement along the Incense Road. From the Roman period until the advent of Islam the site was the seat of influential Iudaeo-Arabian tribes. Iathrippa would become an important center of Islam. Muhammad fled here from Mecca in 622 and the site was renamed Al-Madīna. It remained a key center until 656. It is the site of Muhammad's grave and a place of Muslim pilgrimage.

properties.description: A thermal site located near Roman Rusellae in regular use and reuse since at least Roman times. Its ancient name is not known. The first modern excavations and mapping efforts date to the 18th century of the modern era.

properties.title: Le Sparne archaeological area
properties.description: An ancient urban area at Poggio Buco in Italy with a defensive wall that included an agger. Also evidence for an elite building of the archaic period.

properties.title: tribus Aemilia
properties.description: The tribus Aemilia is counted among the twenty-one oldest rural tribes of Rome. Its location is uncertain.

properties.title: House of Flavius Germanus
properties.description: Roman Peristyle House with interior garden and pool.

properties.title: Kiz Bridge
properties.description: A historical bridge near the Mianeh in East Azerbaijan partially destroyed in 1946.

properties.title: Los Vilars
properties.description: A fortified Iberian site in use from ca. 750 B.C. to 325 B.C.

properties.title: Palma
properties.description: The Spanish village of Palma was located in the western part of the province of Córdoba. In the thirteenth century, it belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X.

properties.title: Dun Carloway
properties.description: Dun Carloway Broch is a well preserved broch in Scotland that was in use from ca. the first century BC until ca. AD 1300.

properties.title: Choragic Monument of Lysicrates
properties.description: The Choragic Monument of Lysicrates is a round structure erected in 334 BC in Athens to honor the victory of a choregos in a dramatic competition.

properties.title: Larak
properties.description: A city located near the Tigris River, possibly east or northeast of Nippur.

properties.title: Piscina Mirabilis
properties.description: A freshwater cistern at Bacoli on the Gulf of Naples, the Piscina Mirabilis likely provided sailors of the Roman fleet with drinking water. Its capacity is estimated at 12,600 cubic meters.

properties.title: Aqueduct of the Gier
properties.description: A Roman aqueduct of the first century AD supplying Lugdunum.

properties.title: Beauport Park Archaeological Site
properties.description: The largest known Roman iron-making site in the Weald, with the remains of a substantial bath house.

properties.title: Pharos of Portus Dubris
properties.description: The remains of the Roman lighthouse group at Portus Dubris.

properties.title: Mikro Kameni
properties.description: Mikro Kameni is a non-extant island that was formed in the Santorini caldera some time before 1851, when it was attested in the Admiralty Chart of Robert Graves, HMS Volgae. It was joined to Nea Kameni at some point after this, probably in the major period of volcanic activity in 1866-1870.

properties.title: Cahercommaun
properties.description: A triple stone ringfort built ca. AD 800.

properties.title: Audleystown Court Cairn
properties.description: A dual court grave near the south shore of Strangford Lough in County Down, Northern Ireland.

properties.title: San Pietro a Badia Pozzeveri
properties.description: An abbey with tenth century origins connected to the pilgrimage route known as the Via Francigena.

properties.title: Chibanes
properties.description: A fortified site in use from the third millennium BC to the Roman period.

properties.title: Apollo Cynneius
properties.description: Sanctuary of Apollo Cynneius near or in Temnos, destroyed by Prusias II in 155 BCE. Its precise location is unknown today but certainly lies within Barrington Atlas Map 56 grid E4.

properties.title: Roman theater at Spoletium
properties.description: The Roman theater at Spoletium dates to the first century B.C.

properties.title: Saint Hripsime Church
properties.description: A fourth century AD church rebuilt in the seventh century AD in order to house remains of the eponymous saint. The church is located in the city of Vagharshapat (Etchmiadzin), in the Armavir Province of Armenia. Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

properties.title: Vicus Iugarius
properties.description: An ancient street that led from the Forum Romanum to the porta Carmentalis, passing between the basilica Iulia and the temple of the Castors.

properties.title: Trakhtemyrivsʹke horodyshche
properties.description: A Scythian-period (seventh-sixth centuries BCE) hillfort site on the right bank of the Dnieper River, consisting of a large fortified territory (Velyki Valky) surrounding a smaller acropolis (Mali Valky).

properties.title: Pomeroy Wood
properties.description: Site of a late first-century Roman military base and later roadside civilian settlement. The fort is also known as Gittisham Roman fort.

properties.title: Gal'adi
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources; the modern site is Khirbet Ǧalʿad.

properties.title: Gimtu
properties.description: Gath, Gat, or Geth (Hebrew: גַּת)) is mentioned in the El-Amarna letters as Gimti/Gintu/Gimtu. It was one of the five Philistine city-states. The town is mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources; the modern site is Tel es-Safī.

properties.title: Hellenistic Balaneion, Amathous
properties.description: A circular public bath building dating to the Hellenistic period in the agora of Amathous.

properties.title: Nuraghe Flumenelongu
properties.description: Nuraghe Flumenelongu (Alghero-Sassari) is an important archaeological site for considerations of prehistoric maritime commerce in the Mediterranean.

properties.title: Gebel el-Haridi
properties.description: An archaeological site located within Sohag Governate, near the village of El-Khazindariya, with evidence for human activity stretching from the Sixth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom to the late Roman Empire and the Coptic period.

properties.title: Sant'Agata di Militello
properties.description: A modern town in Sicily that has been associated with the location of the ancient settlement of Agathyrnum.

properties.title: Yiftahel
properties.description: An archaeological site of the Lower Galilee in northern Israel, Yiftahel has evidence for occupation beginning in the Pre-Pottery Neolithic B. By the early Bronze Age the settlement consisted of approximately 20 oval structures. Excavations took place here between 1992 and 2008.

properties.title: Basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe
properties.description: A basilica begun in the sixth century AD by Bishop Ursicinus with financial support from the Greek banker Iulianus Argentarius.

properties.title: Hamam (Hamamköy)
properties.description: Hamam is a modern Turkish village near Erzurum in the Northeast of Turkey. Here an inscription of the Urartian king Argišti I, son of Minua (eighth century BCE), was found which reports the filling of a grain silo.

properties.title: Habıbuşağı (İzoli)
properties.description: Habıbuşağı (İzoli) was an Urartian fortress situated near Kömürhan, at the left shore of the river Euphrates in the Elazığ Province of eastern Turkey. Today it is covered by the reservoir behind the Karakaya dam. Habıbuşağı is best known on account of a rock inscription of the Urartian king Sarduri II, son of Argišti (eighth century BCE) which reports the expedition of Sarduri to this region. Habıbuşağı is, in fact, the westernmost known fortress of the Urartian kingdom.

properties.title: Step Gate of the Gardens
properties.description: Nineveh's western wall had seven (or eight) gates: the Step Gate of the Gardens was the third gate from the northern city wall. The Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib constructed it sometime between 694 and 691 B.C. and he gave it the Akkadian ceremonial name Igisigsig-mušammeh-ṣippāti, which means "The God Igisigsig Is the One Who Makes Orchards Flourish." The gate is still unlocated, but, based on its everyday name Akkadian name mušlālum ša kirî ("Step Gate of the Gardens"), it must have led up to Sennacherib's Palace on the citadel, perhaps at the foot of the sloping passage Room LI of the South-West Palace.

properties.title: Kaymakçı
properties.description: A large Bronze Age settlement on the western shore of lake Marmara in western Anatolia, overlooking the central Gediz river valley. The site is composed of an 8 hectare fortified citadel situated on a ridge, with evidence for a larger lower town below on the surrounding plain.

properties.title: Garn Fadryn
properties.description: A 5 ha Iron Age hill fort located in Wales.

properties.title: Castro de Alvarelhos
properties.description: A multi-period fortified site with occupation stretching from the Bronze Age to the Middle Ages.

properties.title: Roman siege Camp E'
properties.description: Remains of a Roman siege camp from the siege of the fortress of Masada in A.D. 72.

properties.title: Area della Guastuglia
properties.description: The archaeological site "Area della Guastuglia" at Gubbio is an architectural complex likely connected with civic religion during Gubbio's Roman phase.

properties.title: Temple of the Sibyl
properties.description: A second century B.C. Roman temple located on the acropolis of ancient Tibur.

properties.title: Civita Giuliana
properties.description: The Civita Giuliana is located in the northern suburbium of Pompeii, about 700 meters from the city walls. Thus far the site has produced archaeological evidence of suburban villas in Pompeii's hinterland. Early twentieth-century excavations were carried out here, only to be published in 1994. Clandestine looting at the site brought about a cooperative effort to resume excavations in the interests of heritage protection in 2017.

properties.title: Mogil'nik Maĭtan
properties.description: Bronze Age burial ground in east-central Kazakhstan.

properties.title: Necropoli di San Placido
properties.description: A large Roman necropolis in Messina, uncovered in 1914 during the works to build the modern Palazzo della Prefettura.

properties.title: vicus vitrarius
properties.description: A street in Regio I known only from the Regionary Catalogues.

properties.title: Albendin
properties.description: Albendin, in the district of Baena, is located near Córdoba. It once belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X and is today known as Albendín.

properties.title: Palaiochora
properties.description: A fortified Medieval settlement of Aegina. Built in the ninth century, the site was the island's capital until 1826.

properties.title: Lazarides
properties.description: A Mycenaean settlement was excavated near Lazarides on Aegina.

properties.title: Edurkuga
properties.description: The dais of the Igīgū gods, Edurkuga (“House, Pure Abode”), was located in the TE.E (read as either Tê or Kisīri) district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of two daises in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: San Crisogono
properties.description: San Crisogono (sacred to San Crisogono) is one of the early parish churches (tituli) of Rome. Pope Silvester I (314–335) likely builds the first iteration in the fourth century AD; later reworkings occur in the twelfth and seventeenth centuries, respectively.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Thuburbo Maius
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Thuburbo Maius is an extramural structure constructed by hollowing out elevated terrain.

properties.title: Badnigerimhuluha
properties.description: Nineveh’s outer stone wall was called Badnigerimhuluha ("Wall, Terrorizer of Enemies"). It was constructed by the Neo-Assyrian king Sennacherib after he moved the Assyrian capital to Nineveh. The visible remains of the twelve-kilometer-long wall and some of its gates are still visible today.

properties.title: Castellet de Bernabé
properties.description: An Iberian town dating between the fifth century B.C. and the third century A.D. It has a quasi-orthogonal plan and cover approximately 1,000 square meters.

properties.title: Hippodrome at Ptolemais/Barkes Limen
properties.description: The Hippodrome at Ptolemais/Barkes Limen (Cyrenaica, Libya).

properties.title: Pont Serme
properties.description: A Roman bridge on the Via Domitia.

properties.title: Kirmington
properties.description: A Roman fort of early Claudian date.

properties.title: Roman bridge of Saint-Vincent
properties.description: A Roman bridge built across the Cillian stream in the Valle d'Aosta, Italy.

properties.title: Seruci
properties.description: A nuragic complex including a central nuraghe and an associated village.

properties.title: Stadium
properties.description: The stadium at Aphrodisias dates to the later first century A.D. and is thought to be part of a comprehensive program of monumental construction undertaken at the site. The stadium's form is unusual and scholars assign it to a category referred to as στάδιον ἀμφιθέατρον (an "amphitheatral stadium").

properties.title: Sandarakourgion Oros
properties.description: A mountain and extensive mining works mentioned by Strabo in the vicinity of Pimolisa in Pontus. Its exact location cannot be determined today.

properties.title: Chûn Quoit
properties.description: Chûn Quoit is a dolmen-type tomb located in Cornwall. The quoit was likely originally covered by a barrow.

properties.title: Titus Tunnel
properties.description: A Flavian period channel cut for the purpose of diverting the course of a river.

properties.title: S'Imbalconadu Roman villa
properties.description: A multi-phase rustic structure (fattoria) located near Olbia, Sardinia. The quadrangular structure consists of twenty-some rooms arranged around a central courtyard; the built surface covers ca 1,000 square meters.

properties.title: Balochistan (region)
properties.description: A desert and mountainous region located between the Plateau of Iran and the Indian subcontinent, comprising the modern regions of southeastern Iran (Sistan and Baluchestan province), western Pakistan (Balochistan province), and southern Afghanistan (Nimruz, Helmand and Kandahar provinces). The region's name is derived from the Baloch people, who have inhabited the region since at least the ninth century CE. In antiquity, the southern part of the region, along the coast of the Arabian Sea, was known as Maka in the Achaemenid period and Gedrosia in the Hellenistic period.

properties.title: Kidmuri temple (Kalhu)
properties.description: When Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud) became the principal administrative center of the Assyrian Empire in the ninth century BC, king Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) built (or rebuilt) numerous temples. One of those was dedicated to the divine Kidmuri (probably a collective name for a group of gods).

properties.title: Thatcham, Berkshire
properties.description: A minor Romano-British Settlement.

properties.title: Radlett
properties.description: A Roman villa and bath building, dating between the second and fourth centuries AD.

properties.title: Palatium Sessorianum
properties.description: Palatium Sessorianum is of unknown origins. It was situated at the extreme south-east of Region V and it adjoined the amphitheatrum Castrense. It pre-dated the Aurelian wall. The portions of the complex within the line of the walls was an imperial residence by the time of Constantine.

properties.title: Nausharo
properties.description: Archaeological site in Balochistan, Pakistan associated with the Indus Valley civilization. The site shows signs of habitation from the early third-early second millennium BCE.

properties.title: Tel Yarmut
properties.description: Bronze Age site near Tel Beit Shemesh in Israel. The site shows signs of habitation from the 17th century BCE-4th century CE.

properties.title: Insula dei Dipinti
properties.description: A Hadrianic insula in Ostia Antica between the north wall of the castrum and the Tiber, comprising the houses of Jove and Ganymede, of the Infant Bacchus, and of the Paintings, arranged according to an L-shaped plan. Its façade faced onto two streets, forming a corner, while its inner sides looked out onto a large garden, without porticoes.

properties.title: Hypios (river)
properties.description: A river mentioned in ancient sources. Modern scholars identify it with the lower/larger (Büyük) course of the modern Melen Çay (Buyukmelen), which drains the marshy Efteni Golü (much diminished from its pre-modern extent). Ancient people seem to have extended the "Hypios" name past the lake and up one of its tributaries, but scholarly opinion is divided as to whether this was the modern Ugursuyu/Ogursu/Akarsu (Robert 1980, whence Foss in BAtlas) or the upper/smaller (Küçük) Melen Çayı (Strobel in New Pauly).

properties.title: Tel Kabri
properties.description: Archaeological site near the modern settlement of Kabri in northern Israel. The site shows signs of occupation from the late Neolithic period and the Early (Ia-II) and Middle (IIA-B) Bronze Ages. The site was an important city in the Middle Bronze Age, rapidly expanding during the 18th century BCE with the construction of a rampart and one of the largest known Canaanite palaces. It was abandoned by about 1500 BCE, and later habitations (in the Iron Age, Hellenistic, and Ottoman periods) were of smaller scale.

properties.description: Theron was a fifth century B.C. tyrant of Akragas. A tomb located near the Porta Aurea of the city is traditionally referred to as being that of the tyrant.

properties.title: Gymnasium at Akragas
properties.description: An architectural complex in the upper agora of Akragas (modern Agrigento) dedicated to Hermes and Heracles that was probably used as gymnasium. It appears to have been built in Hellenistic time and renovated in the Augustan period.

properties.title: Gallese
properties.description: Gallese is a settlement located about 14 km north of Civita Castellana. It was active especially in Faliscan times and again during late antiquity and the middle ages.

properties.title: Grotta Porciosa, Borghetto
properties.description: Grotta Porciosa, near Borghetto, was the site of a small but prosperous settlement in the Ager Faliscus.

properties.title: Curia Iulia
properties.description: The building of the Curia Julia was begun by Julius Caesar and completed by Augustus in 29 BCE. It replaced the former senate house, the Curia Hostilia.

properties.title: Pula Arena (Roman amphitheater)
properties.description: The Pula Arena is a Roman amphitheater dating to the first century.

properties.title: Basilica of Saint-Pierre-aux-Nonnains
properties.description: A Christian basilica that incorporates the remains of a fourth century AD Roman gymnasium.

properties.title: Hatnub
properties.description: An Ancient Egyptian alabaster quarry used intermittently from the Fourth Dynasty through the Roman period.

properties.title: Villa di Podere Anna
properties.description: The ruins of a Roman villa rustica were discovered in the 1990s along via Diego Fabbri. The site dates to the first century B.C. and remained in use at least until the fifth century A.D. The remains of a bath complex are substantial.

properties.title: Elkharas
properties.description: Khwarazmian site on the bank of the Amu Darya River. The site was excavated in 1973-1975 prior to flooding due to dam construction. The primary occupation at the site is dated from the 6th century BCE-3rd century CE, with evidence of later occupation as late as the 11th century CE.

properties.title: Temple of Ellesyia
properties.description: A small rock-cut temple dedicated to Amun, Horus, and Satis dated to the 18th Dynasty. Originally located near Qasr Ibrim/Premis, the temple was relocated to the Museo Egizio in Turin, Italy, in the 1960s prior to the area's flooding beneath the surface of Lake Nasser.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Tipasa
properties.description: A Roman amphitheater at Tipasa.

properties.title: Khorsabad Residence M
properties.description: The eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) had several royal residences constructed in the citadel of his new capital, Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad). Residence M, which has constructed on the western side of the citadel, is presumed to have been for one of the highest officials of the Assyrian Empire. Since no inscriptions were discovered in the ruins of the building, the owner/principal occupant of the this Assyrian palace is not known.

properties.title: House of Publius Casca Longus
properties.description: The House of Publius Casca Longus (I, 6, 11) is located on the Via dell'Abbondanza and is also known as the Casa dei Quadretti Teatrali.

properties.title: House of the Prince of Naples

properties.title: Theban necropolis

properties.title: Guglia di Marcello
properties.description: The so-called "Guglia di Marcello" or "Aguglia d'Agosta" is a Roman funerary monument located along the ancient via Pompei that once connected Syracuse and Messina. It dates to the period from the first century B.C. to the first century A.D.

properties.title: Carthage military harbor

properties.title: Roman forum of Col. Clunia (Sulpicia)

properties.title: Catacomb of Ponziano

properties.title: Avebury

properties.title: Danebury Hill Fort

properties.title: Via Domitia
