properties.title: Great Mosque of the Umayyads
properties.description: The Great Mosque of the Umayyads is located in the old city of Damascus and is one of the largest and oldest mosques in the world. It was completed in 715.

properties.title: Gaimanova Mogila
properties.description: A Scythian burial site containing burials from the fourth to second centuries B.C.; located near the Dnieper River, southeast of the modern village of Balky.

properties.title: Acropolis of Cumae
properties.description: The Acropolis of Cumae was used across multiple periods, beginning with the foundation of the Greek colony in the eighth century B.C.

properties.title: Tel Erani
properties.description: One of the largest Early Bronze Age mounds in the southern Levant, located approximately 20 km east of Ashkelon. The site shows signs of habitation as early as the Chalcolithic Era, with a significant remains from the Bronze Age and additional remains from the Iron Age, Persian, Hellenistic, and Islamic periods.

properties.title: Sepulcretum
properties.description: A modern appellation of the ancient Iron Age necropolis uncovered along the Sacra Via adjacent to the Temple of Antoninus and Faustina in April 1902. Giacomo Boni and others conducted extensive excavations at the site.

properties.title: Hellenistic theater at Dion
properties.description: The heavily reconstructed remains of the Hellenistic theater at Dion. Parts of the ancient underground stage system are preserved.

properties.title: Nuraghe Santa Barbara
properties.description: A nuragic site located on Monte Manai in Sardinia.

properties.title: Housesteads Mithraeum
properties.description: Temple of Mithras at Roman fort of Housesteads (Vercovicium)

properties.title: Roman theater of Herculaneum
properties.description: The Roman theater of Herculaneum was constructed during the Augustan period. The theater was discovered first in 1709 while a well was being dug.

properties.title: Via Severiana
properties.description: The Via Severiana was a coastal route running from Ostia to Terracina, a distance of ca. 80 Roman miles.

properties.title: Mahabalipuram
properties.description: This group of sanctuaries was carved out of rock along the Coromandel coast in the seventh and eighth centuries. The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

properties.title: Nuraghe Serbissi
properties.description: A nuragic complex located near Osini, Sardinia.

properties.title: Malchittu nuragic temple
properties.description: A sacred structure with an 'in antis' plan located near Arzachena in Sardinia.

properties.title: Carrowmore Megalithic Cemetery
properties.description: A grouping of fourth-millennium BC Neolithic monuments located on the Cúil Irra peninsula near Sligo, Ireland.

properties.title: Libersart
properties.description: A pair of Gallo-Roman burial mounds are located at Libersart in Belgium. The tombs may relate to a second and third century AD vicus in the area.

properties.title: Fundus Appianus
properties.description: The estate of Aurelius Appianus, located near Beneventum and Ligures Baebiani (Circello). It's precise location is not known.

properties.title: Abrau (peninsula)
properties.description: The northwestern end of the Caucasus Mountains, forming a short peninsula in the northeastern Black Sea.

properties.title: Temple of Asclepius
properties.description: The Temple of Asclepius (VIII, 7, 25) in Pompeii is located at the intersection of the Via del Tempio di Iside and the Via Stabiana. It is also referred to as the Temple of Jupiter Meilichius.

properties.title: Angkor Wat
properties.description: The principal temple of Angkor, the capital city of the Khmer empire, Angkor Wat was constructed in the 12th century CE. Angkor was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1992.

properties.title: Nuraghe Bruncu Maduli o Bruncu Madugui
properties.description: A Middle Bronze Age nuraghe and a proto-nuragic village located on the plain known as Giara di Gestur.

properties.title: Odeon
properties.description: The Odeon (VIII, 7, 19) is a small roofed theater in Pompeii. It was built between 80 and 75 BC, under commission by two public officials, C. Quinctius Valgus and Marcus Porcius.

properties.title: Arch of Trajan at Canosa
properties.description: The Arch of Trajan at Canosa dates to the second century.

properties.title: Solaize Roman Milestone
properties.description: A Roman milestone.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Sutri
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Sutri likely dates to the reign of Augustus.

properties.title: Obelisk of Theodosius
properties.description: Obelisk of Theodosius is an ancient Egyptian obelisk created at Karnak under Thutmoses III (1479–1425 BC) that was transported to Constantinople by the Roman emperor Theodosius I and re-erected in late the fourth century AD.

properties.title: Temple C
properties.description: The so-called "Temple C" of the Largo Argentina sacred area may be dedicated to the Italic goddess Feronia.

properties.title: Temple A
properties.description: So-called "Temple A" is a structure of the third century B.C. and is likely the Temple of Juturna that was vowed by Caius Lutatius Catulus following his victory against the Carthaginians in 241 B.C. It was later converted into a church, the apse of which remains visible.

properties.title: Porta Consolare
properties.description: The Porta Consolare was likely the primary gateway in Hispellum's Roman-era fortification wall.

properties.title: Bakla Tepe
properties.description: A site located on what is now an island in Tahtalı Barajı near Izmir. The site shows signs of habitation from the Chalcolithic period to the Late Bronze Age, as well as a later Romano-Byzantine settlement. The plain surrounding the site was flooded by the Tahtalı Dam in 1999.

properties.title: Temple of Apollo at Hierapolis

properties.title: Place near Taparura

properties.title: Falerii Novi amphitheater

properties.description: An arch erected to honor Trajan between A.D. 100 and 116.

properties.title: Ta' Ħaġrat Temple Complex

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Vindonissa
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Vindonissa was built under the reign of Tiberius.

properties.title: Great Orme

properties.title: Tomb of the Volumnii and Palazzone necropolis
properties.description: A hypogeum-type tomb located in Ponte San Giovanni, a suburb of Perugia. The tomb is generally dated to the third century B.C.

properties.title: Tell Jerablus Tahtani
properties.description: Jerablus Tahtani is a multi-period settlement located south of Carchemish. Excavation has revealed evidence related to the Uruk expansion in the fourth millennium B.C. as well as evidence of the "second urban revolution" in Early Bronze Age Syria. The Bronze Age fortified site is built atop remains of a third millennium B.C. phase. Numerous tombs and stratified mortuary deposits have been excavated, including a prominent tomb near the entrance to the Bronze Age settlement.

properties.title: Qal’eh-i Imam
properties.description: Qal’eh-i Imam (“Imam Fortress”), also call Qal’eh-i Marivan (“Marivan Fortress”), is one of the most important castles and fortresses in the Kurdistan Province, Marivan District, Iran. This now-ruined military fortification played a key role during the Safavid Period (1502–1737) and was an administrative venter of Ardalanians and Babanians rulers in Kurdistan. The discovery of a stele fragment of the Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in the drystone wall enclosing one of the buildings of the village Barqaleh might attest to a settlement there in the eighth century BC.

properties.title: Sinkhar

properties.title: Oviedo
properties.description: Founded in the eighth century, Oviedo was modeled after Toledo and flourished in the ninth century under Asturian King Alfonso II (791-842). It was at that time that Oviedo became the Asturian capital and an episcopal see. Oviedo remained prominent until the early tenth century.

properties.title: Duurlig Nars
properties.description: Xiongnu tomb site near the modern village of Bayan-Adarga, Khentii, Mongolia. The site contains burials dated from the 4th century BCE to the 2nd century CE.

properties.title: Abbeyknockmoy abbey
properties.description: A ruined Medieval Cistercian abbey founded in 1190.

properties.title: Via Herculia
properties.description: A Roman road known through epigraphic attestations, the Via Herculia connected Aquilonia and Aequum Tuticum.

properties.title: Tytkesken-VI
properties.description: Multi-period burial site in the northern Altai region. The bulk of the burials on the site are dated to the Pazyryk period (6th-4th centuries BCE), with additional burials from the Byikenskaya (8th-6th centuries BCE), Bulan-Kobinskaya (2nd-3rd centuries CE), and Turkic (6th-8th centuries CE) cultures.

properties.title: Sanctuary of Poseidon at Tainaron
properties.description: A famous ancient sanctuary of Poseidon located at the southern end of the modern Mani peninsula of the Peloponnese. Literary and archaeological evidence indicate that the sanctuary featured a temple, a cave treated as a mouth of the underworld, and other structural and monumental components. It seems to have served as a sanctuary site for suppliants and a context for the formal manumission of enslaved persons.

properties.title: Kangurttut
properties.description: Bactrian site in southwestern Tajikistan containing a settlement and burial ground dated to the Bronze and early Iron Ages.

properties.title: Villanovaforru, Nuraghe Genna Maria

properties.title: Lu Brandali
properties.description: A nuragic settlement dating to the latter part of the second millennium BC.

properties.title: Khorsabad Gate 6
properties.description: This decorated gate is the northernmost city gate of the southwest wall of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon"), the capital of the Assyrian Empire constructed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC).

properties.title: Khorsabad Gate 7
properties.description: This undecorated gate is the southernmost city gate of the northwest wall of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon"), the capital of the Assyrian Empire constructed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC).

properties.title: Khorsabad Citadel Gate A
properties.description: This decorated gate is located on the western wall of the citadel of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon"), the capital of the Assyrian Empire constructed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC).

properties.title: Khorsabad Gate 5
properties.description: This undecorated gate is the southernmost city gate of the southwest wall of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon"), the capital of the Assyrian Empire constructed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC).

properties.title: Old Winchester Hill
properties.description: Old Winchester Hill is the site of both Bronze Age barrows and an Iron Age hill fort.

properties.title: Nuraghe Asusa
properties.description: A nuraghe standing on a modest hill (502 meters above sea level) on the Brabaciera river. The nuraghe originally had two towers with an intermediary courtyard.

properties.title: Su Fraigu
properties.description: A Punic necropolis.

properties.title: Dinka Settlement Complex
properties.description: A small frontier settlement dated to the Neo-Asssyrian period, located in the Peshdar Plain near the banks of the Lesser Zab River.

properties.title: Euphrasian Basilica
properties.description: An Early Byzantine Christian basilica located in Poreč, Croatia.

properties.title: Arco Felice Vecchio
properties.description: The so-called "Arco Felice Vecchio" is a city gate of the first century A.D. built under the administration of Domitian.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Albano Laziale
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Albano Laziale is generally dated to the mid-third century A.D.

properties.title: Terrace of Zeus
properties.description: The so-called "Terrace of Zeus" or "Terrazza di Zeus" at Elea-Velia.

properties.title: Circus of Maxentius
properties.description: The Circus of Maxentius is part of a complex of buildings built by emperor Maxentius on the Via Appia between A.D. 306 and 312.

properties.title: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
properties.description: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus is a tomb built between 353 and 350 B.C. for Mausolus, a satrap in the Persian Empire. Antipater of Sidon identified it as one of his Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

properties.title: Baku
properties.description: An ancient city located on the Caspian Sea. Baku, now in Azerbaijan, was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

properties.title: Circus of Col. Tarraco
properties.description: The Roman circus of Tarragona dates from the reign of Domitian. The circus measures ca. 325 meters in length and ca. 100 to 115 meters in width.

properties.title: Temple of Ares
properties.description: The sanctuary with a temple dedicated to Ares is located south of the Altar of the Twelve Gods in the Athenian Agora. The temple was originally erected at Pallene ca. 430 BC and sacred to Athena Pallenis at Pallene. The structure was moved to the Agora in the early first century.

properties.title: Stadium of Antoninus Pius (Puteoli)
properties.description: A stadium of ancient Puteoli constructed under Antoninus Pius in the second century A.D. that was revealed by excavation in 2008.

properties.title: Zivistan/Elmalık
properties.description: Elmalık (formerly Zivistan, Zewestan) is a village in the Van Province in the southeast of Turkey ca. 12 km to the south of Van. Two small Urartian fortress have been found in the immediate vicinity, which are known as Aşağı Zivistan Kalesi ("Lower Zivistan Castle") and Yukarı Zivistan Kalesi ("Upper Zivistan Castle"). On the basis of several Urartian stone inscriptions of the Urartian king Išpuini (9th century BCE) (CTU I A 2-2 - A 2-4) and one rock inscription of the same king (CTU I A 2-5), both fortresses can be dated to the the reign of the Urartian king Išpuini (9th century BCE).

properties.title: Halatu

properties.title: Temple of Apollo at Delphi
properties.description: The Temple of Apollo situated in the center of the oracular sanctuary of that god at Delphi.

properties.title: Sanctuary of Apollo at Cyrene
properties.description: A sanctuary at Cyrene dedicated to Apollo Karneios. The sanctuary was in use between the seventh century BC and the second century AD, and included shrines to other gods, including Artemis and Isis.

properties.title: L-Shaped Palace at Gla
properties.description: A complex of multifunctional rooms at Gla with two connected wings that extend from a right angle to form two ʺmegaronsʺ that lacked hearths and throne rooms. The palace was built around 1300 BCE.

properties.title: Motya causeway
properties.description: Remains of a causeway that once connected Motya to the Sicilian mainland.

properties.title: Caesareum of Alexandria
properties.description: Hellenistic temple constructed by Cleopatra VII and dedicated to Julius Caesar, and later rededicated by Augustus to himself. In 13 BCE Augustus relocated two obelisks from Heliopolis to the site. The temple was converted to a Christian church in the mid-4th century.

properties.title: Ptolemaic Kingdom

The city was likely of censorial status thereafter.

properties.title: Pantelleria (island)

properties.description: A Christian church located in the ancient city of Apollonia (Cyrenaica) built approximately in the fifth century A.D., probably on earlier Hellenistic foundations. The site was excavated in 1922 and shows a three-aisled nave with transept at the eastern end, and a single apse. Traces of the mosaic floor are still visible.

properties.title: House of the Baker
properties.description: House in Pompeii (VI,3,3) that most likely dates from the second century BC and experienced extensive remodeling after the earthquake of AD 62.

properties.title: Edikukalama
properties.description: The temple of the god Šamaš, Edikukalama (“House of the Judge of the Land”), was located in the Kumar district of Babylon, in the western half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of seven temples in that part of Babylon. Edikukalama is attested in the Old Babylonian Period and it was rebuilt in the Neo-Babylonian Period by Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–562 BC).

properties.title: Castellum aquae
properties.description: A building in Pompeii serving as the distribution point of water originating from the Acquedotto Serino, Claudio or Augusteo. The structure is also referred to as Castellum Divisorium.

properties.title: Necropolis of Porta Vesuvio

properties.title: Meta Sudans

properties.title: Qlejgħa tal-Baħrija

properties.title: Domus Aurea

properties.description: A cultural landscape located in the southeast of Fars Province, Iran, the Sassanid Archaeological Landscape of Fars Region is the official denomination given by UNESCO to eight Sasanian-era archaeological sites. This landscape was recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site on 30 June 2018.

properties.title: Mystras

properties.title: Garden of the Fugitives
properties.description: The so-called "Garden of the Fugitives" (I, 21,1) is an area of the city that was once given over to habitation but that in the final phase of the city was a vineyard with a summer triclinium. Excavation campaigns of the 1960s and 1970s discovered 13 human victims of the AD 79 eruption that destroyed the city.

properties.title: Roman theater at Brixia

properties.title: Horti Lucull(i)ani
properties.description: An elite villa and garden on the Pincian Hill in Rome laid out originally by Lucius Licinius Lucullus ca. 60 BC. The present day Villa Borghese gardens still cover a portion of the Gardens of Lucullus.

properties.title: Roman theater at Iguvium
properties.description: The Roman theater at Iguvium is located within the Guastuglia archaeological area and dates to the late republican period.

properties.title: Gastaldaga area and the Episcopal complex
properties.description: A Longobard complex in Cividale del Friuli.

properties.title: Temple of Athena Lindia
properties.description: A Doric temple dating ca. 300 BC located on the acropolis of Lindos. The sanctuary stands above a grotto that likely housed the earlier phases of the cult. The amphiprostyle temple has an elongated floor plan and measures 7.75 x 21.65 m.

properties.title: Giant's tomb at Lu Brandali
properties.description: A passage grave associated with the nuragic complex at Lu Brandali near Santa Teresa Gallura.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 unnamed bridge (at Ponte a Buriano)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 unnamed bridge (W Ponte a Buriano, over R. Arno)

properties.title: Unnamed bridge
properties.description: An unnamed ancient bridge located on the Via Aurelia over the Osa river at Telamon.

properties.title: Chew Green
properties.description: Chew Green is the site of a Roman encampment located in Northumberland.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 unnamed bridge group (on Via Cassia, near Sorrina)

properties.title: Unnamed bridge
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1-C4 unnamed bridge (on Via Flaminia (20))

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 unnamed bridge (S Camerinum)

properties.title: Ponte della Rocca, Blera
properties.description: The so-called Ponte della Rocca located on the Via Clodia at Blera is situated adjacent to the Necropolis of San Giovenale and Terrone. Some sources suggest an original date in the third or second centuries BCE.

properties.title: Ponte dell'Abbadia
properties.description: An ancient bridge over the Fiora river (the ancient Armenta) near Vulci. Ancient name unknown.

properties.title: Bridge on Via Cassia near *Volsinii Veteres
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C3

properties.title: Ponte di Pogi
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 unnamed bridge (over *Umbro fl., W Arretium at Pogi)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 unnamed bridge (near Aquae Apollinares? on road to Tarquinii at La Mola)

properties.title: Ponte di Quintodecimo
properties.description: The Ponte di Quintodecimo is located near Acquasanta Terme.

properties.title: Ponte sul Fosso Tre Ponti
properties.description: A Roman bridge on the Via Amerina between ancient Nepet and Falerii.

properties.title: Unnamed bridge over the Nar river near Terni
properties.description: An ancient bridge near the *Via Curia.

properties.title: *Aufenginum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 *Aufenginum

properties.title: Anguillara
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Anguillara

properties.title: Aesis (river)
properties.description: Aesis fl. (modern Esino river) is a river of the Marche region of Italy and flows into the Adriatic Sea.

properties.title: Blera
properties.description: Blera was a significant Etruscan settlement in the vicinity of Tarquinii. It lay along the line of the Roman Via Clodia. It received Roman municipal status and was enrolled in the tribus Arnensis. The city flourished in the sixth and fifth centuries BCE.

properties.title: Chianciano Terme
properties.description: Chianciano Terme begins as an Etruscan site, with a temple located near the natural springs. By the first century B.C. the site was popular with Romans as a healing spa.

properties.title: Cluviae
properties.description: A city of the Carricini Samnites.

properties.title: Ciminius (mountain)
properties.description: A volcanic massif rising 1053 meters above sea level; the modern Monte Cimino.

properties.title: Aternum
properties.description: Aternum (modern Pescara) was a settlement at the mouth of the Aternus river.

properties.title: *Aprutium
properties.description: An ancient region of eastern Italy (modern Abruzzo).

properties.title: Cales
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Cales

properties.title: Aquae Apollinares Novae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Aquae Apollinares Novae

properties.title: Castrum Truentinum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Castrum Truentinum

properties.title: Capena
properties.description: An ancient urban center in Faliscan territory adjacent to Etruria, Capena was sacked by the Romans in 390 BC.

properties.title: Asciano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Asciano

properties.title: Capestrano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Capestrano

properties.title: Casuentillani
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Casuentillani

properties.title: Aquae Apollinares
properties.description: The Aquae Apollinares were thermal springs located between Careiae and Tarquinii, perhaps to be associated with the Bagni di Stigliano or Bagni di Vicarello.

properties.title: Caletranus Ager
properties.description: The Caletranus Ager was the territory surrounding the Etruscan city of Caletra.

properties.title: Aspia (river)
properties.description: The Aspio river.

properties.title: Ciminius (lake)
properties.description: A caldera lake of northern Latium.

properties.title: Le Ciliegeta
properties.description: The site of Le Ciliegeta, near the source of the river Arno, served as a rich stips votiva. The site was discovered in 1836. The finds included over 600 bronzes, more than 1,000 pieces of aes rude, 2,000 weapons, and other artifacts.

properties.title: Clusium
properties.description: Clusium, the Etruscan Clevsin (modern Chiusi), was a major city of Etruria. Lars Porsena was a sixth century B.C. king of Clusium.

properties.title: Aesis
properties.description: An Umbrian town that became a colonia civium Romanorum under the name of Aesis in 247 B.C.

properties.title: Ancon(a)
properties.description: A port city founded by colonists from Syracuse in 387 BC.

properties.title: Aufinum
properties.description: Aufinum, long thought to have been located at modern Ofena, which reflects the ancient name, has been shown by recent excavations to have been located some 5km further south, near modern Capestrano. Aufinum was an ancient center of the Abruzzo. Pliny lists the Aufinates Cismontani among the communities of the Vestini.

properties.title: Axia
properties.description: Axia was an Etruscan center located to the west of Viterbo.

properties.title: Allumiere
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Allumiere

properties.title: Aquae Passeris
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Aquae Passeris

properties.title: Castro
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Castro

properties.title: *Aurinia/Saturnia
properties.description: An Etruscan town that Dionysius of Halicarnassus claimed had been founded by the Pelasgians, Saturnia received a Roman colony in 183 BC.

properties.title: Amiternum
properties.description: Amiternum was an ancient settlement of the Sabines that Rome captured in 293 BC. The settlement was situated at the intersection of four Roman roads: the Via Caecilia, the Via Claudia Nova, and the two branches of the Via Salaria. The historian Sallust was born at Amiternum in 86 B.C.

properties.title: Alba Fucens
properties.description: A town of the Aequi along the Marsic frontier where the Romans established a Latin colony in 304/3 B.C. Alba Fucens was a significant center of the middle republican period and became a place where Rome kept state prisoners, including Syphax of Numidia, Perseus of Macedonia, and Bituitus, king of the Arverni.

properties.title: Balneum Regis
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C3 Balneum Regis

properties.title: Armenta (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Armenta fl.

properties.title: Clitumnus (river)
properties.description: A small river of Umbria.

properties.title: Castelluccio di Pienza
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Castelluccio di Pienza

properties.title: Civitalba
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D2 Civitalba

properties.title: Castellum Firmanorum
properties.description: Castellum Firmanorum was the ancient port of Firmum Picenum.

properties.title: La Cività di Spedino
properties.description: La Cività di Spedino was a fortified upland center (951 m ASL) in the territory of the Aequi.

properties.title: Cliternia
properties.description: A city of the Aequiculi located in the valley of the Salto river.

properties.title: Batinus? (river)
properties.description: The Batinus? is mentioned by Pliny and may correspond to the Tordino river.

properties.title: Ager Gallicus (region)
properties.description: A region of Italy in which Gallic settlement had taken place after 400 BC. This territory was captured by Rome following the battle of Sentinum in 295 BC.

properties.title: Ameria
properties.description: Ameria, claimed by Cato the Elder as the oldest town in Umbria, was an important center that may have gained Roman municipal status as early as 338 B.C., following the Latin War.

properties.title: Auximum
properties.description: Auximum (modern Osimo) is an ancient settlement of Picenum. The original foundation was likely carried out by Greeks from Ancona. The Romans made it a base for military operations from 174 B.C.

properties.title: Arretium
properties.description: Arretium (the Etruscan Aritim) was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae and described by Livy as one of the "Capitae Etruriae". The Romans captured the city in 311 B.C. and it became a station on the via Cassia.

properties.title: Carsulae
properties.description: An ancient settlement originating the late fourth or third centuries BC and lying along the route of the Roman Via Flaminia.

properties.title: Castrum Novum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Castrum Novum

properties.title: Aquae Cutiliae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Aquae Cutiliae

properties.title: Algae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Algae

properties.title: Clasius? (river)
properties.description: Clasius? fl., a river of Umbria and part of the Tiber river's basin.

properties.title: Casone
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A2 Casone

properties.title: Castelsecco
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Castelsecco

properties.title: Cività di Bagno
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Cività di Bagno

properties.title: Cluana
properties.description: Cluana was an ancient settlement in Picenum.

properties.title: Baccanae
properties.description: Baccanae was a road station along the Via Cassia.

properties.title: Albula (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Albula fl.

properties.title: Alviano Scalo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C3 Alviano Scalo

properties.title: Aveia
properties.description: Aveia was a settlement of the Vestini in the valley of the Aterno river.

properties.title: Avens (river)
properties.description: A river of the Sabine territory.

properties.title: Alsietinus lacus
properties.description: The Alsietinus lacus, modern Lago di Martignano, is a small volcanic crater-lake in southern Etruria. The lake was the source of the Augustan aqueduct aqua Augusta Alsietina that served non-potable water to the Transtiberim and Ianiculum.

properties.title: Albinia (river)
properties.description: The Albegna is a river of southern Tuscany and flows from Monte Amiata to the Tyrrhenian Sea.

properties.title: Badies
properties.description: Badies is a site (vicus) along the Via Salaria mentioned in the Antonine Itinerary. Its location is no longer certain.

properties.title: Clocoris (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G4 Clocoris fl.

properties.title: Civita
properties.description: The Civita di Bagnoregio was originally founded by the Etruscans.

properties.title: Aquae Tauri
properties.description: A thermal site in Etruria northeast of Centumcellae.

properties.title: Castiglione del Lago
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C2 Castiglione del Lago

properties.title: Clanis (river)
properties.description: Clanis fl. (Chiana river) is a river of central Italy that flows into the Tiber river.

properties.title: Castellina
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A2 Castellina

properties.title: Arna
properties.description: Arna was an ancient city of Umbria that was controlled by Etruscans in the fourth century BCE.

properties.title: *Cingulus (mountain)
properties.description: Monte S. Vicino.

properties.title: Clusinus L.
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Clusinus L.

properties.title: Caelanum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Caelanum

properties.title: Aequiculi
properties.description: Aequiculi was a municipium in the territory of the Aequi.

properties.title: Anxanum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G4 Anxanum

properties.title: Aternus (river)
properties.description: The Aterno-Pescara river.

properties.title: Asisium
properties.description: A Roman settlement built over an Umbrian one on a western foothill of the Apennines, Asisium received municipal status and was assigned to the Tribus Sergia. Totila destroyed most of the city in A.D. 545.

properties.title: Camerinum
properties.description: Camerinum was a town in Umbria on the frontiers of Picenum that was allied to Rome from 309 B.C.

properties.title: Colle Plinio
properties.description: A hilltop villa near Tifernum Tiberinum commonly associated with one of the villas of Pliny the Younger.

properties.title: Centum Cellae
properties.description: Centum Cellae (modern Civitavecchia) was an ancient coastal settlement in Tyrrhenian Etruria. The emperor Trajan re-builds the harbor at the site in 106/7 and Pliny the Younger mentions its name, Centum Cellae. Saracens destroyed the city in A.D. 812.

properties.title: Aqua Viva
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Aqua Viva

properties.title: Colle delle Fate
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Colle delle Fate

properties.title: Cetamura
properties.description: Cetamura is an ancient hilltop settlement with occupation phases stretching from the Etruscans to the Romans to the Medieval period. The site is located near Gaiole, Radda and Castellina in Chianti, Italy.

properties.title: Campovalano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Campovalano

properties.title: Asculum
properties.description: Asculum (modern Ascoli Piceno) was the principal city of the Piceni.

properties.title: Attidium
properties.description: An ancient settlement of Umbria mentioned only by Pliny the Elder. Numerous inscriptions discovered at the site indicate that Attidium achieved the status of a municipium.

properties.title: Anneianum
properties.description: Anneianum was located in the Etruscan Apennines, along the road from Faventia to Florentia.

properties.title: *Cluentus (river)
properties.description: The Chienti river is found in Italy's Marche region. It flows from near Serravalle di Chienti to the Lago di Pievefavera and from there it joins the Fiastra river and eventually flows into the Adriatic Sea.

properties.title: Cingulum
properties.description: Cingulum was a town in Picenum.

properties.title: Unnamed aqueduct near Amiternum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 unnamed aqueduct (near Amiternum)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An aqueduct located near the sulphurous springs at Aquae Tauri, northeast of Centumcellae.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 unnamed aqueduct (Spoletium)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A1 unnamed aqueduct (Florentia)

properties.title: Roman aqueduct at Arretium
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 unnamed aqueduct (Arretium)

properties.title: Bratolyubovskii Kurgan
properties.description: A Scythian burial mound dated to the fourth century B.C. located near the village of Bratolyubivka in Kherson Oblast, Ukraine.

properties.title: Cosa
properties.description: A Latin colony in south Etruria founded ca. 273 B.C.

properties.title: Forum Decii
properties.description: A town of the Sabines mentioned by Pliny the Elder.

properties.title: Cunerum (promontory)
properties.description: A promontory on the Adriatic coast of Italy, south of Ancona near Monte Conero.

properties.title: Lugnano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C3 Lugnano

properties.title: Marta (river)
properties.description: The Marta river flows from Lake Bolsena to the Tyrrhenian Sea. Its course flows past both Tuscania and Tarquinia and enters the Tyrrhenian Sea near Lido di Tarquinia.

properties.title: Manliana
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Manliana

properties.title: Helvia Ricina
properties.description: An ancient settlement in Picenum at modern Villa Potenza in Marche, Comune di Macerata, Italy.

properties.title: Farfarus (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Farfarus fl.

properties.title: Falerio
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Falerio

properties.title: Hispellum
properties.description: Hispellum (modern Spello) is an ancient settlement of Umbria that became a Roman colony in the first century BC.

properties.title: Histonium
properties.description: Histonium, on the Adriatic coast, was a chief town of the Frentani.

properties.title: Falerii Veteres
properties.description: Falerii Veteres was the principal city of the Faliscans. It is located on a tuff outcropping at the point where several tributaries of the Treia join to flow into the Tiber. After rebelling against Rome in 241 B.C., Falerii suffered serious reversals of fortune.

properties.title: Fanum Fugitivi
properties.description: A road station on the Via Flaminia, located between Interamna and Spoletium.

properties.title: Magliano Sabina
properties.description: Magliano Sabina is located in Lazio, some 50 km north of Rome and some 30 km west of Rieti.

properties.title: Helvillum
properties.description: Helvillum was a vicus in Umbria located about 10 Roman miles from Aesis (Jesi).

properties.title: Marsiliana d’Albegna
properties.description: An ancient settlement located near the confluence of the rivers Albegna and Elsa.

properties.title: Lucus Feroniae
properties.description: A sanctuary and grove of Feronia and an associated settlement located along the Via Tiberina in the territory of Capena.

properties.title: Cumara? (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Cumara? fl.

properties.title: Forum Flaminii
properties.description: A town founded in 220 B.C. by Caius Flaminius during the construction of the Via Flaminia.

properties.title: Fulginiae
properties.description: Fulginiae was an ancient town of Umbria, Italy, on the later line of the Via Flaminia, ca. 20 km south of Nuceria.

properties.title: Cortona
properties.description: An Umbrian city that, under Etruscan influence, expanded and came to be called 'Curtun'. Later it became the Roman colony of Cortino.

properties.title: Grotte di Torri
properties.description: Grotte di Torri is located on the left bank of the Tiber river in the modern comune of Montopoli di Sabina. It has been inhabited since pre-Roman times.

properties.title: Flaminia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Flaminia

properties.title: Eretum
properties.description: Eretum was a settlement of the Sabines and is involved in legendary accounts of early Rome.

properties.title: Metaurus (river)
properties.description: Metaurus fl. (Metauro river) flows from near Monte dei Frati in the Apennine Mountains to the Adriatic Sea. The Metaurus was the site of two key battles in antiquity. The first, in 207 B.C., saw the defeat of Hasdrubal Barca by the consuls Marcus Livius Salinator and Gaius Claudius Nero. The second, the Battle of Fano, saw Aurelian defeat the Alamanni in A.D. 271.

properties.title: Contrada Altavilla
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Contrada Altavilla

properties.title: Ghiaccio Forte
properties.description: Ghiaccio Forte was an Etruscan settlement, most likely founded in the fourth century B.C., that was sacked by the Romans ca. 280 B.C.

properties.title: Fons Clitumni
properties.description: Originally the site of a shrine dedicated to the river god Clitumnus and later a paleochristian shrine. The temple was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011.

properties.title: Maternum
properties.description: Maternum was a settlement of ancient Etruria that is known from the Peutinger Table. It is located along the Via Clodia between Saturnia and Tuscana.

properties.title: Martanum
properties.description: An ancient harbor of the city of Tarquinia.

properties.title: Interpromium
properties.description: A village of the Marrucini, forming a station on the Via Claudia Valeria between Corfinium and Teate.

properties.title: Fontecchio
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Fontecchio

properties.title: Graviscae
properties.description: The port of the Etruscan city of Tarquinia.

properties.title: Collepezzuto
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Collepezzuto

properties.title: Matrinus? (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Matrinus? fl.

properties.title: Fisternae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Fisternae

properties.title: Iguvium
properties.description: An Umbrian hilltown, Iguvium is best known as the find-spot of the Iguvine Tables.

properties.title: Firmum Picenum
properties.description: Firmum Picenum was founded as a Latin colony in 264 B.C. with 6,000 colonists. It received municipal status after 48 B.C.

properties.title: Grotte di Castro
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Grotte di Castro

properties.title: Interamna Nahars
properties.description: An Umbrian center founded in the seventh century B.C. that became an important Roman municipality along the Via Flaminia.

properties.title: Matrinum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G3 Matrinum

properties.title: Flusor (river)
properties.description: The Potenza river.

properties.title: Interocrium
properties.description: A Sabine town that was later known as a mansio on the course of the Via Salaria.

properties.title: Cutiliensis L.
properties.description: A lake located near ancient Reate.

properties.title: Foruli
properties.description: Foruli was a Sabine town located between Amiternum and Interocrea.

properties.title: Galeata
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Galeata

properties.title: Corchiano
properties.description: Corchiano was the site of a wealthy settlement in the Ager Faliscus that was in proximity to the Via Amerina.

properties.title: Contrada S. Rustico
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Contrada S. Rustico

properties.title: Forum Aurelii
properties.description: A settlement in Etruria situated on the Via Aurelia between Centumcellae and Cosa according to the Antonine Itinerary.

properties.title: Cures
properties.description: Cures (also Cures Sabini) was a Sabine city located in the Tiber river valley along the Via Salaria. The Romans conquered Cures in 290 B.C. under M'. Curius Dentatus and granted it status as a municipium in the tribus Sergia.

properties.title: Intercisa/Petra Pertusa
properties.description: Intercisa/Petra Pertusa was a road station on the Via Flaminia. The toponym derives from the rock-cut tunnel or galleria that dates to the reign of Vespasian.

properties.title: Florentia
properties.description: Florentia (modern Florence / Firenze) was founded as a colony for military veterans ca. 80 B.C. by Lucius Cornelius Sulla.

properties.title: Interamnia Praetuttiorum
properties.description: Originally a settlement of the Praetuttii located at the confluence of the rivers Tordino and Vezzola (modern Teramo).

properties.title: Matilica
properties.description: Matilica was a municipium in Umbria located near the source of the river Aesis and close to the borders of Picenum. The Liber Coloniarum identifies the settlement as one of the “Civitates Piceni.”

properties.title: Grotte di S. Nicola
properties.description: The so-called Grotte di S. Nicola, the remains of the platform and cryptoporticus of a late republican Roman villa.

properties.title: Doganella
properties.description: Doganella was an important Etruscan settlement of the Albegna valley, occupied between ca. 600 and 400 B.C. The city may have comprised as many as 240 ha.

properties.title: Hatria (Picenum)
properties.description: An ancient city of Picenum that may have originated as colony established by Etruscans from Adria in the Veneto region. An alternate narrative suggests that the city's origins may be as a late sixth century B.C. colony founded by Aegina.

properties.title: *Firmidianum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 *Firmidianum

properties.title: Etruria/Tuscia (region)
properties.description: Etruria/Tuscia was an ancient region of Central Italy inhabited by the Etruscans.

properties.title: *Incerulae
properties.description: *Incerulae, an ancient sanctuary site in the territory of the Vestini.

properties.title: Marsi
properties.description: The Marsi were an ancient Italic tribe. Their chief center was located at Marruvium.

properties.title: Fanum Fortunae
properties.description: Fanum Fortunae, the site of a shrine to Fortuna, is first mentioned in the ancient sources in 49 B.C. when Iulius Caesar held the town. An Augustan colony was established at the site and the Romans prevailed in the Battle of Fano in A.D. 271. The town was eventually destroyed by the Ostrogoths.

properties.title: Helvinus? (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F2 Helvinus? fl.

properties.title: Cupra Montana
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Cupra Montana

properties.title: Forum Cassii
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Forum Cassii

properties.title: Furfo
properties.description: A vicus of the Vestini located in the upper Aterno valley in Abruzzo. The ancient settlement was located some 15 km south of modern L'Aquila, in the vicinity of S. Maria di Forfona near Barisciano. Furfo lay on the Via Claudia Nova between Amiternum and Peltuinum.

properties.title: Corfinium
properties.description: Corfinium was the principal city of the Paeligni in the valley of the Aternus river. The site becomes the capital of the breakaway Italic groups that oppose Rome during the Social War.

properties.title: Horta
properties.description: The Etruscan settlement of *Hurta (the modern Orte) was close to the Vadimonis Lacus where the Romans fought, and won, two engagements against Etruscan armies.

properties.title: Falerii
properties.description: A fortified town located some 6 km from Falerii Veteres and established by the ancient Romans ca. 241 B.C.

properties.title: Fescennium
properties.description: Fescennium (modern Narce) was a Faliscan settlement located ca. 5 km south of Falerii Veteres.

properties.title: Heba
properties.description: A Roman colony that was established in the third or second century B.C., Heba lay near modern Magliano. Funerary evidence indicate previous Etruscan occupation at the site.

properties.title: Forum Novum (Vescovio)
properties.description: Forum Novum was a Roman town and an early medieval bishopric. It is located in the Sabine hills and was likely founded as a market center during the Republican period. It had achieved the status of municipium by the first century A.D. The market center seems to have remained active until at least the fourth century and by the fifth century, a bishopric is established there.

properties.title: La Cuma, Monte Rinaldo
properties.description: The principal archaeological remains found in the "La Cuma, Monte Rinaldo" site are those of a late Republican sanctuary dating to the third through first centuries B.C.

properties.title: Crustumius (river)
properties.description: Crustumius fl. (Conca river)

properties.title: Forum Sempronii
properties.description: An ancient Roman colony, founded in the time of Gaius Sempronius Gracchus.

properties.title: *Hercules Curinus
properties.description: A sanctuary in the territory of the Paeligni dedicated to Hercules Curinus situated on an artificial terrace on the slopes of Mount Morrone. The terrace sanctuary looks over Sulmo in the valley below.

properties.title: Ferentium
properties.description: Ferentium (modern Ferento) was a city of Etruria first mentioned in the Liber Coloniarum ca. 123 BC that became a Roman municipium after the Social War. Substantial remains of the city remain; the site was the birthplace of Otho and noted for its fine stone monuments and statues.

properties.title: Faesulae
properties.description: Faesulae (modern Fiesole) was an Etruscan foundation called Viesul, Viśl, or Vipsul. The city was conquered by Romans in 283 B.C. Sulla would settle Roman veterans there. Citizens of the town supported the conspiracy of Catiline.

properties.title: Corciano
properties.description: The environs of Corciano were inhabited by Etruscans and, later, there is evidence for Roman villas. In 1812, a series of bronze panels from an Etruscan parade chariot was discovered at Castel San Mariano di Corciano.

properties.title: Forum Clodii
properties.description: An ancient road station on the Via Clodia.

properties.title: Cupra Maritima
properties.description: Cupra Maritima was a coastal city of Picenum (regio V) assigned to the tribus Velina.

properties.title: Himella (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Himella fl.

properties.title: Luni sul Mignone
properties.description: Luni sul Mignone is a site with archaeological evidence for habitation in the later second millennium BC, continuing into the Italian Iron Age. Excavations conducted by the Swedish Institute in Rome (1960-1963) exposed three phases of settlement activity.

properties.title: Falisci
properties.description: The name for a group of Italic people who occupied the Ager Faliscus within Etruria.

properties.title: Marrucini
properties.description: The Marrucini were an Italic tribe centered around Teate in the Abruzzo. In conflict with Rome through the end of the Second Samnite War, the Marrucini became allied with Rome thereafter. Their language was likely in the Sabellic family.

properties.title: Roman villa of Cortijo Robledo
properties.description: A Roman villa rustica dated between the first and fifth centuries. The site occupies a low hill located to the south of Cerro de Robledo, near the Roman settlement of Aratispi. Archaeological fieldwork has demonstrated that the site was involved in the production of olive oil until the later Roman period.

properties.title: Triumphal Arch of Orange
properties.description: A triumphal arch most likely built during the reign of Augustus to honor veterans of the Gallic Wars and Legio II Augusta.

properties.title: Villa S. Silvestro
properties.description: The remains of a Republican temple podium now support a Christian church at Villa S. Silvestro in Umbria. The temple's podium likely dates, in its first phase, to the third century B.C.

properties.title: Vomanus (river)
properties.description: The Vomano river in Abruzzo flows into the Adriatic Sea.

properties.title: Sarsina
properties.description: Sarsina was a town of the Umbri that was captured by Cornelius Scipio in 271 B.C. and was the birthplace of the Latin author Plautus. The necropolis at Sarsina has been extensively studied.

properties.title: Tres Tabernae
properties.description: An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: near Trevi.

properties.title: Trasumennus L.
properties.description: Trasumennus L. (Lake Trasimeno) is the largest lake of the Italian peninsula and the site of a major engagement of the Second Punic War on June 21, 217 B.C.

properties.title: Sena Gallica
properties.description: Located at the mouth of the river Misa, Sena Gallica was founded by the Senonian Gauls in the fourth century B.C. and became the site of Rome's earliest Adriatic colony before 280 B.C. Pompeius Magnus destroyed the city in 82 B.C.

properties.title: Volsiniensis L.
properties.description: A volcanic lake of northern Latium formed by the collapse of the Vulsini volcano. Roman sources record volcanic activity at the site as late as the second century B.C.

properties.title: Tadinae
properties.description: Tadinae (Sant'Antonio della Rasina to the west of Gualdo Tadino) is an ancient municipium of Umbria and was a road station on the Via Flaminia.

properties.title: Superaequum
properties.description: One of three towns of the Paeligni which possessed municipal rights.

properties.title: Velini L.
properties.description: In the Roman period the Lacus Velinus was a larger body of water than the surviving remnant that is now known as Lake Piediluco. Modern intervention drained water away from the lake into the lower Nera River.

properties.title: Vadimonis (lake)
properties.description: A partially dry lake of ancient Etruria near Orte. The Romans were victorious in two battles fought against the Etruscans there (310 and 283 BC).

properties.title: Talamone
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A3 Talamone

properties.title: Urvinum Mataurense
properties.description: Urvinum Mataurense (modern Urbino).

properties.title: Volsinii
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Volsinii

properties.title: Senones
properties.description: An ancient Gallic tribe that entered Italy after 400 BC and settled on the Adriatic coast from Forlì to Ancona, marking the so-called Ager Gallicus.

properties.title: Traianus?
properties.description: A Roman villa that is typically associated with the emperor Trajan.

properties.title: Trebula Mutuesca
properties.description: Trebula Mutuesca or Trebula Mutusca was one of two Sabine cities bearing the name Trebula.

properties.title: Sarteano
properties.description: Sarteano is located between the Val d'Orcia and the Valdichiana. It is known in particular for its rich evidence of Etruscan funerary culture.

properties.title: Vulci
properties.description: Vulci (originally Velch or Velx in Etruscan) was an Etruscan city 80 km northwest of Rome. Vulci was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae.

properties.title: Villalfonsina
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 H4 Villalfonsina

properties.title: Tetricus (mountains)
properties.description: A mountain group in Italy, part of the central Apennines, the Tetricus mons is known today as the Monti Sibillini (Sibylline Mountains).

properties.title: Spoletium
properties.description: An ancient city along the route of the Via Flaminia; an initial colony was established there in 241 BC.

properties.title: Vettona
properties.description: Vettona (modern Bettona) is an ancient settlement of Umbria located between Perusia and Mevania. Pliny the Elder lists it among the municipalities of Umbria, and it also numbered as one of the “xv Populi Umbriae".

properties.title: Vicus Novus/Ad Novas
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Vicus Novus/Ad Novas

properties.title: Tinna (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F2 Tinna fl.

properties.title: Settefinestre
properties.description: A Late Republican Roman slave-run villa owned by the senatorial family of the Volusii.

properties.title: Soracte (mountain)
properties.description: Soracte M. (Monte Soratte) is a mountain near Rome, Italy, the highest peak of which rises to 691 masl (2,267 ft). A site of ritual activity in antiquity, the mountain was sacred to Dis Pater.

properties.title: Tinea (river)
properties.description: The Topino river in Umbria.

properties.title: Tuscana
properties.description: An ancient city that traced its legendary origins to Ascanius, son of Aeneas. The site became an important Etruscan mercantile center and eventually achieved Roman municipal status in 88 B.C.

properties.title: S. Pier Maggiore
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A1 S. Pier Maggiore

properties.title: Zerninus? (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Zerninus? fl.

properties.title: Vignanello
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Vignanello

properties.title: Vestini
properties.description: The Vestini were an ancient tribe of Italy and lived in the southern part of the modern Abruzzo, between the Gran Sasso and the northern bank of the Aterno river. A major center was located at Pitinum.

properties.title: Statonia
properties.description: An ancient city of south Etruria.

properties.title: Umbria (region)
properties.description: The eponymous region of the Umbri, an ancient Italic people who spoke the Umbrian language. The physical geography of the landlocked region is hilly and dominated by the Appennine Mountains.

properties.title: Sorano
properties.description: Sorano was a Villanovan and, later, Etruscan settlement.

properties.title: Vespasiae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vespasiae

properties.title: Statulae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Statulae

properties.title: Septempeda
properties.description: Septempeda was an ancient settlement of Picenum. Its Roman phase began as a conciliabulum in the third century B.C.

properties.title: Tirinus (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Tirinus fl.

properties.title: Tuficum
properties.description: Tuficum was an ancient city of Umbria located on the Aesis river. It became a municipium of the tribus Oufentina.

properties.title: S. Valentino
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 S. Valentino

properties.title: Vicarello
properties.description: A large, Roman imperial estate covering ca. 2,000 ha on the shores of Lake Bracciano. The name may derive from Vicus Aurelius, suggesting a connection with Marcus Aurelius.

properties.title: Tifernum Mataurense
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Tifernum Mataurense

properties.title: Vicus Martis
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vicus Martis

properties.title: Vicus Matrini
properties.description: Vicus Matrini was a mansio along the Via Cassia, located between Sutri and Forum Cassi. The site's name is attested on the Peutinger Table.

properties.title: Tifernum Tiberinum
properties.description: An Umbrian hilltown in the floodplain of the Tiber river north of Perusia.

properties.title: S. Vittore
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 S. Vittore

properties.title: Tuder
properties.description: Tuder, modern Todi, is an ancient city of Umbria. Its foundation likely occurred during the eighth/seventh centuries BC, although legendary traditions associate the site with the activities of Herakles.

properties.title: Tiora Matiene
properties.description: Tiora Matiene was the site of an ancient oracle of the god Mars. The Barrington Atlas tentatively placed it at modern Teora, near Barete.

properties.title: Sestinum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Sestinum

properties.title: *Umbro (river)
properties.description: The Ambra flows from the foot of Monte Luco to the Arno river.

properties.title: Tessuinus (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Tessuinus fl.

properties.title: Suana
properties.description: Suana (Sovana) has Etruscan origins but later became a Roman municipium. In the fifth century A.D. it became an episcopal see.

properties.title: Verucchio
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Verucchio

properties.title: Sorrina
properties.description: Sorrina was a small Etruscan settlement on Viterbo's Colle di San Lorenzo, of which some traces remain. Epigraphic evidence also attests to a Roman municipium - Surrina Nova - that was likely located between Viterbo and Lake Bullicame.

properties.title: Sentinum
properties.description: An ancient town in the region of Italy now known as Le Marche, Sentinum is perhaps best known for the pivotal Battle of Sentinum of the Third Samnite War that took place nearby in 295 BC.

properties.title: Tolenus (river)
properties.description: A river of Lazio and Abruzzo that is a tributary of the Velino.

properties.title: Truentus (river)
properties.description: A river of Picenum that flows from its source on the Gran Sasso d'Italia to the Adriatic Sea at Porto d'Ascoli.

properties.title: Sutrium
properties.description: An ancient settlement along the line of what would become the Roman Via Cassia and described by Livy, together with Nepet, as one of the keys to Etruria. A Latin colony was founded at the site after the fall of Veii.

properties.title: Visentium
properties.description: Visentium (Bisenzio) was an Etruscan settlement located on the shores of Lago di Bolsena. The site has yielded especially important evidence for Iron Age and Etruscan period burials.

properties.title: Vacchereccia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Vacchereccia

properties.title: Trebiae
properties.description: Trebiae was an ancient city of Umbria (regio IV) located near the line of the Via Flaminia.

properties.title: Velzna/*Volsinii Veteres/Urbiventus
properties.description: Volsinii Veteres was one of the most powerful and important cities of Etruria, as it was the location of the important federal sanctuary located at the Fanum Voltumnae.

properties.title: Suasa
properties.description: Suasa was the site of a Roman municipium in Umbria. It lies in the Piano Volpello along a road from Cales to Sena Gallica. Alaric razed the settlement in 409.

properties.title: Tarchna/Tarquinii
properties.description: An ancient city of Etruria and the leading city of the doudecim populi Etruriae, Tarquinia (called Tarch(u)na or Tarchna in Etruscan) was a major urban center of ancient Italy.

properties.title: Urvinum Hortense
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Urvinum Hortense

properties.title: Urbs Salvia
properties.description: An ancient city of Regio V (Picenum) where a Roman colony was founded in the second century B.C.

properties.title: Teate
properties.description: Originally named Teate Marrucinorum, Teate (modern Chieti) was the principal settlement of the Marrucini. Strabo attributes its origins to Arcadian Greeks.

properties.title: Succosa
properties.description: Succosa was located between the Portus Cosanus and the Via Aurelia Antica to the north. It is mentioned in the Itineraries and located on the Tabula Peutingeriana. F.E. Brown suggests that Succosa, derived from "sub-Cosa", emerges in the first century B.C. following the decline of the hill-top colony. It may also be the "Respublica Cosanorum" that is mentioned in Severan inscriptions known from the hill-top town.

properties.title: Velini (lake)
properties.description: A lake formed by three rivers (Avens, Himella and Tolenus) in the territory of the Sabines.

properties.title: Sena (river)
properties.description: The Nevola river.

properties.title: Trea
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Trea

properties.title: Vittorito
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Vittorito

properties.title: Volusii
properties.description: A villa associated with the Volusii Saturnini built ca. 50 B.C.

properties.title: Sappinates?
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Sappinates?

properties.title: Trevignano
properties.description: Trevignano Romano, located on the shores of Lake Bracciano, lies some 47 km from Rome. Archaeological evidence for Etruscan occupation, in the form of tombs dating to the eighth - sixth centuries B.C., has been discovered to the north of the modern town. A medieval castle was built there under Innocent III ca. 1200.

properties.title: Tolentinum
properties.description: Tolentinum was a town of Picenum that is listed as having municipal status in the Liber Coloniarum.

properties.title: Sepernates?
properties.description: An ancient people of Etruria inhabiting the area around Nazzano Romano.

properties.title: Ben Shemen Forest
properties.description: Ben Shemen Forest is the largest forest in Central Israel and it contains several archaeological sites, including Bir a Shemi, Tel Gimzo, Tel Hadid, and several Hasmonean-period tombs.

properties.title: Negub tunnel
properties.description: The Negub tunnel was part of an irrigation system that supported the Assyrian royal city of Nimrud.

properties.title: Sur Jureh
properties.description: Sur Jureh (also Sur Jurʿeh, Sūr Ğurʿa) is a site in the middle Euphrates region in what was part of the ancient kingdom of Suhu. The city, which is probably to be identified with ancient Gabbāri-bānî (or Gabbāri-ibni), was situated on the north bank of the Euphrates, opposite Gleieh (which lies on the southern bank). Like many towns and cities of the ancient kingdom of Suhu, Sur Jureh/Gabbāri-bānî is now underwater; the area was flooded after the construction of the Haditha dam.

properties.title: Pol-e Dokhtar
properties.description: Pol-e Dokhtar (also Romanized as Pol Dokhtar and Pul-i-Dukhtar) is a city in the Lorestan Province of Iran. The ruins of a Sasanian bridge over the Kashkan River are still visible today a few kilometers north of the city; that structure was part of a Sasanian Royal road that connected the Persian capitals Istakhr and Bishapur with towns in central and northern Mesopotamia. In 1992, a horde of ancient objects were found in the nearby Cave Kalmakareh (also referred to as Cave Kalmakarra).

properties.title: Al-Ghab
properties.description: The al-Ghab (also el-Ghab) plain is located in northwest Syria, in the Al-Suqaylabiyah District.

properties.title: S. Casciano dei Bagni
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 S. Casciano dei Bagni

properties.title: Quinto Fiorentino
properties.description: Quinto Fiorentino is a place located in the plain of the Arno River to the west of Florence. Its location corresponds to the fifth mile of the Roman road. The site is especially known for two Etruscan tholos-type tombs a thòlos, one of which is the Tomba della Mula, and the other the Tomba della Montagnola.

properties.title: Ostra
properties.description: Ostra was an ancient town of Umbria.

properties.title: Pallia (river)
properties.description: The Pallia is a tributary of the Tiber river.

properties.title: Monti della Tolfa
properties.description: Monti della Tolfa, a volcanic group of mountains in the Anti-Apennines in the northern part of Lazio in central Italy.

properties.title: Minio (river)
properties.description: A river that flows some 62 km from the Monti Sabatini to the Tyrrhenian Sea.

properties.title: Pinna
properties.description: Pinna (modern Penne) was a center of the Vestini. The site came under Roman control after the Social War (89 BC).

properties.title: Nelurus (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Nelurus fl.

properties.title: Prolaqueum
properties.description: A statio on the road from Nuceria to Ancona.

properties.title: Planina
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Planina

properties.title: Ortona
properties.description: An ancient site in Italy that most likely originates with the Frentani.

properties.title: Pitino
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Pitino

properties.title: Pitigliano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Pitigliano

properties.title: Naharcer
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Naharcer

properties.title: Osa (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A3 Osa fl.

properties.title: Pitinum Pisaurense
properties.description: An ancient settlement in Umbria, known mostly via its inclusion in the texts of Pliny the Elder and Ptolemy, as well as by means of various epigraphic evidence.

properties.title: Nemora Vacunae
properties.description: Shrine dedicated to a rural divinity of the Sabina.

properties.title: Pieve Socana
properties.description: Pieve di Sant'Antonino a Socana, a Medieval parish church, is built atop the remains of an Etruscan sanctuary.

properties.title: Misco? (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Misco? fl.

properties.title: Pallanum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G4 Pallanum

properties.title: Raiano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Raiano

properties.title: S. Erasmo di Cesi
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 S. Erasmo di Cesi

properties.title: Quintianum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Quintianum

properties.title: Nepet
properties.description: Nepet had become a Roman town before 396 B.C. when Livy dubs it, along with Sutrium, as one of the "keys" to Etruria. It became a Roman colony in 383 B.C. and a municipium after the Social War.

properties.title: Praetuttii
properties.description: The Praetuttii were an ancient tribe of central Italy.

properties.title: Plestinus L.
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D2 Plestinus L.

properties.title: Pescara
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Pescara

properties.title: Montedoro di Scapezzano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E1 Montedoro di Scapezzano

properties.title: Numana
properties.description: Numana was a settlement of ancient Picenum located south of Ancona.

properties.title: Sabatinus lacus
properties.description: A volcanic lake in Latium north of Rome (modern Lago di Bracciano).

properties.title: Rosia Campus
properties.description: A plain in the territory of the Sabines near Reate, reputed to have the most fertile soils in Italy.

properties.title: Ponte a Buriano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Ponte a Buriano

properties.title: Passo Corese
properties.description: Passo Corese is located near Cures (Fara in Sabina). The site is often connected with Titus Tatius' march on Rome in 747 B.C.

properties.title: Montelibretti
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Montelibretti

properties.title: Misus (river)
properties.description: A river that flows from just south of Arcevia to the Adriatic Sea. The Nevola river joined the Misa before it drains into the sea near Senigallia.

properties.title: Picenum (region)
properties.description: Picenum was a region of Central Italy, extending along the coast of the Adriatic Sea from the mouth of the Aesis to that of the Matrinus, and inland as far as the central Apennines.

properties.title: Piano Tondo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Piano Tondo

properties.title: Mola di Monte Gelato
properties.description: An ancient settlement 30 km north of Rome that was excavated from 1986-90. An imperial villa existed on the site up until the third century AD.

properties.title: Monterano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Monterano

properties.title: Palmensis Ager
properties.description: Pliny the Elder discusses the Palmensis Ager in connection with his description of the Praetutii.

properties.title: Rostrata Villa
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Rostrata Villa

properties.title: Polimartium
properties.description: An ancient Roman settlement (modern Bomarzo in Italy)

properties.title: Sabini
properties.description: The Sabini (Sabines) were an Italic tribe of central Italy and belonged to the Osco-Umbrian language group. Their territory straddled parts of the modern regions of Lazio, Umbria, and the Abruzzo. Ancient writers connect them with Rome at the time of its foundation, as represented by the episode of the 'rape of the Sabine women' reported by various ancient authors.

properties.title: Nursia
properties.description: Nursia was the northernmost city of the Sabines.

properties.title: Monte S. Angelo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Monte S. Angelo

properties.title: Perusia
properties.description: A city of ancient Umbrian and Etruscan origin, Perusia aided Rome during the Second Punic War but was sieged and reduced by Octavian in the first century B.C. during campaigns against Lucius Antonius. It was rebuilt by Augustus and became Colonia Vibia Augusta Perusia quite late, in A.D. 251-3, under Trebonianus Gallus.

properties.title: [Orcla]
properties.description: [Orcla] or Norchia is an ancient Etruscan settlement located near Tarquinia and along the line of the Roman Via Clodia.

properties.title: Plestia
properties.description: Plestia was a municipium of the tribus Ufentina.

properties.title: Potentia
properties.description: A city settled in an area subjugated by Rome during the fourth century B.C. The local populace rebelled against Rome after the defeat at Cannae (216 B.C.), however the defeat of the Carthaginians eventually led to Potentia's reincorporation into the Roman sphere.

properties.title: Nequinum/Narnia
properties.description: Nequinum/Narnia (modern Narni) was an ancient settlement in Umbria. It became a Latin colony in 299 BC.

properties.title: Poggio Sommavilla
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Poggio Sommavilla

properties.title: Rusellae
properties.description: An Etruscan city captured by Rome in 294 B.C., Rusellae's >2 mile circuit of megalithic walls represent an important early instance of stone fortification walling in the Italian peninsula.

properties.title: Novilara
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Novilara

properties.title: Phalacrinae
properties.description: A Roman town in which the emperor Vespasian was born in A.D. 9.

properties.title: Montariolo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Montariolo

properties.title: Monteferetra
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Monteferetra

properties.title: Peltuinum
properties.description: Peltuinum was a settlement of the Vestini located along the Via Claudia Nova. The town is notable as the birthplace of the Roman general Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo.

properties.title: Regis Villa/Regae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Regis Villa/Regae

properties.title: Sacraria
properties.description: A station on the Via Flaminia near Le Vene.

properties.title: Saena
properties.description: Saena was an Etruscan city that received a Roman colony (Saena Iulia) in the time of Augustus.

properties.title: Respampani
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Respampani

properties.title: Pausulae
properties.description: Pausulae was a town of Picenum mentioned by Pliny the Elder. It was a Municipium of Regio V.

properties.title: Montefortino
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D2 Montefortino

properties.title: Monte Calvo
properties.description: The remains of a Roman villa that belonged to the family of the Bruttii Praesentes were found in the locality known as 'Madonna dei Colori' near the ancient road station Vicus Novus/Ad Novas, modern Osteria Nuova, some 53 km northeast of Rome.

properties.title: Nuceria
properties.description: Nuceria (modern Nocera Umbra) is an ancient town in Umbria, perhaps founded in the seventh century B.C. by Camerinum.

properties.title: Ponte Capo d’Acqua
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Ponte Capo d’Acqua

properties.title: Poggio Buco
properties.description: Poggio Buco was a pre-Roman site located in the valley of the Fiora river. Its archaeological remains include those of a circuit wall and a necropolis. The archaeological site is located ca. 9 km west of Pitigliano.

properties.title: Ocriculum
properties.description: An ancient Umbrian city that became allied with Rome in 308 B.C.

properties.title: Pisaurus (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Pisaurus fl.

properties.title: Mevania
properties.description: Mevania (modern Bevagna) was a Roman municipium in Umbria located on the Via Flaminia. The town was enrolled in the tribus Aemilia.

properties.title: Poggio Civitate (Murlo)
properties.description: An Etruscan elite complex of the seventh and sixth centuries B.C. located at Poggio Civitate, a hill adjacent to the medieval town of Murlo and about 25 km south of Siena.

properties.title: Paganica
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Paganica

properties.title: Rapinium
properties.description: Rapinium is located on the coast of Etruria between Centumcellae and Graviscae, at modern Bagni Sant'Agostino.

properties.title: Sagrus (river)
properties.description: A river of eastern Italy (modern Sangro).

properties.title: Ossaia
properties.description: Site of a Late Republican and Imperial Roman villa (first to fifth centuries A.D.)

properties.title: Pitinum Mergens
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Pitinum Mergens

properties.title: Qatna
properties.description: A city in western Syria first settled in the Early Bronze Age III (ca. 2700-2600 BCE). In the Middle Bronze Age (2000-1600 BCE), it became a major trading center and the capital of a regional kingdom. In the Late Bronze Age Qatna the city became a vassal of first the Mitanni Kingdom, then the Neo-Hittite Empire and Egypt. The city's acropolis was abandoned in the Late Bronze Age I, though the surrounding area remained inhabited. It was resettled in the 10th century BCE as part of the Aramaean kingdom of Hamath, but was sacked by the army of Sargon II in 720 and ultimately abandoned in the 6th century BCE.

properties.title: Central Palace at Kalhu
properties.description: The eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III (r. 744–727 BC) built himself a grand, ornately-decorated royal residence at Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud). This (large) palatial complex, which included a pillared-portico (a bīt-ḫilāni), was constructed south of the Northwest Palace (built by Ashurnasirpal II [r. 883–859 BC]). The “Cedar Palace” (as it is referred to in at least one contemporary Akkadian inscription) was largely dismantled by the seventh-century-BC ruler Esarhaddon (r. 680–669 BC), who had its (sculpted and inscribed) limestone slabs reused in his own royal residence (the Southwest Palace). The building is now generally referred to as the “Central Palace,” a modern designation given to it by its excavators since the palace was constructed in the central part of the Kalhu citadel.

properties.title: Southwest Palace at Kalhu
properties.description: The seventh-century-BC Assyrian king Esarhaddon (r. 680–669 BC) started building a royal residence in the southwest corner of the citadel of Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud). Sculpted and inscribed limestone slabs from the Central Palace (constructed by Tiglath-pileser III [r. 744–727 BC]) and the Northwest Palace (built by Ashurnasirpal II [r. 883–859 BC]) were used as building materials for this royal residence, which very likely remained unfinished at the time of Esarhaddon’s death in 669 BC. Its excavators called it the “Southwest Palace” since it was located in the southwest corner of the citadel.
