properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Arretium was built during the late first and early second centuries. It measures 121 by 68 meters.

properties.title: Villa of the Papyri
properties.description: A suburban villa located northwest of Herculaneum that was originally owned by Lucius Calpurnius Piso Caesoninus.

properties.title: San Giacomo di Rialto
properties.description: A church in Venice, Italy. San Giacomo di Rialto is claimed to be the oldest church in the city, with AD 421 as the traditional date of its consecration. The first documented attestations of the church belong to AD 1152.

properties.title: Case Romane del Celio
properties.description: An archaeological area beneath the basilica of the martyrs John and Paul that has been explored by means of excavation, revealing a series of Imperial period domestic remains dating between the second and fourth centuries A.D.

properties.title: Rahi-ilu
properties.description: An unlocated city/town in the kingdom of Suhu that was situated on an island in the Euphrates River.

properties.title: Forum Iulium
properties.description: The Forum Iulium (or Forum of Caesar, Forum Caesaris) is a forum built by Iulius Caesar and dedicated ca. 46 B.C. The main cult of the forum is that of Venus Genetrix.

properties.title: Arènes de Cimiez
properties.description: A Roman amphitheater of the second century that was enlarged during the course of the third, the so-called Arènes de Cimiez measures 67 by 56 meters.

properties.title: Stadium at Aizanoi
properties.description: The Stadium at Aizanoi is adjacent to the theater.

properties.title: Temple de Diane
properties.description: The so-called "Temple de Diane" is a first century Roman monument on the Gard river dedicated to Augustus.

properties.title: Tour Magne
properties.description: Situated atop Mount Cavalier, the so-called "Tour Magne" is a tower on the fortified walls of ancient Nemausus. The tower dates to the time of Augustus.

properties.title: Roman theater of Aspendos
properties.description: The Roman theater at Aspendos dates ca. AD 155 and is perhaps the best preserved example of a Roman theater building.

properties.title: Lion gate of Butrint
properties.description: The so-called "Lion gate" of Butrint is a fifth century A.D. gateway that reuses an Archaic Greek sculpted relief.

properties.title: Northwest Palace at Kalhu
properties.description: An impressive and ornately-decorated palace constructed at Kalḫu (modern Nimrud, biblical Calah) by the ninth-century-BC Assyrian ruler Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC), likely completed between 865 and 869 BC. This multi-winged palatial complex served as the primary residence and chief administrative center of the Assyrian Empire until Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) moved the imperial capital to Dūr-Šarrukīn in 706 BC. The Northwest Palace, the name given to it by its excavators (since it was built in the northwestern part of Kalḫu’s citadel), remained in use until the very end of the Assyrian Empire (612 BC). The southern half of the building also functioned as the burial place of prominent royal women, including Mullissu-mukannišat-Ninua, the wife of Ashurnasirpal and the mother of Shalmaneser III.

properties.title: So-called Temple of Hercules
properties.description: A site on the Via Appia that is likely commercial in nature but that has long been associated with a shrine mentioned by Martial.

properties.title: Pont Romà
properties.description: A Roman bridge on the island of Majorca (Pollença, Mallorca, Spain).

properties.title: Nuraghe Sa Bosa
properties.description: The remains of a nuraghe near an industrial zone near Sassari.

properties.title: Viglafia tower
properties.description: The remains of a square tower in Lakonia.

properties.title: Archaic tholos tomb at Pharsalos
properties.description: Center point of Archaic period tholos tomb of Pharsalos, used until the Hellenistic period.

properties.title: Nuraghe Zuras
properties.description: A later nuragic site, in use from the fourteenth to the twelfth centuries BC.

properties.title: Janiculum
properties.description: This hill is located outside of the ancient city of Rome to the west of the Tiber and is not considered one of the Seven Hills of Rome. From an early stage the Janiculum was connected to the city by fortifications and a bridge over the Tiber. It also was the site of important water-powered mills in the Roman Empire.

properties.description: The Roman city wall of Zaragoza was begun under Tiberius, although work continued through the third century. The wall once stretched some 3,000 meters and had 120 defensive towers.

properties.title: Public Bath of Pella
properties.description: The Public Bath at Pella is a bathing complex constructed and continuously renovated between the 4th and the 1st centuries BCE.

properties.title: Arch of Augustus at Aosta
properties.description: The Arch of Augustus at Aosta is a commemorative arch dedicated to Augustus ca. 25 BC following victories over the Salassi.

properties.title: Arco di Trevi
properties.description: An opus quadratum monument with an arched gateway perhaps marking a boundary between the territory of the Equi and the Hernicans.

properties.title: Italic temple of Castel di Ieri
properties.description: The remains of an Italic temple, in the locality known as "Pié di Francia". The sanctuary dates from the fourth to first centuries B.C.

properties.title: Rablê
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources; the modern site is Riblah, located ca. 35 km south of Ḥomṣ.

properties.title: Villa of Horace
properties.description: The archaeological remains of a villa near Licenza, Italy, that are traditionally connected with the Latin poet Horace.

properties.title: Temple of Ramesses II
properties.description: The Temple of Ramesses II at Abydos in Egypt.

properties.title: Arles Amphitheatre
properties.description: The Arles Roman amphitheater or Arènes d'Arles was built ca. A.D. 90 and could seat over 20,000 spectators.

properties.title: Longula
properties.description: Longula was an early settlement of Latium Vetus, although its location is no longer known. A Volscian city, Longula was first taken by the Romans in 493 B.C. under the consul Postumus Cominius. It subsequently changes hands several times during the fifth and fourth centuries B.C. It likely lay between Ardea and Antium.

properties.title: Corbio
properties.description: Corbio was an ancient city of Latium located on the northeastern flank of the Alban Hills, although its precise location is no longer secure. This Latin city is said to have fallen to the Aequi and then been the subject of contention between the Aequi and the Romans, ultimately recaptured by the latter after Cincinnatus' victory at Mons Algidus in 458 B.C.

properties.title: Capitulum Hernicum
properties.description: A Hernican town that still existed in Pliny's time, Capitulum Hernicum received colonists under both Sulla and Iulius Caesar.

properties.title: Laterium
properties.description: A villa of Q. Tullius Cicero located in the territory of Arpinum, near Cereatae.

properties.title: Cameria
properties.description: An ancient city of Latium that is noted by Pliny the Elder as one of the lost cities of central Italy.

properties.title: Lanuenses
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 unlocated Lanuenses

properties.title: Castrum Invi
properties.description: An Italic site located at the mouth of the Incastro river and in the territory of Ardea.

properties.title: Cominium Ocritum
properties.description: Cominium Ocritum was a Samnite stronghold captured in 291 BC by Quintus Fabius Maximus Gurges.

properties.title: Allia (river)
properties.description: The Allia river was a tributary of the Tiber, but is now unlocated. It joined the Tiber some 18 km (11 miles) north of Rome and was most famous as the site of a battle in which the Romans were defeated by Brennus and the Gauls ca. 387 B.C.

properties.title: Ameriola
properties.description: An ancient town of Latium that was a member of the Latin League. It was located to the northeast of Rome, but its precise location cannot be determined today.

properties.title: Arenata
properties.description: An ancient place mentioned in the correspondence of Pope Gregory the Great (ca.  540 – 12 March 604) wherein Gregory permits the Bishop of Velletri to transfer his seat from Velletri to Arenata. This may refer to the modern comune of Rocca Massima in the Latina province.

properties.title: Arcanum
properties.description: Arcanum was the location of an estate that belonged to Quintus Cicero. it was located between Aquinum and Arpinum.

properties.title: Apiolae
properties.description: An ancient city of Latium that led the Latin resistance against Tarquinius Priscus.

properties.title: Amunclus (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 unlocated Amunclus fl.

properties.title: Tifata (Latium)
properties.description: Tifata is a site in Latium listed as defunct by the elder Pliny. Palmer notes that Festus (43 L) raises the question of an identically named Roman curia.

properties.title: Romulea
properties.description: Now unlocated, Romulea was captured by the Romans during the Third Samnite War.

properties.title: Vicus Palatius
properties.description: A district or small extra-urban settlement, mentioned in an inscription, that seems to have been connected with the Roman colonial foundation at Cales in Campania.

properties.title: Roboaria
properties.description: Now unlocated, Roboaria was a road station of the fifteenth mile of the Via Latina. It was likely sited near Molara and some have suggested a nearby ruin as a possible location.

properties.title: Via Popilia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 unlocated Via Popilia

properties.title: Pedum
properties.description: Pedum was an ancient city of Latium that was part of the Latin League. Located between Tibur and Praeneste, its precise location is now unknown. Some suggest that modern Gallicano is the site of the ancient city.

properties.title: Petrinus Vicus
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 unlocated Petrinus Vicus?

properties.title: Verrugo
properties.description: Verrugo was a Volscian settlement at the borders of Latium. Its location is now uncertain.

properties.title: Pollusca
properties.description: Pollusca was an early city of Latium Vetus connected with Longula and Corioli. These three cities were captured by Coriolanus in 488 BC. The location of Pollusca is no longer known.

properties.title: Tifernum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 unlocated Tifernum

properties.title: Pyramid of Khentkawes
properties.description: Khentkawes I was a queen of the 4th dynasty of ancient Egypt. She may have been a daughter of the pharaoh Menkaure, and the wife of both kings Shepseskaf and Userkaf. Her tomb at Giza – LG100 – is located close to Menkaure's pyramid complex.

properties.title: Uraš Gate
properties.description: The Uraš Gate is one of Babylon's eight city gates and it is situated on the southeastern side of the inner city, directly south of the Šuanna quarter. King Nebuchadnezzar II built the gate ca. 575 B.C.

properties.title: Roman forum at Tergeste
properties.description: The Roman forum of Tergeste.

properties.title: Roman baths at Vertillum
properties.description: The remains of baths at the Gallo-Roman site of Vertillum.

properties.title: Ara della Regina
properties.description: A fourth to third century B.C. sanctuary at Tarquinia.

properties.title: Salteras
properties.description: An ancient and medieval Spanish village located north of Sevilla that belonged to the thirteenth-century kingdom of Alfonso X.

properties.title: Oakmere hill fort
properties.description: Oakmere hill fort is an Iron Age hill fort located in the county of Cheshire in northern England.

properties.title: Aymont
properties.description: A Spanish village that borders Portugal and is located in the southwest of the province of Huenca. Known as Ayamonte today, it once belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X.

properties.title: Andeualo
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the southwest of the province of Huelva that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. It is now known as El Andévalo.

properties.title: Sîn temple (Kalhu)
properties.description: When Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud) became the principal administrative center of the Assyrian Empire in the ninth century BC, king Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) built (or rebuilt) numerous temples. One of those was dedicated to the moon-god Sîn. Although its location is not known, the Sîn temple at Kalhu is thought to have been situated within the Ninurta temple complex, in the northwest corner of the citadel.

properties.title: Ulrichsberg
properties.description: The ruins of a Late Gothic Church of St. Ulrich which gave its name to the mountain on which it stands.

properties.title: Damietta Branch
properties.description: The Damietta branch is an eastern distributary of the Nile Delta and gives its name to an associated settlement.

properties.title: Tell Sukas
properties.description: The ancient Shuksi or Suksi, the archaeological site of Tell Sukas is a Late Bronze Age tell located south of Jableh, Syria. It is situated at the center of the fertile plain of Jableh and had access to two natural harbors.

properties.title: Roman theater at Cádiz
properties.description: The Roman theater at Cádiz was one of the largest in the Roman world, accommodating some 20,000 spectators. It dates originally to the first century B.C. In the thirteenth century it was incorporated into a fortress built by King Alfonso X of Castile.

properties.title: Sacra Via
properties.description: The Sacra Via (Sacred Way) is one of Rome's oldest urban streets and its main sacred route, extending from the top of the Velia (summa Sacra Via) to the Forum Romanum.

properties.title: Roman city gate, Mainz

properties.title: Pandataria (island)
properties.description: An island in the Pontine archipelago of the Tyrrhenian Sea, Pandataria is volcanic in origin and is best known, in historical terms, as the place to which Augustus banished Julia the Elder, his daughter, in 2 BC and to which Tiberius banished Agrippina the Elder in AD 29.

properties.title: Pontia

properties.title: Punta Eolo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D4 Punta Eolo

properties.title: S. Rocco
properties.description: The San Rocco villa was built during the second quarter of the first century B.C. It was initially a simple villa rustica and it was later enlarged substantially.

properties.title: S. Benedictus

properties.description: Also called the Bay of Naples, the Puteolanus Sinus is a gulf located on the southwestern coast of Italy. It opens west to the Mediterranean Sea and is bordered on the east by Mt. Vesuvius and the south by the Sorrentine Peninsula.

properties.description: Samnium is the Latin name for a region of south and central Italy inhabited by the Samnites. The geographic limits of this region prior to sustained Roman contact are poorly defined. With the Augustan reorganization of Italy, the pre-Roman Samnium is subdivided among three of the Augustan regions.

properties.title: Roman villa at Positano
properties.description: An opulent Roman villa maritima destroyed by the A.D. 79 eruption of Vesuvius. The remains of an opulent and well-decorated Roman villa have been known at Positano since at least 1758 when ruins were discovered during work on the bell tower of the church of S. Maria Assunta. Karl Weber conducted excavations there in the same year. Modern work, begun in 1999, has stabilized and consolidated the site.

properties.title: Misenum (promontory)
properties.description: A promontory that sheltered the ancient Portus Julius, the harborage of the Roman western imperial fleet. The feature takes its name from Misenus, one of the sailors aboard Aeneas' ship.

properties.description: Minori is the site of a major villa located on the Amalfi coast, some 11 km WSW of Salerno. Destroyed by a possible landslide, the villa was in use from the Iulio-Claudian period through to the Flavian period.

properties.title: Nola
properties.description: The city of Nola (Nuvlana) is considered one of the oldest in Campania. Under Augustus the settlement became a Roman colony; it was the spot where Augustus died in A.D. 14.

properties.description: The hamlet of Malborghetto, located on the ancient Via Flaminia, is traditionally linked with Constantine the Great and his visions of victory that occurred prior to the battle of Saxa Rubra on 28 October A.D. 312. The quadrifons arch, dating to the fourth century, marks the intersection of the Via Flaminia and the Via Tiberina.

properties.title: Latium Adiectum
properties.description: A region of ancient Italy characterized as an area of Latin colonial expansion; also referred to as Latium Novum.

properties.title: Minturnae
properties.description: Originally an Ausonian town that fought against Rome in 314 B.C., Minturnae became a colony in 296 B.C. The site is located on the Garigliano river (ancient Liris) and served an important economic function. The Via Appia passes through the city.

properties.title: Montevetrano

properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Monte del Fico

properties.title: Oplontis
properties.description: An ancient place (modern Torre Annunziata in Italy), lying between Pompeii and Herculaneum and buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE. Its ancient name is known only from Peutinger's Roman Map.

properties.title: Nuceria (Alfaterna)
properties.description: Nuceria (Alfaterna) (modern Nocera Inferiore) is an ancient settlement in Campania. In pre-Roman times this was the chief settlement of the Sarnus river valley.

properties.title: Ligures Baebiani
properties.description: Ligures Baebiani was a Ligurian settlement in Samnium.

properties.title: Monte Cila

properties.title: Monte Castellone (Torcino)
properties.description: A fortified center located in the comune of Ciorlano.

properties.title: Liternum
properties.description: An ancient city of Campania located near the mouth of the Volturnus river; a Roman colony was established at Liternum in 194 B.C. The site is most famous as the location of the villa of Scipio Africanus, as described by Seneca.

properties.title: Massicus
properties.description: Mons Massicus, a mountain ridge of ancient Italy, in the territory of the Aurunci, at the border of Latium and Campania.

properties.title: Marruvium
properties.description: Ancient Marruvium was the principal city of the Italic tribe of the Marsi.

properties.title: Monteverde
properties.description: The eleventh century monastery of Santa Maria di Monteverde sits atop and reuses elements of Roman and pre-Roman settlements on the hilltop.

properties.title: Aufidena
properties.description: A probable Samnite center, the Romans captured Aufidena in 298 BC. It only became a municipium after 49 B.C.

properties.title: Castrum Novum
properties.description: Castrum Novum was a colonia maritima established on the coast of Etruria.

properties.title: Bovianum
properties.description: Bovianum was a Samnite center and the capital of the Pentri tribe. It received Roman municipium status ca. 87 B.C. By the late first century A.D. it was occupied by veterans of Legio XI and known as the "colonia Bovianum Undecimanoruin".

properties.title: Caiatia
properties.description: A Samnite town that eventually became a Roman municipium of the tribus Falerna ca. 89 B.C.

properties.title: Casinum
properties.description: A Volscian hilltop settlement that became a Roman colony in 312 B.C.

properties.title: Aversa
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Aversa

properties.title: Campi Phlegraei
properties.description: The Campi Phlegraei (Phlegraean Fields) is a large caldera (13 km wide) in the Bay of Naples region of Italy. In total, the the area comprises 24 craters, although a good portion of the caldera now lies under water. The area was important in Greek and Roman times; the Greeks established their first mainland colony at Cumae within the Campi Phlegraei.

properties.title: Capreae (island)
properties.description: An island of the Bay of Naples off the Sorrentine Peninsula that has, since the time of the Roman Republic, been a popular seaside resort area. The emperor Tiberius maintained twelve villas on the island.

properties.title: Atella (Campania)
properties.description: A city of Campania located between Capua and Neapolis.

properties.title: Cocullo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Cocullo

properties.title: Caecubus Ager
properties.description: A tract of Latium that bordered the Gulf of Amyclae, lying in the territory of Fundi.

properties.title: Cliternia

properties.title: Clanius (river)
properties.description: A river of Campania that likely flowed into the Tyrrhenian Sea near Liternum.

properties.title: Capriati
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Capriati

properties.title: Campobasso
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Campobasso

properties.title: Avernus L.
properties.description: A volcanic crater lake located in the Phlegraean Fields, Lake Avernus served a major ritual role for ancient Romans and Greeks as they viewed it as an entrance to Hades.

properties.title: Boscotrecase
properties.description: Located on the southern slopes of Vesuvius, Boscotrecase is a Campanian site destroyed by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79. Numerous opulent villas are known in the area by way of archaeological exploration.

properties.title: Caudium
properties.description: A city of Samnium located between Capua and Beneventum. In 321 B.C. the Samnites under C. Pontius encamped there before defeating the Romans at the battle of the Caudine Forks.

properties.title: Atina
properties.description: Atina was a Samnite hill town with a polygonal masonry fortification wall.

properties.title: Capo di Sorrento
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Capo di Sorrento

properties.title: Campania
properties.description: Campania was a region of southern Italy.

properties.title: Capua
properties.description: An important ancient city of Campania with Villanovan and Etruscan origins.

properties.title: Astura
properties.description: Astura was once a coastal island of Latium and is now a small peninsula at the southeastern edge of the Bay of Antium.

properties.title: Chiauci
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Chiauci

properties.title: Colle Tassito
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Colle Tassito

properties.title: Cales
properties.description: Cales was an ancient city of Campania of Ausonian origins. The Romans captured the town in 335 B.C. and established a colony there.

properties.title: Kirkaion Akron/Veneris Pr.
properties.description: Kirkaion Akron/Veneris Pr. (Monte Circeo) is a mountainous promontory on the Tyrrhenian coast of Italy.

properties.title: Boscoreale
properties.description: A settled area of Campania that is especially well known for the Roman country villas of the first century BC that were destroyed by the eruption of Vesuvius in A.D. 79.

properties.title: Caieta Pr.
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Caieta Pr.

properties.title: Cascano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Cascano

properties.title: Casilinum
properties.description: A settlement located in the border region between the ager Falernus and the ager Campanus, north of Capua.

properties.title: Caieta
properties.description: Caieta was a town of ancient Latium located on the Tyrrhenian Sea coast between Tarracina and Formiae.

properties.title: Carovilli
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Carovilli

properties.title: Calatia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Calatia

properties.title: Colle Sparanise
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Colle Sparanise

properties.title: Arx Fregellana
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Arx Fregellana

properties.title: Carecini Infernates
properties.description: Carecini Infernates, one of the four ancient tribes that made up the Samnite population.

properties.title: Campanus Ager
properties.description: The Campanus Ager was the region around Capua that the Romans confiscated in 211 B.C. during the Second Punic War.

properties.title: Circeii 2
properties.description: A port on the Tyrrhenian coast. In myth, the site was considered to be one of the stopping points of the hero Odysseus.

properties.title: Carecini Supernates
properties.description: The Carecini Supernates were a tribe of Samnites.

properties.title: Baianus Sinus
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Baianus Sinus

properties.title: Carsioli
properties.description: An ancient settlement along the Via Valeria, Carsioli was established as a Latin colony in the territory of the Aequi ca. 298 BC.

properties.title: Callifae?
properties.description: A city of the Samnites that, according to Livy, was captured by the Romans in Republican times. Probably at or in the vicinity of modern Roccavecchia di Pratella in Italy.

properties.title: Beneventum/Maleventum
properties.description: Beneventum/Maleventum (modern Benevento) was an ancient city of Campania of Samnite origin.

properties.title: Colles Leucogaei
properties.description: A name for volcanic hills of a whitish hue around Puteoli.

properties.title: Cereatae Marianae
properties.description: Cereatae Marianae, purported to have been the birthplace of Gaius Marius, is thought to have been located where the 13th century abbey church of Casamari now stands (in the modern province of Frosinone, Lazio, Italy).

properties.title: Cerfennia
properties.description: A settlement of the Marsi and a Roman road station on the Via Valeria.

properties.title: Bauli
properties.description: Bauli (near modern Bacoli) was an ancient settlement of the Campi Phlegraei.

properties.title: Baiae
properties.description: A Roman seaside community on the Bay of Naples that included thermal springs.

properties.title: Calor (river)
properties.description: A river of Samnium and a major tributary of the Volturno river.

properties.title: Arpinum
properties.description: An ancient center that originated as early as the seventh century B.C. that became a civitas sine suffragio in 305 B.C. Arpinum was the birthplace of Caius Marius and Marcus Tullius Cicero.

properties.title: Colle Mitra
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Colle Mitra

properties.title: Circeii 1
properties.description: Circeii received a Latin colony ca. 390 B.C. The remains on the site include an enclosure wall built in polygonal masonry. "Circeii 1" refers to the earlier Roman colony founded at the eastern side of Monte Circeo. The settlement eventually moved to the western side of the peninsula.

properties.title: Cluturnum
properties.description: Cluturnum was a site in Samnium, located near Aesernia. Its exact location cannot be determined.

properties.title: Castellina
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 A1 Castellina

properties.title: Buca
properties.description: Buca was an ancient settlement of the Frentani.

properties.title: Castro dei Volsci
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D3 Castro dei Volsci

properties.title: Atessa
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F1 Atessa

properties.title: Aurunci
properties.description: The Aurunci were an Italic tribe of south Italy. Their territory was incorporated into the Roman territory in the fourth century B.C.

properties.title: Campus Stellas
properties.description: The name for a region of Campania that adjoined the Ager Falernus.

properties.title: Capreae
properties.description: Settlement on the island of Capreae.

properties.title: Civitanova
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Civitanova

properties.title: Castropignano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Castropignano

properties.title: Caedicius? Campus
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Caedicius? Campus

properties.title: Clostra (Romana)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 C3 Clostra (Romana)

properties.title: Angitiae Lucus
properties.description: Angitiae Lucus refers to the grave of Angitia, a divine figure of the Marsi tribe.

properties.title: Acerrae
properties.description: Acerrae was an ancient Oscan city of Campania, perhaps originally named Akeru. The Romans granted it civitas sine suffragio in 332 BC.

properties.title: Agnone
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Agnone

properties.title: Abella
properties.description: Abella was an ancient settlement of Campania of Samnite origin.

properties.title: Aquinum
properties.description: Aquinum was a municipium by the time of Cicero. It was thought to be the place of birth for the satirist Juvenal and the emperor Pescennius Niger.

properties.title: Apollo et Nymphae Nitrodes, T.
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E4 Apollo et Nymphae Nitrodes, T.

properties.title: Ad Teglanum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Ad Teglanum

properties.title: Ad Septimum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Ad Septimum

properties.title: Ad Octavum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Ad Octavum

properties.title: Aquae Sinuessanae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Aquae Sinuessanae

properties.title: Alfedena
properties.description: A Samnite settlement occupying a strategic location in the valley of the Sangro river.

properties.title: Amalfitana Civitas
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Amalfitana Civitas

properties.title: Ad Flexum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Ad Flexum

properties.title: Amasenus (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D3 Amasenus fl.

properties.title: Aquae Caeretanae
properties.description: Therapeutic springs located near Caere.

properties.title: Ad Medias
properties.description: Ad Medias was a mutatio on the ancient Via Appia. It was located at the halfway point of the so-called Decennovium.

properties.title: Aquae Vescinae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Aquae Vescinae

properties.title: Ad Turres Albas
properties.description: Ad Turres Albas lay on the Via Severiana, midway between Circeii and Astura.

properties.title: Aesernia
properties.description: An ancient settlement (modern Isernia in Italy)

properties.title: Amplero
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Amplero

properties.title: Aletrium
properties.description: A Hernican hill town that formed part of a sixth century B.C. defensive league against Volscian and Samnite aggression and allied itself to Tarquinius Superbus. Rome eventually took Aletrium in 306 B.C.; by the first century B.C. the site was a Roman municipium.

properties.title: Ad Quartum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Ad Quartum

properties.title: Aenaria/Pithekoussai (island)
properties.description: Aenaria/Pithekoussai Ins. (modern Ischia) is a volcanic island located in the northern part of the Bay of Naples.

properties.title: Aequana
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Aequana

properties.title: Alfaterni
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Alfaterni

properties.title: Acqua Claudia
properties.description: A Roman villa at Anguillara Sabazia that may have been built in order to take advantage of mineral springs. The villa dates to the Late Republican period but has only been partially excavated. A large hemicycle with ambulatio is extant; this feature may have been coordinated with the villa's garden.

properties.title: Amyclanus Sinus
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Amyclanus Sinus

properties.title: Ad Rotas/Rotae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Ad Rotas/Rotae

properties.title: Al(l)ifae
properties.description: An ancient town of either Oscan or Samnite origin situated in the Volturno river valley.

properties.title: Afragola
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Afragola

properties.title: Agellum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Agellum

properties.title: Ad Turres
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D3 Ad Turres

properties.title: Antinum
properties.description: A town of the Marsi in the valley of the Liris river.

properties.title: Abellinum
properties.description: Abellinum was a settlement of the Hirpini in Campania.

properties.title: Acherusia Palus
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Acherusia Palus

properties.title: Epomeus M.
properties.description: The highest mountain on the island of Ischia.

properties.title: Gaurus M.
properties.description: An eruptive volcanic vent in the Phlegraean Fields.

properties.title: Lactarius (mountain)
properties.description: A mountain ridge of Campania that is a spur branching off of the Apennines. Many Roman villas in this vicinity were preserved by the eruption of Mt. Vesuvius.

properties.title: Imeus (mountain)
properties.description: Imeus Mons is the name given in the Peutinger Table to a pass that leads from the Fucine lake to the territory of the Peligni; the Via Valeria crossed the pass which is now known as the Forca Caruso.

properties.title: Furculae Caudinae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G3 Furculae Caudinae

properties.title: Duronia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Duronia

properties.title: Lago di Paola
properties.description: A villa of the emperor Domitian located in the area of Circeii.

properties.title: *Lavernae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 *Lavernae

properties.title: Herculis Petra
properties.description: An islet in the Gulf of Naples.

properties.title: Interamna Lirenas
properties.description: A Latin colony founded ca. 312 B.C. along the Via Latina. The site was sacked by Samnites (ca. 294 B.C.) and subsequently by Hannibal (212 B.C.). It received Roman municipal status in 90 B.C.

properties.title: Fregellanum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Fregellanum

properties.title: Frosolone
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Frosolone

properties.title: Fabrateria Vetus
properties.description: Fabrateria Vetus was a Volscian settlement that surrendered to Rome in 424 B.C.

properties.title: Hamae
properties.description: Hamae is an ancient site of Campania located between Capua and Cumae, although its precise location is difficult to fix. The people of Capua gathered there for a solemn religious festival.

properties.title: Iuvencus (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Iuvencus fl.

properties.title: Grottacce
properties.description: At Grottacce are the remains of a Roman seaside villa or villa maritima.

properties.title: Ferentinum
properties.description: A Hernican town along the Via Latina that the Romans captured in 364 B.C. Later in the Republican period (after 195 B.C.) the city received Roman municipal status.

properties.title: Ferrazzano
properties.description: A fortified ancient hilltop, Ferrazzano is usually identified as a Samnite site.

properties.title: Giurlanda
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Giurlanda

properties.title: Fagifulae
properties.description: Fagifulae was a center of the Pentrian Samnites.

properties.title: Damecuta
properties.description: An Imperial villa excavated by A. Maiuri in the 1930s, Damecuta was connected to the Iulio-Claudian emperors. The construction of later Medieval and Bourbon fortifications on the site significantly damaged the ancient remains. The Medieval Damecuta tower stands atop part of the Roman villa.

properties.title: Fregellae
properties.description: Fregellae was a city of Latium Adjectum that became a Roman colony in 328 B.C., but was subsequently captured by the Samnites; a Roman presence was re-established in 313 B.C. Loyal to Rome during the Second Punic War, Fregellae revolted in 125 B.C. and the site was razed.

properties.title: ‘Invinias’
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 ‘Invinias’

properties.title: La Giostra
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 La Giostra

properties.title: Fucinus L.
properties.description: A lake of ancient Italy, site of a major battle of 89 BC. Flood and drainage controls were attempted by both Claudius and Hadrian. The Torlonia family drained the lake in the nineteenth century.

properties.title: Decennovium
properties.description: Decennovium refers to a 19-mile stretch of the Via Appia from the Forum Appii to Tarracina that continued through the paludes Pontinae.

properties.title: Fratte
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Fratte

properties.title: ‘Iovis Lareni’
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F1 ‘Iovis Lareni’

properties.title: Kupelternum/Cubulteria
properties.description: Kupelternum/Cubulteria was an ancient Samnite settlement.

properties.title: Falernus Ager
properties.description: The Ager Falernus comprised the northern portion of Campania from the Massican hills to the Vulturnus river. The area was celebrated for its fertility and, in particular, for its wines.

properties.title: Cumae/Kyme (Campanian)
properties.description: An ancient settlement of Campania, Cumae was the first Greek colony established on the Italian mainland in the eighth century BC.

properties.title: Frentani
properties.description: An Italic people of eastern Italy occupying a territory between the Apennines and the Adriatic seaboard, the Frentani had a close cultural connection with the Samnites.

properties.title: Gioia dei Marsi
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Gioia dei Marsi

properties.title: Herculaneum
properties.description: An ancient Roman town of Campania destroyed by the eruption of Mt. Vesuvius in A.D. 79. Named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

properties.title: Fabrateria Nova
properties.description: Fabrateria Nova received a Roman colony in 124 B.C. that was dispatched by Caius Gracchus. The relationship between Fabrateria Nova and the earlier Volscian site of Fabrateria Vetus remains unclear. The favored location for Fabrateria Nova is at S. Giovanni Incarico, where the Liri and Sacco rivers intersect.

properties.title: Fibrenus (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Fibrenus fl.

properties.title: Cumanus Sinus
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E4 Cumanus Sinus

properties.title: Faustianum?
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Faustianum?

properties.title: Iuvanum
properties.description: A Roman municipium founded in 87 BC after the Social War, Iuvanum sits on the site of a pre-existing Samnite settlement that occupies an upland plateau.

properties.title: Diana Tifatina, T.
properties.description: The Fanum Dianae Tifatinae located on the slopes of Mt. Tifata in Campania.

properties.title: Cretone
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 C1 Cretone

properties.title: Frusino
properties.description: Frusino (modern Frosinone) was a town in Latium along the Via Latina that was originally a Volscian settlement.

properties.title: Gallinaria Silva
properties.description: An evergreen thicket of the area around Cumae.

properties.title: Gianola
properties.description: The site of a villa associated with Lucius Vitruvius Mamurra.

properties.title: ‘Herculis Rani’?
properties.description: A large fanum sacred to ‘Herculis Rani’? at Campochiaro, the name of which is then preserved in the station mentioned on the Peutinger Table. Scholars like A. La Regina support linking this fanum to a place mentioned by Livy, although see discussion by Oakley.

properties.title: Fundi
properties.description: Fundi achieved civitas sine suffragio after the Latin War in 338 B.C.

properties.title: Digentia (river)
properties.description: A stream in the ager Sabinus.

properties.title: Forum Popillii
properties.description: An important town of the Ager Falernus, not to be confused with Forum Popili, the modern Polla.

properties.title: Fonte Romito
properties.description: A pre-Roman and Roman settlement of Samnium.

properties.title: Formiae
properties.description: An ancient settlement of likely Greek origin along the Via Appia. Cicero was assassinated near Formiae (now Formia) in 43 B.C.

properties.title: Dikaiarcheia/Puteoli
properties.description: A maritime city of Campania situated on the Phlegrean Peninsula. The settlement started as a Greek colony and became a Roman colony under the name Puteoli in 194 B.C.

properties.title: Fundanus L.
properties.description: A brackish lake ca. 90 km southeast of Rome.

properties.title: Eumorfiana? Ins.
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D4 Eumorfiana? Ins.

properties.title: Velabrum
properties.description: The Velabrum is a valley in Rome that connects the Forum Romanum to the Forum Boarium.

properties.title: Porte de France, Nemausus
properties.description: A first century B.C. city gate of ancient Nemausus.

properties.title: Lucus Furrinae
properties.description: The Lucus Furrinae or Syrian Sanctuary is a sanctuary site on the Janiculum Hill in Rome. The first known construction at the site took place during the late first century CE and it remained in use until the mid-fourth century CE.

properties.title: Beit Shemesh
properties.description: City 30 km west of Jerusalem inhabited from the Bronze Age until its destruction in 701 CE.

properties.title: Arcadian Gate
properties.description: The Arcadian Gate is a monumental city gate constructed in the fourth century BCE in Messene.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D3 unnamed canal (in Pomptinae Paludes)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D3 unnamed canal (Circeii 1-Circeii 2)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 unnamed canal (Baiae)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D2 unnamed canal (from Fucinus L., near Pitonia?)

properties.title: Tell El Kowm
properties.description: Neolithic site in Syria with signs of habitation dated to the 7th-6th millennia BCE.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Volaterrae
properties.description: The archaeological remains of an amphitheater were discovered at Volterra in 2015. Preliminary work suggests that the structure measured ca. 70 x 90 meters and had three tiers of seats that could accommodate 8,000 to 10,000 spectators.

properties.title: Residential Palace ("P")
properties.description: Residential Palace ("P") is often regarded as the residence of Cyrus the Great at Pasargadae.

properties.title: Tall-i Takht (Throne Hill)
properties.description: The ancient citadel of Pasargadae.

properties.title: Basilica at Saepinum
properties.description: The Basilica at Saepinum is positioned at the intersection of the cardo and the decumanus.

properties.title: St Michael's Mount
properties.description: A tidal island located in Mount's Bay, Cornwall, England. Known for the castle crowning the island, this place has been inhabited since the Neolithic period.

properties.title: Adamkayalar
properties.description: A site of rock-cut relief sculpture, perhaps dating to the second century.

properties.title: Thermae Diocletiani
properties.description: Public baths near the Viminal Hill in Rome constructed under Diocletian from 298-306 CE.

properties.title: Podere Marzuolo
properties.description: Podere Marzuolo was the site of Roman pottery production from the first century B.C. until the early fourth century A.D. The site has yielded evidence for the production of terra sigillata pottery as well as evidence of blacksmithing.

properties.title: Jazirat Sabuniya (island)
properties.description: An island of the Socotra archipelago.

properties.title: Zalu Ab
properties.description: Zalu Ab (also Romanized as Zālū Āb and Zālūāb) is a village in Zalu Ab Rural District, in the Central District of Ravansar County, Kermanshah Province, Iran. Several ancient objects, including a bronze bowl of a Chaldean tribal leader, are reported to have been discovered in this rural Iranian village.

properties.title: Wadi al-Jarf
properties.description: Site on the Red Sea Coast in Egypt, used in the Fourth Dynasty as a port for importing turquoise and copper from Sinai. The oldest surviving papyrus from Egypt, dated during the reign of Khufu (26th century BCE), was found at the site.

properties.title: Khirbet Beit-Bassa
properties.description: An ancient fortress located in Beit Sahour, in the district of Bethlehem in Palestine.

properties.title: Tall-e Geser
properties.description: Village in Iran inhabited since the 6th millennium BCE.

properties.title: Roman theater at Augusta Bagiennorum
properties.description: The Roman theater at Augusta Bagiennorum

properties.title: Römersteine im Zahlbachtal
properties.description: Site of the remains of the Roman aqueduct, Römersteine im Zahlbachtal, in the district of Mainz-Bretzenheim.

properties.title: Sawtry
properties.description: Modern day site of a Roman-British settlement dating from the second to fourth centuries AD.

properties.title: Raṣappa
properties.description: A land (and later an Assyrian province) mentioned in first-millennium B.C. Akkadian texts from Assyria and Suhu. Scholars generally believe that this land/province is located east of the Habur River, south of Jebel Singar, and northeast of the land Bit-Halupê.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 43 (villas on Via Castrimeniense)

properties.title: So-Called Tomb of Clodius
properties.description: The so-called Tomb of Clodius along the Via Appia near Castel Gandolfo.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D4 no. 59 (bridge (Ponte S. Felicità))

properties.title: Ponte Amato
properties.description: The bridge known as Ponte Amato carries the Via Praenestina near Gallicano.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 27 (bridge on Via Labicana)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 E2 no. 62 (temple NW Anagnia)

properties.title: Unnamed villa

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 no. 38 (bridge (Ponte dell’Acqua Nera))

properties.title: Ponte di Traiano at Tor Tre Ponti
properties.description: A Roman bridge located on the Via Appia at modern Tor Tre Ponti.

properties.title: Roman Villa at Lago di Nemi
properties.description: A Roman Villa on the shores of Lago di Nemi.

properties.title: Mugilla?
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 42 (settlement (Mugilla?))

properties.title: Ponte Ceccara
properties.description: The Ponte Ceccara, also referred to as the ponte di Terra, is a Republican period bridge located on the fosso di Passerano along the Via Praenestina. It is located within the modern comune of Zagarolo, some 30.5 km southeast of the center of Rome.

properties.title: Quarries at Aquae Albulae
properties.description: The quarries at Aquae Albulae were a source of travertine.

properties.title: Ponte Loreto
properties.description: A Roman bridge at Lanuvium.

properties.title: Unnamed forts near Aefula
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 no. 33 (forts near Aefula)

properties.title: Villas at Castelporziano
properties.description: The 6,000 ha estate at Castelporziano has been, since antiquity, an elite seaside compound. Where a modern pleasure villa for the Italian president now sits are remains of Roman villas of the Laurentine shore; these remains have been the object of continued study since 1983.

properties.title: Unnamed Roman villa
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 no. 57 (villa near Norba)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 no. 56 (temple at Algidus M.)

properties.title: Unnamed temple near Solforata
properties.description: An ancient temple located near Solforata, between Lavinium and the Alban Lake in modern Italy.

properties.title: Roman bridges at Tibur
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 no. 32 (bridges at Tibur (2))

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 no. 52 (temple near Ardea)

properties.title: Villa del Torraccio, Torrenova
properties.description: The Forma Italiae notes the presence of drainage channels, foundations, and a cistern that are taken to be indicative of a Roman villa in the locale known today as Torrenova in the eastern portion of modern Rome.

properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 no. 31 (bridge over R. Acquoria, temple and quarries)
