properties.title: Unnamed Roman villa
properties.description: A villa rustica located near the coast, southwest of Ardea.

properties.title: Ponte di Mele
properties.description: A Roman bridge along the Via Appia.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 no. 34 (bridge at S. Stefano)

properties.title: Tombs near Villa Adriana
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 no. 30 (tombs near Villa Adriana)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 E3 no. 61 (cult place near Trerus fl.)

properties.title: So-called Villa on the Lake
properties.description: Lugli describes the remains of a sumptuous, porticoed villa in the Doric order facing onto the Alban lake. Marzano clarifies Lugli's earlier summary of the site, which was in turn based on observations made in 1912. The remains of the villa include a 200-m long portico on two levels. About 260 m from the portico are the remains of a cistern in opus reticulatum. Chiarucci documented a structure with five barrel-vaulted rooms of unclear function. Lugli's initial report suggests that this late republican villa was eventually incorporated into the Villa of Domitian.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 25 (settlement and villa at Colle dello Stinco)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 no. 41 (villa near Praeneste)

properties.title: Colle Rasto Settlement
properties.description: A site to the west of modern Praeneste in Italy where surface material, remains of structures, and graves were discovered in the 19th century. These finds provide evidence for a settlement possibly dating to as early as the fifth or fourth century BCE but with likely occupation throughout the subsequent Roman period.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 24 (villa, NW Pantano Secco)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 44 (villa at Vigna Spinabella)

properties.title: Roman villa near Setia
properties.description: The platform, including cryptoporticus, of a republican period villa originally dating to the first century B.C. with evidence for second century A.D. renovations.

properties.title: Temple of Castor and Pollux, Cora
properties.description: The Temple of Castor and Pollux at Cora was originally built between the fourth and the second centuries B.C. The partially extant architrave carries an inscription of the first century B.C.

properties.title: Roman siege camp
properties.description: A siege camp dating to the Roman siege of the fortress of Masada in A.D. 72.

properties.title: Caer Gai
properties.description: The site of a Roman fort in Wales occupied during the late first and early second centuries A.D.

properties.title: Unnamed temple
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 no. 12 (temple at EUR)

properties.title: Villa delle Grotte at Grottarossa
properties.description: A villa with beginnings in the early Republican period, continuing in use to the middle Imperial period.

properties.title: Ponte Ladrone
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 no. 16 (bridge (Ponte Ladrone))

properties.title: Unnamed tuff quarry
properties.description: A tuff quarry located at Castelporziano, to the east of Ostia Antica.

properties.title: Unnamed villas and a tomb near Pons Mulvius
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 no. 9 (villas (2) and tomb near Pons Mulvius)

properties.title: Ponte di Vallerano
properties.description: The Ponte di Vallerano is a second century Roman bridge that carried the via Ostiensis across the fosso di Vallerano.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 no. 6 (bridge over Cremera fl.)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C1 no. 18 (tomb near Nomentum)

properties.title: Roman villa and aqueduct at Ponte delle Sette Miglia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 22 (villa and aqueduct at Ponte delle Sette Miglia)

properties.title: Cemeteries around Caere
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 no. 1 (cemeteries around Caere)

properties.title: Villa and aqueduct at Vermicino
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 23 (villa and aqueduct at Vermicino)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 19 (villa near S. Sinforosa)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 7 (villa N Fidenae)

properties.title: Roman bridge at Palidoro
properties.description: An ancient Roman bridge along the Via Aurelia.

properties.title: Cemetery of Gordianus, Epimachus, Apronianus
properties.description: A burial ground for the the Christian martyrs Gordianus, Epimachus, and Apronianus at the seventh mile of the Via Latina.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 no. 4 (bridge over R. Arrone)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 no. 5 (bridge over Fosso di Prima Porta)

properties.title: Unnamed bridge over R. Quartaccio
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 no. 2 (bridge over R. Quartaccio)

properties.title: Parco delle Tombe di via Latina
properties.description: A cluster of Roman Imperial tombs along the Via Latina excavated in the nineteenth century.

properties.title: Unnamed bridge
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 no. 14 (bridge at Mezzocamino)

properties.title: Unnamed bridge in the Piazza Eugenio Biffi
properties.description: The remains of an ancient Roman bridge in the present Piazza Eugenio Biffi in Rome. This bridge is thought to have spanned the Almo river.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 11 (bridge near so-called Tomb of Geta)

properties.title: Ponte di Malafede
properties.description: A Roman bridge that is no longer extant. Quilici notes that the bridge was destroyed both by the Second World War and by urbanization that followed in the post-war period. Blake publishes a photo of E. B. van Deman and indicates that the bridge was built in peperino and of "indeterminate date". She compares the Ponte di Malafede with the construction of the Via Appia viaduct that lies just beyond Ariccia, a structure that was Augustan in its date.

properties.title: Sahab
properties.description: A farming village southeast of Amman, Jordan, inhabited from the late Neolithic Period through the sixth century BCE, and briefly inhabited again from the eleventh-thirteenth centuries; now the site of the modern town of Sahab.

properties.title: Rofalco
properties.description: A fortified Etruscan site located in the territory of Vulci.

properties.title: Maes Knoll hill fort
properties.description: Maes Knoll hill fort is an Iron Age hillfort in Somerset, England.

properties.title: Nuraghe s'Ulimu
properties.description: A two-tower nuraghe located near Ulassai in the province of Nuoro.

properties.title: Temenos of Athena
properties.description: Area on the north-east side of the Piana di Himera, delimited by walls and containing four religious buildings (temples A, B, C and D), probably dedicated to Athena. The foundations are still visible in the archaeological site of Himera.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: The Salinae Romanae at Ostia were said to have been established by Ancus Marcius.

properties.title: Roman baths at Sexi/Saxetanum
properties.description: The Roman baths at Sexi/Saxetanum date to the first century.

properties.title: Castro de Borneiro
properties.description: An oppidum of the Castro Culture.

properties.title: Castro de Troña
properties.description: An elliptical, terraced Iron Age settlement of the Castro culture located in Pias, near Mondariz, Spain. The sites is located at an altitude of 280 meters above sea level.

properties.title: Barbury Castle
properties.description: Barbury Castle is an Iron Age hill fort in Wiltshire, England.

properties.title: Stoa in the sanctuary of Zeus Lykaios
properties.description: A 62 m long stoa, probably of the fourth century BC.

properties.title: San Nicola di Trullas
properties.description: A Medieval church on the island of Sardinia that is dated to 1133.

properties.title: Madinat Hamad 2 Burial Mound Field (Karzakkan)
properties.description: A necropolis of the early Dilmun culture, dating to the second millennium B.C.

properties.title: Temple to Ramesses II at Abu Simbel
properties.description: The larger of the two temples at Abu Simbel, dedicated to the triad of Amun, Ra-Horakhty, and Ptah, as well as the deified Ramesses II. The temple was relocated between 1964 and 1968 to prevent its submersion under Lake Nasser after the construction of the Aswan High Dam.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 unnamed aqueduct (Ostia)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C4 unnamed aqueduct (Torre del Monumento)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C4 unnamed aqueduct (Antium)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 unnamed aqueduct (Gabii)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 unnamed aqueduct (Lavinium)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 unnamed aqueduct (Vicus Augustanus)

properties.title: Tomb of the Five Chairs, Caere
properties.description: An Etruscan tomb at Caere dated ca. 625-600 B.C.

properties.title: La Rustica
properties.description: La Rustica was a Latin site located along the Via Collatina.

properties.title: Settecamini
properties.description: An archaeological site located at the midpoint of the Via Tiburtina linking Rome and Tibur.

properties.title: Tor de’ Cenci
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Tor de’ Cenci

properties.title: Serrone di Bove
properties.description: The small hill that is known as "Il Poggio di Serrone di Bove" is located in the hinterland of ancient Norba and was the site of ancient settlement activity. Architectural remains on the site include those of a polygonal masonry sub-struction or platform as well as an ancient roadway that may be part of the road tract from Norba to Cora.

properties.title: Sacro Speco
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 E2 Sacro Speco

properties.title: S. Lidano
properties.description: The so-called "Archi di San Lidano" are the remains of a Roman stone bridge in the Pontine plain, near the modern locality of Sezze Scalo. The bridge likely dates originally to the second century B.C. Evidence of an ancient sanctuary have also been detected in the vicinity.

properties.title: Ponte Mammolo
properties.description: Ponte Mammolo is the modern name of an ancient bridge over the Aniene river. It gives its name to a neighborhood and metro station in the northeast part of the modern city of Rome. Archaeological evidence of ancient quarrying and a settlement have also been found in the vicinity of the bridge.

properties.title: Pompeo
properties.description: A villa attributed to Cnaeus Pompeius.

properties.title: S. Passera
properties.description: S. Passera is a Christian church on the Tiber river in Rome, opposite the Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls. The current church dates to the ninth century and incorporated the remains of a Roman tomb. The church is traditionally connected to a community of local miners.

properties.title: Il Torraccio
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Il Torraccio

properties.title: Tomba di Marco Plauzio Lucano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Tomba di Marco Plauzio Lucano

properties.title: Tomb of Vibius Marianus
properties.description: An imperial Roman tomb of Publius Vibius Marianus, erroneously identified as the Tomba di Nerone (Tomb of Nero) by G. B. Piranesi.

properties.title: Il Torraccio
properties.description: A circular mausoleum dating to the Late Republican period along the Via Praenestina.

properties.title: S. Martino
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 S. Martino

properties.title: Ponte Salario
properties.description: The Ponte Salario is a Medieval bridge with Roman origins. It is located at the point where the Via Salaria crosses the Anio, about 3 km north of the Colline Gate.

properties.title: S. Laurentius
properties.description: The Papal Basilica of Saint Lawrence outside the Walls (Basilica Papale di San Lorenzo fuori le Mura) is one of the Seven Pilgrim Churches of Rome. The basilica serves as the shrine and tomb dedicated to Saint Lawrence and its earliest phases likely belong to the fourth century AD.

properties.title: Salinae
properties.description: Salt pans located to the east of Ostia and to the north-east of Portus around the Tiber river estuary.

properties.title: Tor Marancia
properties.description: The modern toponym Tor Marancia is claimed to derive from the Praedium Amaranthianus, a villa belonging to the second-century A.D. freedman Amaranthus.

properties.title: Sep. Plautii
properties.description: The Mausoleum of Plautii dates to the first century B.C.

properties.title: Settebagni
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Settebagni

properties.title: S. Clemens
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 E2 S. Clemens

properties.title: Priscilla
properties.description: A Christian catacomb within an ancient quarry on the Via Salaria that was in use from the second until the fourth centuries AD. The Catacomb of Priscilla was likely named for Priscilla, a member of the gens Acilia, and contains the oldest known Marian painting (third century AD).

properties.title: Pietra Papa
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Pietra Papa

properties.title: S. Sinforosa
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 S. Sinforosa

properties.title: Il Torraccio
properties.description: The so-called "Il Torraccio (1)" is the cement core of a Roman tomb located at the twelfth milestone of the Via Appia Nuova, on the left side.

properties.title: Quintilio Varo
properties.description: A villa located near the sanctuary of Madonna di Quintiliolo (Tivoli) that is traditionally associated with Quintilius Varus. The remains of the basis villae may date as early as the third century B.C.

properties.title: Torre di Palidoro
properties.description: A coastal Roman villa that is succeeded by a Medieval coastal tower.

properties.title: Sublanuvio
properties.description: Sublanuvium was an ancient station (statio) along the Via Appia, located between Aricia and Ad Sponsas. While its precise location is unknown, the site is located at the twentieth milestone of the Appia.

properties.title: Saxa Rubra
properties.description: Saxa Rubra (modern Grottarossa) is the name of a road station on the Via Flaminia nine Roman miles from the center of ancient Rome. It was at Saxa Rubra that Constantine I defeated Maxentius in A.D. 312.

properties.title: S. Alessandro
properties.description: The basilica and catacombs of S. Alessandro are located at the seventh milestone of the Via Nomentana.

properties.title: S. Antonio
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 S. Antonio

properties.title: Satricum
properties.description: An ancient settlement on the right bank of the river Astura, Satricum has a mixed heritage of Latins and Volscians. In 499 B.C. Satricum was a member of the Latin League, but was under Volscian control in 488 B.C. The site is noted for its sanctuary of Mater Matuta.

properties.title: Torre Pascolaro (settlement)
properties.description: A Final Bronze Age settlement of four to five hectares in South Etruria.

properties.title: La Storta
properties.description: A station on the Via Cassia attested in an inscription dated to A.D. 379-383.

properties.title: Tomba degli Orazi e Curiazi
properties.description: A Roman tomb near Albano Laziale connected in tradition with the story of the contest between the Horatii and Curiatii.

properties.title: Torre Caldara
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C4 Torre Caldara

properties.title: S. Sebastianus
properties.description: S. Sebastianus (San Sebastiano fuori le mura) is a Christian basilica outside the walls of Rome; the earliest phase belongs to the fourth century AD.

properties.title: Pietralata
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Pietralata

properties.title: S. Cesareo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 S. Cesareo

properties.title: S. Callisto
properties.description: A large catacomb on the Via Appia south of Rome notable especially for its so-called 'Crypt of the Popes'. The catacomb covers approximately 15 hectares.

properties.title: Tiberis (river)
properties.description: The Tiber river is the third-longest river of the Italian peninsula, flowing 406 km (252 mi) from the Apennine Mountains to the Tyrrhenian Sea.

properties.title: Torre del Monumento
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C4 Torre del Monumento

properties.title: S. Scholastica
properties.description: A convent founded within the area of the Villa Neronis (BAtlas 43 E2 S. Scholastica)

properties.title: Piscina Torta
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 Piscina Torta

properties.title: Prati Fiscali
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Prati Fiscali

properties.title: S. Felicita
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Felicita

properties.title: S. Agata
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Agata

properties.title: Sep. C. Maenius Bassus
properties.description: The tomb C. Maenius Bassus is located along the Via Valeria. This podium tomb with superstructure is dated to either the reign of Caius or that of Claudius. Epigraphic evidence mentions that C. Maenius C. f. Cam. Bassus was an Augustalis, an aedile, and praefectus fabrum.

properties.title: Solforata
properties.description: At Solforata along the Via Ardeatina activity related to the extraction of sulfur has been identified.

properties.title: Redicolo
properties.description: The Tomb of Annia Regilla (vix. A.D. 125-160), the wife of Herodes Atticus. The tomb is also erroneously known as the "Temple of the God Rediculum" and was used in the Middle Ages as a hay barn.

properties.title: S. Vincenzo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D1 S. Vincenzo

properties.title: Quadraro
properties.description: A Roman villa near the line of the Aqua Claudia located in the modern Via del Quadraro. The villa is dated to the first century B.C. or first century A.D. Following remodelling in the third century, the villa's occupation ends in the fourth century.

properties.title: Quintilii
properties.description: A suburban villa built by Sextus Quintilius Maximus and Sextus Quintilius Condianus (consuls in A.D. 151).

properties.title: S. Valentino
properties.description: A Christian catacomb along the Via Flaminia dedicated to S. Valentino.

properties.title: Regillus? L.
properties.description: An ancient lake in Latium that was the site of a Roman military victory in 496 BC; the precise location of the lake cannot be determined, although some scholars place its location at Pantano Secco near Frascati, Italy.

properties.title: Scalzacane
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Scalzacane

properties.title: S. Agnese
properties.description: A titular church on the Via Nomentana, S. Agnese houses the remains of the eponymous saint. The present church was built by Pope Honorius I in the seventh century AD, on the site of a fourth century basilica built by Constantine I.

properties.title: S. Ermete
properties.description: S. Ermete is the site of a Paleochristian basilica and catacomb; the catacombs are also referred to as the Catacombs of Bassilla, and both names occur in the documentary sources.

properties.title: Prima Porta
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B1 Prima Porta

properties.title: S. Rufina
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Rufina

properties.title: Sublaqueum
properties.description: An ancient settlement, located at modern Subiaco in Italy, Sublaqueum was located in the territory of the Aequi that was annexed by Rome in 304 B.C.

properties.title: Torre del Padiglione
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Torre del Padiglione

properties.title: Tibur
properties.description: A Sabine town, 30 km east-north-east of Rome, Tibur was the seat of the Tiburtine Sibyl.

properties.title: S. Carlo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 S. Carlo

properties.title: Salone
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Salone

properties.title: Sep. Geta
properties.description: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia that is traditionally believed to be that of Publius Septimius Geta, the younger son of Septimius Severus.

properties.title: Simbruina Stagna
properties.description: A series of three artificial lakes created along the river Anio.

properties.title: Robigo?, T.
properties.description: The sanctuary of the god Robigus, located at the sixth mile of the Via Cassia. The Romans celebrated the festival of Robigalia on 25 April.

properties.title: Pons Mulvius
properties.description: Pons Mulvius (the Milvian Bridge) is a Roman bridge over the Tiber river. The original phase of the bridge dates to the consulship of Gaius Claudius Nero in 206 B.C. The bridge is most famous as the site of a decisive battle between Maxentius and Constantine I fought in A.D. 312.

properties.title: S. Maria di Galeria
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B1 S. Maria di Galeria

properties.title: Sette Bassi
properties.description: A large, suburban villa complex on the Via Tuscolana. The villa was in use from the reign of Antoninus Pius until the fourth century A.D.

properties.title: Il Tondo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Il Tondo

properties.title: Tor Paterno
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 Tor Paterno

properties.title: Sabina
properties.description: The one-time territory of the ancient Sabine people of central Italy.

properties.title: S. Petrus
properties.description: The Basilica of St. Peter in Vatican City; currently a Renaissance edifice standing on the site of Old St. Peter's Basilica, a church built by Constantine I between AD 319 and 333. The holy site is located on the Mons Vaticanus in connection with the purported site of the burial of the Christian Saint Peter. (cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Petrus)

properties.title: Plinio
properties.description: The so-called villa of Pliny the Younger, also known as the Villa delle Palombara. The villa's first phases date to the Iulio-Claudian period. It continues in use, and continues to undergo modifications, through the second century A.D.

properties.title: Portus
properties.description: The great ancient maritime port of Rome, located on the right-hand bank of the Tiber river.

properties.title: S. Ippolito
properties.description: A catacomb connected with the Christian Saint Hippolytus of Rome along the Via Tiburtina.

properties.title: S. Gennaro
properties.description: A minor settlement.

properties.title: Praeneste
properties.description: An ancient city of central Italy, the eighth and seventh century B.C. origins of which demonstrate high-level trade contact with the Eastern Mediterranean world. The city withdrew from the Latin League (499 B.C.) and opposed Rome in the Latin war; Cincinnatus eventually subdued Praeneste. Sulla founded a new colony there in the first century B.C.

properties.title: Pometia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Pometia

properties.title: S. Paulus
properties.description: One of Rome's four major papal basilicae, S. Paulus was founded by Constantine I in the early fourth century A.D. and expanded by Valentinian I in the 370s.

properties.title: Sacer Mons
properties.description: Sacer Mons is a hill on the banks of the Anio river and is connected, traditionally, with the episode of the secession of the Roman plebs of 494 BC.

properties.title: Torraccia dell’Inviolata
properties.description: A Roman tomb, known as the Torraccia dell’Inviolata. This tomb has a cruciform plan that is inscribed within a circular structure. Based on masonry techniques the tomb dates to the later first or second century.

properties.title: Setia
properties.description: A Volscian settlement of the fifth century B.C. that became a Latin colony in 382 B.C.

properties.title: Tor Angela
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Tor Angela

properties.title: SS. Marcellino e Pietro
properties.description: The church of Saints Marcellinus and Peter is a Roman Catholic church located on the Via Merulana in Rome. Pope Siricius built the original church in the fourth century A.D., close to the catacombs of Marcellinus and Peter. The relics of the saints were deposited in the church in 1256.

properties.title: Ponte di Tuscolo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Ponte di Tuscolo

properties.title: Roma
properties.description: The capital of the Roman Republic and Empire.

properties.title: Signia
properties.description: A city of Latium Adjectum established as a Latin colony ca. 494 B.C.

properties.title: Mausoleum of Caecilia Metella
properties.description: A tomb on the Via Appia south of Rome belonging to Caecilia Metella, a daughter of Metellus Creticus. She was born ca. 100 BC. In 1303 the tomb was incorporated into the Castrum Caetani, serving as the main tower of the fortification.

properties.title: S. Agapito
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 S. Agapito

properties.title: Roman baths at Trier
properties.description: The Imperial Baths at Trier (also referred to as "Kaiserthermen") are a large Roman bath complex in Trier, Germany. The site was designated as part of the "Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St. Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier", a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The complex dates to the fourth century A.D.

properties.title: Rathlin Island
properties.description: An island offshore from modern Northern Ireland with evidence of human habitation stretching back to the Mesolithic period. It is one possible identification for an ancient "Riginia" island mentioned in ancient sources.

properties.title: Nichoria
properties.description: Located in Messenia, Nichoria was a site with important Bronze Age and Iron Age phases.

properties.title: Villa Torlonia
properties.description: The extant Villa Torlonia occupies the site of an ancient Roman villa.

properties.title: Le Vignacce
properties.description: A Roman villa located on via Lemonia in Rome's suburbium attributed to Quintus Servilius Pudens.

properties.title: Il Torrino
properties.description: An Iron Age settlement in Latium.

properties.title: Valvisciolo
properties.description: An Iron Age settlement and necropolis located in the Monti Lepini near the abbey of Valvisciolo, characterized by polygonal masonry terrace walls. While the ancient name of the site is unknown, various proposals have been raised, including Sulmo (Savignoni, Mengarelli) and Pometia (Ogilvie). The settlement corresponds to the Latial II B phase and occupation ends ca. the late sixth century B.C.

properties.title: Varia
properties.description: Varia (modern Vicovaro) was a settlement of the Sabines.

properties.title: Trebula Suffenas
properties.description: An ancient Sabine city.

properties.title: Villa Aldobrandini
properties.description: The Villa Aldobrandini is located on the outskirts of Frascati. The current villa of the site was built in 1550 by a Vatican prelate named Alessandro Rufini. Subsequently, Pope Clement VIII gave the villa to his nephew Cardinal Pietro Aldobrandini in 1598. The Papal villa and gardens occupy the site of a Roman terrace villa.

properties.title: Villamagna
properties.description: A large imperial Roman villa known from letters of Marcus Aurelius.

properties.title: Via delle Piagge
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Via delle Piagge

properties.title: Tredici Altari
properties.description: A Latin federal sanctuary at Lavinium, consisting of a series of altars that range in date from the sixth to the second century BC and a sacred site (or heroon) connected with the hero Aeneas.

properties.title: Villa Lucidi
properties.description: A large villa complex built sometime in the first century B.C. and in use until at least the third century.

properties.title: Tusculum
properties.description: Tusculum was a Latin city of the Alban Hills in central Italy. After 381 BC Tusculum became the first "municipium cum suffragio".

properties.title: Villa Pamphili
properties.description: The church of San Pancrazio was founded in the sixth century A.D. by Pope Symmachus. It stands beyond the Porta San Pancrazio on the Ianiculum. Below the church is a massive catacomb referred to as S. Pancrazio or Ottavilla.

properties.title: Villa di Vibio Varo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Villa di Vibio Varo

properties.title: Villa Domitiani
properties.description: Villa Domitiani, a large imperial villa near the Alban Lake, now the site of the Papal retreat at Castel Gandolfo.

properties.title: Villa Torlonia
properties.description: A Jewish catacomb discovered in 1919 on the grounds of the Villa Torlonia park in Rome.

properties.title: Villa Maxentii
properties.description: A complex on the Via Appia constructed by Maxentius in the early fourth century A.D.

properties.title: Valerio Messala Corvino
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Valerio Messala Corvino

properties.title: Trerus/Tolerus (river)
properties.description: A river of central Italy and a right tributary of the Liris.

properties.title: Tres Tabernae
properties.description: A statio at the point where the Via Appia crosses the Via Ninfina.

properties.title: Villa Esmeade
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Villa Esmeade

properties.title: Villa Muti
properties.description: The Villa Muti in Grottaferrata occupies, at least in part, the site of a Roman republican villa built on a series of terraces and likely dating to the third and second centuries B.C. Lanciani excavated a series of rooms at the site. The site also had an early to mid-Imperial phase that included elaborate floors and decoration in imported marble.

properties.title: Villa Neronis
properties.description: The Villa Neronis was a rural villa of the emperor Nero, likely built early in his reign (perhaps before AD 60).

properties.title: Villa Hadriani
properties.description: The Villa of Hadrian (Villa Adriana in Italian) is a sprawling archaeological complex at Tivoli, Italy. The villa complex was designed and used by the emperor Hadrian in the second century A.D.

properties.title: Troia?
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 Troia?

properties.title: Vicus Alexandri
properties.description: A settlement at the third milestone of the Via Ostiensis.

properties.title: Veii
properties.description: An important city of South Etruria located north-northwest of Rome, Veii was eventually sacked by the Romans in 396 B.C. The ancient city covered some 180 ha.

properties.title: Torre S. Angelo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Torre S. Angelo

properties.title: Torre Sessano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Torre Sessano

properties.title: Velitrae
properties.description: Velitrae (modern Velletri) was an ancient Volscian settlement. In the Roman Republican period, Velitrae was attacked by Marcus Furius Camillus (379 B.C.) and again by Cincinnatus (377 B.C.); the Romans controlled the site by 365 B.C. The gens Octavia hailed from the city and a youthful Octavian spent time there.

properties.title: Vicus Augustanus Laurentium?
properties.description: The Vicus Augustanus Laurentium is an ancient settlement in coastal Latium located between the shore and the Via Severiana. The site was first described by Rodolfo Lanciani in 1903. The British School at Rome carried out excavations in the 1980s.

properties.title: Pollenzo Roman amphitheater
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at ancient Pollentia (modenr Pollenzo).

properties.title: Tell Beydar
properties.description: Tell Beydar (ancient Nabada) is an archaeological site in NE Syria that was first settled ca. 2600 BC.

properties.title: Vieil-Évreux Roman Baths
properties.description: The Vieil-Évreux Roman Baths of the second and third centuries A.D. have four architectural phases that have been identified.

properties.title: Grotte di Pertosa
properties.description: The Pertosa Caves, a system of karst caves located in the comune of Pertosa, province of Salerno, Campania, Italy.

properties.title: Aqua Iulia
properties.description: A Roman aqueduct built by Marcus Agrippa in 33 BC and expanded by Augustus between 11 and 4 BC.

properties.title: Aqua Virgo
properties.description: The Aqua Virgo was one of the 11 aqueducts supplying the city of Rome and was completed by Marcus Agrippa in 19 BC. The aqueduct was later revitalized by Pope Adrian I in the eighth century.

properties.title: Aqua Marcia
properties.description: The Aqua Marcia was the longest of Rome's 11 aqueducts.

properties.title: Aqua Alsietina
properties.description: The Aqua Alsietina was an aqueduct built by Augustus that drew water from the lacus Alsietinus (Lago di Martignano) and conducted it to Rome.

properties.title: Aqua Appia
properties.description: The earliest of Rome's aqueducts, the Aqua Appia was constructed in 312 BC by the censor Appius Claudius Caecus. The aqueduct runs a course of 16.4 km, entering Rome at the Porta Maggiore. Frontinus estimated the daily volume at 75,537 cubic meters.

properties.title: Aqua Claudia
properties.description: The Aqua Claudia was one of the four great aqueducts of the ancient city of Rome. It was begun by Caius in A.D. 38 and completed by Claudius in A.D. 52.

properties.title: Aqua Anio Novus
properties.description: Aqua Anio Novus is an ancient aqueduct supplying the city of Rome. Begun by Caius in A.D. 38, it was completed and dedicated by Claudius in A.D. 52.

properties.title: Aqua Anio Vetus
properties.description: Aqua Anio Vetus, an aqueduct serving Rome and built originally during the third century BC. The Anio Vetus carried water to Rome from the Aniene near Vicovaro.

properties.title: Aqua Antoniniana
properties.description: The Aqua Antoniniana was a branch of the Aqua Marcia that carried water to the Baths of Caracalla.

properties.title: Aqua Alexandrina
properties.description: The Aqua Alexandrina was an ancient Roman aqueduct that carried water 22.4 km from Pantano Borghese to the Baths of Alexander in the Campus Martius. It was in use from the third to the eighth century AD.

properties.title: Aqua Tepula
properties.description: The Aqua Tepula was an aqueduct built in 126 BC by the censors G. Servilius Caepio and L. Cassius Longinus.

properties.title: Aqua Traiana
properties.description: The Aqua Traiana was an aqueduct built by Trajan and inaugurated in AD 109.

properties.title: Lucullo
properties.description: Plutarch describes a villa owned by Lucullus near Tusculum.

properties.title: Gabii
properties.description: An ancient Latin city located on the line of the Republican Via Praenestina connecting Rome to Praeneste. Gabii is allied to Rome from an early date and flourished during the archaic period, declining by the time of Augustus.

properties.title: Forte Tiburtina
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Forte Tiburtina

properties.title: Monte del Grano
properties.description: Monte del Grano is a popular name that was assigned to a mausoleum once thought to belong to Alexander Severus, although that assignation is no longer supported. The archaeological remains are now part of the Parco XVII Aprile 1944.

properties.title: Compitum
properties.description: A multi-period sanctuary near Anagnia.

properties.title: Iuppiter Latiaris, T.
properties.description: An important Latial sanctuary of Iuppiter located on Mons Albanus (modern Monte Cavo).

properties.title: Marco Pedonio
properties.description: The villa of Marcus Pedonius.

properties.title: Nomentum
properties.description: The Latin town of Nomentum and Rome were linked by means of the Via Nomentana. In Livy's history the town, a member of the Latin League, is captured by Lucius Tarquinius Priscus. Nomentum was one of a number of towns captured by Tarquinius. The Romans granted the town civitas sine suffragio after 338 B.C.

properties.title: Fosso della Crescenza
properties.description: Ward-Perkins identified the archaeological site at Fosso della Crescenza during the South Etruria Survey. Excavations of a Iulio-Claudian mausoleum were undertaken in 1962. Additional excavation revealed portions of the Via Veientana. Post-excavation work did not occur until the 1980s, by which time Fentress 1983 notes that the the archaeological landscape had been largely eradicated by the burgeoning growth of suburban Rome.

properties.title: Colle Rotondo
properties.description: Colle Rotondo was the site of a prehistoric settlement inhabited from the Bronze Age until the early Iron Age.

properties.title: Ladispoli
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 Ladispoli

properties.title: Cremera (river)
properties.description: The Cremera is a small stream in Lazio that played a role in the fourth century BC war between Rome and the Etruscan city-state of Veii.

properties.title: Crepaddosso
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Crepaddosso

properties.title: Hernici
properties.description: The Hernici (Hernicans) were an Italic tribe of first millennium B.C. Latium. Their territory was bounded by the Trerus fl. (Sacco) and the Lacus Fucinus (Fucine Lake).

properties.title: Labicum
properties.description: Originally a member of the Latin League, the city of Labicum was taken by the Romans ca. 418 B.C. By the time of Augustus, the site was almost certainly deserted and its precise location remains debated today.

properties.title: Colle Tasso
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Colle Tasso

properties.title: Villa of the Octavii
properties.description: The archaeological remains of a Roman villa on the hill of San Cesareo are speculatively identified as belonging to the gens Octavia, according to Della Portella 2004 op. cit.

properties.title: Frascati
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Frascati

properties.title: Magliana Vecchia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Magliana Vecchia

properties.title: Norba
properties.description: Norba, located in the Monti Lepini, was a member of the Latin League (ca. 499 B.C.) and became a Latin colony ca. 492 B.C. The city was destroyed in the early first century B.C.

properties.title: Isola Sacra
properties.description: An extensive second and third century A.D. necropolis located between the city of Ostia and Portus.

properties.title: Cora
properties.description: A Latin center in the Monti Lepini that was already a Roman municipium by 211 B.C.

properties.title: Mondragone
properties.description: A Renaissance villa (Villa Mondragone) was built atop the platform of a Roman villa dating to the first century B.C.

properties.title: Fortis Fortuna, T.
properties.description: A sanctuary (fanum) of Fors Fortuna in Trastevere. Varro ascribes its foundation to Servius Tullius.

properties.title: Lucio Vero
properties.description: A Roman villa located at Acquatraversa on the Via Cassia that is frequently attributed to Lucius Verus.

properties.title: Munazio Planco
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Munazio Planco

properties.title: Grotta di Paris
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Grotta di Paris

properties.title: Montioni
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Montioni

properties.title: Colle Nocello
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Colle Nocello

properties.title: Lamnae/Ad Lam(i)nas
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C1 Lamnae/Ad Lam(i)nas

properties.title: Crustumerium
properties.description: An ancient town of Latium located at the headwaters of the Allia river, very close to the territory of the Sabines, Crustumerium figures in Rome's early history. The Romans conquered the site in 500 B.C. and formed the tribus Crustumina or Clustumina in 471 B.C.

properties.title: Lorium
properties.description: An ancient town on the Via Aurelia.

properties.title: Giordani
properties.description: A fourth century A.D. catacomb along the via Salaria at Rome.

properties.title: Ficulea
properties.description: Ficulea was an ancient city of Latium situated between Rome and Nomentum.

properties.title: Montedoro
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Montedoro

properties.title: Laurentes
properties.description: Laurentum was an ancient city of Latium located some 16 miles from Rome, between Ostia and Lavinium. Its precise location can no longer be determined. In Rome's legendary history Laurentum is the site of king Latinus' dwelling.

properties.title: Latium Vetus (region)
properties.description: Latium Vetus is an historical region of Italy. Latium Vetus begins south of the Tiber river and extends as far as Circeo, at which point the boundary of Latium Adiectum is reached.

properties.title: Monte dell'Oro
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Monte dell'Oro

properties.title: Fidenae
properties.description: Fidenae was an ancient city of Latium.

properties.title: La Giostra
properties.description: A fortified site on the Via Appia dating to the Republican period.

properties.title: Lolli Paolini
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Lolli Paolini

properties.title: Grotta Oscura
properties.description: The quarries at Grotta Oscura were an important source of high-quality tuff located in the territory of Veii. This was the "tuffo giallo della via Tiberina" that was used at Rome from the Archaic period onward.

properties.title: Laghetto di Colonna
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Laghetto di Colonna

properties.title: Colle Rosa
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Colle Rosa

properties.title: Monteverde
properties.description: The hill of Monteverde, a part of the Ianiculum hill to the west of the Tiber river, was a source of a brown, lithoid tuff (tufo di Monteverde) that was quarried for use as a building material from the second century BC.

properties.title: Pedum?
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Pedum?

properties.title: Grotta Papale
properties.description: The site of a Roman villa situated on two terraces. The modern toponym "Grotta Papale" derives from a partially subterranean apsidal nymphaeum. The villa was extensive, covering some 23,000 square meters and has both a late republican and an imperial phase.

properties.title: Muraccio dell’Omo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Muraccio dell’Omo

properties.title: Dea Dia (temple)
properties.description: The Arval Brethren cultivated the cult of the Dea Dia. Remains of this Augustan era temple, located at La Tavernaccia restaurant in the Magliana vecchia neighborhood of Rome, are subterranean and not open to the public.

properties.title: Grottarossa
properties.description: Grottarossa is located at the intersection of key roadways in northern suburbium of Rome, lying along the Via Flaminia as well as at the point where the Via Veientana separated from the Via Cassia and thereby connected Rome with Veii. There is archaeological evidence for tombs, both built tombs and rock-cut tombs in the exposed tuff escarpments, as well as villas.

properties.title: Largo Preneste
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Largo Preneste

properties.title: Colle Medico
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Colle Medico

properties.title: Osteria dell’Osa
properties.description: The site of a major Iron Age necropolis (Latial chronology) composed of over 600 burials.

properties.title: Pianabella
properties.description: A large Christian basilica discovered in 1976 several hundred meters southeast of the Porta Laurentina of Ostia. The original phase dates to the end of the fourth century A.D.

properties.title: Monte Tosto
properties.description: An Etruscan and Roman site lying 4 km to the west of Caere along the monumental road leading to Pyrgi. Until the early 1960s, the site was known for the monumental tumulus that Mengarelli had excavated in the 1920s. Subsequent excavation revealed other evidence, including an elite compound that served as a sanctuary.

properties.title: Villa Gordiani
properties.description: A third century A.D. villa complex along the Via Praenestina connected with Gordian I, Gordian II, and Gordian III.

properties.title: Lepinus (mountain)
properties.description: Lepinus M., a mountain range of central Italy that belongs to the Anti-Apennines.

properties.title: Lavinium
properties.description: An ancient city of Latium on the Numicus river that was founded, according to Virgil, by Aeneas.

properties.title: Grotta del Mortale
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Grotta del Mortale

properties.title: Ficana
properties.description: An ancient city of Latium that was said to have been conquered by Ancus Marcius, Ficana was located near the eleventh mile of the Via Ostiensis. Excavation at the site has produced important evidence for the urban center beginning from the eighth century BC. Pliny the Elder mentions Ficana as one of the lost cities of Latium.

properties.title: Pianelle
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Pianelle

properties.title: Monteroni
properties.description: Monteroni, near Ladispoli, is the site of an Etruscan necropolis.

properties.title: Naumachia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Naumachia

properties.title: Ostia
properties.description: The port city of ancient Rome located at the mouth of the river Tiber.

properties.title: Colle Monitola
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Colle Monitola

properties.title: Lanuvium
properties.description: Lanuvium was an important city of Latium located south of the Alban Hills. After opposing Rome at the battle of Aricia (504 B.C.) and Lake Regillus (496 B.C.), Lanuvium was captured by the Romans in 338 B.C.

properties.title: Grottaferrata
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Grottaferrata

properties.title: Temple of Diana at Nemi
properties.description: A site sacred to Diana near Lake Nemi, comprised of a Tuscan-style sanctuary and a sacred grove.

properties.title: Marmenia
properties.description: The Domus Marmeniae is a villa located on the Via Appia near the fourth milestone. The villa grounds hosted a pagan necropolis and tradition holds that the matrona, Marmenia, relocated the body of St. Urban to a mausoleum built on the grounds.

properties.title: Fortuna Muliebris, T.
properties.description: A sanctuary dedicated to Fortuna Muliebris along the Via Latina. Tradition holds that it was dedicated in 487 B.C.

properties.title: Fregenae
properties.description: An ancient town of Etruria, Fregenae was located between Alsium and the mouth of the river Tiber.

properties.title: Numicus (river)
properties.description: The Numicus flumen was a river of Latium connected with the legendary history of Aeneas. Modern Fosso di Pratica in Italy.

properties.title: Corniculum
properties.description: An ancient town of Latium connected with the origins of Serivus Tullius.

properties.title: Inviolata
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Inviolata

properties.title: Colle Vitriano
properties.description: Colle Vitriano is the site of a Roman villa supported on two artificial terraces that utilize megalithic walling in the polygonal masonry technique as well as caementicium.

properties.title: Opimiano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Opimiano

properties.title: Nemorensis (lake)
properties.description: Nemorensis Lacus (modern Lake Nemi) is a small, volcanic lake in Latium located south of Rome. The lake is known for its adjacent sanctuary of the goddess Diana and for a number of sunken Roman ships of the first century AD that were recovered from it.

properties.title: Nettuno
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C4 Nettuno

properties.title: Ospedale di S. Camillo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Ospedale di S. Camillo

properties.title: La Colombella
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 La Colombella

properties.title: Iuppiter?, T.
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Iuppiter?, T.

properties.title: Corzano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Corzano

properties.title: Forum Appii
properties.description: An ancient road station on the Via Appia located 69 km southeast of Rome.

properties.title: Marina di S. Nicola
properties.description: Marina di S. Nicola is located close to Alsium.

properties.title: Torre Caetani
properties.description: A Medieval tower located on Tiber Island.

properties.title: Nuraghe Santu Antine
properties.description: A nuragic structure dating originally ca. 1,600 to 1,450 BC.

properties.title: Poliochne
properties.description: A Bronze Age settlement on the island of Lemnos, Poliochne pre-dates Troy I and shows influence from the Greek mainland during Early Helladic II (ca. 2500 BC). Mycenaean horizons have also been identified.

properties.title: Temple of Hera II (Neptune)
properties.description: A fifth century B.C. Doric temple, the so-called Temple of Hera II is also sometimes referred to as the Temple of Neptune.

properties.title: Aeflanus (mountain)
properties.description: Colle Ripoli-Monte S. Angelo.

properties.title: Collatia
properties.description: Collatia was an ancient city of Latium located between Gabii and the Anio fl. A colony of Alba Longa, Collatia was one of the most ancient cities of Latium. Subjugated by Rome under the Tarquins, Collatia would decline during the Republican period and numbers among the lost Latin cities by the accounting of Pliny the Elder.

properties.title: Case Nuove 2
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Case Nuove 2

properties.title: Campo del Fico
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Campo del Fico

properties.title: Antemnae
properties.description: Antemnae is an ancient Latin settlement located north of Rome near the point where the Anio and Tiber rivers intersect. Connected with Rome's early history, Antemnae was involved in episodes such as the 'Rape of the Sabine Women' and Romulus is said to have celebrated a triumph over the Antemnates in 752 BC.

properties.title: Cimitero Maggiore
properties.description: A major Roman necropolis and catacomb along the Via Nomentana.

properties.title: Castel Madama
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Castel Madama

properties.title: Aquae Albulae
properties.description: A group of springs located west of Tibur (modern Tivoli). The main spring, known as Lago della Regina, preserves traces of an ancient Roman bath.

properties.title: Ad Sponsas
properties.description: Ad Sponsas was a road station on the Via Appia.

properties.title: Cabum?
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Cabum?

properties.title: Ad Statuas
properties.description: Ad Statuas was a road station on the Via Labicana located east of Rome.

properties.title: Aquae Albulae
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Aquae Albulae

properties.title: Castelporziano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 Castelporziano

properties.title: Cinecittà
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Cinecittà

properties.title: Antium
properties.description: Antium ranked as one of the most important and most powerful centers of Latium and was captured by Rome at the close of the Latin War in the fourth century B.C. Imperial Antium was well known for its number of coastal villas.

properties.title: Calepodius
properties.description: A Christian catacomb originally containing the tombs of Pope Callixtus I and Pope Julius I, along with that of the eponymous Saint Calepodius.

properties.title: Colle Gentile
properties.description: Colle Gentile is a naturally defensible hill with good visibility located in the environs of Norba. While the site has not been scientifically excavated, it has been surveyed. The Groningen Institute of Archaeology identified traces of polygonal masonry fortification walls as well as surface ceramics that indicate settlement activity associated with Archaic and Republican phases. Imperial period activity is absent.

properties.title: Case Nuove 1
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Case Nuove 1

properties.title: Aefula
properties.description: Aefula was an ancient settlement of Latium that had disappeared by the time of Pliny the Elder, although the cult of Bona Dea there continued to flourish.

properties.title: Cessati Spiriti
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Cessati Spiriti

properties.title: Castel Savello
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Castel Savello

properties.title: Ad Decimum
properties.description: The road station of Ad Decimum corresponds with the archaeological area of Castel di Decima where archaeological excavations in the 1970s identified the remains of a settlement covering some 11 hectares that dates to the eighth through sixth centuries BCE. Excavations revealed not only habitation evidence but also several hundred tombs.

properties.title: Bel Poggio
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Bel Poggio

properties.title: Albanus M.
properties.description: The second highest summit of the Alban Hills, Mons Albanus is an extinct volcano with an elevation of 950 m (3,117 ft). In the middle of the first millennium B.C. there may have been volcanic activity as noted by the historian Livy. The mountain was sacred for Latin peoples who held important festivals there and a major shrine to Iuppiter Latiaris stands on the mountain top.

properties.title: Casale di Gregna
properties.description: A villa at the seventh mile of the Via Latina.

properties.title: Centroni
properties.description: The Villa dei Centroni, located on the modern via Anagnina, lay at the ninth mile of the ancient via Latina. It dates from the first century B.C. onward.

properties.title: I Cappuccini
properties.description: The church and convent "I Cappuccini" in Frascati was the site of a Roman villa.

properties.title: Algidus (mountain)
properties.description: Algidus (mons) refers to the eastern rim of the dormant Alban volcano in the Alban Hills of central Italy, known today as  Monte Artemisio.

properties.title: Alsium
properties.description: Alsium served as a port for Caere, together with Fregenae.

properties.title: Ceres et Faustina, T.
properties.description: The Roman temple dedicated to Ceres and Faustina received patronage from Herodes Atticus. Its remains were eventually repurposed in the construction of the church of Sant'Urbano.

properties.title: Cappellette
properties.description: The site of a villa located between Frascati and Monte Porzio Catone. It is associated with Matidia Augusta on account of an inscribed fistula discovered there in 1888.

properties.title: Casale del Cavaliere
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Casale del Cavaliere

properties.title: Albuccione
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Albuccione

properties.title: Il Barco
properties.description: The so-called "Barco Borghese" is an archaeological site located in Monte Porzio Catone (Roma) in Italy. This multiperiod site began as a Roman terracing or substructure, perhaps originally meant to support a villa (basis villae). Subsequent modification and reuse converted the Roman structure into a "barco", an enclosure for animal hunts.

properties.title: Ad Decimum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Ad Decimum

properties.title: Ad Nonum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Ad Nonum

properties.title: Astura (river)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D4 Astura fl.

properties.title: Castra Albana
properties.description: Castra Albana was a permanent, fortified camp of the Legio II Parthica constructed during the Severan period.

properties.title: Ciciliano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Ciciliano

properties.title: Bruto e Pisoni
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Bruto e Pisoni

properties.title: Ad Aquas Salvias
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Ad Aquas Salvias

properties.title: Ad Nonum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Ad Nonum (1)

properties.title: Artena
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Artena

properties.title: Casal Rotondo
properties.description: A Roman tomb that supports a Medieval farmhouse (casale) at the sixth mile of the Via Appia. The tomb originally dates ca. 30 BC; it was a large, circular tomb with a diameter of approximately 35 m.

properties.title: Castrimoenium
properties.description: A Latin settlement that became a Roman municipium.

properties.title: Cervara 1
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Cervara 1

properties.title: Albunea (river)
properties.description: A toponym connected to the semi-legendary topography of Latium as described in the Aeneid.

properties.title: Ad Duas Lauros
properties.description: The toponym 'Ad Duas Lauros' refers to a large imperial property at the third mile of the Via Labicana and today comprised of the archaeological park of Centocelle. The site is mentioned in the Liber Pontificalis as that of a large imperial villa in which Helena, mother of Constantine I, lived. Archaeological work conducted in the late 1990s identified the remains of substantial Republican period villas in the same area, with evidence of both elite dwellings and viticulture. The villas identified are the Villa della Piscina and the Villa Ad Duas Lauros.

properties.title: Il Barco
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Il Barco

properties.title: L’Altare
properties.description: A small site in Latium (?1.2 hectares) that may have been fortified as early as the eighth century BCE.

properties.title: Capitolium
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Capitolium

properties.title: Casale Morena
properties.description: A villa located at the eighth mile of the ancient Via Latina. The villa was first built in the first century B.C. and continued in use until the fourth century. During its life span there were several phases of architectural modification and expansion.

properties.title: Alba Longa
properties.description: Alba Longa, located in the Alban Hills southeast of Rome, was the chief city and founder of the Latin League. Conflict with Rome caused Alba's destruction in the seventh century B.C. The legendary history of Romulus and Remus connects them to the royal lineage of the city. The ancient city is probably to be located at and around the site of modern Castel Gandolfo.

properties.title: Albanus L.
properties.description: A volcanic lake in ancient Latium at the foot of Albanus Mons, Albanus Lacus (Alban Lake) is connected with the site of the city of Alba Longa and, later, with imperial properties of the Flavian house.

properties.title: Casale Martellona
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Casale Martellona

properties.title: Capannacce
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Capannacce

properties.title: Anagnia
properties.description: Anagnia was a Hernican town that sided with Rome against the Volscians and later became civitas sine suffragio.

properties.title: Baebiana
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 Baebiana

properties.title: Ad Gallinas Albas
properties.description: Ad Gallinas Albas refers to a location along the Via Flaminia.

properties.title: Algidus
properties.description: An ancient settlement of Latium located in the territory of the Aequi.

properties.title: Cervara 2
properties.description: In the vicinity of Tor Cervara are anio tuff (tufo d'Aniene) quarries.

properties.title: Careiae
properties.description: An ancient town on the Via Clodia.

properties.title: La Cecchina
properties.description: The so-called "Torraccio della Cecchina" is a Roman funereal monument dating to the second century A.D. It is located at the ninth kilometer of the modern Via Nomentana.

properties.title: Aricia
properties.description: Aricia is an ancient Latin settlement and a member of the Latin League.

properties.title: Ad Pictas
properties.description: Ad Pictas is a road station east of Rome, known mostly for its role in Sulla's march on Rome in 88 B.C. The precise location of the statio continues to be debated.

properties.title: Ad Bivium
properties.description: A statio in Latium located at the intersection of the Via Latina and the Via Labicana, near the modern Valmontone.

properties.title: Bovillae
properties.description: A town of ancient Latium along the line of the Via Appia, Bovillae is traditionally considered to be a colony of Alba Longa and was one of the thirty cities of the Latin League.

properties.title: Caere
properties.description: Caere (also known as Cisra or Cerveteri) was a major Etruscan polis located ca. 50 km north-northwest of Rome in southern Etruria.

properties.title: Ad Turres
properties.description: Ad Turres was located on the Via Aurelia some 10 miles from Lorium and 12 miles from Pyrgi.

properties.title: Anio (river)
properties.description: The Anio river (modern Aniene) is a river of northern Latium.

properties.title: Campus Martius
properties.description: The Campus Martius or "field of Mars" is the name given to the level ground between the slopes of the Capitoline, the Quirinal, and Pincian hills, and the Tiber river.

properties.title: Casali Vitriano
properties.description: T. Ashby notes the presence of a villa platform to the west of the "upper Casale Vitriano". This platform seems to be a terrace at least 34 m in length.

properties.title: Aequi
properties.description: The Aequi were an ancient Italic tribe of northeast Latium in the first millennium BC.

properties.title: Buon Riposo
properties.description: Buon Riposo is a small, fortified settlement covering some 2 hectares. Its fortifications date to the seventh century BCE or later.

properties.title: Acqua Acetosa
properties.description: A settlement along the Via Laurentina that has yielded significant evidence for protohistoric occupation, including funereal evidence of the eighth and seventh centuries B.C.

properties.title: Ad Quintanas
properties.description: Ad Quintanas is the name of a road station on the Via Labicana.

properties.title: Ardea
properties.description: Ardea was an ancient settlement of the Rutuli in Latium.

properties.title: Villa degli Antonini
properties.description: The so-called 'Villa of the Antonines', located near Genzano di Roma in the Alban Hills, lies just south of the Via Appia between the road's 18th and 19th milestones.

properties.title: Castel Campanile
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 Castel Campanile

properties.title: Cassio
properties.description: A villa in Tibur that has been incorrectly linked to Gaius Cassius Longinus. In the eighteenth century, the site produced a cache of Egyptianizing sculpture that likely dates to the reign of Hadrian and is now held in the Vatican Museums.

properties.title: Civitana
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Civitana

properties.title: Case Rosse
properties.description: Ashby describes a rich archaeological landscape that once included the remains of Roman-period tombs and villas, the latter appointed with mosaics. The modern toponym "Case Rosse" is said to derive from a well-preserved Roman tomb executed in brick that was purposefully destroyed in 1824.

properties.title: Clodio
properties.description: Cicero describes the villa of Publius Clodius Pulcher as being located at the thirteenth mile of the Via Appia near Bovillae.

properties.title: Le Castella
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Le Castella

properties.title: Arcinazzo
properties.description: An imperial villa of the Trajanic and Hadrianic periods located on the Altipiani di Arcinazzo.

properties.title: Ad Sextum
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Ad Sextum

properties.title: Acquafredda
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Acquafredda

properties.title: Buglioncino
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Buglioncino

properties.title: Afilae
properties.description: Located in the Anio river valley to the south of Subiaco, Afilae was a municipium that was likely assigned to the tribus Aniensis.

properties.title: Casali
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Casali

properties.title: Campoverde
properties.description: Campoverde (Lazio) lies some 60 km south of Rome. In 1977-1978 a quantity of votive material was recovered from a body of water known as the "Laghetto del Monsignore". This spring-fed body of water was interpreted as an open-air votive depository.

properties.title: Annunziatella
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Annunziatella

properties.title: Adriano
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Adriano

properties.title: Tomb of Seti I
properties.description: Tomb KV17 in the Valley of Kings was the burial place of the 19th dynasty Pharaoh Seti I.

properties.title: Theater at Patara/Arsinoe
properties.description: The Theater at Patara/Arsinoe dates to the reign of Tiberius and was subsequently renovated under the Antonines.

properties.title: Pons Aemilius
properties.description: The Pons Aemilius was the first stone bridge across the Tiber river at Rome (241 B.C.). Its remains are known today as the 'Ponte Rotto'.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 unnamed bridge (Ad Sponsas)

properties.title: Untitled

properties.title: Untitled

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 unnamed bridge (Ad Turres)

properties.title: Unnamed bridge
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 unnamed bridge (Cora)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 unnamed canal (Villa Domitiani, from Albanus L.)

properties.title: Emissarium of Lake Nemi
properties.description: An artificial canal originally dating to the fourth century BCE that was built by the inhabitants of Ariccia in order to regulate the waters of Lake Nemi.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 unnamed canal group (Portus)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 unnamed canal (SE Ostia)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D4 unnamed canal group (SW Forum Appii)

properties.title: Unnamed canals
properties.description: unnamed canal group (NW Pomptinae Paludes)

properties.title: Nuraghe Santa Sarbana
properties.description: A nuragic complex in Silanus, Sardinia, dating to the period ca. 1500-1000 BC.

properties.title: Bilske Horodyshche
properties.description: Archaeological site near the village of Bilsk in Ukraine; possibly the site of Gelonos, identified by Herodotus as the capital city of the Budini.

properties.title: Lacus Curtius
properties.description: The Lacus Curtius is an area in medio foro connected with the earliest phases of Rome's occupation. By the late Republican period it had become a small basin set inside a paved area. Livy relates the famous episode of the Sabine Mettius Curtius in relation to his description of the site.

properties.title: Tongeren Gallo-Roman temple complex
properties.description: The Gallo-Roman temple complex of Tongeren is located in the northwestern part of the city of Tongeren. The site pre-dates the Roman city wall.

properties.title: Tchogha Zanbil
properties.description: An ancient Elamite complex founded ca. 1250 BC by the king Untash-Napirisha. Tchogha Zanbil was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979.

properties.title: S’Ena ’e Thomes
properties.description: A well-preserved 'giant's tomb' dating ca. 2000-1600 BC.

properties.title: Wansdyke (earthwork)
properties.description: Wansdyke is a series of Medieval defensive linear earthworks in the West Country of England.

properties.title: Gravelly Guy
properties.description: A settlement near modern Stanton Harcourt, Oxfordshire, England, occupied from the late Neolithic through the Roman periods.

properties.title: Jabal al-Bayḍā
properties.description: Hill southwest of Mount 'Abd al-'Aziz in Syria. The peak at the southwestern end of the hill is known as Rās et-Tell. Excavations were carried out there by Max von Oppenheim in the early 20th century, uncovering sculptures and graves from the Bronze Age.

properties.title: Dhāt Kāhl
properties.description: Large town in the Arabian Peninsula inhabited from the 4th century BCE-5th century CE. The town was the capital of the Kindah Kingdom.

properties.title: Santa Prisca
properties.description: A titular church on Rome's Aventine Hill dedicated to Saint Prisca. A Mithraeum dating to the late first century A.D. was discovered on the site in 1934.

properties.title: Khirbet Qeiyafa
properties.description: Khirbet Qeiyafa, also known as Elah Fortress, is an Iron Age fortress site located about 40 kilometers southwest of Jerusalem, overlooking the Elah Valley. The site was likely constructed in the late eleventh century BCE and destroyed or abandoned in the mid- to late tenth century BCE.

properties.title: Scheggia Pass
properties.description: The Scheggia Pass marks the division between the Central and Northern Apennines in northern Umbria. Its elevation is 632 meters above sea level.

properties.title: So-called Arch of Hadrian (Capua)
properties.description: The remains of a triple arch in opus latericium marking the pomerium of Capua. It is perhaps originally constructed under the Flavians.

properties.title: El-Qitar
properties.description: Bronze Age fortified site located on the Euphrates in Syria.

properties.title: Trenčin castle
properties.description: A castle located above the town of Trenčín in western Slovakia that preserves epigraphic evidence of Roman military activity during the Marcomannic Wars.

properties.title: Mausoleum of Menenius Agrippa
properties.description: The so-called mausoleum of Menenius Agrippa stands along the Via Nomentana.

properties.title: Ad Mallias
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 46 unlocated Ad Mallias

properties.title: Pandosia
properties.description: Pandosia was an ancient city of Bruttium.

properties.title: Tell Abu Hureyra
properties.description: A tell with human settlement horizons stretching from the Epipaleolithic period to the Neolithic period. The remains of the site are now inundated by Lake Assad.

properties.title: Roman theater at Amman/Philadelpheia
properties.description: A second century Roman theater at Amman that could seat 6,000 spectators.

properties.title: Regio II, Pompeii
properties.description: The so-called Regio II, an archaeological subdivision located in the eastern section of Pompeii, includes the Amphitheater and the Large Palaestra, as well as a number of residences and commercial structures.

properties.title: Seleucid Empire
properties.description: The Seleucid Empire was a Hellenistic kingdom, founded by Seleucus I Nicator, and ruled by the Seleucid dynasty from 312 to 63 BCE. At its height it stretched from the Aegean Sea to northern India, but it steadily lost territory and prestige. The remnants of the kingdom were eventually incorporated into Roman territory as the province of Syria in 64 BCE.

properties.title: Aššur-mušalbir-palê-šarri-ēpišīšu-nāṣir-ummānīšu
properties.description: The Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) surrounded his new capital Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") with a rectangular-shaped, 16,280-cubit-long inner and outer city wall. The name of the city wall (dūru) was Aššur-mušalbir-palê-šarri-ēpišīšu-nāṣir-ummānīšu ("The God Aššur Is the One Who Prolongs the Reign of Its Royal Builder (and) Protects His Troops") according to some Akkadian royal inscriptions, but Aššur-mulabbir-palê-šarri-ēpišīšu-nāṣir-perʾīšu ("The God Aššur Is the One Who Prolongs the Reign of Its Royal Builder (and) Protects His Offspring") according to other texts written in the name of Sargon II.

properties.title: Suhail
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Subura
properties.description: Subura (or Suburra) refers to an area of ancient Rome, although the precise spatial definition of this area is unclear. In the earliest instances, this toponym may refer to the valley lying between the Oppian and the Caelian. As such it corresponds to one of the four urban regions known as the "Servian" regions. In later times the Subura referred to a part of the Augustan regio IV which was known as a densely populated area between the Esquiline, Quirinal, Viminal, and Cispian hills and had a rough and seedy reputation.

properties.title: Montelabate
properties.description: The Montelabate estate of the Gaslini foundation has been investigated by means of both field survey and excavation. This upland area sits astride a frontier zone, one that separates Perugia (Etruria) from Gubbio (Umbria). Simon Stoddart, Maurizio Matteini Chiari, Gabriele Cifani, and other scholars have noted that this ancient frontier zone was in place by the fifth-fourth centuries BC and denotes the differential urbanism practices of Etruscans and Umbrians, respectively.

According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of four temples in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Ekišnugal
properties.description: The temple of the god Sîn, Ekišnugal (“House of the Great Light”), was located in the Kullab district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of four temples in that part of Babylon. The temple is mentioned in Old Babylonian Period texts and was (re)built by the Old Babylonian king Abī-ēšuh (r. ca. 1711–1684 BC) and the Neo-Babylonian ruler Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–562 BC). The temple survived into the Hellenistic Period.

properties.title: Emah
properties.description: The temple of the goddess Ninmah/Bēlet-ilī, Emah (“Exalated House”), was located in the Ka-dingirra district (modern Kasr) of Babylon. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, this was one of four temples in that part of the city, which was located in the northern part of the eastern half of Babylon. Emah was rebuilt by the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal (r. 668–ca. 631 BC) and the Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–562 BC).

Egišhurankia seems to have been located near Imgur-Enlil, along the northern wall.

These formal gardens occupied what had previously been the agger of the Servian walls and the adjacent necropolis that had an unsavory reputation. Following the death of Maecenas, the gardens became imperial property.
