properties.description: Circus Gaii et Neronis was originally built as a private racecourse for the emperor Caius. In the fourth century A.D., the north side of the circus was destroyed in order to make room for the first basilica of St. Peter.

properties.title: Hurri/Ba'il-hurri
properties.description: A mountain, probably located on Cyprus, possibly near Larnaka/Kition, perhaps in the vicinity of Stavrovouni Monastery.

properties.title: Cardo Maximus
properties.description: The Cardo Maximus of Saepinum.

properties.title: Isis Tomb
properties.description: Now lost, the so-called "Isis Tomb" was excavated at Vulci in the 19th century. Based on finds evidence, the tomb is traditionally dated ca. 625 to 550 B.C. Its traditionally assigned name is likely a misnomer, based on a contemporary identification of a bronze bust as representing the Egyptian goddess Isis. The subsequent back-filling of the tomb and uncareful recording at the time have caused the tomb's location to be lost to us.

properties.title: Lyne
properties.description: A Roman auxiliary fort in Scotland guarding the road from Trimontium to Castledykes.

properties.title: Corinth Theater
properties.description: The origins of the theater at Corinth lie in the fifth century B.C. The complex was further expanded during the Hellenistic period. An elaborate renovation during the reign of Hadrian further improved the complex and added a new orchestra and scaenae frons.

properties.title: Mastaba of Ptahshepses at Abusir
properties.description: The mastaba-style tomb of Ptahshepses, vizier to the Fifth Dynasty Pharaoh Nyuserre Ini. Following the intial elite burials in the Old Kingdom, the mastaba became a funerary site for new burials during the Late Period.

properties.title: Arzâ
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources; the modern site is T. Ǧāmā.

properties.title: Skarkos Hill
properties.description: Site of a prehistoric settlement of the Cycladic civilization on the island of Ios.

properties.title: Alalaḫ
properties.description: A major Late Bronze Age city in the Amuq River Valley, inhabited during the Second Millennium BCE until about the 12th century BCE.

properties.title: Palace of Adad-nārārī III
properties.description: The Assyrian king Adad-nārārī III (r. 810-783 BC) constructed a palace for himself at Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud). This royal residence, whose walls were covered with white plaster and painted with geometric and floral motifs, was built immediately to the south of the palace of his great-grandfather Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC).

properties.title: Durisdeer
properties.description: The best preserved of the series of Roman fortlets established in upper Annandale and Nithsdale, dating ca. A.D. 140.

properties.title: Drumlanrig
properties.description: A Roman auxiliary fort located at Drumlanrig in Scotland.

properties.title: Unnamed tunnel on the aqueduct supplying Saldae
properties.description: An aqueduct tunnel, near Saldae, sometimes referred to as the Nonius Datus tunnel.

properties.title: Goshavank
properties.description: Monastery in modern Tavush province, Armenia, constructed in the 12th-13th centuries CE.

properties.title: Eumachia Building
properties.description: Located on the east side of Pompeii's forum (VII, 9, 1), the so-called Eumachia building is a large, public building financed by Eumachia, a public priestess of Venus in Pompeii during the middle of the first century AD.

properties.title: tribus Sergia
properties.description: An older rural tribe of ancient Rome.

properties.title: Spurie (island)
properties.description: An island now known as Yılanlı Island.

properties.title: Areni
properties.description: The so-called "Areni-1 cave complex" is an archaeological site located near the Areni village in southern Armenia along the Arpa River. The site shows evidence for both ritual and occupational activity in the late Chalcolithic to Early Bronze Age.

properties.title: al-Kuwait
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Theatrum Marcelli
properties.description: Theatrum Marcelli (Theater of Marcellus) is an ancient Roman theater in the Circus Flaminius. Augustus completed its construction and dedicated it in 12 BC.

properties.title: Regio I (Porta Capena)
properties.description: Regio I (Porta Capena), one of the administrative regions of the city of Rome instituted by Augustus in 7 BCE. In addition to the named monuments and buildings, the Regionary Catalogues indicate that this district also included 10 vici (streets), 10 shrines (aediculae), 3,250 blocks of apartment buildings (insulae); 120 houses (domus); 16 grain warehouses (horrea); 86 bath-houses (balinea); 81 or 87 cisterns/fountains (lacos), and 20 bakeries or mills (pistrina). Its administrative apparatus included 48 vicomagistri and two curators (curatores). Its circumference is given as 12,211 paces (pedes).

properties.title: Tarbiṣu
properties.description: Tarbiṣu, now modern Sherif Khan, was an Assyrian city located about 5 kilometers north of Nineveh. It was the principal cult center of the god Nergal in Assyria. Starting in the 8th and 7th centuries B.C., Tarbiṣu was a royal city and one of the primary residences of the Assyrian crown prince, who was trained in the art of kingship in the palace built there.

properties.title: Underground Shrine (Paestum)
properties.description: A small, underground tomb-like structure located in the agora of Paestum, thought to be either a shrine or a heroon.

properties.title: Mount Fumaiolo
properties.description: A mountain of the northern Apennines (elevation 1,408 m; 4,619 ft) from which the Tiber River originates.

properties.title: Unnamed iron mine
properties.description: Located to the west of Hippo Regius (modern Annaba in Algeria).

properties.title: Hagia Sophia
properties.description: A major paleochristian, then Byzantine, church in Istanbul; subsequently an Islamic mosque, and today a museum.

properties.title: Ponte Romano Di Largo Impero, Santa Marinella
properties.description: The remains of a Roman bridge located in the comune of Santa Marinella.

properties.title: Ponte di Apollo, Punicum
properties.description: A Roman bridge.

properties.title: Temple of Augustus et Livia
properties.description: The so-called Temple of Augustus et Livia dates ca. 10 B.C. and was originally dedicated to Roma and Augustus. The temple was located on the ancient forum of the city. By the fifth century the temple had become a Christian church. It was extensively restored in the nineteenth century.

properties.title: Komaros Limen
properties.description: A harbor near Actium.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 F3 unnamed bridge (S Rusicade)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 H3 unnamed bridge (S Hippo Regius)

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 H3 unnamed bridge (N Niniba)

properties.title: Stadium at Nemea
properties.description: The ancient Greek stadium at the pan-hellenic sanctuary of Nemean Zeus.

properties.title: Palace of Ashurbanipal
properties.description: The Neo-Assyrian king Ashurbanipal built a grand royal residence in the citadel of Nineveh. It was located north and east of the temples of the god Nabû (Ezida) and the goddess Ištar (Emašmaš), and it was constructed on the site of an older, smaller palace. Ashurbanipal referred to this palace as the bīt redûti ("House of Succession"); in scholarly literature, it is often referred to as the "North Palace." A small portion of the once-grand Assyrian palace is still visible today.

properties.title: Bowes Moor
properties.description: A small, square Roman temporary camp along the main Roman road between York and Carlisle.

properties.title: Tempio di Venere, Baiae
properties.description: The so-called "Tempio di Venere" is likely part of a bathing complex dating to the reign of Hadrian. The surviving structure has an octagonal plan.

properties.title: Shurdhah (modern island)
properties.description: An island in northern Albania, created in modern times when surrounding land was flooded by the creation of a reservoir. It is the site of the llyrian settlement of Sarda.

properties.title: Yeavering Bell
properties.description: The Yeavering Bell is a twin-peaked hill in Northumberland, England, that forms part of the Cheviot Hills.

properties.title: Roman theater of Stobi
properties.description: The Roman theater of Stobi dates to the second century.

properties.title: Aphrodision
properties.description: Located outside the city walls of Pergamon, this temple, according to an inscription (OGIS 273-9), was supposedly the site of a victory of Attalos I over the Tolistogi, Galatians, and Antiochus Hierax. it was likely later destroyed by Philip V.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 B4 no. 1 (mausoleum)

properties.title: Mausoleum of Quintus Lollius Urbicus
properties.description: Quintus Lollius Urbicus served as a governor of Britannia between 139 and 142. His career is detailed on a pair of inscriptions from his hometown of Tiddis. His mausoleum is located at Tiddis.

properties.title: Ajanta Caves
properties.description: The Ajanta Caves are among the earliest Buddhist cave monuments and date from the second and first centuries B.C. During the Gupta period (fifth and sixth centuries A.D.), additional decorated caves were added to the group.

properties.title: Old Winteringham
properties.description: Site of extensive Roman occupation and possible Claudio-Neronian military base where Ermine Street crosses the river Humber, opposite the fort at Petuaria (Brough-on-Humber).

properties.title: Tell Qasile
properties.description: Archaeological site on the Yarkon River in modern Tel Aviv, identified as a Philistine city inhabited during the 12th and 11th centuries BCE.

properties.title: Almendres Cromlech
properties.description: A megalithic complex located near Guadalupe, Portgual, dating to the Early Neolithic period.

properties.title: So-called Area X in Berenike
properties.description: The ruins of a small building (possibly first century AD) with a shrine, in the archaeological site of Sidi Khiribech, in Berenike. According to some archaeologists, it might have been connected to the adjacent Area A, and constitute together a single unit. In other interpretations, it is an independent sacred space.

properties.title: Via Portuensis?
properties.description: The Via Portuensis is an ancient Roman road that connected Rome and Portus. It proceeded along the right bank of the Tiber river, starting from the Pons Aemilius. In the first part of its course it is identical to the Via Campana.

properties.title: Torre del Giudizio
properties.description: Torre del Giudizio is a Medieval tower built atop a pre-existing Roman site located near the fluvial harbor of vicus Alexandrini.

properties.title: Grange stone circle
properties.description: Grange stone circle or Lios na Grainsi is the largest stone circle in Ireland, consisting of 113 stones and was built ca. 2100 BC.

properties.title: Tall-e Bakun A
properties.description: The larger of the two mounds that make up the Tall-e Bakun site.

properties.title: Monteriggioni
properties.description: A Medieval settlement where numerous important Etruscan tombs have been excavated.

properties.title: Porta Trigemina
properties.description: Now lost, the Porta Trigemina was one of the main gates of the Servian Wall.

properties.title: Vagnari
properties.description: A villa, vicus, and necropolis site in modern Puglia, Italy, located near the modern city of Gravina. The site was active from the first to fourth centuries CE.

properties.title: Sam'alla (kingdom)
properties.description: Sam'alla (šmʾl; also known as Bīt-Gabbāri and yʾdy) was a small Aramean kingdom/city-state during the first half of the first millennium BC. It is named after its capital city Sam'al (modern Zincirli Höyük).

properties.title: Chalandriani
properties.description: A major Early Bronze Age necropolis on Syros, Chalandriani contains tombs related to the Keros-Syros culture of the Early Cycladic II period.

properties.title: Kastri
properties.description: The fortified settlement of Kastri near Chalandriani on the Cycladic island of Syros is an important Early Cycladic II site. This fortified hill-top settlement is a very early example of a site in the Aegean with a fortification wall reinforced by means of stone bastions.

properties.title: Upper Chambers at Kalhu
properties.description: This ornately-decorated, elevated building might have been the residence of Sammu-ramat (the legendary Semiramis) in the palace of her son Adad-nārārī III (r. 810-783 BC) at Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud). Because these rooms were built noticeably higher than the surrounding area, its first excavator Austen Henry Layard believed that he had uncovered part of an upper floor of an Assyrian palace and, therefore, referred to this area as the “Upper Chambers.”

properties.title: Organa/Turgana (island)
properties.description: An island located near the Strait of Hormuz. Some sources suggest that Organa be equated with Lārak island, while others suggest Hormuz island.

properties.title: Anamis/Andanis/Ananis (river)
properties.description: Anamis/An(d)anis fl. was a river located in Carmania.

properties.title: Zetis
properties.description: Zetis was an ancient city of Carmania, although its location can no longer be determined.

properties.title: Jaén
properties.description: A Spanish city located in Andalusia that once belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. It is now known as Jaén.

properties.title: Surviving colonnade of the imperial temple at Mérida
properties.description: The incorrectly so-called "Temple of Diana."

properties.title: Abu Bakr cemetery
properties.description: Burial area in the northwestern portion of the Giza Necropolis containing burials dated to the Fourth-Fifth Dynasties.

properties.title: Fingrinhoe Roman Site
properties.description: A multi-acre site, now located within the bounds of the Fingringhoe Wick Nature Discovery Park in Colchester. The site may have been or included a Roman military supply base that was in use until ca. A.D. 120. The site included several structures, a ditched enclosure, and a possible villa.

properties.title: Il Tondo
properties.description: A first century AD Roman amphitheater located in Latium near Zagorolo, Italy.

properties.title: Nuraghe Ruju
properties.description: A hilltop nuragic complex with a central tholos tower dating to the Middle and Final Bronze Age (1600-1000 BC).

properties.title: Gallo-Roman bath complex at Mackwiller
properties.description: A Gallo-Roman bath complex located at the modern town of Mackwiller in the French commune of Waldhambach.

properties.title: Trevinano
properties.description: Trevinano is a human settlement in Italy, located in the Province of Viterbo of northern Lazio. In antiquity the site was settled by Etruscans. In the eleventh century, the powerful Boncompagni-Ludovisi family built a castle there.

properties.title: Numidia (region)
properties.description: Numidia was an ancient region of North Africa. From the late third century B.C. to 40 B.C. the territory was controlled by the ancient kingdom of the Numidians. In pre-Roman terms the polity was divided between the Massylii in the east and the Masaesyli in the west.

properties.title: So-called Roman Baths in Apollonia
properties.description: An architectural complex near the sea in Apollonia. It went through different stages and alterations between, roughly, the fourth century B.C. and the seventh century A.D. It was probably used as a private villa, then as public baths and, perhaps, as cisterns in later years.

properties.title: Adad temple (Khorsabad)
properties.description: As part of the palatial complex of Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad), the eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) constructed six temples, including one to the god Adad.

properties.title: Šamaš temple (Khorsabad)
properties.description: As part of the palatial complex of Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad), the eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) constructed six temples, including one to the god Šamaš.

properties.title: Ningal temple (Khorsabad)
properties.description: As part of the palatial complex of Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad), the eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) constructed six temples, including one to the goddess Ningal.

properties.title: Qalaat al-Madiq
properties.description: A town and medieval fortress in northwestern Syria adjacent to the site of ancient Apamea.

properties.title: Rabati Malik
properties.description: An eleventh-century caravanserai along the Silk Road, now located in Uzbekistan. Rabati Malik Caravanserai was built under Karakhanid Shams-al-Mulk Nasr, son of Tamgachkhan Ibragim who ruled in Samarkand from 1068 to 1080. The site was added to the UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List in 2008.

properties.title: Tomba della Medusa (Roma)
properties.description: A Roman chamber tomb now located on the grounds of the Policlinico Umberto I hospital in Rome.

properties.title: Cricklade
properties.description: Modern day site of a Romano-British settlement in Wiltshire dating from first to fourth centuries A.D.

properties.title: Yurtbaşı/Melik Şerif
properties.description: A modern village in the Refahiye region of Turkey's Erzincan province where remains of ancient roads and routes converge and where a Roman milestone has been found. In Roman times, it was likely a walled town or fort, garrisoned at some point by the cohors I Lepidiana. Scholarly opinions differ as to its possible names in antiquity.

properties.title: Forum Boarium (at Pompeii)
properties.description: The so-called "Forum Boarium" in Pompeii was erroneously named by its 1755 excavators who discovered the bones of large bovids and assigned the name that still is used to describe this insula in Pompeii's Regio II (II, 5).

properties.title: Proposed location of Artulu 2 (Kayseri)
properties.description: Another proposed location of ancient Artulu is at or in the vicinity of modern Kayseri.

properties.title: Piazza d'Oro at Hadrian's Villa
properties.description: One of the largest and most luxurious complexes of Villa Hadriani. It is situated at the northern end of the Villa, and consists of a vast building, with a vaulted, octagonal vestibule to the north, a cenatio to the south, and a central quadriporticus, down the middle of which runs a canal.

properties.title: Casa dell’ Amore punito
properties.description: A domus excavated in 1844 and 1867.

properties.title: Kabnak
properties.description: An important town of the Middle Elamite period discovered at the archaeological site of Haft Tepe in southwestern Iran. The site was an important center of the Elamite kingdom in the 15th century BCE, and also shows signs of inhabitation from the Parthian to the Early Islamic periods.

properties.title: Amphitheater of Pompeii
properties.description: The Amphitheater of Pompeii is the earliest known surviving example of a Roman amphitheater. It was built between 80 and 70 B.C.

properties.title: Aquincum Military Amphitheater
properties.description: The Aquincum Military Amphitheater dates to the reign of Antoninus Pius.

properties.title: Rusahinili
properties.description: Rusahinili (modern Toprakkale) was an ancient fortress of Urartu built by Rusa I.

properties.title: Castle Dore
properties.description: Castle Dore is a fort located near Fowey in Cornwall that originated in the Iron Age and was re-occupied in the sixth century AD and again during the Middle Ages.

properties.title: Almo (river)
properties.description: A small river of the Ager Romanus that once joined the Tiber just below the walls of Rome. Almo, the eldest son of Tyrrhus, who is one of the heroes in Virgil's Aeneid, shares the river's name.

properties.title: Arch of Septimius Severus
properties.description: The Arch of Septimius Severus is situated at the northwest corner of the Forum Romanum. It was dedicated in A.D. 203 and serves to commemorate the Parthian victories of Emperor Septimius Severus and his two sons against the Parthians (194/195 and 197–199).

properties.title: Sanctuary of Iuno Gabina
properties.description: The Sanctuary of Iuno Gabina at Gabii.

properties.title: Corvey
properties.description: The abbey was first founded in 815 by Charlemagne's cousins, Wala and Adelard.

properties.title: Shahr-e Sukhteh
properties.description: A Bronze Age urban settlement, associated with the Jiroft culture, located in Sistan and Baluchistan provinces in the southeastern part of Iran. The site was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2014.

properties.title: Horti Maiani
properties.description: An urban garden of imperial Rome located on the summit of the Esquiline Hill. Based on an inscription dating to the reign of Claudius, it is believed that these gardens were administered by the same magistrate in charge of the Horti Lamiani, an official with the title "procurator hortorum Maianorum et Lamianorum".

properties.title: Hekateion
properties.description: The Hekateion is a monumental temple for the goddess Hekate constructed in Lagina ca. 125 BCE.

properties.title: Sanctuary of Isis at Dion
properties.description: The sanctuary of Isis at Dion dates to the second century A.D.

properties.title: Anduarsalia
properties.description: A fortress in the vicinity of Til-garimmu fortified by the Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721-705 BC) against Urarṭu.

properties.title: Arch of Septimius Severus at Lepcis Magna
properties.description: The Arch of Septimius Severus at Lepcis Magna dates ca. A.D. 203.

properties.title: Malvaccaro Roman villa

properties.title: Cistern
properties.description: A Roman period cistern of Olbia on Sardinia.

properties.title: St. Pauls villa
properties.description: A Late Roman villa discovered ca. 2005.

properties.title: Mures
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the south of the province of Jaén, near the current boundary of the province of Granada, that once belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X.

properties.title: Regio III (Isis et Serapis)
properties.description: The third Augustan administrative region of the city of Rome was centered on the Oppian Hill and derived its name from the Isis et Serapis on the Via Praenestina. In addition to the named monuments, the region included 12 streets, 12 shrines, 2,757 blocks of flats, 60/160 houses, 17 horrea, 80 bathhouses, 65 cisterns, and 16 bakeries or mills. The region had 48 magistrates and two curators. The perimeter of the region was 12,350 Roman feet.

properties.title: Tell el-Hayyat
properties.description: Village site located southwest of Pella (Tabaqat Fahl in Jordan). It was inhabited during the Early and Middle Bronze Age.

properties.title: Black Pyramid
properties.description: The pyramid of the Middle Kingdom Pharaoh Amenemhat III.

properties.title: Temple of Victory
properties.description: A Greek temple of the Doric order (peripteral hexastyle), built in the fifth century BC, possibly to celebrate a victory against the Carthaginians. Its ruins are still visible in the archaeological site of Himera.

properties.title: Ager Cosanus survey area
properties.description: The term "Ager Cosanus" refers to the territorium (territory) of the Latin right colony of Cosa, reportedly established by Rome in south Etruria in 273 B.C. following conflict with the Etruscan city of Vulci. The colonial center of Cosa has been the subject of ongoing archaeological inquiry since the late 1940s. Beginning in the 1970s, the hinterland of the city was subjected to intensive archaeological field survey. The Wesleyan University survey of the rural hinterland of Cosa identified approximately 132 sites.

properties.title: Khorsabad Gate 4
properties.description: This undecorated gate is the southernmost city gate of the southeast wall of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon"), the capital of the Assyrian Empire constructed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC).

properties.title: Plattetombe of Waasmont
properties.description: The Plattetombe (flat tomb) is a Gallo-Roman burial bound of the second century AD.

properties.title: Libraries' Courtyard at Hadrian's Villa
properties.description: The Libraries' Courtyard belongs to the republican period and is one of the most ancient gardens at Hadrian's Villa. It is enclosed in a large peristyle 48 m wide, 72 m long, and is located at the northern end of Villa Adriana.

properties.title: Sudelfels

properties.title: Akkad Survey Area
properties.description: The first archaeological survey of an area of north Babylonia associated with ancient Akkad. The survey was conducted in the 1950s by Robert Adams and Vaughn Crawford and published as an appendix to Gibson 1972. Its extent and methods were influential in the subsequent development of Mesopotamian archaeology.

properties.title: Mitteltaurus
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Frielas
properties.description: A Roman villa.

properties.description: A Roman villa located near several productive sites.

properties.title: Basilica Neptuni
properties.description: A building in the Campus Martius that originally dates to ca. 25 BCE.

properties.title: Review Palace
properties.description: An Assyrian armory was built to the south of the citadel at Nineveh. The ruins of the 7th-century B.C. architectural complex are directly below the modern settlement built on top of Nebi Yunus, the site's smaller mound.

properties.title: Pagus Ianiculensis
properties.description: Pagus Ianiculens is a name for a district of the Transtiberim during the Republican period. The name is attested in two inscriptions of ca. 100 B.C., one of which was found in an opus signinum pavement near the church of Santa Maria dell'Orto.

properties.title: Prata Mucia
properties.description: The so-called Prata Mucia was a meadow granted to the Roman Republican hero Mucius Scaevola in recognition of his heroism in the face of the invasion of Lars Porsena of Clusium.

properties.title: Nuraghe Coa de Serra
properties.description: A nuragic complex near Baunei, Sardinia.

properties.title: Temple of Jupiter
properties.description: The Temple of Jupiter (VII,8,1) in Pompeii sits at the north end of the forum. It was built in the middle of the second century BC.

properties.title: Ianus Quadrifons
properties.description: A quadrifrons triumphal arch at Rome that is located at a crossroads in the area of the Velabrum and the Forum Boarium. It dates to the early fourth century AD; its construction employed spolia and it likely honored either Constantine I or Constantius II.

properties.title: Sun Temple of Niuserre
properties.description: Temple dedicated to the god Ra in the 5th dynasty by the pharaoh Niuserre (Nyuserre).

properties.title: Tomb of Senwosret III
properties.description: The tomb of Senwosret III, a pharaoh of the 12th Dynasty in Egypt.

properties.title: Monte Nuxi
properties.description: A proto-nuragic settlement on Monte Nuxi that covered approximately one hectare. The remains of various built springs are evident.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Augusta Raurica
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Augusta Raurica accommodated ca. 13,000 spectators and was built ca. A.D. 170.

properties.title: Arch of Galerius
properties.description: The extant remains of a triumphal arch, constructed from 298 to 299 CE and dedicated in 303 CE under the tetrarch Galerius. It commemorates the capture of Ctesiphon from the Sassanids and forms part of a monumental entrance to the palace of Galerius.

properties.title: Latomos Monastery
properties.description: A late fifth century AD church, later associated with a small monastery in Thessaloniki, Greece.

properties.title: Church of Prophet Elijah
properties.description: A fourteenth century AD church in Thessaloniki.

properties.title: Tel Michal
properties.description: A site on the Mediterranean coast of Israel with signs of habitation from the Middle Bronze Age and the Persian through the Roman periods. In the Hellenistic and Roman periods, its purpose was primarily military, and a series of forts occupied the site until around 50 CE. A small watchtower or lighthouse was built on the site in the eighth-ninth centuries CE, after which it was abandoned.

properties.title: Verlamion
properties.description: An extensive Pre-Roman settlement near Roman Verulamium connected with the ruler Tasciovanus, whose coins bear its name as 'Verlamion'.

properties.title: Hypogeum of the Aurelii
properties.description: A third century AD hypogeum tomb on the Esquiline hill in Rome with both pagan and Paleochristian iconography.

properties.title: Monte Baranta
properties.description: A pre-nuragic architectural complex near Olemdo, Sardinia.

properties.title: Arch of Augustus at Ariminum
properties.description: The Arch of Augustus at Ariminum was dedicated in 27 B.C. and marked the end of the Via Flaminia.

properties.title: Fórnea Roman villa
properties.description: An imperial villa, occupied between the second and fourth centuries AD.

properties.title: Panjakent
properties.description: The easternmost city of Sogdiana, inhabited from the fifth-ninth centuries CE.

properties.title: San Roque Theatre - Carteia
properties.description: The Roman theater of Carteia.

properties.title: Arienzo
properties.description: A villa of the second century AD that was destroyed by a flood in the fourth century.

properties.title: Varignano Vecchio
properties.description: A villa maritima in eastern Liguria, inhabited from ca. 100 BC to the fifth century AD.

properties.title: Uršu/Waršuwa
properties.description: Uršu/Waršuwa was an Assyrian trading colony (kārum) located on the route between Aššur and Kaneš. This important city is attested in Eblaite and Sumerian sources, including an inscription of Gudea of Lagaš that describes the rebuilding of the temple of the god Ningirsu at Girsu; numerous Old Assyrian and Old Babylonian texts; and Hittite sources, for example, the annals of king Hattusili I, a literary composition generally referred to as ‘The Siege of Uršu,’ a treaty between the Hittite king and Sunassura of Kizzuwatna, and a land grant to a nobleman (Sahurunuwa).

properties.title: Loughbrickland Crannóg
properties.description: A Bronze Age crannog settlement located south west of Banbridge, County Down, Northern Ireland.

properties.title: Ponte Rotto necropolis
properties.description: The Ponte Rotto necropolis is associated with the Etruscan city of Vulci.

properties.title: Roman theater at Mogontiacum
properties.description: The site of the Roman theater in Mainz.

properties.title: Unnamed villa
properties.description: An unnamed villa from the Boreum region

properties.title: Theater at Saepinum
properties.description: The intramural theater at Saepinum is one of the best preserved structures at the site. Located in the northern part of the walled area, it is likely built between 2. B.C. and A.D. 4.

properties.title: Hypogeum of via Dino Compagni
properties.description: A Christian catacomb on the ancient Via Latina used during the fourth century.

properties.title: Bagneux Megalith
properties.description: A megalithic dolmen located in Saumur, France. This is one of the largest dolmens in France.

properties.title: Area Carruces
properties.description: Mentioned only in the Regionary Catalogues, the Area Carruces was perhaps a square where travelers were accustomed to leaving their carriages.

properties.title: Temple of Dionysos at Teos
properties.description: A Temple of Dionysos in the Ionic order begun in the Hellenistic period.

properties.title: Jā' (region)
properties.description: A region on Cyprus (Akkadian Jadnana). The eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II states that seven kings of Jāʾ, a region of Jadnana, sent him tribute.

properties.title: Kammanu/Meliddu (kingdom)
properties.description: A kingdom in eastern Anatolia, whose capital is classical Melitene (modern Arslantepe). Meliddu, which is sometimes referred to as Kammanu, was conquered by the eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II and its territory was given to Kummuhu.

properties.description: The Dipylon Gate was the sole double gate in Athens, erected next to the Holy Gate, near the Kerameikos.

properties.title: Akītu-Temple of Ištar
properties.description: The New Year’s House (or Akītu Temple) of Nineveh's tutelary deity Ištar appears to date back at least to the Middle Assyrian period (reign of Tukultī-Ninurta I). Its Sumerian ceremonial name is not preserved in extant cuneiform sources. This temple's exact location remains unknown and it is certain whether Ištar's Akītu Temple was located in the citadel or in the lower town.

properties.title: Tall Marjab
properties.description: Tall Marjab is a small, heavily denuded mound in the Dhi Qar province of southern Iraq, some 15 kilometers south of Nasiriya and ca. 10 kilometres southeast of Ur. Traces of a small settlement dating to fourth and third millennium BCE were found here in the course of brief excavations by British archaeologists Leonard Woolley and Max Mallowan in 1929-30.

properties.title: Bulla Regia
properties.description: A center for Numidian royalty, Bulla Regia first became an oppidum liberum in the reign of Augustus and then a colony under Hadrian. The site, which boasts significant archaeological remains, lies in modern Tunisia, about 5km north of the modern city of Jendouba. The site was reportedly known in the 19th century as Hammam-Darradji. Today, a small modern settlement named Aïn Babouch abuts the site (not to be confused with Babouch, which lies further north along the border with Algeria).

properties.description: The Santuario di Barbana is an ancient Marian shrine that dates ca. 582. It is said that Elia, the Patriarch of Aquileia, built a church near the hut of a hermit from Treviso by the name of Barbanus.

properties.title: So-called House of Jason Magnus
properties.description: A very large Roman house on the acropolis ridge of Cyrene.

properties.title: Korakou
properties.description: Korakou is a hill located on the Corinthian Gulf near New Corinth. It rises to 35 m above sea level. Carl Blegen conducted excavations at the site in 1915 and 1916. Archaeological remains show continuous use from the Early Helladic (EH) to Late Helladic periods (LH). It is suggested that the site served as a Mycenaean emporion. By the Archaic period the abandoned site gives way to burials.

properties.title: Eanšar

properties.title: Jerash Hippodrome

properties.title: Temple of Aphrodite Euploia
properties.description: The temple of Aphrodite Euploia is a tholos constructed in the fourth century BC in Knidos, a coastal city on the Datça Peninsula. It was built to house Praxiteles' famous nude statue of Aphrodite.

According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, this was one of two temples in that part of the city, which was located in the southern part of the eastern half of Babylon. The building was rebuilt by the Neo-Babylonian king Nabopolassar (r. 625–605 BC).

properties.title: Šamaš Gate

properties.title: Alepotrypa
properties.description: A cave in Diros Bay in Greece used as a settlement in the middle and late Neolithic Period. The site was sealed by an earthquake and abandoned around 3200 BCE.

properties.title: Arras-sur-Rhône Roman Milestone
properties.description: A Roman milestone located in the modern French commune of Arras-sur-Rhône, registered as a historical monument in 1926 when it was to be found in the cemetery of the church of Saint Clair.

properties.title: Tell Tweini
properties.description: Tell Tweini is an archaeological site located near Jableh, Syria. It was inhabited from the third millennium BC to the Persian period.

properties.title: Ekklesiasterion
properties.description: The Ekklesiasterion of Morgantina is located in the center of the ancient city. While its form resembles that of the Greek theater, it is posited that it functioned as a public building akin to the Roman comitium. It likely dates to the later fourth century B.C.

properties.title: Arch of Diocletian
properties.description: The Arch of Diocletian dates to the late third century.

properties.title: Ruinas de Tróia
properties.description: The Tróia peninsula in Portugal is the site of a large facility for the production of Roman fish sauce (garum) and ruins of a large industrial area for the processing has been excacated there.

properties.title: House of the Ara Maxima
properties.description: The House of the Ara Maxima, located on the Via del Vesuvio, is also known as the House of Pinarius and the House of Narcissus (VI, 16, 15-17).

properties.title: Fosso della Fiora
properties.description: One of the sources of the Aqua Traiana.

properties.title: Capitolinus Mons
properties.description: The smallest of Rome's hills and one of its most important, the Capitoline served as the citadel (arx) of the city and as the site of its poliadic temple.

properties.title: Nuraghe Cuccurada
properties.description: A nuragic complex composed of the nuraghe itself, a large wall, and a megalithic structure.

properties.title: Roman theater at Helikore/Nicaea
properties.description: Pliny the Younger discussed the restoration of the theater in a letter sent to the Roman emperor Trajan.

properties.title: Tomb of Trebius Iustus
properties.description: A Late Antique hypogeum tomb discovered in 1911 and dedicated to Trebius Iustus and Honoratia Severina.

properties.title: Temple of Khonsu at Karnak
properties.description: New Kingdom temple to the god Khonsu, constructed by Ramesses III and expanded by Ptolemy III Euergetes.

properties.title: Pian del Vescovo
properties.description: The Pian del Vescovo is the western necropolis of Blera and perhaps the most extensive. A variety of tomb types dating to the seventh and sixth centuries BCE are attested.

properties.title: Coddu Vecchiu
properties.description: A Bronze Age megalithic gallery grave on Sardinia that belongs to the "giants' tomb" classification.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater of Saintes
properties.description: The Gallo-Roman amphitheater of Mediolanum Santonum.

properties.title: Kara-Tepe

properties.title: Polonnaruwa
properties.description: An ancient city of the Kingdom of Polonnaruwa dating ca. AD 1070. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.

properties.title: Sepolcro dei Veienti
properties.description: The so-called "Sepolcro dei Veienti" is a ruined tomb of Roman imperial date. Built in opus caementicium and travertine, only the core of the rectangular structure remains. Likely located along the ancient Via Veientana, the tomb today stands in the modern Parco Papacci.

properties.title: Roman Baths (Bath)
properties.description: Bathhouse complex in Aquae Sulis, modern-day Bath. This well-preserved site is now a museum and the bathing complex itself is below modern street-level.

properties.title: Stifone
properties.description: Evidence of a Roman shipyard has been discovered at the locality of Stifone within the comune of Le Mole of the town of Narni. This shpiyard was connected to an artificial canal dug adjacent to the river Nera.

properties.title: Tomb of Virgil
properties.description: The so-called tomb of the Latin poet Virgil.

properties.title: Šamaš Gate
properties.description: The Šamaš Gate, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Šamaš-mušakšid-ernittīya ("The God Šamaš Is the One Who Makes Me Triumph"), is the first of the eight city gates of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") listed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in inscriptions recording the construction of his new capital. This gate is the first of the east-facing entrances to the city.

properties.title: Khorsabad Citadel Gate B
properties.description: This decorated gate was the principal entrance to the citadel of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon"), the capital of the Assyrian Empire constructed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC).

properties.title: New Basilica of Saint Apollinaris
properties.description: A basilica in Ravenna, Italy, erected by Theodoric the Great in the first quarter of the sixth century AD.

properties.title: Arian Baptistry

properties.title: Sepulcrum Hirtii
properties.description: The tomb of Aulus Hirtius, consul in 43 B.C., was discovered beneath the northwest corner of the Palazzo della Cancelleria in Rome in 1938.

properties.title: Beirut Souks
properties.description: Area along the western harbor of Beirut developed during phases of urban expansion from the 4th century BCE through the 1st century CE. The area was inhabited into late antiquity, with limited use into the medieval period. Rescue excavations were conducted in the area prior to its commercial redevelopment in the 1990s and early 2000s.

properties.title: Tell al-Ubaid

properties.description: An ancient suburban villa outside of Spoletium, occupied from the Augustan period to the third century A.D. The remains are on the grounds of the modern Villa Redenta complex.

properties.title: Investiture relief of Ardashir I

properties.title: Lago di San Floriano
properties.description: The lake of San Floriano is located in the Maremma plain near Capalbio.

properties.title: Capalbio
properties.description: Capalbio is a municipality in the Province of Grosseto. It is first attested in A.D. 805 when Charlemagne donated the locality to the Abbey of the Tre Fontane.

properties.title: Semien Mountains
properties.description: A mountain range of northern Ethiopia first mentioned in the Monumentum Adulitanum and now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

properties.title: Pietrera tomb
properties.description: An Etruscan tholos tomb of the seventh century B.C. at Vetulonia.

properties.title: Qal’at Sem’an/Church of Saint Simeon Stylites
properties.description: An ancient church, located in modern Syria. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011 as part of the "Ancient Villages of Northern Syria."

properties.title: Necròpolis fenicia de Jardin
properties.description: A Punic necropolis located in Los Toscanos, Spain, that was in use from the sixth to the fourth centuries BCE.

properties.title: Kidmuri Temple
properties.description: The bīt Kidmuri is one of the temples located in the citadel of Nineveh. Its Sumerian ceremonial name is not preserved in extant cuneiform sources. Although the temple's exact location remains unknown, it is generally believed to have been between the temple of the goddess Ištar (Emašmaš) and the Citadel Gate (East Gate).

properties.title: Cattigara
properties.description: Cattigara was a port city of the Sinae, located south of Thinae near the mouth of the river Cottiaris. Ptolemy considers the city to be the extreme southeastern-most point of the known world.

properties.title: Via Sebaste: Apollonia ↔ Antiochia ↔ Neapolis
properties.description: A road network in Pisidia originally built by the governor Cornutus Aquila, beginning ca. 6 BC.

properties.title: Forum baths
properties.description: A bath complex adjacent to Pompeii's forum that was built after 80 BC (Reg VII, Ins 5, 2, 5, 7, 24). The baths are publicly financed by the duovir Lucius Caesius and the aediles Caius Occius and Lucius Niraemius.

properties.title: Velefi
properties.description: An ancient settlement or road station attested in the Peutinger Map, but otherwise unknown and unlocateable. The map places it together with several other unlocated places on a route in modern Algeria between Gadifaula (modern Ksar Sbehi) and Vatari (which might be modern Fedj es Siouda).

properties.title: Industrial area at Sexi/Saxetanum
properties.description: Extensive archaeological evidence of the fish processing industry is evident at Sexi/Saxetanum.

properties.title: Mausoleum Hadriani
properties.description: Mausoleum Hadriani (now Castel S. Angelo) located on the right bank of the Tiber river was an imperial mausoleum built by Hadrian in the AD 130s.

properties.title: Pons Aelius
properties.description: The Pons Aelius or Aelian Bridge (now Ponte Sant'Angelo) was completed by Hadrian in AD 134 to span the Tiber opposite the new mausoleum of the emperor.

properties.title: Ay-ibūr-šabû
properties.description: The processional road of the god Marduk in Babylon, whose Akkadian ceremonial name means "May the Arrogant Not Flourish." The street runs north-south through the city, from the Ištar Gate to the Esagil temple. The northern stretch of Ay-ibūr-šabû is sometimes referred to as Ištar-lamassi-ummānīšu ("The goddess Ištar is the Guardian Angel of Her Troops").

properties.title: Porta Leoni
properties.description: A Republican gate of Verona dedicated by P. Valerius, Q. Caecilius, Q. Servilius and P. Cornelius.

properties.title: The Siphnian Treasury
properties.description: Treasury building erected by the citizens of the island city of Siphnos at Delphi in the late Archaic period, famous for its caryatid columns.

properties.description: The theater at Delphi near the Temple of Apollo.

properties.title: Stadium of Delphi

properties.title: Flavian Amphitheater at Puteoli
properties.description: The Flavian Amphitheater at Puteoli is an amphitheater constructed in the port town of Puteoli under the Flavian dynasty around 80 CE.

properties.title: Phalarium
properties.description: A fortress named after Phalaris, a tyrant of Acragas and located near the Himera River.

properties.title: Barbarano Romano
properties.description: Barbarano Romano is a Medieval town in the province of Viterbo that has produced substantial archaeological evidence of Villanovan and Orientalizing habitation.

properties.title: Hagia Sophia, Thessaloniki

properties.title: Arcus Argentariorum
properties.description: A commemorative arch located in the Velabrum dedicated to the Severan emperors in AD 204 by the local association of money-changers (argentarii) and merchants (negotiantes). It was later incorporated into the church of S. Giorgio al Velabro.

properties.title: Synagogue at Dura-Europos
properties.description: The Dura-Europos synagogue is one of the oldest known synagogues in the world. According to an Aramaic inscription, its final phase of construction took place in A.D. 244. It was uncovered during excavations in 1932.

properties.title: Albufera
properties.description: Once a Spanish city, Albufera is today located in the south of Portugal, in the region of Algarve. It belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X (XIII century). Its modern Portuguese name is Albufeira.

properties.title: Roman theater of Zaragoza
properties.description: Dating to the first century, the Roman theater of Zaragoza accommodated about 6,000 spectators.

properties.title: Peshwaran
properties.description: An archaeological site located in Afghanistan's Nimruz Province, some 25 km south of Lash Juwain. Materials on the site ate to the period between the ninth and thirteenth centuries. A large archaeological complex estimated at 9.5 by 13 km has been documented, containing numerous smaller sites. A large citadel is the primary feature of Peshwaran. It measured 200-300 m in diameter and had brick walls standing to 17 m in height. There were at least two large towers. According to Ball there has been no significant fieldwork since the works carried out in 1936 by the DAFA survey (Delegation Archaeologique Française en Afghanistan).

properties.description: An architectural complex located on the West side of the East Church in Apollonia (Cyrenaica). Excavated in 1954-55, it was first thought to be a temple of Isis (Stucchi 1975). According to Kenrick (2013), it is more likely to have been a small production centre, maybe for the fermentation of wine.

properties.description: Great Zimbabwe was the capital of the Queen of Sheba, according to legend. The city, covering ca. 80 hectares, belongs to the Bantu civilization of the Shona culture and dates between the eleventh and fifteenth centuries. It was an important trading center.

properties.description: The archaeological area of Piano (or Quarto) di Comunità is an area of Etrusco-Roman Veii where there is evidence for a Republican domus that is modified during the Augustan period. The area is then used as a necropolis in Late Antiquity (fourth and fifth centuries).

properties.title: Asklepieion and Lerna
properties.description: A sanctuary complex on the northern margins of ancient Corinth near the theater.

properties.title: Panaztepe
properties.description: A mound site located approximately 35 km northwest of modern Izmir, Turkey, with signs of habitation from the 3rd millennium BCE through the early Iron Age.

properties.title: Cleddans
properties.description: A Roman fortlet on the Antonine Wall in Scotland.

properties.title: Summerston
properties.description: A Roman military installation of 2.4 ha associated with the Antonine Wall that was identified in 1980.

properties.title: Unnamed aqueducts
properties.description: unnamed aqueduct group (near estates NW Djlima)

properties.title: Unnamed aqueducts
properties.description: unnamed aqueduct group (Ksar-el-Guellal)

properties.title: Unnamed Aqueduct at Cillium
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 33 C2 unnamed aqueduct (at Cillium)

properties.title: Wadi Bastura Tunnel Inscription
properties.description: Several stone blocks forming the entrance to a tunnel make up part of an aqueduct that Sennacherib had built to divert water from the Bastura River (a tributary of the Upper Zab) to Arbela, a principal cult city of the goddess Ištar. One ashlar block bears an eight-line inscription recording the construction of a (subterranean) watercourse.

properties.title: Temple of Apollo at Metropolis
properties.description: A peripteral Doric temple built in the mid-6th c. BCE and destroyed by fire in the 2nd c. BCE. The temple faces east, and was built of mudbrick on foundations of local sandstone, with sandstone column drums and a terracotta roof. A 4th c. BCE dedicatory inscription found in the cella attests the worship of Apollo. The structure was discovered in 1994 following the activity of looters.

properties.title: Egalmah
properties.description: The temple of the goddess Gula (as Ninisinna) at Larsa. The Sumerian ceremonial name Egalmah means "Exalted Palace."

properties.title: Nuraghe S. Cadrina
properties.description: A nuragic village of the Middle Bronze Age (ca. 1700-1350 BC), Nuraghe S. Cadrina has a central tower with an original diameter of 11.70 m.

properties.title: Akdamar Island
properties.description: The second largest of the four islands in Lake Van, in eastern Turkey.

properties.title: Cathedral of the Holy Cross at Aghtamar
properties.description: Armenian church built on the island of Aghtamar by King Gagik I Artsruni between 915-921 CE.

properties.title: Moulis
properties.description: A Gallo-Roman mole that, in 1965, was preserved to a height of 6.4 meters.

properties.title: Puzriš-Dagan
properties.description: An ancient city of Lower Mesopotamia, Puzriš-Dagan was founded in the twenty-first century B.C. by King Shulgi of Ur.

properties.title: Usian
properties.description: A fortress in the vicinity of Til-garimmu fortified by the Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721-705 BC) against Musku (Phrygia).

properties.title: Haçilar
properties.description: An early human settlement located in southwestern Turkey. Human occupation began at the site toward the end of the eighth millennium B.C.

properties.title: Temple of Ba'al at Palmyra
properties.description: Temple of Ba'al (or Bel) in the ancient city of Palmyra.

properties.title: Marqasi (province)
properties.description: Gurgum (kingdom) became an Assyrian province after Sargon II captured its capital Marqasi in 711 BC.

properties.title: Hexagonal mausoleum
properties.description: A hexagonal tomb, perhaps that of a Roman centurion, dating to the late second or early third century AD.

properties.title: `Iraq al Amir
properties.description: A multi-period settlement mound located 18 km west of Amman, Jordan.

properties.title: So-called Temple of Aphrodite
properties.description: A temple located on the acropolis of Cyrene.

properties.title: 'Ain Ghazal
properties.description: A Neolithic settlement inhabited from ca. 7250 BC to 5000 BC; located in the northwest of Jordan.

properties.title: Terme di Tito
properties.description: The so-called "Terme di Tito" is a terraced Roman villa site located in the modern comune of Castel Sant'Angelo near Lago Paterno.

properties.title: Nērebtum
properties.description: Nērebtum is a medium-sized Bronze Age settlement located east of Baghdad on the left bank of the Diyala river. Nērebtum was inhabited from the third to the early second millennium BCE. Excavations at the site by the University of Chicago from 1934 to 1936 exposed two extensive temple structures, one dedicated to the moon god Sîn, another to the goddess Ištar-Kititum, along with extensive fortification walls and private houses.

properties.title: Via Appia
properties.description: An early Roman road (via publica) originating at Rome and terminating at Brundisium, the Via Appia was begun in the fourth century B.C. by the censor Appius Claudius Caecus. The Latin author Statius described the Via Appia as "queen of the long roads".

properties.title: Amphitheater of Dura-Europos
properties.description: Intramural amphitheater located within the military sector on the north side of Dura-Europos. Built on the site of the former Bath F3, which was destroyed by fire. The amphitheater's dedication in 216 CE is attested by an inscription found fallen from above entrance C on the south side of the amphitheater.

properties.title: Arènes de Nîmes
properties.description: The Arènes de Nîmes is a Roman amphitheater built at the end of the first century.

properties.title: Erek Dağ
properties.description: Erek Dağ is a mountain in the Van Province in eastern Anatolia. It is the second-highest peak of the province of Van, rising to 3200 meters above sea level.

properties.title: Qattara?/Karana?
properties.description: Tell al-Rimah, is the site of a settlement inhabited from the third to first millennium BCE that has been identified as the site of either Qattara or Karana.

properties.title: Basilica di Santa Balbina all'Aventino
properties.description: The basilica of Santa Balbina is a paleo-Christian basilica in Rome, located on the "little Aventine".

properties.title: Domus Cilonis
properties.description: The house of Lucius Fabius Cilo, praefectus urbi in 203, consul in 193 and 204, and a close friend of the emperor Septimius Severus. The house was a gift of the Severans and appears on the Severan marble plan. Its site is now occupied by the basilica of Santa Balbina on the "little Aventine".

properties.title: Tomb of Quintus Sulpicius Maximus
properties.description: The tomb of the boy poet Quintus Sulpicius Maximus on the Via Salaria in Rome. He died in 94 CE, aged just 11 years.

properties.title: *Via Curia
properties.description: A Roman road connecting Reate (Rieti) with Interamna Nahars (Terni).

properties.title: Forum of Septimius Severus
properties.description: The Forum of Septimius Severus at Lepcis Magna

properties.title: Ešasurra
properties.description: The temple of the god Išhara, Ešasurra (“House of the Womb”), was located in the Šuanna district (modern Ishin Aswad) of Babylon. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, this was one of two temples in that part of the city, which was located in the southern part of the eastern half of Babylon.

properties.title: Göltepe
properties.description: Archaeological site in the Central Taurus Mountains dated to the early Bronze Age. The Göltepe hill contains traces of a village associated with the nearby mine site of Kestel.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Lixus
properties.description: The ruins of a Roman amphitheater at Lixus, one of only a few such structures known in Berber North Africa.

properties.title: Arzawa
properties.description: A kingdom or federation in western Anatolia, whose exact location(s) and extent are matters of scholarly debate. The presence and nature of Arzawa is gleaned primarily from Hittite royal annals and diplomatic texts of the LBA, as well as the two letters from Amarna between Amenhotep III and the king of Arzawa. These texts, however, do not reveal the temporal span of Arzawa, and should be treated as snapshots in time. Arzawa reached its greatest prominence in the middle of the fourteenth century BCE, but had been reduced to a rump state by the end of the century. The remaining territory formed the core of the kingdom of Lydia.

properties.title: So-called Caesareum of Cyrene
properties.description: A large architectural complex on the east side of the acropolis ridge in Cyrene that was probably built at the beginning of the first century AD and used as a gymnasium, but was later repurposed as forum in Flavian times, when the rooms north of the complex were levelled in order to build a large basilica. Various ruins can still be seen, including the podium of a temple in the central area, possibly dedicated to Dionysos. A fragmentary inscription referring to the "portico of Caesar", found over the inner side of the porch, made the place known as Caesareum.

properties.title: Assyria (kingdom)
properties.description: Aššur, later Māt Aššur ('the land of the god Aššur'), grew from a small city-state and important trading center to a powerful, wide-spread empire. At is zenith in the seventh century BC, the Assyrian Empire (883-609 BC) dominated much of the Middle East and the Eastern Mediterranean, stretching from the Persian Gulf in the south to the Mediterranean Sea in the west. Assyria's heartland, an area also referred to as Subartu, roughly corresponds to northern Iraq (Nineveh Governorate) and includes the numerous important cities, especially Aššur (Assyria's traditional religious and administrative capital), Kalhu, Dur-Šarrukin, and Nineveh (the capital of the Assyrian Empire).

The ancient name of this large site, which was occupied in the Neolithic Period, is not known.

properties.title: Late Antique domus
properties.description: The structure that now stands at Via in Selci no. 82 in the city of Rome rests on the structural remains of a late Roman building that likely date to the fourth or fifth century. These structural remains are likely those of the basilical hall that often was part of a Late Antique domus.

properties.title: Dede Harabeleri

properties.title: Centocamere at Lokroi Epizephyrioi
properties.description: The so-called "Centocamere" is an urban complex within the city walls dating to the fourth and third centuries B.C. This complex is laid out a organized city blocks separated by planned streets.

properties.description: The Aestii were an ancient people living on the shores of the Baltic Sea, as described by Tacitus.

properties.title: Castalian spring
properties.description: A spring in the ravine between the Phaedriades cliffs (on the lower southern slope of Mt. Parnassos) at Delphi.

properties.title: Mons Claudius
properties.description: A mountain range; BAtlas 20 lists it as unlocated but near either Moslavačka gora or Ivančica, Croatia.

properties.title: Ermine Street
properties.description: The Ermine Street was a major Roman road of Britain, running from Londinium to Colonia Lindum and Eburacum.

properties.title: San Gimignano
properties.description: San Gimignano has origins as an Etruscan settlement but is best known as a Medieval town renowned for its fortified towers.

properties.title: Barnhouse Settlement
properties.description: The Barnhouse Settlement is a Neolithic village of approximately 15 houses located adjacent to the Loch of Harray, Orkney Mainland, Scotland.

properties.title: Standing Stones of Stenness
properties.description: The Standing Stones of Stenness is a Neolithic monument on the mainland of Orkney, Scotland, generally dated to the third millennium BC.

properties.title: Dağönü
properties.description: Once known as İririn or Érérin and now known as Dağönü, this modern Turkish village located in the Van Province of eastern Turkey at the eastern coast of Lake Van lies ca. 10 km north of Ayanis. Here a stela with an inscription of the Urartian king Minua (9th / 8th century BCE) has been found (CTU I A 5-18).

properties.title: Villa of the Lillies (Amnisos)
properties.description: A Bronze Age house at Amnisos, Crete.

properties.title: Imgur-Enlil
properties.description: The great, inner wall of Babylon was called by the ceremonial Akkadian name Imgur-Enlil, which means "The God Enlil Showed Favor." According to the text Tintir = Babylon, Imgur-Enlil had eight city gates, four on the eastern side of the Euphrates and four on the western side of the river. The Assyrian kings Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal and the Babylonian kings Nabopolassar, Nebuchadnezzar II, and Nebonidus all undertook construction on Babylon’s great wall. Imgur-Enlil is one of the seven wonders of the ancient according to some classical sources.

properties.title: Sumer
properties.description: Sumer (Akkadian Šumeru; Sumerian Kiengir) is the name of a historical region of southern Mesopotamia, now modern-day southern Iraq. It is home to one of the world’s earliest civilizations and one of the places where writing was first developed. Eridu, Girsu, Lagash, Shuruppak, Umma, Ur, and Uruk are among its most well-known urban centers.

properties.title: Vasanello
properties.description: The modern Vasanello lies on the line of the Via Amerina. Some scholars have long speculated that it is a candidate for being the ancient "Castellum Amerinum". Settlement at the site begins with the Etruscans.

properties.title: House of Julia Felix
properties.description: The so-called House of Iulia Felix (II, 4, 3) is situated on the south side of the Via dell'Abbondanza, near the Palaestra and the Amphitheater. The estate was formed from two complete insulae that were merged. About one-third of the area was occupied by the house, the remainder by a large garden. Following the AD 62 earthquake the proprietress seems to have leased out portions of the property.

properties.title: Emar
properties.description: An important Bronze Age trading center in northern Syria. The site is known today as Tell Meskene.

properties.title: Nevalı Çori
properties.description: An early Neolithic settlement in the middle Euphrates river valley.

properties.title: Kaleköy
properties.description: Kaleköy is a modern village situated ca. 15 km northeast of Mazgirt and ca. 90 km to the north-northeast of Elaziğ in the southeast of Turkey. In the cliff face above the village, lies an Urartian rock-cut tomb. At the left of its entrance is a rock-cut inscription of the Urartian king Rusa, son of Argišti II (seventh century BCE) (CTU I A 12-6). Nowadays the inscription is heavily damaged.

properties.title: Bath city walls
properties.description: The circuit walls of Aquae Sulis, enclosing an area of some 23 ha, began in the Roman period and were later reinforced in the Anglo-Saxon and Medieval periods. Various remains are visible at points along the original circuit.

properties.title: Ganesh Ratha
properties.description: Modern name of a seventh-century Pallava rock-cut temple at Mahābalipuram.

properties.title: Kasku (region)
properties.description: A region in northeastern Anatolia mentioned in second- and first-millennium-BC Assyrian and Hittite sources.

properties.title: Pavlopetri
properties.description: A now submerged Bronze Age settlement in coastal Laconia.

properties.title: Via Herdonitana
properties.description: A Roman road connecting Herdonia and Ausculum.

properties.title: Via Aurelia Aeclanensis?
properties.description: A road in Apulia leading from Aeclanum toward Vibinum. The Via Aurelia Aeclanensis? intersects the Via Herculia.

properties.title: Vallerano
properties.description: A necropolis located on the southern outskirts of Rome. The necropolis is located near a villa site along a road running through the suburbium of Rome. Excavated between 1992 and 1993.

properties.title: Lobeton
properties.description: A now unlocated site that was the center of the Lobetani in ancient Iberia.

properties.description: Site of the most completely excavated timber-built auxiliary fort (with annexe) in the Roman Empire, situated in present-day Midlothian, Scotland. Roman occupation was short-lived, having been established in the early 70s CE and abandoned in or shortly after 86. Now completely built over by the Royal Bank of Scotland Data Centre.

properties.title: Regio XIV (Transtiberim)
properties.description: The fourteenth regio of imperial Rome was created by the Augustan administrative reform of 7 BCE. This region contained, in addition to the named monuments, the statio of the seventh cohort of the Vigiles, 78 shrines (aediculae), 150 townhouses, 22 warehouses (horrea), 86 bathhouses, and 180 fountains. At the beginning of the fifth century, the Regio was subdivided into 78 districts or vici and 4,405 insulae.

properties.description: Seuthopolis was an ancient Thracian city that followed Hellenistic paradigms in terms of city planning. properties.description: A Roman stone bridge on the Tiber river, spanning the river channel from the Tiber Island westward to the Transtiberim (Trastevere). The original bridge dates to the first century BC.

properties.title: Aliphera sanctuary
properties.description: Pausanias observed sanctuaries of both Asclepius and Athena at Aliphera, as well as an altar of Zeus Lecheates.

properties.title: Oluz Höyük
properties.description: Mound site in Amasya province, Turkey. First inhabited in the Early Bronze Age (ca. 4500 BCE), the site was abandoned sometime during the Hittite Period (15th-13th centuries BCE). It was briefly resettled during the Iron Age-Hellenistic period (8th-1st centuries BCE).

properties.title: Roman bridge at Valeriana
properties.description: A bridge constructed across the Danube at the Roman fort of Valeriana.

properties.title: Aspronisi
properties.description: A volcanic island that formed on the southwestern edge of the Santorini archipelago following a major volcanic eruption that occurred ca. 1625 BC.

properties.title: Santuario di Fondo Patturelli
properties.description: A Samnite sanctuary of ancient Capua that was initially discovered in 1845. Active from the sixth century B.C. until the first century B.C., the Santuario di Fondo Patturelli is noted for its architectural terracotta as well as for the presence of a sacred maternal cult.

properties.title: Samnite House
properties.description: The so-called "Samnite House" is a domus in Herculaneum that originally dates to the second century B.C., making it one of the oldest buildings discovered at the site.

properties.title: Manor House Roman villa
properties.description: The site of a Roman corridor villa with a separate bathhouse. Three phases dating from the late first century AD into the fourth century. It possibly forms part of a complex with the villa uncovered ca. 250 meters to the south and east.

properties.title: Khirbat Iskandar
properties.description: A fortified site on the banks of the Wadi al-Wala in Jordan inhabited in the Early Bronze IV period.

properties.title: Zingsheim
properties.description: A Gallo-Roman temple of the Matronae Aufaniae.

properties.title: Urartu
properties.description: An eastern Anatolian kingdom on the eastern shore of Lake Van. Originating from a regional collection of principalities first mentioned in the 13th century BCE, it had become a single political entity by the 9th century BCE. Urartu was a powerful rival to the Neo-Assyrian Empire. It ceased to exist sometime in the late 7th or early 6th century BCE.

properties.title: Palaikastro, Crete
properties.description: Palaikastro, located in eastern Crete, was an important trading center in antiquity, from the Bronze Age going forward.

properties.title: Domus dei Coiedii
properties.description: The so-called Domus dei Coiedii is a domus located at Suasa. It dates to the first century B.C.

properties.title: Emašdari
properties.description: The temple of the goddess Ištar of Agade at Babylon. The Sumerian ceremonial name Emašdari means "House of Animal Offerings." The Neo-Babylonian king Nabonidus rebuilt/renovated it.

properties.title: Emeslam
properties.description: The temple of the god Nergal at Cutha. The Sumerian ceremonial name Emeslam means "House, Warrior of the Netherworld."

properties.title: Bēlet-ilī Gate
properties.description: The Bēlet-ilī Gate, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Bēlet-ilī-murappišat-talittīšu ("The Goddess Bēlet-ilī Is the One Who Increases Its (Animals’) Offspring"), is the eighth of the eight city gates of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") listed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in inscriptions recording the construction of his new capital. This gate is the second of the south-facing entrances to the city, but its precise location remains unknown.

properties.title: Ea Gate
properties.description: The Ea Gate, which was given the Akkadian ceremonial name Ea-muštēšir-nagbīšu ("The God Ea Is the One Who Keeps Its Spring(s) in Good Order"), is the seventh of the eight city gates of Dūr-Šarrukīn ("Fort Sargon") listed by Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) in inscriptions recording the construction of his new capital. This gate is the first of the south-facing entrances to the city, but its precise location remains unknown.

properties.title: Al-'Assāsīf
properties.description: Necropolis on the West Bank of the Nile near Thebes containing tombs from the 18th, 25th, and 26th dynasties.

properties.title: Daskalio
properties.description: An island of the Cyclades that is now uninhabited. The Cambridge Keros Project identified a large Bronze Age settlement on the island.

properties.title: Temple of Al-Lat at Palmyra
properties.description: A temple sacred to the goddess Al-Lat in Palmyra. The earliest shrine on the site was constructed in the mid-first century BCE, and was greatly expanded during the second century CE. The temple was closed and its altar destroyed during the 380s CE.

properties.title: Savignano sul Rubicone Roman bridge
properties.description: A Roman bridge on the Rubicon at Savignano sul Rubicone.

properties.title: Altar at the temple of Amphiaraos
properties.description: An altar located to the east of the temple of Amphiaraos.

properties.title: Etruscan necropolis of Pianacce
properties.description: An Etruscan necropolis located near the center of Sarteano with tombs dating from the sixth to the second centuries B.C.

properties.title: Etruscan necropolis of Malignano
properties.description: An Etruscan necropolis south of Sovicille in the province of Siena. The tombs date from the fifth century B.C. onward.

properties.description: Burial ground near Yüceören Hill in Cilicia containing tombs from the Hellenistic, Roman, and Byzantine periods.

properties.title: Džanfida
properties.description: Džanfida is a village located in the Armavir province of southwestern Armenia, ca. 9 km south of Sardarabat. Here a stone block with an inscription of Sarduri II (8th century BCE) was found which curses anyone who dares to damage or destroy his fortress or inscription.

properties.title: Phylakopi
properties.description: A major Bronze Age settlement on Melos with evidence for continuous occupation from the third millennium BC until the twelfth century BC, Phylakopi provides important information about the Cycladic civilization.

properties.title: Sanctuary of Artemis Limnatis at Messene
properties.description: A sanctuary on the slopes of Mount Ithome and within the city walls of ancient Messene in the Peloponnese. It was developed beginning in the 4th-3rd centuries BCE.

properties.title: Ezida
properties.description: One of the temples in the citadel of Nineveh that was dedicated to Nabû, the god of scribes; it is located north of the temple of the goddess Ištar (Emašmaš). The Sumerian ceremonial name Ezida means "True House."

properties.title: Castle an Dinas
properties.description: Castle an Dinas is an Iron Age hillfort near St. Columb Major in Cornwall, United Kingdom, built during the third and second centuries BC.

properties.title: Untitled
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 29 D2 unnamed fort (SW Ghar Roubane)

properties.title: Osmanthorpe Roman vexillation fortress
properties.description: The remains of Osmanthorpe Roman vexillation fortress are situated on a hilltop in the valley of the River Greet.

properties.title: Temple of Hibis
properties.description: A large temple located in the Kharga Oasis that is dated to the Saite-Persian period.

properties.title: Māri
properties.description: Mari (Tell Hariri) was an ancient Semitic city that flourished as a trade center and hegemonic state between 2900 BC until 1759 BC. The site was submitted as a tentative candidate for the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1999.

properties.title: Untitled

properties.title: Pons Sublicius
properties.description: The Pons Sublicius is traditionally held to be the earliest Roman bridge across the river Tiber. The textual tradition assigns its construction to the king Ancus Marcius in 642 B.C. It crossed the Tiber near the Forum Boarium just downstream from the Tiber Island.

properties.title: Castle of Serravalle
properties.description: The Castle of Serravalle is a twelfth century castle located in Bosa, province of Oristano, Sardinia. It is connected with the Tuscan Malaspina family.

properties.title: Ness of Brodgar
properties.description: Ness of Brodgar is an archaeological site near Loch of Harray, Orkney. The site covers 2.5 hectares.

properties.title: Nesiotic League (First)
properties.description: The Nesiotic league (the League of the Islanders) was a federal organization of Greek poleis in the Cyclades islands, organized in ca.  314/3 BCE under the direction of Antigonus Monophthalmus. Control passed to the Ptolemies ca. 287 BCE; the league eventually dissolved in the mid-3rd century BCE.

properties.title: Mausoleo della Conocchia
properties.description: A Roman mausoleum dating most likely to the second century.

properties.title: Absheron (peninsula)
properties.description: A peninsula in the South Caucasus, extending approximately 60 km into the Caspian Sea.

properties.title: Mausoleum Augusti
properties.description: A monumental tomb built in the Campus Martius at Rome by Augustus and dedicated in 28 B.C. The mausoleum served as a family tomb for the Iulio-Claudians.

properties.title: Catacombe San Marcellino e Pietro
properties.description: The Catacombs of Marcellinus and Peter lies some 3 km southeast of Rome along the ancient Via Labicana. They date to the fourth century A.D.

properties.title: Arch of Septimius Severus
properties.description: The Arch of Septimius Severus dates to 205.

properties.title: Jrvezh
properties.description: Village east of Yerevan in Armenia. The town, which has been settled since at least the 5th century CE, contains a 7th-century chapel.

properties.title: Hambledon Hill
properties.description: Hambledon Hill is a prehistoric hill fort in Dorset, England, with occupation beginning in the Neolithic period.

properties.title: Basilica of Thyrsos
properties.description: A fifth or sixth century AD (Early Christian) triple-aisled basilica including mosaic floors.

properties.title: Tumulus of Glimes
properties.description: A Gallo-Roman tumulus located near Incourt, Belgium.

properties.title: Trou de Billemont Tumulus
properties.description: The Trou de Billemont Tumulus is a second century AD Gallo-Roman tumulus in Belgium.

properties.title: Heroön
properties.description: The so-called Heroön at Sagalassos dominates the Upper Agora in the northwest sector of the city.

properties.title: Dema Tower
properties.description: A round defensive tower located to the east of the Dema Wall in Attica.

properties.title: Cluster of 9 mausolea
properties.description: South of modern Kherba Sidi el Ahmar in Algeria (BAtlas 29 G1 unlabeled)

properties.title: Nazzano Romano
properties.description: Nazzano Romano was the site of an Etruscan settlement covering some 7 hectares and dating between the eighth and fifth centuries B.C.

properties.title: Tino (island)
properties.description: An island in the Ligurian Sea designated as part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Tino is connected with the life of the seventh century AD Christian Saint Venerius.

properties.title: Vigna Parrocchiale archaeological area
properties.description: A complex of civic and sacred buildings in the urban area of ancient Caere, including the so-called "elliptical building".

properties.title: Arco del Sacramento
properties.description: A Roman arch of the second century A.D. that faced on to the forum of Beneventum.

properties.title: Elugalgalgasisa
properties.description: The ziggurat of the god Sîn at Ur. The Sumerian ceremonial name Elugalgalgasisa means "House of the King who Lets Counsel Flourish". The platform temple was originally built during the Early Bronze Age and was then restored in the sixth century B.C. by King Nabonidus.

properties.title: Chillon
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the south of the province of Ciudad Real that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. Today knowh as Chillón.

properties.title: Almaden
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the south of the province of Ciudad Real that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. Today known as Almadén.

properties.title: Hattusa
properties.description: The Late Bronze Age capital of the Hittite empire (near modern Boğazkale in Turkey). The site was enrolled as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

properties.title: Temple G at Selinus
properties.description: Remains of an octastyle Doric temple begun in the sixth century B.C. but left unfinished.

properties.title: Khorsabad Residence J
properties.description: The eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) had several royal residences constructed in the citadel of his new capital, Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad). Residence J, which has constructed on the western side of the citadel, is presumed to have been for one of the highest officials of the Assyrian Empire. Since no inscriptions were discovered in the ruins of the building, the owner/principal occupant of the this Assyrian palace is not known.

properties.title: Grotta di Cocceio
properties.description: A 1-km long ancient tunnel connecting Lake Avernus with Cumae. It dates ca. 38-36 B.C.

properties.title: Via Celle necropolis
properties.description: A Roman necropolis with 14 tombs constructed during the first and early second centuries A.D.

properties.title: Niebla
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the northeastern part of the province of Huelva that once belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X.

properties.title: Moger
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the east of Huelva that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. While there is on-site evidence for long-term human activity since antiquity, the present settlement, known in modern terms as Moguer, is traditionally said to have been founded in 1333 by the Señorío de Moguer ("Seigneury of Moguer").

properties.description: A surviving gate of the ancient city walls of Tergeste that dates to the first century B.C.

Discoveries at the site included stone walls, a courtyard, a portico, baths, a mosaic floor, a bordering Roman-era roadway.
