properties.title: Suhu
properties.description: The kingdom of Suhu was situated on the middle Euphrates and stretched from the northwestern border of Babylonia in the south to Hindanu in the north. During the 9th and 8th centuries B.C., its rulers held authority over the cities Anat (Anatho), Suru, Rahi-ilu, and even Mari. Approximately thirty Akkadian inscriptions of its rulers Šamaš-rēša-uṣur and Ninurta-kudurrī-uṣur were discovered in the region of Haditha in the early 1980s, prior to the construction of the Haditha dam, which flooded the region; many of Suhu's cities are now underwater.

properties.description: La Graufesenque is the name of an archaeological site located in southern France at the point of the confluence of the Tarn and Dourbie rivers. properties.title: Pompei Tropaea
properties.description: In 71 BC as Pompey returned to Italy from Iberia he set up a monument in the Pyrenees known as the Pompei Tropaea. This monument commemorated the 876 cities Pompey had conquered. Pompey's monument was spoliated in late antiquity and a medieval church and later priory were built on the site. Spoliated in turn, what is left of all these structures now comprises the Sitio arqueológico de Panissars on the French/Spanish border.

properties.description: A village in Turkey, the site of a late antique Georgian church constructed in the 7th century.

properties.description: A fortified pre-Roman Iberian oppidum.

properties.description: A Gallo-Roman villa.

properties.title: Meyrargues aqueduct
properties.description: Remains of a Roman aqueduct.

properties.title: Grimspound
properties.description: A prehistoric settlement of the late Bronze Age located in the Dartmoor area of south Devon, England. The remains of 24 stone houses survive within a massive boundary wall.

properties.title: So-called Theatre 3
properties.description: A Roman theatre on the acropolis ridge of Cyrene, conventionally numbered "3".

properties.title: Girmua
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources; the modern site is Ǧirwān/Jerwan.

properties.title: Manganello Sanctuary
properties.description: The Manganello Sanctuary is located at the northern edge Caere's urban plateau.

properties.title: Mané-Vechen, Plouhinec
properties.description: A Gallo-Roman villa excavated in 1970-1971. A possible fanum was identified 50 meters to the northwest of the villa.

properties.title: Hovhannavank
properties.description: Medieval Armenian monastery in the village of Ohanavan, Aragatsotn Province, Armenia. The site originated as a single-nave church in the 4th century CE, was expanded in the 4th-5th centuries, and was substantially renovated in the 17th-18th centuries.

properties.title: Anfiteatro di Bleso
properties.description: The "Anfiteatro di Bleso" is a second century A.D. Roman amphitheater at Tibur (modern Tivoli in Italy).

properties.title: Pont de Bornègre
properties.description: A Roman aqueduct bridge connected to the Roman aqueduct of Nîmes.

properties.title: Gallo-Roman settlement, locality of Courac
properties.description: Near the locality of Courac, just north of modern Tresques, are the remains of a diffuse Gallo-Roman settlement occupied from the first to fourth centuries A.D.

properties.title: Cercina (Etruria)
properties.description: A now-unlocated place near to Florentia in Etruria (Regio VII) known from epigraphic sources. Caius Caesar, the father of Iulius Caesar, helmed a veterans' colony there.

properties.title: Roman theater at Verona
properties.description: The Roman theater at Verona dates from the late first century B.C.

properties.title: So-called Central Church in Apollonia
properties.description: A three-aisled basilical church, with an external apse, situated near the centre of the ancient settlement of Apollonia (Cyrenaica), about half way between the East and West churches. The building has a narthex, a small western atrium and a range of added rooms along the north flank. The mosaics have been dated around the sixth century AD, but the building seems to have been built in earlier times (possibly fifth century AD).

properties.title: Saint-Pierre-d'Aurillac
properties.description: Remains of Gallo-Roman substructures that support the choir of the present church.

properties.title: Temple of Veiovis
properties.description: The Temple of Veiovis, also attested as Aedes Vediovis, was a temple of ancient Rome located on the Capitoline Hill in a location known as "inter duos lucos" that is interpreted to mean a saddle between the two summits of the hill. The remains of a temple podium were discovered beneath the northwest corner of the Palazzo Senatore in 1938-1939.

properties.title: Tor di Mezzavia di Frascati
properties.description: The Tor di Mezzavia is a Medieval tower located along the modern Via Tuscolana, marking the midway point between Rome and Frascati.

properties.title: Mausoleum of Lucius Munatius Plancus
properties.description: A Roman mausoleum that is associated with Lucius Munatius Plancus.

properties.title: Necropoli Romana
properties.description: A Roman necropolis at Brixia.

properties.title: Münster-Sarmsheim Roman Villa
properties.description: Remains of a Roman villa, including mosaic pavements, were discovered.

properties.title: Kemmelberg
properties.description: A tertiary hill (154 m high) dominating the surrounding flatland in Belgium's West Flanders province close to the French border. Archaeological remains ranging from the Middle Paleolithic to the 5th century BC. Also the site of heavy fighting during World War I.

properties.title: Caput Africae
properties.description: A place in Rome's second Augustan region that was perhaps a paedagogium for the training of imperial pages.

properties.title: Vicus Nediensis
properties.description: A Roman vicus, attested by name in inscriptions discovered in the 19th century. Based on the reported findspots of the inscriptions, the vicus seems to have been located in the vicinity of modern Spechbach, located southeast of Heidelberg, Germany.

properties.title: Li Muri necropolis
properties.description: A necropolis with four dolmens surrounded by small kerbstone circles.

properties.title: Chassenon Roman amphitheater
properties.description: Remains of a Roman amphitheater at Chassenon.

properties.title: Carrowkeel Megalithic Cemetery
properties.description: A Neolithic cemetery dated to 3400 to 3100 BC. Fourteen passage tombs have been identified.

properties.title: Ezida (Kalhu)
properties.description: When Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud) became the principal administrative center of the Assyrian Empire in the ninth century BC, king Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) built (or rebuilt) numerous temples. One of those was dedicated to the god Nabû. Unlike most of the religious buildings constructed at Kalhu, the Ezida ("True House") was built in the southeast corner of the Citadel.

properties.title: Hexamilion wall
properties.description: The Hexamilion wall is an ancient defensive wall built across the Isthmus of Corinth that protected the only land route into the Peloponnese from mainland Greece.

properties.title: Ménec alignments
properties.description: A complex comprised of 11 rows of megaliths covering an area of 1,165 x 100 meters.

properties.title: Petit-Ménec alignments
properties.description: An alignment of megaliths located east of Kerlescan.

properties.title: Theater at Letoon
properties.description: An ancient theater associated with the Letoon, a sanctuary of Leto near the ancient city Xanthos in Lycia. The theater is located on the Roman agora, to the the north of the acropolis.

properties.title: Tilmen Höyük
properties.description: A bronze age settlement in the Islahiye valley of modern Turkey where habitation seems to have begun as early as the Late Chalcolithic.

properties.title: Tomb of Hilarus Fuscus
properties.description: The Late Republican tomb of the freedman Hilarus Fuscus along the Via Appia (ca. 30 B.C.).

properties.title: Hot Baths
properties.description: Remains of a large building and baths uncovered between Bilbury Lane and Lower Borough Walls, beneath what is now known as the Gainsborough Spa in Aquae Sulis, modern-day Bath.

properties.title: Enamhe
properties.description: The temple of the gods Adad and Apla-Adad at Anat (Anatho). The Sumerian ceremonial name Enamhe means "House of Plenty."

properties.title: Beacon Hill Hill fort
properties.description: Beacon Hill Hill fort is an Iron Age hill fort in Hampshire, England.

properties.title: Battlesbury Camp
properties.description: Battlesbury Camp is an Iron Age hillfort located in Wiltshire, England.

properties.title: Temple of Jupiter, Damascus
properties.description: The Temple of Jupiter in Damascus was begun during the rule of Augustus and completed during the rule of Constantius II.

properties.title: Nether Denton Roman fort
properties.description: A Roman fort site at Nether Denton that was identified via cropmarks. The fort formed part of the Stanegate frontier system, and thus pre-dates Hadrian's Wall. It was abandoned ca. 122.

properties.title: Boothby Roman fort
properties.description: A Roman fortlet that was part of the Stanegate system, dating to the late first to second centuries.

properties.title: Göbekli Tepe
properties.description: The site of Göbekli Tepe, located in the Germuş mountains of south-eastern Anatolia, was the location of a Neolithic hilltop sanctuary. This sanctuary, thought to be a series of stone enclosures with T-shaped pillars carrying carving of wild animals, was built in the Pre-Pottery Neolithic and ranges in date from 9,600 to 8,200 B.C.

properties.title: Roman villa at Maasbracht
properties.description: A Roman villa near the modern village of Maasbracht, Limburg, Netherlands, famous for its murals. The earliest structures on the site are dated to the second century CE, and the villa was abandoned by the middle of the third century.

properties.title: Civitavecchia di Arpino
properties.description: The fortified acropolis of the ancient city of Arpinum.

properties.title: Cadmea
properties.description: The acropolis / fortress of Thebes. The fortress was destroyed by Alexander the Great in 335 B.C. and later rebuilt by Cassander in 316 B.C.

properties.description: The remains of a Roman villa on the Via Ostiense have been linked to Lucius Nonius Calpurnius Torquatus Asprenas.

properties.title: tribus Teretina
properties.description: Established in 299 B.C., the tribus Teretina was one of the later rural tribes of ancient Rome.

properties.title: Spring at Amphiareion
properties.description: The spring at the healing sanctuary at Amphiareion and a site of votive deposits in the form of coins. It still flows today.

properties.title: Segovia aqueduct
properties.description: Supplied Segovia with water from mountains to the southeast

properties.title: Dún Ailinne
properties.description: An ancient ceremonial site located in County Kildare, Ireland. The circular enclosure once covered ca. 13 ha.

properties.title: Nuraghe Maronzu
properties.description: Remains of a nuraghe in the territory of the comune of Olbia.

properties.title: Nuraghe Sa Ucchiusura
properties.description: A monopteral nuraghe built of trachite. The ruined walls stand to at least four meters in height.

properties.title: Egalgabarinutukua
properties.description: The palace of the eighth-century-BC Assyrian Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) at Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad), Egalgabarinutukua ("Palace That Has No Equal"), was constructed between 717 BC and 706 BC. This royal residence was constructed on a high, mud-brick terrace located within the city’s citadel, which was located against the northwestern stretch of the city wall. This large, ornately-decorated palace complex consisted of over two hundred rooms (including chapels to the deities Ea, Sîn, Ningal, Adad, Šamaš, and Ninurta) and courtyards, as well as a ziggurat.

properties.title: Porticus Octaviae
properties.description: A porticus in the area of the Circus Flaminius, the Porticus Octaviae was dedicated by Augustus sometime after 27 B.C. in honor of his sister, Octavia Minor. The porticus replaced the Porticus Metelli. It was restored twice after major urban fires in A.D. 80 and 203.

properties.title: Sra Ghundai, Ghazni
properties.description: Remains of a walled ancient city in the Ghazni province of Afghanistan. Its remains date to various periods according to W. Ball (1982): Late Sassanian and Turki Shahi (sixth–ninth century AD) and Early Islamic (tenth -twelfth century).

properties.title: Pust-i Gau
properties.description: A large, multi-period site in modern Afghanistan. One of its key feature is a large, fortified enclosure with 48 towers.

properties.title: Via Campana?
properties.description: A road located on the right bank of the Tiber leading to the Campus Salinarum romanarum and sharing the first part of its course with the Via Portuensis.

properties.title: Acarnanian League
properties.description: The Acarnanian League was a tribal confederation of the Acarnanians that later transformed into a league by the 5th century BCE. The league was incorporated into the Roman province of Achaea following the battle of Actium in 31 BCE.

properties.title: Minoan Palatial Center (Knossos)
properties.description: An extensive, multi-period bronze age palace complex, located south of modern Heraklion in central Crete.

properties.title: Camp of Diocletian at Palmyra
properties.description: Camp of Diocletian in the Ancient City of Palmyra. Coordinates determined by eye in Google Earth in November 2012, following description in UNESCO World Heritage List.

properties.title: Sanctuary at Leben
properties.description: Leben is known for a sanctuary of Asklepios dating to the first and second centuries CE.

properties.title: Lobera
properties.description: A Spanish village located in the northwest of the province of Jaén, between Jaén and Córdoba, that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. It is now known as Lopera.

properties.title: Clepsydra of the Oropos Amphiareion
properties.description: The Oropos Amphiareion clepsydra is a hydraulic inflow clock serving the Sanctuary of Amphiaraus. Situated on the southeast bank of the sacred spring of Amphiaraus, this inflow hydraulic clock dates to the 4th century BCE.

properties.title: Ponte del Diavolo
properties.description: A bridge in the territory of Blera known as the "Devil's Bridge".

properties.title: Can Blai
properties.description: A Late Roman fortlet on the island of Formentera.

properties.title: Pozzuolo necropolis
properties.description: A necropolis of Etruscan Veii.

properties.title: Corinth Roman Amphitheater
properties.description: The small Roman amphitheater at Corinth was located northeast of the Temple of Apollo. It has been suggested that it dates to the early days of the Roman colony, perhaps placing its construction in the first century B.C.

properties.title: Poikile Petra
properties.description: Poikile Petra is the name of a road connecting Seleucia ad Calycadnum and Corycus.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Thermae Himeraeae
properties.description: Roman amphitheater at Termini Imerese was of modest size and is today poorly preserved.

properties.title: Torre d'en Galmés
properties.description: Torre d'en Galmés was a Talaiotic settlement of Bronze Age Minorca and was established ca. 1400 BC.

properties.title: Ploutonion at Hierapolis
properties.description: The Ploutonion at Hierapolis is a walled sanctuary dedicated to Pluto and Kore.

properties.title: Cetona
properties.description: The present town of Cetona grew around the rocca (fortress) of the tenth century A.D., although occupation at the site reaches back to the Paleolithic when a number of caves show evidence for human activity. There are also indications of an Etruscan phase of occupation.

properties.title: Maiden Castle, Dorset
properties.description: One of the largest and most complex Iron Age hillforts in Europe, Maiden Castle, in Dorset, was occupied from the Neolithic period through to the fourth century A.D.

properties.title: Roman theater at Amiternum
properties.description: The Roman theater at Amiternum could seat approximately 2,000 people. It was abandoned after the fourth century and became a necropolis.

properties.title: Komninon (Macedonian tomb), Stavroupolis
properties.description: Stavroupolis is the site of the largest Macedonian tomb known in Thrace.

properties.title: House of Julius Polybius
properties.description: The House of Julius Polybius (IX 13,1.3) sits on the north side of the Via dell'Abbondanza and dates from the second century BC.

properties.title: Castello di Agropoli
properties.description: A Medieval castle built atop Byzantine foundations. Location based on OpenStreetMap.

properties.title: Arch of Hadrian at Athens
properties.description: The Arch of Hadrian is a monument in the form of a Roman triumphal arch, constructed by the citizens of Athens in AD 131 or 132 to honor the Roman emperor Hadrian.

properties.title: Roman theater of Neapolis
properties.description: The Roman theater of Neapolis is a structure of the first century B.C. that is built atop the pre-existing fourth century B.C. Greek theater.

properties.title: Bouleuterion of Onchestos
properties.description: The Bouleuterion of Onchestos has been identified adjacent to the Temple of Poseidon.

properties.title: Nuraghe Su Valsu
properties.description: A Middle Bronze Age nuraghe located southwest of Florinas in Sardinia.

properties.title: Via Ciminia
properties.description: The Via Ciminia was a Roman road that left the Via Cassia and continued toward the Ciminian hills. Its course likely ran from Sutrium to near Viterbo.

properties.title: Odéon at Carthage
properties.description: The theater and odéon of Roman Carthage stood in the northeast of the city, some three blocks from the cardo maximus.

properties.title: Neolithic Settlement at Knossos
properties.description: A neolithic settlement on a hill known today as Kephala, south of Heraklion on the island of Crete. It preceded the Bronze Age (Minoan) palace and settlement on this site.

properties.title: Civitas Leonina
properties.description: The Civitas Leonina or Leonine City is a portion of the city of Rome on the left bank of the river Tiber around which Pope Leo IV commissioned the construction of the Leonine Wall in the ninth century AD. This followed the Saracen sack of Rome in AD 846.

properties.title: Qutb Minar
properties.description: The second tallest minar (73 m) in India after Minar-E-Fateh was built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak beginning in AD 1192. The monument is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

properties.title: Tell Um Hammad al-Gharbi
properties.description: Archaeological site on the banks of the Zerqa River with signs of habitation in the Early Bronze Age I-II and IV. The eastern portion of the larger Tell Um Hammad site is called Um Hammad Sharqiya; the western section is Um Hammad al-Gharbi. The two may have been linked as a single village in the Early Bronze Age IV.

properties.title: Belverde Necropoli della Cavetta
properties.description: The Cavetta necropolis at Pantalica includes tombs and rock-cut houses of the prehistoric and later periods.

properties.title: Arkalochori cave
properties.description: A Bronze Age cave sanctuary on Crete known for the votive deposits of Bronze Age weapons recovered by archaeology.

properties.title: Herculaneum Gate
properties.description: A city gate of Pompeii that dates to the time of Sulla.

properties.title: Sanctuary of Zeus Panhellenios (Aegina)
properties.description: An oracular mountaintop sanctuary of Zeus on the island of Aegina.

properties.title: Roman theater at Asculum
properties.description: The Roman theater at Asculum was discovered during excavations in 1932. The structure dates to the first century A.D.

properties.title: Fortunatae Insulae? (Madeira Islands)
properties.description: The modern, Portugeuse archipelago of Madeira seems to have been identified by some ancient authors with the "Fortunatae Insulae" or "Blessed Islands".

properties.title: Poggio Civitella
properties.description: The hill of Poggio Civitella near Montalcino, Italy, rises to a height of 661 meters above sea level. Beginning in 1993, excavation campaigns revealed a series of settlement horizons dating to the first millennium BCE, ranging from the archaic to the Hellenistic periods. The hilltop was fortified during this period.

properties.title: Sam'alla (province)
properties.description: The eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Shalmaneser V (r. 726-722 BC) conquered Sam'al and its territory and established the city as the administrative capital of an Assyrian province named after it.

properties.title: Nikonion
properties.description: Nikonion received a sixth-century B.C. colony from either Miletos or Istros. It was assessed tribute by the Delian League in 425/4 B.C. Authors such as Pseudo-Skylax refer to the site as a polis in the urban sense. The colony was under the protection of the Skythian king Skyles. The ancient city was located on the on east bank of the Dniester river where Roksolany, Ukraine, is now located.

properties.title: Uronarti
properties.description: An ancient settlement located on an island in the Nile just south of the Second Cataract, now in the north of Sudan. An ancient fortress dating to the reigns of the Middle Kingdom pharaohs (19th century BC) Senusret I and Senusret III is found there.

properties.title: Cadbury Camp Hill Fort
properties.description: A 2.8 ha hill fort near Tickenham, Somerset, England, in use from the Bronze Age to the Anglo Saxon period.

properties.title: Church of St. George
properties.description: One of of a group of eleven rock-hewn monolithic churches located in Lalibela, a city in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia. The church likely dates to the twelfth or thirteenth century.

properties.title: Southeastern Cluster
properties.description: The Southeastern Cluster of rock-cut churches at Lalibela.

properties.title: Roman theater at Antium
properties.description: The Roman theater at Antium is most likely built in the second half of the first century.

properties.title: Kaims Castle
properties.description: Kaims Castle is a Roman fortlet located between the forts of Ardoch and Strageath.

properties.title: House of the Triclinium at Italica
properties.description: House of the Triclinium is located in the area southeast of the House of Hylas.

properties.title: House of the Fishes
properties.description: A domus in Ostia Antica, whose two building phases have been dated, respectively, to the middle and last quarter of the third century CE.

properties.title: Malkata
properties.description: Site located south of the Theban Necropolis containing a New Kingdom palace complex constructed by Amenhotep III of the 18th Dynasty.

properties.title: Garden Houses
properties.description: A large residential complex, built in ca. 128 CE as part of the Hadrianic remodeling of Ostia. Its central area was occupied by two blocks, each comprising four houses, surrounded by a garden furnished with six fountains.

properties.title: Adad Gate
properties.description: The Adad Gate is one of Babylon's eight city gates and it is situated on the western side of the inner city, directly west of the nu-x-ù quarter. King Nebuchadnezzar II built the gate ca. 575 B.C.

properties.title: North Palace at Babylon
properties.description: The Neo-Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–562 BC) constructed a new royal residence for himself at Babylon. This grand palace was constructed north of the so-called “South Palace,” the traditional royal residence of the kings of Babylon. The building, which is referred to as the “new palace” (ēkallu eššu) in Achaemenid-period texts, is generally called the “North Palace,” “Nordburg,” and “New Palace.”

properties.title: Tell Leilan
properties.description: Tell Leilan is situated near the Wadi Jarrah, in the Khabur River basin in Al-Hasakah Governorate, northeastern Syria. The ancient names of the site are Shekhna and Shubat-Enlil.

properties.title: Gleieh
properties.description: Gleieh (also Gleiʾeh, Glaiʿā) is small site in the middle Euphrates region and was part of the kingdom of Suhu. The city, which is probably to be identified with ancient Kār-Apladad, was situated on the south bank of the Euphrates, opposite Sur Jureh (which lies on the northern bank). Like many towns and cities of the ancient kingdom of Suhu, Gleieh/Kār-Apladad is now underwater; the area was flooded after the construction of the Haditha dam.

properties.title: Larisa
properties.description: An ancient settlement, described by Strabo as lying "on the left of the Pontus, between Naulochus and Odessos, near Mount Haimos". Its modern location is uncertain, although it may correspond to a fortified settlement on the St. Athanasius Cape near modern Byala in Bulgaria.

properties.title: Oboulensioi

properties.title: Regio I, Pompeii
properties.description: The so-called Regio I, an archaeological subdivision located in the southeastern section of Pompeii, contains a mixture of residences and commercial structures.

properties.title: Bozca

properties.title: Praetorian Guard Barracks at Amba Aradam Metro Station
properties.description: Excavations for Rome's Metro C public transit line at the Amba Aradam Station revealed the remains of a second century A.D. barracks connected with the Praetorian Guard, along with a domus identified as that of a praetorian commandant. Although ruinous, the architectural complex demonstrates good preservation of some features, notably floor mosaics and wall paintings. The second century A.D. stratigraphic horizon was reached at a depth of approximately 12 meters.

properties.title: Herakleion
properties.description: An ancient sanctuary of Hercules (Melqart) that Strabo places at one end of the long island (Cotinussa) that extended south from ancient Gades. Significant landscape and coastal change have occurred since antiquity, disrupting the integrity of these islands. Nonetheless, modern scholars have consistently identified the location of the sanctuary as at or near the 17th-18th century Castillio de Sancti Petri, which today occupies a separate homonymous islet. Archaeological finds possibly associated with the sanctuary have been made in the vicinity (both terrestrial and underwater) over the years, but precise location of foundations or other identifiable architecture have remained elusive.

properties.description: Following TIR, the Barrington Atlas tentatively placed this ancient settlement at the archaeological site in Spain known today as Cerro del Cogolludo, which is located near the modern town of Navalvillar de Pela. The latter two differ in provincial association, leading some scholars to speculate that two separate settlements with similar names existed in ancient times.

properties.title: San Martino ai Monti

properties.title: Monastery of Saint John the Theologian

properties.title: Lutibu
properties.description: Lutibu is a fortified city in Sam'alla that is mentioned in royal inscriptions of the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III (r. 858-824 BC). It is often identified with Sakçagözü (Coba Höyük), which is ca. 20 km northeast of Sam'al (Zincirli Höyük).

properties.title: Ekinu
properties.description: The temple of the goddess Aya at Sippar. The Sumerian ceremonial name Ekinu means "House, Bed-Chamber."

properties.title: Poggio Capalbiaccio
properties.description: The hill Poggio Capalbiaccio is located in the Maremma plain.

properties.title: Temple of Talamonaccio
properties.description: An Etruscan temple of the fourth century BCE, associated with the ancient settlement of Telamon. It lies on Mount Talamonaccio, across the bay from the modern village of Talamone, north of Orbetello, Italy.

properties.title: Pieve di San Giovanni Battista a Sillano
properties.description: A ruined church that was once part of the diocese of Volterra, San Giovanni Battista a Sillano is unique in Tuscany for having a Romanesque-Norman façade. The ruined edifice likely dates to the twelfth and thirteenth centuries although the parish exists as early as the mid-tenth century.

properties.title: Ringwall Rentmauer (Weilrod)

properties.title: Celebandicum Iugum

properties.title: Beta Samati

properties.title: Mogil'nik Ashpyl

properties.title: Nabû temple (Khorsabad)
properties.description: The eighth-century-BC Assyrian king Sargon II (r. 721–705 BC) had a temple to the god Nabû, the god of scribes, built in the citadel of his new capital, Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad). Building H is the largest temple in Sargon’s newly-constructed city and it was built on a platform in the western side of the citadel, rather than on the palace terrace. The Nabû temple was connected to the temple district, which formed part of Sargon’s royal residence, by a stone bridge.

properties.title: Sebetti temple (Khorsabad)
properties.description: A temple dedicated to the Sebetti, the divine seven, was excavated by Iraqi archaeologists in 1957. This temple at Dūr-Šarrukīn (modern Khorsabad) is located just west of the citadel, near Citadel Gate A and City Gate 7.

properties.title: Temple of Apollo at Corinth
properties.description: The second temple of Apollo at Corinth whose reconstructed remains are visible on the site today. The structure dates ca. 540 B.C.

properties.title: Mithraeum at Vulci
properties.description: A mithraeum was discovered at Vulci in 1975 during excavations of a Roman aristocratic house. The shrine was well preserved with two tauroctony scenes dating to the third century. The site was destroyed in the fourth century A.D.

properties.title: Roman theater of Acinipo
properties.description: The Roman theater of Acinipo dates ca. 59-53 B.C.

properties.title: Künzing Roman amphitheater
properties.description: A Roman timber amphitheater dating from the first to fifth centuries, the Künzing Roman amphitheater measured 46 by 40 meters. The site was discovered during excavations carried out in 2003 and 2004. The archaeological site is no longer visible but a reconstructed evocation of the ancient structure marks the location.

properties.title: Roman necropolis at Carmo
properties.description: A necropolis of the Roman period wherein most tombs date between the first century BC and the second century AD.

properties.title: Italia, Regio IX
properties.description: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Liguria. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

properties.title: Pyramid of Unas
properties.description: A pyramid at Saqqara built for Unas, the final ruler of Egypt's Fifth Dynasty.

properties.title: Eandasaya
properties.description: The temple of the goddess Ištar of the Star, Eandasaya (“House Which Rivals Heaven”), was located in the New City district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of two temples in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: Ekitušgirzal
properties.description: The temple of the goddess Bēlet-Eanna, Ekitušgirzal (“House, Abode of Joy”), was located in the New City district of Babylon, in the eastern half of the inner city. According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon Tablet IV, it was one of two temples in that part of Babylon.

properties.title: So-called Tempio di Venere e Cupido
properties.description: The so-called Temple of Venus and Cupid at Rome is part of the complex of buildings associated with the Sessorian palace. The structure's modern assignation is owed to the discovery of a fragmentary statue of Sallustia Orbiana in the guise of Venus Felix. Sallustia Orbiana was the wife of Alexander Severus. The statue is now held in the Museo Pio Clementino in the Vatican Museums.

properties.title: Terme Aquae Passeris
properties.description: A Roman bath located at Aquae Passeris.

properties.title: Villa di Casale Ghella
properties.description: A villa complex at the eighth mile of the Via Cassia, to which it was linked by means of a paved diverticulum. The first phase dates to the first century BCE and the villa remains in use until the Late Antique period.

properties.title: Unnamed Roman tomb
properties.description: An unnamed Roman tomb that is located near Casale Ghella.

properties.title: Etruscan necropolis of Dometaia
properties.description: An Etruscan necropolis dating to the sixth century B.C.

properties.title: The House of the Masks
properties.description: The House of the Masks (also known as the House of the Comedians), built around 150-100 BC, was a luxurious residential complex that may have housed traveling troops of actors performing at the theater in Delos.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Grumentum
properties.description: Grumentum's amphitheater (first century B.C.) is the only known example in Lucania. The arena measures ca. 62.5 by 60 meters.

properties.title: Porticus margaritaria
properties.description: A place located in regio VIII that was connected with jewelers. While the porticus itself is mentioned only in the Regionary Catalogues, numerous extant inscriptions attest to the shops of jewelers in the vicinity of the Sacra Via.

properties.title: Forum Suarium
properties.description: A forum venalium of ancient Rome linked to the sale of pork, the Forum Suarium is mentioned in two inscriptions date ca. 200 CE. The forum lay near the barracks of the urban cohorts (cohortes urbanae) in the northern portion of the Campus Martius, perhaps near the location of the present Via di Propaganda in metropolitan Rome.

properties.title: Abbotsbury Abbey
properties.description: Abbotsbury Abbey is a Benedictine abbey located in Dorset, England. It was founded in c.1026 for secular canons, became a monastery of the Benedictine order in 1044, and was dissolved in 1539.

properties.title: Claudia
properties.description: A Roman rural tribe that was one of the most ancient of Rome's gentes. The gens Claudia traced its history to the earliest days of the Roman Republic. Appius Claudius Sabinus Regillensis, in 495 B.C., was the first of its members to hold the consulship.

properties.title: Mes Aynak
properties.description: The site of Mes Aynak in modern Afghanistan flourished between the between the fifth and seventh centuries A.D. More than 400 Buddha statues, stupas, and a 40 ha monastery complex have been documented at the site.

properties.title: Hubušnu (kingdom)
properties.description: Hubušnu is a small kingdom in Tabal that is mentioned in Assyrian royal inscriptions of the first millennium BC.

properties.title: Mulî (mountain)
properties.description: Mulî is a mountain in Tabal. Inscriptions of the ninth-century-BC Assyrian king Shalmaneser III (r. 858-824 BC) refer to it as "the mountain of alabaster."

properties.title: Via Triumphalis necropolis
properties.description: A segment of an imperial necropolis preserved along a portion of a consular road on the Vatican Hill. The Via Triumphalis necropolis was uncovered during the construction of a parking structure in the Via del Pellegrino.

properties.title: Greek theater at Alabanda
properties.description: The Greek theater at Alabanda dates to the Hellenistic period.

properties.title: Tell Taya
properties.description: Tell Taya is an archaeological site located in Iraq's Nineveh Province. The site was occupied from the third to the first millennia B.C.

properties.title: Tell al-Fakhar
properties.description: Tell al-Fakhar is located in northeastern Iraq. Excavations between 1967 and 1969 two occupation phases dating to the Mitanni/Kassite and Neo-Assyrian periods.

properties.title: Hirbemerdon Tepe
properties.description: A settlement in the upper Tigris River Valley inhabited from the Chalcolithic period through the Iron Age.

properties.title: Kalatepe
properties.description: A Chalcolithic mound near the village of Büyükgülücek, 15 km. north of Alaca Höyük.

properties.title: A'ali Mound Cemetery
properties.description: A large complex of burial mounds located near the town of A'ali in central Bahrain. The burials date to the early Dilmun era, ca. 2050-1700 BCE.

properties.title: Palace of Tupkish
properties.description: Palace at the Hurrian city Urkesh, constructed by Tupkish in the late third millennium BCE.

properties.title: Serra Orrios
properties.description: An important nuragic complex that includes remains of a megalithic megaron-type structure.

properties.title: Achaia (spring)
properties.description: An ancient spring said by Pausanias to be near Dorion in Messenia, its precise location is unknown.

properties.title: Amiternum (Samnium)
properties.description: An ancient city in Samnium located between Interamna Lirenas and Atina perhaps corresponding to the modern comune of Sant'Elia Fiumerapido (FR).

properties.title: Arene
properties.description: A spring that Pausanias places at Lepreon. Its precise location is not known today.

properties.title: Pontinos (river)
properties.description: A river of the Argolid, near Lerna, mentioned by Pausanias. Its precise location cannot be determined today.

properties.title: Pontinos (mountain)
properties.description: A mountain peak mentioned by Pausanias whose precise identity and location can not be determined today. Pausanias places it in Argolis, above Lerna and reports that a ruined sanctuary of Athena Saitis was to be found at its summit in his day.

properties.title: Castra of Drobeta
properties.description: A Roman castrum dating to the reign of Trajan located on the Danube, at Turnu-Severin, Romania.

properties.title: Grotta Porcina tumulus
properties.description: A rock-cut tumulus of the first half of the sixth century B.C.

properties.title: Hagno (spring)
properties.description: A spring on Mount Lykaion, mentioned by Pausanias and associated in his narrative with the sanctuary of Zeus Lykaios. The exact location of the spring is uncertain today.

properties.title: Euoras
properties.description: An ancient place in the Taygetos mountain range, described by Pausanias as being near a peak called Taleton. Its precise location cannot be determined today.

properties.title: Taleton Akra
properties.description: A peak in the Taygetos range, mentioned by Pausanias. Its precise location cannot be determined today.

properties.title: Villa della Pisanella
properties.description: A Roman villa rustica at Boscoreale that was first discovered in 1868 by Modestino Pulzella. The villa is best known as the findspot of the so-called "Boscoreale Treasure". Following excavation, the remains of the villa were reinterred.

properties.title: Sikani
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources that is generally identified with Tell Fekheriye (Tell Faḫārīya).

properties.title: Mandra Castellone
properties.description: A fortified Oscan center at high altitude (647 meters) located near Capriati al Volturno. The site is difficult to access and the fortifications measure 80 meters in diameter.

properties.title: Minorca (island)
properties.description: Minorca is one of the Balearic Islands of the Mediterranean Sea. Its name likely derives from the Latin 'Insula minor'.

properties.title: Chatal Höyük (Amuq)
properties.description: Mound site in the Amuq Plain inhabited from the late 4th millennium BCE-mid-1st millennium BCE. In the Late Bronze Age Chatal Höyük was the site of a sizeable town with connections to the Hittite Empire. In the Iron Age the town was within the sphere of the Syro-Hittite state of Unqi, based at Tell Tayinat/Kinaliya. The town gradually declined, but remained inhabited without interruption until at least the fifth century BCE.

properties.title: Villa Prato, Sperlonga
properties.description: A villa rustica excavated by the École française de Rome between 1979 and 1984.

properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Paestum was built ca. 50 B.C., making it one of the earliest extant amphitheaters.

properties.description: Minar-i Chakri, located in the Kabul province of Afghanistan, was the site of a Kushan-era pillar dating to the second or third century AD that was destroyed in the later twentieth century by the Soviet army.

properties.title: Peshawar
properties.description: Ancient Peshawar was a capital of the Gandharan kingdom from the second century AD, when it was known as Purushapura.

properties.title: Platea (island)
properties.description: An island in the Aegean Sea mentioned by Pliny. It is probably to be identified with the modern Khamilonisi.

properties.title: Palaiokastro
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 57 B6 Palaiokastro

properties.title: Catacomba di San Giovanni
properties.description: Ancient catacombs in the city of Siracusa, built between AD 315 and 360. The main gallery re-purposes parts of an earlier aqueduct.

properties.title: Byrsa
properties.description: Walled citadel in Carthage built in the early first millennium BCE. The site was destroyed during the Third Punic War in 146 BCE by the forces of Scipio Aemilianus. The hill became the site of the city's forum in the Roman period.

properties.title: Roman villa
properties.description: Archaeological remains of modest Roman villas in the theater district of Colonia Iulia Carthago.

properties.title: Bouleuterion at Patara/Arsinoe
properties.description: The Bouleuterion at Patara/Arsinoe sits on the agora opposite the theater.

properties.title: Caupona and Domus of L. Vetutius Placidus and Ascula
properties.description: A thermopolium with a marble counter (I.8.8), connected to a private house (I.8.9) in Regio I, insula 8 in Pompeii. The walls of the house show extensive decoration in the Third style.

properties.title: Caminia (island)
properties.description: An island mentioned in ancient sources, probably to be associated with modern Astakida.

properties.title: Cyclades Islands
properties.description: An island group in the Aegean Sea composed of over 200 islands.

properties.title: Aegaeum Mare
properties.description: The Aegean Sea is the largest body of water between Greece and Asia Minor and an embayment of the Mediterranean Sea.

properties.title: Aigila/Ogylos (island)
properties.description: Aigila/Ogylos Ins. (Antikythera) is an island in the Aegean Sea located between Crete and the Peloponnese.

properties.title: Torre di Pietra Pertusa
properties.description: A Medieval tower along the Via Flaminia near Prima Porta.

properties.title: Ponte Molino
properties.description: A Roman segmental arch bridge across the Bacchiglione river in Padua, Italy.

properties.title: Ponte di San Lorenzo
properties.description: An early segmental arch bridge, built between 47 and 30 B.C.

properties.title: Grimes Graves
properties.description: Grimes Graves is the site of a Neolithic flint mining complex near Brandon in England that was in use from ca. 3000 to 1900 BC.

properties.title: Etruscan sanctuary of San Lorenzo Nuovo
properties.description: An Etruscan sanctuary located on Monte Landro northwest of Lake Bolsena.

properties.title: Arch of Malborghetto
properties.description: A fourth century A.D. tetrapylon arch at the intersection of the Via Flaminia and a road linking the Via Tiberina and Veii.

properties.title: Pen-y-crug
properties.description: Pen-y-crug is the location of an Iron Age hill fort in south Wales.

properties.title: Offa's Dyke
properties.description: Offa's Dyke is a linear earthwork of the eighth century that formed a boundary between the Anglian kingdom of Mercia and the Welsh kingdom of Powys.

properties.title: Large Theater
properties.description: The so-called "Large Theater" at Pompeii was built in the Greek style during the second century B.C. Its capacity was approximately 5,000 spectators.

properties.title: Fontager necropolis
properties.description: A necropolis in Gallia Narbonensis discovered within the thirteenth century Chateau de Fontager in 1963-1964.

properties.title: Aswan Quarry Landscape
properties.description: Quarry region around the town of Aswan in Upper Egypt.

properties.title: Beycesultan
properties.description: An ancient Anatolian settlement occupied from the Late Chalcolithic period through the Bronze Age.

properties.title: Arch of Trajan at Benevento
properties.description: A triumphal arch built in honor of Trajan at Beneventum; it marks the Trajanic extension of the Via Appia.

properties.title: Quartier du Stade at Delos
properties.description: Neighborhood surrounding the stadium in the settlement of Delos, constructed during the Hellenistic period.

properties.title: Quadriporticus of the theatre
properties.description: A four-sided portico standing behind the large theater of Pompeii (VIII, 7, 16-17). The complex was constructed ca. 80 BC.

properties.title: Eniggidrukalamasuma
properties.description: The temple of the god Nabû of the ḫarû as at Borsippa. The Sumerian ceremonial name Eniggidrukalamasuma means "House which Bestows the Scepter of the Land."

properties.title: Aštamaku
properties.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources that is identified with modern Tell Mastumah.

properties.title: Salvatoretto
properties.description: The remains of a Roman villa and cistern.

properties.title: Acropolis?
properties.description: The possible location of the acropolis of Makra Kome, according to Stählin (1924, 224) and Béquignon (1937, 316).

properties.title: Lacus pastorum
properties.description: A place in Regio III, likely located to the south of the Baths of Trajan.

properties.title: Lyubotin Gorodishche
properties.description: Fortified Scythian settlement near the town of Lyubotin in eastern Ukraine, inhabited from the late 8th century BCE-3rd century CE.

properties.title: Church of the Holy Apostles
properties.description: A fourteenth century church at Thessalonica.

properties.title: Puentecillas
properties.description: A bridge of the sixteenth century that rests on Roman foundations.

properties.title: Mount Nebo
properties.description: A mountain in Jordan rising to ca. 817 meters (2680 feet) above sea level, Mount Nebo is connected with the Hebrew prophet Moses and a Christian site (4th century AD) stands on its summit.

properties.title: Enlil temple (Kalhu)
properties.description: When Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud) became the principal administrative center of the Assyrian Empire in the ninth century BC, king Ashurnasirpal II (r. 883–859 BC) built (or rebuilt) numerous temples. One of those was dedicated to the god Enlil. Although its location is not known, the Enlil temple at Kalhu is thought to have been situated within the Ninurta temple complex, in the northwest corner of the citadel.

properties.title: Ara del Tufo necropolis
properties.description: An Etruscan necropolis at Tuscania.

properties.title: Solsbury Hill
properties.description: Solsbury Hill is a flat-topped hill in Somerset, England, that is the site of an Iron Age hill fort.

properties.title: Small Down Knoll hill fort
properties.description: Small Down Knoll is the site of a Bronze Age hill fort near Evercreech in Somerset, England.

properties.title: Temple of the Oxus
properties.description: The Temple of the Oxus is a Seleucid-era temple situated within the citadel of Takhti-Sangin, a Graeco-Bactrian town between the Vakhsh and Panj rivers.

properties.title: Tamiryn Ulaan Khoshuu
properties.description: Burial site located near the northern bank of the Tamir River in Mongolia. The site contains nearly 300 burials dated to the Xiongnu period (ca. 3rd century BCE-1st century CE).

properties.title: Arkaim
properties.description: A third- and second-millennium BC archaeological site located in the Southern Urals steppe.

properties.title: Lupercal
properties.description: A cave located at the foot of the Palatine Hill in Rome in which the she-wolf was said to have been found suckling the twins, Romulus and Remus.

properties.title: Akkad
properties.description: Akkad (Māt-Akkadî) is the name of a historical region of central Mesopotamia (northern Babylonia). During the Sargonic/Akkadian Period (ca. 2334-2113 B.C.), its capital was the city of Agade, which may have been located somewhere near the confluence of the Diyala and Tigris Rivers. In cuneiform texts of the first millennium B.C., the term Māt-Akkadî was used for the name of the region roughly comprising the northern half of Babylonia, now modern-day central Iraq.

properties.title: Hatti (region)
properties.description: In Assyrian and Babylonian texts of the first millennium BC, Hatti is a purely geographical term referring to North Syria, the area roughly covered by Syro-Hittite states west of the Euphrates River.

properties.title: Castro de Coaña
properties.description: A Pre-Roman oppidum located in the modern Spanish province of Asturias.

properties.title: Murat Tepe
properties.description: Settlement on the Murat River inhabited during the Urartian and Byzantine periods. It is located near, but distinct from, the Bronze Age-Medieval site of Murat Höyük.

properties.title: Accu Sa Pira Nuraghe
properties.description: A monopteral nuraghe located near Quartu Sant'Elena.

properties.title: Adapazarı Ovası
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Sumere
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Arbēla
properties.description: A place from the TAVO Index

properties.title: Archiepiscopal Chapel of Ravenna
properties.description: A private, early Christian oratory in Ravenna, Italy, erected by Peter II as archbishop in A.D. 495.

properties.title: Šūhi Canal Gate
properties.description: The Neo-Babylonian kings Nabopolassar (r. 625–605 BC) and Nebuchadnezzar II (r. 604–562 BC) constructed an outer wall around the eastern side of Babylon. That mudbrick wall is reported to have had 120 towers and 5 entrances, including the Šūhi Canal Gate. This access point to the city was probably located on the northeastern stretch of the wall.

properties.title: Nossa Senhora da Tourega
properties.description: An imperial villa located in the territory of Ebora.

properties.title: House of the Sundial at Baelo
properties.description: House at Baelo Claudia located across the colonnaded street from the House of the West.

properties.title: Metsamor
properties.description: A prehistoric site with megalithic standing stones.

properties.title: Porticus Aemilia
properties.description: A utilitarian porticus and storage building located outside the Porta Trigemina, the Porticus Aemilia was erected in 193 BCE by Marcus Aemilius Lepidus and and Lucius Aemilius Paullus.

properties.title: Molino San Vincenzo
properties.description: Field survey, geophysical prospection, as well as targeted research and training excavations, have revealed the remains of a mid- to late imperial rural settlement with evidence for agricultural activity. However, the earliest finds (e.g. bucchero) date to the sixth/fifth century B.C., indicating the likelihood of Etruscan settlement activities at this site. The entire site seems to have undergone severe recycling and reuse processes in late antiquity and the remaining structures have broken down systematically in modern times. Ongoing intensive agricultural activities affect the few archaeological structures that remain, resulting in a poor state of preservation.

properties.title: Palace of Naqi'a
properties.description: The influential Neo-Assyrian queen Naqi’a built a royal residence for her son Esarhaddon in the citadel of Nineveh. This palace, which may have served as a summer residence for the Assyrian king and his mother, remains unlocated. It is certain from contemporary Akkadian inscriptions that the palace was constructed near the Sîn-Šamaš temple, but the exact location of that temple is not known.

properties.title: Eildon Hill hill fort
properties.description: Eildon Hill hill fort, a hill fort located on the northern peak of Eildon hill, is the largest Iron Age fort in Scotland, covering 39 acres.

properties.title: Crac des Chevaliers
properties.description: An ancient castle, located in modern Syria. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2006 as part of the "Crac des Chevaliers and Qal’at Salah El-Din" listing.

properties.title: Qalb Lozé
properties.description: An ancient place, located in modern Syria, with remains of an ancient basilica. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011 as part of the "Ancient Villages of Northern Syria."

properties.title: Deirouné
properties.description: An ancient place, located in modern Syria, with remains of a monastic chapel. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011 as part of the "Ancient Villages of Northern Syria."

properties.title: Kafr Aqareb
properties.description: An ancient place, located in modern Syria, with remains of Roman praetorium, a temple and grottoes for pagan worship, a Byzantine basilica, and a large communal reservoir. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011 as part of the "Ancient Villages of Northern Syria."

properties.title: Galatas
properties.description: A Minoan palatial center on Crete dated ca. 1700-1600 BC that was discovered in the 1990s.

properties.title: Narekavank
properties.description: Narekavank, or Narek Monastery, was a tenth-century Armenian monastery near the southern shore of Lake Van. It was a major monastic center, and the mystical poet Grigor Narekatsi (951-1003) studied and resided there. The monastery was abandoned and demolished in the 20th century.

properties.title: Fort Shalmaneser
properties.description: The ninth-century-BC Assyrian king Shalmaneser III (r. 858–824 BC) constructed an impressive palatial complex in the southeastern corner of the city Kalhu (biblical Calah). This armory, which the seventh-century-BC ruler Esarhaddon (r. 680–669 BC) referred to as an ēkal māšarti (‘review palace’), was completed ca. 846 BC. Fort Shalmaneser, the name of building dubbed by its excavators, remained in use until the very end of the Assyrian Empire (612 BC), although its importance was significantly diminished after the Assyrian court moved away from Kalhu at the end of the eighth century BC, first to Dūr-Šarrukīn and then to Nineveh.

properties.title: Mugharet Abu Halimeh
properties.description: Cave tomb near the modern village of Silat aḑ-Ḑahr containing burials from the Roman and Byzantine periods (1st-early 7th century CE). The cave is named after the Abu Halimeh family, which owned the land on which the cave is located at the time of its excavation in 1949.

properties.title: Governor's Palace at Kalhu
properties.description: This beautifully-decorated Assyrian palace is located just north of the Nabû temple Ezida, in the southeast quarter of the citadel of Kalhu (biblical Calah, modern Nimrud). The building likely served as the office and/or residence of several important individuals in the administration of the Assyrian Empire, probably including the governor of Kalhu. Numerous cuneiform tablets were discovered in three rooms north of the central courtyard. Because many of those Akkadian texts relate to the activities of several governors, British excavators in the 1950s dubbed the building the "Governor's Palace."

properties.title: Mousa
properties.description: Mousa is an island in Shetland, Scotland.

properties.title: Sitagroi
properties.description: Sitagroi is the location of an important archaeological site from the late Neolithic period and early Bronze Age.

properties.title: Mausoleum of Bibi Maryam at Qalhat
properties.description: The Mausoleum of Bibi Maryam at Qalhat was built for Baha al-Din Ayaz, the successor of Mahmud b. Ahmad al-Qusi al-Qalhati, the founder of the Hormuz empire which flourished from the eighth to the fourteenth century.

properties.title: Veranes
properties.description: A Roman villa.

properties.title: Tell Ischali
properties.description: Tell Ishchali is an archaeological site in Iraq's Diyala province. Its main floruit in antiquity was from ca. 2700–1800 BC, primarily Dynastic through the Isin–Larsa period. The site was part of the city-state of Eshnunna.

properties.title: Untitled

properties.title: Theater at Leuke
properties.description: The theater is located at the north-east end of Kouphonesi. It was a stone-built building that could accommodated ca. 1000 spectators.

properties.title: Band-e Kaisar
properties.description: A third century AD Roman bridge located near Shushtar, Iran.

properties.title: Cave of Anigrid Nymphs
properties.description: A healing sanctuary connected with the river nymphs of the river Anigros. The cave is in proximity to the thermal springs of Lake Kaiafas.

properties.title: Kaneš
properties.description: Kaneš or Kanesh (Hittite: Neša) is located adjacent to modern Kültepe, thus at times the site is referred to as Kültepe Kaneš. The site was one of continuous occupation from the Chalcolithic period to the time of the Roman empire, although its cultural zenith was as a major Hittite site that was the site of a large merchant quarter (kârum) of the Old Assyrian kingdom (ca. twentieth to sixteenth centuries BC).

properties.title: Temple of Thelsae
properties.description: A well-preserved Roman period temple located in modern Dmeir, Syria. The sanctuary was later converted into a fortification.

properties.title: Sîn-Šamaš Temple
properties.description: One of the temples in the citadel of Nineveh that was dedicated to the moon-god Sîn and the sun-god Šamaš. Its Sumerian ceremonial name is not preserved in extant cuneiform sources and its exact location remains unknown. The temple is generally believed to have been east of the temples of Ištar (Emašmaš) and Nabû (Ezida) and south of the North Palace (palace of Ashurbanipal).

properties.title: Saint-Aunès milestone
properties.description: A Roman milestone of the Via Aurelia.

properties.title: Oppidum du Castellan
properties.description: A Gallic oppidum occupied from the sixth century B.C.

properties.title: Roman amphitheater at Trier
properties.description: The Roman amphitheater at Trier dates to the reign of Antoninus Pius and was renovated under Constantius Chlorus. The arena measures ca. 71 x 47.5 meters.

properties.title: Balsignano
properties.description: A fortified Medieval site located in Puglia.

properties.title: Theater of Zea
properties.description: Visible remains of a Hellenistic theater located to the west of the Zea Harbor in Piraeus, dating ca. 200 B.C.

properties.title: Nuraghe Palmavera

properties.title: Poggino necropolis

properties.title: Villa del Vergigno, Montelupo Fiorentino
properties.description: A large villa rustica inhabited from ca. 100 B.C. to A.D. 500, located near Montelupo Fiorentino in the mid-Arno Valley of northern Tuscany, approximately twenty km west of Florence.

properties.title: Marina di Palo Roman villa
properties.description: An Imperial maritime villa located in Ladispoli, Italy.

properties.title: Temple of Hera, Olympia
properties.description: The Temple of Hera at Olympia, also known as the Heraion, is a peripteral temple in the northwest corner of the Altis precinct that is dedicated to Hera. Built ca. 600-590 B.C., the Heraion is the oldest temple at Olympia and one of the earliest known examples of the Doric order in Greece.

properties.title: Temple of the Severan family
properties.description: Near a complex of baths built under Commodus a Severan complex that included a plaza, porticoes, and a temple dedicated to the Severan family was added.

properties.title: Sceilg Mhichíl
properties.description: A monastic complex on Skellig Michael established in the seventh century A.D. and enrolled as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.

properties.title: Colombarone
properties.description: An archaeological site that preserves remains of a Late Roman settlement along the Via Flaminia.

properties.title: Sant'Ilario
properties.description: A paleochristian site located at the thirtieth mile of the ancient via Labicana, near to the ancient road station 'ad Bivium'.

properties.title: Tre Ponti necropolis
properties.description: A necropolis along the Via Amerina, likely in use from the third century BC until the third century AD.

properties.title: Villa di Teodorico
properties.description: A palatial Roman villa and bath complex that has been connected with Theodoric the Great, with twentieth century interpretations labeling it as Theodoric's "hunting lodge". More recent excavations have uncovered evidence for earlier building phases, dating from the first century B.C. through the third century A.D.

properties.description: A Neo-Babylonian rock relief of Nebuchadnezzar II was found in the area of the modern city Qubbayat, close to the Wadi Oustane and the Jebel Akroum. The monument at Shir as-Sanam is about 16 Km from Qubbayat, on the road to Chambouq and Hermel. It is about located ca. 120 meters from the road, on the western side, 15 m. above the ground.

properties.description: Mentioned by Thucydides, the "Phaleric Wall" (a third major component of Athens' "Long Walls") extended toward Phaleron, but became obsolete already late in the Peloponnesian War. It may have been destroyed or allowed to deteriorate and was subsequently spoliated and reused for building matieral: no trace of this fortification has been identified in modern times.

properties.title: Dema wall
properties.description: The so-called Dema wall was a built fortification of ancient Attica that was intended to a close a gap between between Aigaleos and Parnes. The wall's course originally ran more than 4 km.

properties.title: Makra Teiche
properties.description: The Makra Teiche or "Long Walls" of Athens were built in the middle of the fifth century B.C. and connected Athens to its ports at Piraeus and Phalerum. They were destroyed by the Spartans after the Athenian surrender in 403 B.C., and rebuilt during the beginning of the Corinthian War, which started in 395 B.C. The walls were ultimately destroyed by Sulla during his siege against Athens in 86 B.C.

properties.title: Tomb of Seuthes III
properties.description: An elaborate tomb located near Kazanlak, Bulgaria. The Tomb of Seuthes III, who was King of the Odrysian Kingdom from ca. 331 to ca. 300 BC, is found in the Valley of the Thracian Rulers.

properties.title: Tumulus of Xhendremael

properties.title: Stiris/Steiris
properties.description: An ancient settlement of eastern Phocis. The site of ancient Steiri has only ever been partly explored and defined. The city was located in an area known locally today as Paliokhori. The acropolis has been identified on a hill locally known today as Bouli, where a church or monastery of Agios Nikolaos (now ruined?) reportedly succeeded it. The site was not coincident with the modern town that has inherited the ancient name. Rather, ancient Stiris was located to the south and east of the famous monastery of Hosios Loukas, which lies between modern Steiri and modern Kyriaki (archaeological evidence for fortifications and other structures have, however, been noted both at modern Steiri and at Hosios Loukas as elsewhere in the area).

properties.description: According to the Babylonian topographical text Tintir = Babylon, New City (ālu eššu) was one of the six city districts of the eastern half of the inner city of Babylon and it contained two temples and one dais. properties.title: House of the Vettii
properties.description: The so-called House of the Vettii (VI, 15, 1) is a luxurious townhouse (domus) located in Pompeii. The house's owners in its final phase were the freedmen brothers Aulus Vettius Conviva, an Augustalis, and Aulus Vettius Restitutus. Among other features the house is important for its Fourth Style wall paintings.

properties.title: Mithraeum at Fertőrákos
properties.description: A well-preserved Mithraeum with modern stone vault above ground and site below in Fertőrákos, Hungary, at the site of ancient Scarbantia.

properties.title: Royal Palace of Māri
properties.description: Royal residence of the rulers of the kingdom of Mari. Constructed in the 24th century BCE, the site is also known as the Palace of Zimri-Lim, the ruler who completed extensive renovations of the structure around 1800 BCE.

properties.title: Barbarathermen at Trier
properties.description: Dating to the second century, the so-called "Barbara Baths" (Barbarathermen in German) are the largest Roman bath complex known north of the Alps. The bath complex was reused first as a Medieval castle and then as a seventeenth century Jesuit college. The ruins were designated as part of the "Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St. Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier" UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

properties.title: Bulls of Guisando
properties.description: A series of Celtiberian sculptures located near El Tiemblo, Ávila, Spain. These statues were perhaps originally created during the second century BC.

properties.title: Gaziantep
properties.description: Gaziantep, also referred to as Antep, is located in southeastern Turkey. The site has a long history of settlement that begins in the Neolithic period. The site has a significant Hittite presence. Some scholars suggest it is the site of the Hellenistic city of Antiochia ad Taurum.

properties.description: Excavations on site of post office at 49 Ben Ami St. revealed Hellenistic remains, including a dedication to Zeus Soter on behalf of Antiochos VII by a courtier (SEG XIX 9094). This inscription was associated with Hellenistic architecture of a temple-like character. Nearby workshops also uncovered.

properties.title: Theater of Cyrene

properties.title: Tell 'Ali
properties.description: A small site on the left bank of the Lower Zab where an archive of ca. twenty-five Middle Assyrian texts was discovered. The town was situated more or less where travellers from Aššur to the cities Nuzi and Arrapha would have crossed the Lower Zab. Tell 'Ali is identified with ancient Atmannu.

properties.title: Tell Bazmusian
properties.description: A site on the right bank of the Lower Zab that was excavated by Iraqi archaeologists in 1956–58. Tell Bazmusian, whose ancient name is not known, is one of the largest archaeological sites in the Ranya Plain (Sulaymaniyah Governorate, Iraq). The city was occupied from the sixth millennium BCE to the ninth century CE. A small group of Middle Assyrian tablets were discovered in a pit outside the city’s temple. Tell Bazmusian is now submerged under Lake Dukan.

properties.title: Ager Faliscus (region)
properties.description: The territory of the Faliscans that lay between areas where Etruscan, Latin, and Sabellic languages were spoken. The geographic limits of this territory on the right bank of the Tiber River stretch from Grotta Porciosa in the north to Capena in the south.

properties.title: Theater of Melos

properties.title: Temple of Quirinus

The temple was built ex manubiis by Lucius Papirius Cursor in 293 B.C., fulfilling the vow made by his father in 325 B.C. Tradition holds that the republican-period temple was sited on an even earlier altar dedicated by the Sabines. The topography and location of the temple are both matters of significant debate.

This region reportedly contained eight shrines (aediculae), 88 domūs, 18 warehouses (horrea), 75 bath houses, and 78 loci. Its perimeter is given as 13,000 Roman feet (approximately 3.84 km).

In late antiquity it (along with several of the surrounding tombs) was repurposed as an anchorite dwelling, called in modern times the "Monastery of Cyriacus."

properties.title: Pergamum
properties.description: An important ancient settlement, located at modern Bergama in Turkey. It was first described in Xenophon's Anabasis and was later used as a treasury under Lysimachus. Pergamum became the administrative capital and principal city of the Attalid kingdom and dynasty (282-133 BCE) and was briefly the first capital of the Roman province of Asia. It later was a seat of a Christian bishopric and is listed in Revelation as one of the seven churches of Asia. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014 under "Pergamon and its Multi-Layered Cultural Landscape".

properties.title: Razliq
properties.description: Razliq is a village situated ca. 13 km north of the city Sarāb in Eastern Azerbaijan (Iran). Here a rock inscription of the Urartian king Argišti II, son of Rusa (end of 8th / first half of 7th century BCE), has been found which reports military campaigns of Argišti II to this region. As well as the rock inscription of Nashteban (CTU A 11-5) it is situated on the southern slope of the Sabalān Mountains at an altitude of 4810 m. Although the inscription reports the building of a fortress named ‘stronghold of Argišti’ no such archaeological remains have been discovered so far. Together with the rock inscriptions found in Nashteban (CTU A 11-5) and Shisheh (CTU A 11-6) the rock inscription found near Razliq is one of the Urartian inscriptions found furthest to the east.

properties.title: Gövelek
properties.description: Gövelek is a village situated 27 km to the east of Van in the southeast of Turkey. Here the upper part of a stela with an inscription of Rusa, son of Erimena (presumably last quarter of 8th century BCE) was found. It reports his military success and describes deportations from the city Ṭušpa, the building of the city Rusaḫinili, and the creation of an artificial lake called "Lake of Rusa". The lake was supposed to ensure the water supply for the capital Ṭušpa (modern Van Kalesi), a function it still performs today. The lower part of the stela has been found at the shore of the lake.

properties.title: Thermae Helenianae
properties.description: The Thermae Helenianae or Thermae Helenae was a thermal complex located in the Horti Spei Veteris, also referred to as the Horti Variani. The baths were situated near the arcus Neroniani adjacent to the Amphitheatrum Castrense. As Helena, mother of Constantine I, restored them following a fire in 323-326, they are named for her.
